ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.heroSubtitle: Parents type IB IGCSE tuition near me in Ajman because proximity feels like proof. It is not. A graduate living fifteen minutes from Al Nuaimiya may never have marked a Cambridge Extended paper, while a subject specialist on live video can hand you three annotated scripts before you pay for a second session. This page is about that evidence: marked papers, criterion sheets, a written record after every lesson. Nobody inspects private tutors in Ajman on your behalf, so the proof has to be something you can read.

ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE and IB subjects to Ajman students over live video. Each works to a fixed habit: read the student's last marked paper first, name the specific marks lost, then plan the sessions around those marks rather than around the next chapter in the textbook.

intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong test. Marked work is the right one.
paragraphs: A search for tuition near your address is really a search for someone accountable. Distance is the only accountability signal Google can give you, so parents use it. The trouble is that Ajman is small, the pool of people within a ten-minute drive who have actually examined a Cambridge Extended paper or supervised an IB exploration is smaller still, and a short commute tells you nothing about whether the hour was useful. Within a month most families stop asking how far the tutor lives and start asking a harder question: what changed?

That question has a documentary answer. A paper comes back with marks allocated question by question. A criterion sheet shows which band a draft sits in and which sentence moved it there. A session note records what was attempted, what was still wrong at the end, and what the student has to do before the next lesson. None of that depends on geography. All of it depends on whether the tutor marks to the published criteria rather than to a general impression, and on whether anyone shows the marking to the person paying for it.

Ajman makes the argument sharper than Dubai does. Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority with a public tutoring register, and a large share of Ajman families drive their children to schools in Sharjah or Dubai, or work there themselves. A 4pm slot is often impossible; a 7.30pm slot after the Emirates Road crawl is normal. An online specialist can hold that slot every week. Someone driving in from another emirate cannot hold it reliably, and the first thing to slip when traffic is bad is the written record.

So the structure of this page follows the evidence rather than the sales pitch. It starts with what a near-me search actually returns in this emirate, then moves through the first diagnostic, how a script is marked, what a parent receives in week one against week eight, and how to read three data points as a trend rather than a jump. After that come the figures: what the market charges in AED, with each band traced to the provider that published it, and the entry and results dates that decide when work has to be finished.

Two things this page will not do. It will not promise a grade, because no tutor can honestly promise one and the published outcome is the student's. And it will not describe a tutor arriving at an Ajman address: IB Gram delivers one-to-one teaching online across the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Everything below is written on that basis, including the cost comparison, which is more favourable to online delivery than most families expect once travel time is counted honestly.

ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Ajman students sit a narrower spread of qualifications than Dubai students do, and the three below cover almost all of it. What differs between them is not difficulty but where the marks are recorded: IGCSE puts nearly everything in a timed paper, while the MYP and the Diploma spread it across internal work that is marked at school and moderated later.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two to three years of subject courses assessed mainly by written papers, graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus and board. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel runs single-tier papers in most subjects with its own codes. The practical difference for tutoring is the mark scheme: command terms, mark allocation and accepted answers differ between boards even where the topic list looks identical.
programmes.countryNote: Most Ajman private schools entering IGCSE candidates use Cambridge, with Pearson Edexcel appearing more often in schools serving families who moved from a UK or Gulf British-curriculum setting. Ask the school's exams officer which syllabus code each subject is entered under before buying a revision guide, because a 0580 paper and a 4MA1 paper reward different working.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade by published boundaries. There is no external paper in most MYP years, so the entire record is internal: unit tasks, interdisciplinary work and the Personal Project in the final year. That makes the criterion wording the most important document a student owns.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman Academy runs the IB continuum locally, and other Ajman families travel to IB schools in Sharjah and Dubai. Because MYP marks are internal, an Ajman parent cannot compare their child against a national dataset; the only reliable comparison is the criterion descriptor itself, which is why tutoring at this level is mostly about reading the task sheet properly.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus three core components. Each subject carries internally assessed work worth roughly a fifth to a third of the grade, with the rest in externally marked papers sat in one session. Internal deadlines therefore arrive long before the exam window, and a student who misses them loses marks that cannot be recovered by revision.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman Diploma candidates are usually enrolled in Sharjah or Dubai schools, which means their internal deadlines are set by a school in another emirate while their study time is governed by an Ajman commute. Session planning has to start from the school's own deadline calendar, not from a generic Diploma timeline.

ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Ajman families ask about most, described by where the marks are recorded rather than by topic list. In each case the first session looks at the most recent marked piece of work, because that is where the diagnosable evidence already exists.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks are lost in two predictable places: unjustified steps in proof-style questions, and calculator work written down without the method that earns the method mark. The exploration adds a different failure, where a technically correct piece of mathematics scores poorly because the personal engagement and reflection criteria were never addressed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The content is more modelling and statistics, so the marking rewards interpretation sentences that many students skip. A regression line calculated correctly and then left uninterpreted is a half-mark answer, and that pattern repeats across the modelling questions in the final papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Written answers lose marks on precision of language, not on chemistry: 'the rate increases' where the mark scheme wants a named collision-frequency reason. In the internally assessed investigation, uncertainty treatment and a genuine evaluation of method are where otherwise strong work drops a band.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Graph work and data analysis carry more marks than students expect, and gradient-based questions are routinely answered without units. Long-answer questions ask for an explanation in steps; a single-sentence answer to a four-mark question is the most common avoidable loss at both levels.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content hides the real issue, which is command terms. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' have fixed expectations, and a student who writes the same density of answer for all three scores unevenly across a paper without understanding why.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended papers carry the higher grade ceiling and the questions that need multi-step reasoning. Method marks are available on almost every structured question, so working written in rough and not transferred to the answer space is a direct and recoverable loss.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The practical paper rewards knowledge of apparatus, variable control and sources of error rather than recall. Electricity and circuits remain the topic Ajman students most often arrive weakest in, usually because circuit diagrams were never drawn by hand enough times.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables are the two blocks that decide the grade. Students who learn the ion tests as a list rather than as observations tied to a conclusion lose the application marks on the Extended papers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English First Language 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses are marked on specific skills: selection of detail, inference and control of register. Essays written well in general terms but without close textual evidence sit in the middle bands no matter how fluent the prose is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is assessable in its own right, and a correctly labelled diagram with an explanation that does not reference it scores less than a simpler answer that does. Evaluation paragraphs are the standard difference between a middle and a top band at both levels.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material is the examined skill, not knowledge of the tool. A student who explains a Boston matrix in general terms and never applies it to the named organisation in the question has written most of a wrong answer.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Assessed across productive and receptive skills, with marks tied to registers rather than to vocabulary totals. Useful for Ajman students who speak Arabic at home but have been taught the written register only at school, where the gap is usually in formal writing conventions.

ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: Where in Ajman the students are, and what changes locally
ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact enough to drive across in twenty minutes, so the differences between its districts are not about distance. They are about which school the children attend, which emirate the parents work in, and therefore what time a weekly session can realistically start and still be worth paying for.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense, apartment-heavy and close to the Sharjah boundary, with several large Indian and British curriculum day schools in or near it. Sessions here usually start at 6pm or later because the school day ends late and siblings share one study space.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Older central Ajman with a mix of villas and towers near the Corniche. Families here often have one parent working in Ajman and one in Sharjah, which makes a fixed weekday evening slot easier to protect than a weekend one.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Industrial and residential blocks either side of Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, with quick access to Sharjah schools. The commute home is the constraint, so a 7.30pm start that holds every week beats a 5pm start that is cancelled twice a month.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa communities spread over three sub-districts, popular with families whose children attend school in Sharjah. Siblings at different stages are common here, which is why a shared diagnostic session at the start is often more useful than two separate enquiries.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Newer low-rise villa areas towards the Emirates Road side of the emirate. Household internet is generally good, and the practical issue is study-space noise rather than bandwidth, so headphones and a fixed desk matter more than equipment.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zahya
regions.note: Developing communities along the Emirates Road corridor where several families moved from Dubai for space. Parents here most often compare an Ajman online rate with what they were paying for in-home tuition in Dubai, and the gap surprises them.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Seafront towers with a short school run but a long parental commute. Diploma students in this cluster tend to study late, and a 9pm review slot during coursework weeks is more realistic than an early evening one.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: High-rise residential blocks a long way from most Ajman schools, so children here often travel into Sharjah daily. The travel load is the single biggest reason families in this area choose online tuition over an in-home arrangement.

schoolClusters.city: Central Ajman: Al Nuaimiya, Al Rashidiya and Mushairef
schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE and Indian-curriculum candidates in the emirate. Students from these schools arrive with school-marked mocks already in hand, which makes the first diagnostic quick because the evidence exists before the first session is booked.

schoolClusters.city: The Emirates Road corridor: Al Mowaihat, Al Zahya and Al Yasmeen
schoolClusters.note: Newer villa communities feeding the emirate's international schools, including the one Ajman school running the IB continuum. MYP families here are the ones most often working from criterion descriptors rather than past papers.

schoolClusters.city: Cross-border: Ajman homes, Sharjah and Dubai classrooms
schoolClusters.note: A substantial number of Ajman students are enrolled outside the emirate, which means their internal deadlines are set under SPEA or KHDA while their study evenings are governed by an Ajman commute. Planning has to follow the school's calendar, not the emirate of residence.

ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three formats, and the difference between them is how often marked work changes hands. Families looking for tuition near their address usually assume they need the most frequent option; the diagnostic often shows that a fortnightly marking cycle with disciplined practice in between produces more visible movement for less money.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with a marked artefact
modes.description: A single sixty or ninety minute session each week on live video, built around the most recent piece of marked work. The session ends with something written down: an annotated question, a criterion sheet, or a short note naming the next three things to practise. This is the default for exam-year students and for anyone whose grades have moved in the wrong direction.
bullets: Same slot each week, held in Gulf Standard Time
Work marked to the published criteria for that syllabus
A written session note the parent receives, not a verbal summary
Practice set between sessions, reviewed at the start of the next one

modes.title: Fortnightly marking clinic
modes.description: The student works alone for two weeks on a defined set of past questions or a draft, then brings all of it to one longer session. Suited to students who are capable but careless, because the volume of marked evidence per session is higher and the pattern in the errors becomes visible rather than anecdotal.
bullets: A longer session, usually ninety to one hundred and twenty minutes
A batch of work marked together so the error pattern is legible
Cheaper per month than a weekly cycle at the same hourly rate
Works best from Year 10 upwards, where independent practice is realistic

modes.title: Coursework and exploration review blocks
modes.description: A fixed number of sessions timed to a school's internal deadlines for an exploration, Internal Assessment or Extended Essay. The tutor reads what the student has produced, maps it against the criterion wording, and asks questions. The student does the writing, keeps the drafts, and declares the help received if the school asks.
bullets: Scheduled backwards from the school's own internal deadline
Feedback expressed against criterion letters and mark bands
Drafts stay in the student's own file, dated and kept

sections.heading: What a near-me search actually returns in Ajman
paragraphs: Type a tuition query with your location into Google from an Ajman address and you get three kinds of result. First, aggregator listings that match on distance and nothing else, where the tutor's subject depth is a self-written line of text. Second, Dubai and Sharjah agencies that will take an Ajman enquiry but quote a travel surcharge or quietly decline once they see the postcode. Third, individual tutors advertising on classified sites, where the permit position and the subject experience are both unverifiable from the advert.

None of those results contain the information that decides whether the money is well spent. Distance is published; examining experience is not. Price is sometimes published; what the hour produces is not. A parent in Al Mowaihat comparing two listings a kilometre apart is comparing two facts that have no relationship to the grade, which is why so many families change tutor twice before the exam year is over.

The useful reframing is to treat the search as a request for accountability rather than a request for proximity. In an emirate the size of Ajman, the realistic specialist pool for a Higher Level Diploma subject or a specific Cambridge syllabus code is national rather than local, and once the lesson is delivered over video the pool becomes larger still. What you give up is the drive. What you gain is the ability to insist on a subject specialist and to see their marking before committing to a term.

That is the trade this page is arguing for, and it is a trade rather than a free gain. A screen is a worse place to read a long handwritten proof than a kitchen table, and a student who will not sit still for an hour without an adult in the room is a poor fit for online delivery. Both of those are worth saying out loud before a trial lesson rather than after one.
bullets: Distance is the only signal a listing site can rank on, and it predicts nothing about marks
Specialist cover for a single syllabus code is national, not district-level
Ask for marking from an actual student script before the first paid session
Online delivery is a poor fit for a student who cannot work unsupervised for an hour

sections.heading: The first session is a diagnostic, and here is what it reads
paragraphs: A first session that begins with the next chapter of the textbook has wasted the one hour in which the student will answer questions honestly. The first session should read evidence instead. Four documents between them explain almost every stalled grade: the most recent marked paper or mock, the school report with subject comments, the task sheet or criterion wording for any current internal work, and the student's own account of which topics they avoid.

Each of those documents answers a different question. The marked paper shows where marks were available and not taken, which is almost never the same as where the student feels weak. The report shows whether the school sees the same problem the parent does. The task sheet shows whether a piece of internal work is being written against the criteria at all. The student's own account shows what they will actually do between sessions, which determines whether a plan is realistic.

The output of the diagnostic is narrower than most parents expect. Rather than a programme covering the syllabus, it is usually three or four named failures with marks attached: method marks lost in transfer, command terms answered at the wrong depth, a criterion that has never been addressed, a topic genuinely not taught. Those are fixable in a defined number of sessions, and the number can be stated.

It also sometimes produces an honest negative. If the marked evidence shows a student losing marks through unfinished papers rather than through misunderstanding, the problem is timing and stamina, and weekly teaching is an expensive way to fix it. Saying so costs us an enquiry and saves a family a term's fees, which is the kind of judgement a parent should be able to expect before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: How a script is marked so a parent can read the result
paragraphs: Marking that says 'good effort, revise ratios' is not evidence. Marking that can be checked looks different: each question carries its available marks, the marks awarded, and a one-line reason tied to the mark scheme's own language. A parent who cannot read the subject can still read that, because the arithmetic is visible and the reason is specific enough to be argued with.

The mark scheme language matters more than it sounds. Cambridge and Pearson both publish what counts as an acceptable answer, and both award method marks independently of the final answer in structured questions. A student who reaches the right number with no working shown is losing marks that were sitting there, and a student with a wrong final answer and correct method is keeping marks they did not know they had. Neither pattern is visible from a percentage.

The same logic applies to internal work in the MYP and the Diploma, except that the units are criterion letters and band descriptors rather than marks per question. A criterion marked in the second band with a note explaining which sentence in the student's own draft keeps it there is useful feedback. A general comment that the analysis needs to be deeper is not, because the student cannot act on it without guessing.

This is also where honesty about limits belongs. Our marking is a tutor's judgement against published criteria; it is not the school's internal mark, and it is not a prediction of what an examiner will award. Internal work is marked by the school and moderated by the board, and a tutor's band estimate is a planning tool rather than a forecast. Any provider presenting it as a forecast is selling something they cannot deliver.
bullets: Marks available, marks awarded, and the reason in mark-scheme language

sections.heading: Week one against week eight: what the record should contain
paragraphs: Progress is a claim, and a claim needs a paper trail. Over an eight-week block the trail should thicken in a predictable way, and the parent should be able to check it without asking anyone's opinion. In week one there is a diagnostic note and a baseline piece of marked work. By week four there is a second marked attempt at the same question type, which is the first point at which movement can be measured rather than asserted.

By week eight the useful artefact is a timed paper or a full draft, marked the same way as the baseline so the comparison means something. Marking a baseline leniently and a later attempt strictly, or the reverse, destroys the comparison, which is why the same criteria and the same marker should run through the block. If the tutor changes mid-block, the comparison restarts.

What the record should not contain is attendance dressed up as progress. Eight session notes saying the student worked hard tell you only that eight hours were billed. The test to apply is simple: pick any week from the record and ask what was wrong at the start of that session and what was still wrong at the end. If the answer is not written down anywhere, the hour was not documented, whatever else it was.

Families who keep this record are also in a much stronger position with the school. A parents' evening where you can point to two marked attempts at the same question type and ask the teacher whether they see the same pattern is a different conversation from one where you report that your child is having tuition. Several Ajman families have used exactly that to get a subject teacher to look again at a predicted grade.

sections.heading: Reading three data points as a trend, not a jump
paragraphs: One mark is noise. Two marks are a direction. Three marks across different question types begin to be a trend, and a trend is the only thing worth acting on. Parents are usually shown single results, which is why tuition feels either miraculous or useless after a fortnight when in truth neither has been established yet.

The common illusions are worth naming. A student who jumps twelve marks on a topic test the week after that topic was taught has demonstrated recency, not learning; the same question type six weeks later is the real test. A student whose percentage falls while the paper difficulty rises may have improved. A student who gains marks on structured questions and loses them on extended-response questions has not improved overall, but has shown exactly where the next block should go.

This is also where the most common misreading of mock results happens. Mock papers in different schools are marked to different tolerances and sometimes scaled to manage expectations, so comparing a Year 10 school mock with a Year 11 school mock across a curriculum change is comparing two unlike things. The comparison that holds is the same past-paper question type, marked by the same person to the same published criteria, at two points in time.

None of this supports a promise about final grades, and no honest provider will give you one. What it supports is a defensible decision: continue, change the focus, change the tutor, or stop. Reaching that decision from marked evidence after eight weeks, rather than from a feeling after six months, is the practical return on insisting that every session leaves a document behind.

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tuition costs for an Ajman family, in AED
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are scarce, and the ones that exist belong to providers rather than to the market as a whole. The table below gathers what identifiable providers have put in writing, with the source named in the final column, so an Ajman parent can see the span rather than a single number presented as the going rate. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list; our own quote follows the trial lesson and depends on subject, level and frequency.

A few patterns are stable across the sources. Online delivery sits below in-home delivery at every level, and the gap widens in the northern emirates because an in-home visit to Ajman from a Sharjah or Dubai tutor base carries travel the parent ends up paying for in money, in a later start, or in cancellations. Specialist Higher Level and coursework work sits at the top of the range regardless of format, because the pool of people who can do it is small.

Monthly figures are more useful than hourly ones for budgeting, and here the published estimates diverge. Package offers seen in this market include an online monthly rate of roughly AED 799 for eight sessions, against in-home packages of around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. For a single weekly hour, Bestimate's own estimates run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at budget level, AED 600 to AED 1,200 at mid level, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Three things change the number for an Ajman household in particular. Whether the sibling discount applies, because multi-child enquiries are common here. Whether the subject needs a specialist or a generalist, which is the single largest factor. And whether the work is examination preparation or coursework review, since coursework blocks are quoted as a defined set of sessions against a school deadline rather than as an open-ended weekly commitment.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against the in-home market, for an Ajman address
paragraphs: This comparison deserves to be made properly rather than asserted, because an in-home tutor is a reasonable thing for a parent to want. Someone in the room can see the page, stop a bad habit as it forms and keep a reluctant fourteen-year-old at the desk. Those are real advantages and no honest page should pretend otherwise.

The costs are equally real and are usually underestimated. A tutor travelling to an Ajman address from a Sharjah or Dubai base spends between forty minutes and two hours on the round trip, and that time is paid for somewhere: a higher hourly rate, a two-hour minimum, or a start time that drifts. The tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to make that journey, which for a single Cambridge syllabus code or a Higher Level Diploma subject may be nobody. And the arrangement is fragile, because one road closure cancels the session rather than delaying it by five minutes.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that is a deliberate limit rather than an availability problem; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For UAE families, including every Ajman district listed above, teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for working and a document trail afterwards. We would rather state that plainly at the top of a page than let a parent discover it after an enquiry.

The practical case rests on specialist access and reliability rather than on price alone. A family in Al Yasmeen gets a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who marks to the published criteria, in a slot that holds through Ramadan timings, heavy traffic on the Emirates Road and a parent's travel week. The same family searching within a twenty-minute drive would be choosing from whoever happens to live nearby and be free.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines and results dates, counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost every panicked enquiry we take in the northern emirates is a calendar problem rather than a teaching problem. Entries close months before the papers are sat, forecast grades are submitted before the exam window, and coursework deadlines are set internally by the school. A family that learns those dates in January has choices; a family that learns them in March has fewer.

Cambridge publishes its key dates series by series, and the series that matters in Ajman is June, with November as the second window; those are the two Cambridge offers to UAE centres, while the series examined in February and March is an entry route for India. Read backwards from the June papers the sequence is consistent: final entries close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper; forecast grades are submitted by the school before the exam period opens; the papers run through June on the timetable for the centre's administrative zone; and results reach the school on Cambridge Direct in the summer, with certificates later. The entry deadline therefore sits months before the first paper, which is the whole argument for putting it on a family calendar in September rather than discovering it in the spring.

Two Cambridge details catch families out. Cambridge runs its main IGCSE and O Level examining in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is a question to ask the exams officer, not to assume.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the IB, we publish no session or results date here: the IB's own pages are not reliably retrievable for verification, so the only sound instruction is to take those dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: Coursework evidence: what a tutor may annotate and what the student owns
paragraphs: This is the boundary that decides whether tuition helps a student or ends their qualification, and it is worth being unambiguous. Internal work in the MYP and the Diploma, and coursework in those IGCSE subjects that carry it, must be the student's own. The student chooses the question, gathers the data, writes every sentence and keeps the dated drafts. A tutor's role is to teach the skills, read what already exists and ask questions about it.

In practice the useful help looks like this. Reading the criterion wording with the student until they can say what each band actually asks for. Pointing at a paragraph and asking what it is doing in the piece. Noting that a conclusion restates results rather than evaluating them. Teaching the statistical treatment or the citation convention as a skill, on an example that is not the student's own assessed piece. All of that is teaching, and none of it puts a tutor's words into an assessed text.

What falls outside is equally clear. Supplying text, rewriting a paragraph into its final form, selecting the research question on the student's behalf, or producing the data analysis for them. Providers who sell finished Internal Assessments exist in this market at advertised prices, and a student who buys one risks their whole diploma. We refuse that work, and we say so on the page rather than only in a terms document.

There is a record-keeping habit that protects the student. Keep every draft, dated. Keep a note of what help was received and from whom. If the school asks a student to declare support, declare it accurately; honest tuition described honestly causes no difficulty. Schools are generally far more concerned by work that appears from nowhere than by a student who can show how a piece developed over six weeks.
bullets: The student chooses the question, gathers the data and writes every sentence
Skills are taught on examples other than the assessed piece itself

sections.heading: The permit question, and when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated rather than informal. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, and the official service page is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a two working day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. The permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is wider than parents expect. The published categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone. Separately, Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid tutoring of students at their own school, which is worth knowing before asking a class teacher for private lessons.

Then there is availability, which almost nobody in this market discloses. For common subjects at IGCSE and Standard Level, a match is usually straightforward. For a narrow Higher Level combination, a minority language, or a specific coursework supervision need in a short window, there may be no suitable person free at the time you want. The honest options are then a different slot, a waiting period, or a recommendation to look elsewhere.

What we will not do is put a generalist in front of a Higher Level student and let the family find out in March. A page that promises every subject at every level at any hour is describing a sales process rather than a teaching capacity. If the diagnostic shows that what the student needs is not something we can staff properly, that is what the reply will say.

process.title: Send the marked evidence first
process.description: Share the most recent marked paper or school mock, the latest report and any current task sheet. Those three documents do most of the diagnostic work before anyone speaks, which is why the first conversation can be about specific lost marks rather than about general worries.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the evidence in front of the tutor
process.description: One session at no charge and with no card details taken. The tutor works through the marked paper with the student, tests two or three hypotheses about where the marks are going, and you receive a written note afterwards naming what they found.

process.title: Agree a block with a measurable end point
process.description: A defined number of weeks, a named baseline piece of work, and a second attempt at the same question type scheduled inside the block. Agreeing the comparison in advance is what makes the end-of-block review a decision rather than a discussion.

process.title: Weekly sessions that each leave a document
process.description: A fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, work marked to the published criteria, and a session note recording what was wrong at the start and what was still wrong at the end. Practice between sessions is set, returned and marked rather than suggested.

process.title: Review against the baseline, then decide
process.description: At the end of the block, compare the second marked attempt with the baseline, marked the same way by the same tutor. Continue, change focus, change tutor or stop. All four are legitimate outcomes, and the evidence rather than a sales conversation should choose between them.

whyPoints.title: Marking you can check
whyPoints.description: Marks available, marks awarded and a reason in the mark scheme's own language, question by question. A parent who does not know the subject can still audit the arithmetic and argue with the reason, which is the point of putting it in writing.

whyPoints.title: Specialists rather than whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online, the pool for a specific Cambridge syllabus code or a Higher Level Diploma subject is national rather than limited to people willing to drive into Ajman on a weekday evening. That matters most for exactly the subjects where generalist teaching fails.

whyPoints.title: Slots that survive the Ajman commute
whyPoints.description: Later evening starts, shifts to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and no cancellation when the Emirates Road or the Sharjah crossing is blocked. Reliability over a term is worth more than any single excellent session.

whyPoints.title: Figures with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider that published it, and none of them is presented as our own rate. Our quote follows the trial, because it depends on subject, level and how often the student actually needs to be seen.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach the skills, read what the student has produced and ask questions about it. We do not supply text for an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or any coursework, and we would rather lose the enquiry than put a student's qualification at risk.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer when we cannot staff it
whyPoints.description: Some narrow Higher Level combinations and minority languages have no suitable specialist free in the window a family needs. We say so and suggest where else to look rather than placing a generalist and hoping the family does not notice until the exam.

faqs.question: Does searching for tuition near me mean anything if the lesson happens on a screen?
faqs.answer: It means you want someone accountable, and distance is the only proxy a listing site can offer. Once teaching is delivered over live video, the useful questions change: does this tutor know the exact syllabus code, will they mark to the published criteria, and can you read the marking yourself. In an emirate the size of Ajman, insisting on a specialist in a narrow Higher Level subject and insisting on a short drive are often incompatible. Our lessons are online, one-to-one, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so the match is made on subject depth rather than on postcode.

faqs.question: What should we ask to see after the first paid session in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Three things. A note of what the tutor found in the marked evidence, written as specific lost marks rather than as general weaknesses. A named baseline piece of work that will be re-attempted later in the block so progress can be measured. And a between-session task small enough that it will actually be completed. If a provider cannot produce those after an hour of teaching, you have bought attendance rather than diagnosis. A parent in Al Mowaihat or Al Nuaimiya who asks for this at the start almost never has to argue about value at the end of the term.

faqs.question: How do you mark a Cambridge Extended paper so a parent can read the result?
faqs.answer: Question by question, with the marks available, the marks awarded and a one-line reason drawn from the mark scheme's own language. Method marks are recorded separately from the final answer, because the two tell different stories: a right answer with no working is losing marks that were available, and a wrong answer with sound method is keeping marks the student did not know about. A percentage hides both. The resulting sheet is readable by someone who does not know the subject, which is the test it has to pass.

faqs.question: How many weeks before a grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: A measurable change on the same question type usually appears somewhere between week four and week eight, provided the between-session practice is being done. Anything faster is normally recency rather than retention: a jump on a topic test the week after that topic was taught does not survive a six-week gap. The honest framing is that an eight-week block is long enough to produce a defensible comparison between a baseline and a second marked attempt, which is enough to decide whether to continue, change focus or stop.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tutors charge per hour for a family in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Published market figures run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour depending on level and format. EdFlik has published rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; Unitors published IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase published AED 270; BartyED published AED 650. In-home visits in this market run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is built in. Those are other providers' figures, cited so you can see the span. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson, because it depends on subject, level and frequency.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Al Mowaihat or Al Helio?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Teaching for Ajman families is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for working through questions and marked work returned afterwards. The trade is deliberate: you give up having someone in the room, and you gain a subject specialist for the exact syllabus your child sits, plus a slot that holds when the Sharjah crossing is blocked. If an adult in the room is genuinely what your child needs, an in-home provider is the better choice and we will say so.

faqs.question: Which exam board is an Ajman school likely to enter my child for?
faqs.answer: Most Ajman private schools entering IGCSE candidates use Cambridge International, with Pearson Edexcel appearing more often where the school serves families arriving from a UK or wider Gulf British-curriculum background. It is not safe to assume, because a single school can enter different subjects with different boards. Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code per subject, such as 0580 or 0620 for Cambridge, and check it against any revision material you buy. Mark schemes and accepted answers differ between boards even where the topic lists look nearly identical.

faqs.question: What is the last date we can enter our child for a Cambridge series?
faqs.answer: It depends on the series, and the two open to a UAE centre are June and November. For June, Cambridge's final entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper; for November they close well ahead of its own papers. In both cases the exact date reaches the family through the centre rather than from Cambridge, which is why the statement of entry is the document to ask for. The key dates that circulate online for a February and March sitting belong to the India entry route, so they are not a deadline an Ajman family can use. Entries are made by the school rather than by the family, so the practical step is to ask the exams officer in the autumn term which series each subject is entered for, what the centre's own internal deadline is, and to confirm both in writing.

faqs.question: How can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without crossing an IB rule?
faqs.answer: By teaching and questioning rather than producing. A tutor can read the criterion wording with the student until they can say what each band asks for, ask what a given paragraph is doing in the piece, note that a conclusion restates results instead of evaluating them, and teach a statistical method or citation convention using an example that is not the assessed piece. What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a section into final form, choose the research question or carry out the analysis. Keep dated drafts and declare help accurately if the school asks.

faqs.question: Who regulates the private school my child attends in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, rather than an emirate-level authority. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge. This matters for Ajman families because many children are enrolled across the border, so the body that approves their school's fees and curriculum may not be the one covering their home address. Check which authority publishes your school's inspection report before trying to interpret a rating.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: Yes, private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. People tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure quoted to you with scepticism. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE grades does the Ministry of Education equivalency route count?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which does not match the reported rule. Equivalency is handled by the ministry, not by a tutoring provider, so verify the current requirement on the official channel before planning subject choices around it.

faqs.question: Can sessions start late enough for a parent commuting back from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Ajman households it is usually the deciding factor. Evening starts at 7pm, 7.30pm or later hold reliably because nobody is driving to the lesson, and during Ramadan sessions can move to post-Iftar timing for the month and then return. Diploma students in coursework weeks sometimes take a 9pm review slot. The thing to protect is the same slot every week: a fixed hour that survives a traffic day and a parent's travel week produces more marked work over a term than a better hour that gets cancelled twice a month.

faqs.question: Suppose nobody on your side teaches the subject my child is weakest in?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than placing a generalist. For mainstream IGCSE subjects and Standard Level Diploma subjects a match is usually straightforward. For a narrow Higher Level combination, a minority language or coursework supervision inside a short window, there may be nobody suitable free when you want them. The honest options then are a different time slot, a short wait, or a recommendation to look elsewhere, and we will say which applies. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is precisely why it is worth asking every provider the question.

faqs.question: Can we record the lessons as part of the evidence we keep?
faqs.answer: The marked work and the session notes are the evidence that matters, and both are written down and shared. Recording a live lesson involves a second person's voice and a minor's, so it is agreed in advance with the tutor and the family rather than assumed, and plenty of families find they never revisit a recording while they reread the marked paper repeatedly. If reviewing explanations again is genuinely useful, a short written worked example produced during the session is usually more use than an hour of video nobody has time to watch.

faqs.question: How do we stop if the marked work shows nothing changing?
faqs.answer: You stop, and the block structure exists to make that decision easy rather than awkward. Agreeing a baseline piece and a scheduled second attempt at the start means that by the end of the block there is a comparison on the table instead of two opinions. If the second attempt shows no movement and the between-session work was done, the plan or the tutor is wrong and continuing is throwing money at it. We would rather end a block cleanly on evidence than keep a family who cannot see what they are paying for.

ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper, not with the enquiry form
ajman/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you are searching for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Ajman, the most useful thing you can do in the next ten minutes is find your child's most recent marked paper or school mock. Send it with the latest report and any current task sheet, and the first conversation can be about specific lost marks rather than general worry. The trial lesson is free, no card details are taken, and the tutor works through that evidence with your child on live video. Afterwards you get a written note of what they found. From there, agreeing an eight-week block with a measurable end point is a decision you can check rather than a hope you have to hold.

intro.heading: A twelve-month plan beats a nearby name
paragraphs: The thing being searched for is proximity and the thing actually needed is a sequence. A household on Ajman Corniche with a Diploma student and an IGCSE candidate is running two assessment calendars that do not align, inside a UAE academic year that has its own rhythm, in a flat with one quiet room. Finding somebody nearby solves none of that. Writing the year down solves most of it.

The two calendars collide in predictable places. Diploma internal coursework clusters in the autumn of the final year, which is also when a Year 11 sibling's mocks are set and when university applications are written. IGCSE results land in August for the summer series and in January for the autumn one. The Diploma exam window sits in the spring, the IGCSE one in June. Every one of those is knowable a year ahead, and almost none of it is written down anywhere a parent can see.

Ajman Corniche shapes the plan in two specific ways. School runs from the seafront towers are among the shortest in the emirate, often fifteen minutes, which makes an early session genuinely available. And these are apartments, frequently with siblings and a shared living room, so two simultaneous video lessons need two quiet spaces and a household agreement about noise. That is a week-one decision, not a week-five discovery.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is what parents type, and it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition is quoted at here, what the travel premium consists of, and why two independent online bookings serve a two-child household better than one tutor's single journey.

On dates, this page is deliberately asymmetric. Cambridge and Pearson positions are sourced from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026, and are given with their dates. No IB exam or results date appears anywhere, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking and nothing in this project has been verified from the board itself. A date a family plans around has to be right, and an unverified one is worse than an absent one.

One correction that matters locally: Cambridge's February and March series is offered to candidates in India. A centre in Ajman enters the June and November series. Revision material written for an India audience circulates here, and a family working to those dates is working to a different country's calendar. That is the kind of mistake a tuition page can cause without ever teaching a lesson, so the series named below are the ones an Ajman centre actually enters and the official timetable is linked rather than copied out, because boards revise provisional versions.
bullets: Diploma coursework deadlines cluster in the autumn of the final year, alongside Year 11 mocks and university applications.

Cambridge runs June and November; the February and March series is offered in India only.
Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year against the school calendar, so its position in the term changes.
Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education; Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-ajman-co.programmesIntro: A two-board household touches these four at once, which is why reading them side by side is more useful than reading any one of them properly.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, with internal assessment dates spread across the year rather than concentrated in an exam window. The calendar here is real and invisible, because MYP assessment arrives as tasks and projects. A criterion strand left unaddressed costs marks every time it recurs.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the MYP cohort is small, so an internal position tells a parent very little. That is one reason Corniche families often want an external view in Year 10, while the Diploma or IGCSE decision is still open.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with an internally assessed component in every subject. Those components run on school-set deadlines that cluster in one autumn, which is what makes the Diploma a scheduling problem more than an academic one.
programmes.countryNote: The emirate's Diploma cohort is small enough that a student may be one of very few taking a particular Higher Level option, so the school's own deadline calendar is the only calendar they will be handed. Ask for it in September.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Separate subject qualifications with their own codes: Mathematics 0580 split into Core and Extended, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610. The tier is submitted with the entry and fixes a ceiling that cannot be lifted later, which makes the autumn entry conversation more consequential than it feels.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct version of the timetable for the zone is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Different codes and a different assessment shape: 4MA1 Mathematics A with Foundation and Higher tiers, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, with practical knowledge assessed inside the written papers. Cambridge past papers are not a substitute, and the reverse is equally true.
programmes.countryNote: Exams run in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series and then revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version worth revising from.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-ajman-co.subjectsIntro: The Diploma side of a Corniche household, with the calendar pressure point named alongside the content one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper is the reliable source of lost marks. The exploration needs a topic with genuine mathematics in it, chosen a term before it is written rather than a fortnight.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led. Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late in the final year, so a student already behind meets new content and revision at once.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses. The internal assessment needs a method settled early enough to collect usable data, which is the deadline most often missed here.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read instead of calculated, explanations written as equations. Technique responds quickly to timed practice, which makes it a strong candidate for a short pre-series block.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rewards sequence and precision. Statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand, and that is a one-session fix once somebody has named it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries, each needing a genuinely recent article, a labelled diagram and a respected word count. Articles have to be collected as they appear, not hunted the week before.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the case stimulus is the whole paper. The Higher Level pre-released case study is published well ahead, so early structured reading is worth more here than anywhere else.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 rewards argument about how a text works. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it, which is a term's decision.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The two components most often bought late. The essay answers a prescribed title with one line of argument; the Extended Essay needs a question answerable inside 4,000 words.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-ajman-co.igcseSubjectsIntro: And the Year 10 or Year 11 side of the same household, by code, because the code decides which past papers are worth the evening.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier recommendation forms in the spring of Year 10, which is when to intervene. Extended Paper 4 rewards method marks, so working has to be shown even when the answer is obvious.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves carry the heaviest losses and both are taught early, so a Year 10 gap persists quietly until the mocks reveal it.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry sit in the first year of the course and remain the wall. Conversions between mass, moles and volume break down under time pressure rather than in principle.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Long answers reward ordering as much as naming. Extended genetics needs a Punnett square drawn properly rather than reasoned about aloud.

sections.heading: The collision map: where the two calendars hit each other
paragraphs: Two children in two systems do not generate twice as much pressure spread evenly. They generate concentrated pressure in three or four specific windows and long quiet stretches in between, and knowing which is which is the whole value of writing the year down.

The first collision is the autumn of the Diploma's final year. Internal coursework in six subjects falls due in draft or final form, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge essay are written, and university applications are prepared. If a Year 11 sibling's mocks are set in the same term, as they usually are, the household has two children producing high-stakes work in the same eight weeks with one quiet room between them.

The second is results. IGCSE summer results arrived with students on 20 August 2026, in the middle of the summer break, and November results reached students on 22 January 2026, in the middle of a term. Each demands a decision within a fortnight, and each lands when a household is least organised. The third collision is the spring, when the Diploma exam window and IGCSE revision overlap and neither child can be the priority.

The response is not more tuition. It is placing the quiet stretches deliberately: light work in the Diploma student's first year, a summer bridge before the hard autumn, and a protected single slot for the younger child that never becomes the thing cancelled when the older one has a deadline.

sections.heading: The UAE academic year as it actually runs
paragraphs: Every plan in this market is built on a year with features no international template accounts for, and they move. Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, which means its position inside the school year changes: in some years it lands in a quiet term, in others it sits immediately before an exam window. A plan written once and reused is a plan that will eventually put its heaviest weeks inside the month with the least capacity.

During Ramadan school hours shorten and the useful study window moves to after Iftar. For a two-child household that is actually easier online than at any other time of year, because two late sessions can be stacked without anybody driving to a tower at nine in the evening. The failure mode is suspension: a month quietly dropped, resumed in a rush, with a coursework deadline now four weeks closer than the plan assumed.

Eid breaks, UAE National Day on 2 December and the mid-term holidays all sit inside terms rather than between them, which makes them the natural place for coursework rather than for content. A student who uses a mid-term break to finish an internal assessment draft buys two weeks of autumn back. A student who uses it to rest and then returns to both the draft and the content is the standard case.

The summer is the only genuinely unallocated block, and it is treated below as a resource rather than as a gap. The practical point for a Corniche family is that none of these features is a surprise. All of them can be put on a single page in September, and the plan written around them instead of against them.

sections.heading: A twelve-month plan for a two-board household
paragraphs: This is the document the search was really looking for. Written in September, it costs nothing, and it is the difference between a household that places its spending and one that reacts to each report. The version below assumes a Corniche flat, a Diploma student entering the final year, and a sibling in Year 11, with one quiet room and one spare.

The shape is deliberately uneven. The heavy months are the autumn, where coursework and mocks coincide, and the eight weeks before each exam window. The light months are the start of the year and the period immediately after coursework clears, when a household recovers capacity it will need later. Trying to run both children at full intensity for twelve months produces two tired students and a bill nobody can justify.

Two mechanisms make the plan hold. First, every block has an end date written into it at the point it is agreed, so nothing becomes permanent by default. Second, the younger child has one protected weekly slot that is never the thing cancelled when the older child has a deadline, because that cancellation is exactly how a Year 11 drifts for two terms while a Grade 12 is managed.

Adapt the months to your own schools' calendars rather than to this page. The value is in having a plan on one page in September, not in matching somebody else's. Two households on the same Corniche street with the same two year groups will produce different plans, because their schools set different internal deadlines and may sit different boards, and a plan that is not built on your own documents is a template rather than a plan.

sections.heading: What 'near me' can and cannot deliver here
paragraphs: A near-me result is sorted by distance and by who paid to be visible, and neither signal says whether the person has taught the syllabus. On the Corniche the local supply is better than in most of the emirate, because the seafront sits inside the densest school catchment in Ajman, and that makes the distinction between real and apparent proximity sharper rather than softer.

The results divide into three. Agencies in Dubai or Sharjah whose service area is drawn generously and whose tutors would be driving 45 minutes each way in the evening. Individual tutors in the adjoining districts, often strong, usually teaching across a wide span of levels, and rarely able to name the paper structure of the specific qualification entered. And international platforms that never mention the UAE, quote in dollars, and route enquiries to a number outside the country.

Four questions separate them, and a two-board household has to ask all four twice, once per system: which syllabus code did you last teach and when, which papers did your students sit, which topics did that cohort lose marks on, and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. For the Diploma side, add a fifth: have you supervised an internal assessment through to submission, and what did you not do for the student.

The table is a coverage map rather than a claim. Its purpose is to let a Corniche family plan on a correct assumption about what is locally available, instead of spending a term looking for somebody who is not there.

sections.heading: When both children have a deadline in the same week
paragraphs: It happens every year and it is always treated as bad luck rather than as a scheduling problem with a known solution. The week an Extended Essay draft is due is also the week of a Year 11 mock, and the household has one quiet room, one dinner table and a finite amount of attention.

The first move is to decide the priority before the week arrives rather than inside it. In almost every case the component with permanent consequences outranks the one that generates information: a coursework submission that will be marked and counted outranks a mock whose purpose is diagnostic. Saying that out loud in advance removes the argument from the week itself, which is most of the cost.

The second move is to protect the lower-priority child's slot anyway, in a reduced form. A twenty-minute check-in rather than a cancelled session keeps the rhythm and stops the younger child learning that their work is the thing that gets dropped. That lesson, learned twice, is what produces a Year 11 who has quietly disengaged while the household managed a Grade 12.

The third is physical. Two simultaneous video lessons need two spaces, and on the Corniche that usually means one child in a bedroom and one at the dining table with the rest of the household elsewhere for forty-five minutes. Agreeing that once, in week one, is worth more than any amount of goodwill negotiated weekly. The households that lose the fewest sessions across a term are not the most disciplined ones; they are the ones who settled the physical arrangement before they needed it.

sections.heading: Summer: the only block nobody has allocated
paragraphs: Every other period in the year already has a claim on it. The summer does not, which makes it the most underused resource available to a two-board household and the cheapest place to solve a problem that would otherwise cost a term.

Three jobs suit it. The first is the transition from Extended or Higher tier into a Diploma Higher Level course, which is a predictable, subject-specific gap: procedural fluency to proof and modelling in Mathematics, recall to data analysis and extended evaluation in the sciences, comprehension to argument in English. Named early, each of those closes in a defined number of weeks. Met in October alongside everything else, it becomes a term of confusion.

The second is settling an internal assessment topic before term starts, so the autumn cluster begins with a viable question and a workable method rather than with a blank page. The third is closing a content gap the mocks exposed, which is the only time of year when a student can learn new material without also revising old material.

What the summer is not is a place to run a full programme. Three or four weeks with two sessions a week, aimed at one named target, with a written handover at the end, is the version that works. A student who studies through July and August arrives in September already tired, which costs more than the gap would have. The test of a good summer block is that it finishes before term starts and hands over something written: a named gap closed, a topic settled, or a method approved.

sections.heading: The university application calendar, and why it collides
paragraphs: This is the collision least often planned for, because it is not an examination and therefore not on anybody's assessment calendar. University applications are written in the autumn of the Diploma's final year, in the same weeks as the coursework cluster, and they consume exactly the resource coursework needs: sustained written attention from the student and administrative attention from the parent.

The destinations have different rhythms, which is what makes a household plan necessary rather than a generic one. UK applications run through a centralised autumn cycle with a personal statement and predicted grades. UAE universities and many regional institutions run their own admission timelines with their own tests. North American applications have earlier rounds in the autumn and later ones in the winter, plus standardised tests that have to be booked months ahead. A family applying in two directions is managing two of those simultaneously.

The practical consequence for tuition is sequencing rather than content. Predicted grades are produced from work done before the application, which means the autumn of the first Diploma year and the spring following it are where predictions are actually earned. Tuition bought after predictions are issued cannot change them, which is a fact worth knowing a year earlier than most families learn it.

There is one honest limit to state. IB Gram tutors teach subjects; nothing on this page is a claim to manage admissions, write personal statements or guarantee a place anywhere. Where a student needs application support, that is a different service and should be described as one.

sections.heading: The permit, the materials rule and the honesty line
paragraphs: Three boundaries belong on a page that asks a family to plan a year around a tutor, and the first is a calendar item in its own right. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Two years is a date as well as a duration, which makes it a reasonable thing to ask about rather than to assume once.

Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. Separately, an operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, renewed annually with the request at least 30 days before expiry.

The second boundary is materials. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads; the official source should be referenced and linked. That is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure, which is why there are no attachments on this page.

The third is academic. A tutor may teach content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors demand, help narrow a research question, review a method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, exploration, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework, nor supply text to paste in. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and the consequence of buying one falls on the student. No tutor can promise a grade either, and IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.
