process.title: Send both schools' calendars
process.description: The IGCSE child's board, syllabus codes, tier and mock window, and the Diploma child's internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge dates and mock window. Two emails to two schools. That grid determines the whole plan, and almost no family has built it before February.

process.title: Name both children's subjects and levels
process.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Diploma Mathematics AA HL are different requests requiring different tutors, even though both are mathematics. Where the overlap is genuine, as it sometimes is between Extended IGCSE and Standard Level Diploma work, we will say so and one tutor may serve both.

process.title: Set consecutive slots and a protected floor
process.description: Two back-to-back evening slots with two specialists, so the household loses one evening rather than two. Each child gets one session that is never reallocated, whatever the other child's week looks like, because a slot given away repeatedly is a slot that taught nothing.

process.title: Free trial for each child separately
process.description: One lesson each, at no charge and with no payment details collected, on whatever is genuinely due next for that child. Two trials on the same evening also test whether the consecutive-slot arrangement works in your household before you commit to it for a term.

process.title: Reassess at the mock window
process.description: The winter mocks are the one point where both children produce real evidence at the same time. Both sets of scripts are read question by question against the published schemes, and the household allocation is rebuilt from what they show rather than from the assumptions made in September.

whyPoints.title: Both calendars treated as one problem
whyPoints.description: The two qualifications place their pressure in different terms, and a plan that ignores that will over-serve one child and under-serve the other every month. Consolidating both schools' dates into one grid is the first thing we ask for and the thing that changes the plan most.

whyPoints.title: Consecutive slots, one disrupted evening
whyPoints.description: Two specialists back to back on the same night, which is only possible because nobody is travelling. In a household where both parents work clinical or academic hours, protecting four evenings a week instead of two is a material difference.

whyPoints.title: Allocation by permanent loss, not by fairness
whyPoints.description: Hours go where the loss would be irreversible, which in most autumns means the Diploma child, with a protected floor held for the younger one. Equal division feels fair and serves the calendar badly in every term of the year.

whyPoints.title: Board dates sourced, Diploma dates not invented
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the boards' own published pages with historical results dates kept intact. No International Baccalaureate examination or results date appears here, because none could be verified from the organisation itself.

whyPoints.title: Transition work priced into the summer
whyPoints.description: The gaps a new course assumes are specific and predictable by subject, and closing them in August costs a handful of sessions where closing them in November costs a term. This is the cheapest intervention available in a dual-curriculum household.

whyPoints.title: One honesty line for both children
whyPoints.description: Assessed work is the student's own in both qualifications, and the boundary is stated before the deadline rather than negotiated at it. A service that offers to produce coursework is selling a certification risk to the child it claims to be helping.

faqs.question: How do we plan for two children sitting different exams in the same year?
faqs.answer: Build one grid rather than two plans. Put the IGCSE child's board, syllabus codes, tier, mock window and series on it, and the Diploma child's internal assessment deadlines, Extended Essay checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge dates and mock window. Both schools issue this information. What the grid shows is that the year has two or three genuinely contested periods rather than continuous competition, and that the autumn is far harder for the Diploma child than it feels.

faqs.question: Whose deadline should win when both children need the same evening?
faqs.answer: The one whose loss is permanent. A Diploma internal assessment deadline that passes badly is closed: the component is submitted and moderated and cannot be revisited. An IGCSE mock that goes badly is a diagnostic with a June series ahead and a November series behind it. Those are not equivalent losses. The exception is the final term, when both children have fixed papers approaching and the only honest answer is triage plus, if possible, more hours.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both an IGCSE and a Diploma child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes in mathematics, where Extended IGCSE content feeds directly into Standard Level Diploma work, and rarely elsewhere. The levels assess differently even where the content overlaps: Diploma internal assessment criteria and IGCSE paper technique are separate disciplines. Where a genuine overlap exists we will say so, because one tutor across two children simplifies the week. Where it does not, two specialists in consecutive slots is the better arrangement and costs the same evening.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram come to homes in Al Jurf for either qualification?
faqs.answer: No. In-home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Both children's lessons run live over video, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. In a two-child household that is the arrangement that actually works: two consecutive slots with two different specialists on one evening, with nobody waiting for a tutor delayed on the Ajman ring road and no travel premium on either hour.

faqs.question: Why is the autumn term harder for a Diploma student than an IGCSE one?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma's internal components all have to be complete before the examination term, and schools place them where they fit. A DP2 student can face a subject internal assessment draft, an Extended Essay full draft, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition and the first mocks within about six weeks. An IGCSE student's autumn is content teaching with internal assessments only. The pressure reverses in the spring, which is why hours should move between terms rather than being split evenly.

faqs.question: What should the summer between the two school years be used for?
faqs.answer: Two things, and they do not compete. For the IGCSE child, the decisions that follow August results: whether a grade blocks a subject choice, whether a review is being requested, whether a November resit is compatible with starting Year 12. For the Diploma child, settling an internal assessment research question and doing Extended Essay reading, which disarms a large part of the autumn convergence before it starts. Both are cheap in July and expensive in November.

faqs.question: Is a November IGCSE resit compatible with starting Year 12?
faqs.answer: It is possible and it is a real workload. Re-entry means sitting the full paper set for the subject again, not just the paper that went badly, and the result arrives in January: Pearson's November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. For a student whose intended course is blocked by one grade it can be the right call. For a student whose Year 12 start matters more, accepting the grade and protecting the new course is often the better decision.

faqs.question: How should a dual-curriculum household handle Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The post-Iftar window is narrow and in a two-child house it is the most contested hour of the day. Two patterns work: both children in consecutive slots from around 9pm, which suits timed paper practice better than new teaching, or alternate days so each child gets three sessions a fortnight with proper focus. Decide in advance, because late-evening slots fill quickly across the Gulf and a preferred specialist may not be available at short notice.

faqs.question: What gaps does the move from IGCSE into the Diploma leave?
faqs.answer: Specific and predictable ones. A student entering Standard Level Diploma mathematics from Core rather than Extended IGCSE lacks the algebraic fluency the course assumes from week one. A chemistry student from Coordinated Science has not met the organic depth or mole work stoichiometry builds on. A biology student has almost never handled statistics, which is where the internal assessment will be weakest a year later. Each takes a handful of summer sessions and a term to fix later.

faqs.question: Should the younger child's sessions stop during the Diploma crunch?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the commonest household mistake. Continuous assessment has no dramatic deadline to defend it, so the younger child's slot is the one that gets reallocated, and a slot given away three times in a term is a term in which nothing was taught. Keep one protected weekly session for each child that is never moved, and let a flexible pool of hours follow whichever deadline is nearest. That serves both better than an attempt at equal division.

faqs.question: Do the two children's mock windows fall at the same time?
faqs.answer: Often but not always, and it depends on the schools. Ajman and Sharjah schools frequently run mocks on different weeks, and in a household with children at two schools that can be a relief or a collision. Either way the winter mock period is the one time both children produce real evidence simultaneously, and both sets of scripts should be read question by question against the published schemes rather than reported as grades.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a two-child plan need?
faqs.answer: Most Al Jurf households run two to four weekly hours across both children, with a reserve of two or three hours held for the fortnight when something goes wrong. More than that and the students have no time left to do the independent work that makes sessions stick. If four hours genuinely is not enough, the constraint is usually study method or the household's available supervised time rather than teaching volume.

faqs.question: Is the coursework rule different for IGCSE and the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The principle is identical: assessed work must be the student's own. The components differ, with Diploma internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay on one side and IGCSE coursework or controlled assessments on the other, but a tutor's role is the same in both. Teach the skills, explain what each criterion requires, question whether the evidence supports the conclusion, help prioritise. Never write, complete or supply text for submission.

faqs.question: What is the single most useful thing we can do in September?
faqs.answer: Get both schools to put their dates in writing and consolidate them onto one page, then decide in advance which fortnights are contested and what each child's protected session will be. It costs two emails and an hour. Families who do it spend the year making allocation decisions calmly, and families who do not spend the year discovering collisions a week before they happen and buying emergency hours that may not be available.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-jurf.closingHeading: Send both calendars and we will map them
ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-jurf.closingBody: The useful first message from a two-child household in Al Jurf contains four things: both children's subjects and levels, the IGCSE board and syllabus codes with the tier entered, the Diploma internal deadline dates, and the evenings that are realistically available. Each child then takes a free trial lesson on whatever is genuinely due next.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mowai.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Al Mowaihat households state the programme and the code they last taught, and accept a slot that fits around a sibling's session rather than around their own preference. Both grids below show what is most often requested from this school belt.

intro.heading: Two children, two systems, one evening
paragraphs: The single hardest tuition problem in this part of Ajman is not finding a teacher. It is that a Diploma student and an IGCSE student in the same house need different things at the same hour, from different boards, on different internal deadlines, and there is one evening between the school bus and dinner to fit both into. A near-me search cannot help with that, because the thing that needs solving is a timetable rather than a radius.

Al Mowaihat makes the problem more tractable than most of the emirate. The three villa districts sit along Sheikh Ammar Road, within ten to twenty minutes of Ajman's school belt, so buses reach home between 2:45pm and 3:45pm rather than after four. That gives a household roughly two and a half usable hours, which is enough for two short sessions placed back to back if neither of them requires anybody to drive anywhere.

That last clause is the whole argument. An in-home tutor serving two children either teaches them consecutively, in which case the family pays for two hours and the second child starts at 6pm, or makes two journeys, in which case the family pays for the car twice. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so a 4:15pm Diploma session and a 5:15pm IGCSE session are two independent bookings with two different specialists. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

The second thing a two-board household needs is translation. MYP criteria do not map onto IGCSE grades, an IGCSE Extended entry is not the same signal as an MYP 7, and the Year 11 decision between continuing MYP into the Diploma or sitting IGCSEs first is taken on the basis of information most parents are given only once, briefly, at a parents' evening. A section below lays that out as a comparison rather than as advice.

The third is honesty about what the local school belt cannot supply. Al Mowaihat has better tutor availability than Al Zorah or Al Rawda, and that availability is concentrated at the easier end of both systems. For a Higher Level science or a scarce Diploma option the local pool is close to empty, which is a fact worth hearing before paying for a search rather than after it.

What follows is written for that household rather than for a single student: two calendars lined up side by side, a route comparison between continuing the Middle Years Programme and sitting IGCSEs first, a coverage map of what this school belt can and cannot supply, a subject-by-subject account of the jump from Extended tier into a Higher Level course, and a template week with the prayer shift and Ramadan already built into it. Sources are named and dated throughout. Cambridge and Pearson positions come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026, and where a date has not been verified from the awarding body itself this page says so rather than guessing at it, because a date a parent plans around has to be right for their country.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mowai.programmesIntro: A two-board household touches four of these at once, and the planning value comes from seeing them side by side rather than one at a time.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, rewarding process as much as the answer. Students trained to produce neat right answers lose marks for not justifying, not patterning, not reflecting. A strand left unaddressed costs a predictable number of marks, which makes the subject guide the most useful document in the house.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Mowaihat the MYP cohort is small, so a student's internal rank tells a parent very little about national standing. That is one reason families here often want an outside view in Year 10, before the Diploma or IGCSE decision is taken.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, each subject carrying an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of its grade. The internal deadlines sit far ahead of the exam window, which is what makes the Diploma a planning problem rather than a revision problem.
programmes.countryNote: There is no large Diploma cohort in Ajman, so a student may be one of very few in the emirate taking a particular Higher Level option. Online one-to-one is frequently the only route to a second experienced voice on those papers.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Separate subject qualifications with their own codes. Mathematics 0580 splits into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, which runs to A*. Sciences such as Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620 offer Core and Extended papers, with the practical route chosen by the centre rather than by the student.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask the exams officer which zone your centre sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's own codes and structures: 4MA1 Mathematics A with Foundation and Higher tiers, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Practical knowledge is assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical route, so past papers do not transfer between the boards.
programmes.countryNote: Exams run in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so use the live official PDF.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mowai.subjectsIntro: The Diploma side of a two-board household, with the specific place marks go missing in each subject and a note on how scarce the teaching is around Ajman.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is the non-calculator paper and the reliable source of lost marks for students fluent with a GDC. Widely taught locally at Standard Level, thin at Higher Level outside Dubai and Sharjah.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with the GDC central. Students report regression output without interpreting context. HL adds graph theory and matrices, usually taught late in Grade 12.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses, with data questions catching students who state a trend without a cause. Very scarce locally at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit errors, gradients read instead of calculated, explanations written as equations rather than sentences. Very scarce locally at Higher Level; usually an online-only option in Ajman.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Rewards sequence and precision: naming a process earns one mark, ordering its stages earns the rest. Database and statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry heavy marks and are habitually drawn without labelled axes, shifts or new equilibrium. The commentaries need genuinely recent articles and a respected word count.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the case stimulus is the whole paper; a remembered SWOT scores almost nothing. HL adds the pre-released case study, which rewards early structured reading.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is where students summarise instead of arguing about how a text works. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are bought late and in a panic more often than any other component. Both respond to narrowing: a prescribed title answered with one line of argument, a research question answerable inside 4,000 words.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mowai.igcseSubjectsIntro: And the Year 10 or Year 11 side of the same household, by code, because the code decides which past papers are worth the evening.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Practising the wrong tier is the most common wasted term in this subject. Extended Paper 4 rewards method marks, so working must be written out even when the answer looks obvious.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves carry the heaviest losses. Cambridge centres choose between a practical paper and the alternative-to-practical paper, and the two demand different preparation entirely.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall. Students who balance equations confidently still lose marks converting between mass, moles and volume under time pressure.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Long answers reward ordering as much as naming. Extended adds genetics problems where a Punnett square has to be drawn properly rather than reasoned about aloud.

igcseSubjects.name: English (Cambridge 0500 and 0510)

igcseSubjects.description: Both are application papers. Data-response marks come from quoting the figure in the extract; case-study marks come from using the business in the stimulus rather than the theory in the textbook.

sections.heading: One household, two calendars: what actually collides
paragraphs: Put a Diploma student and an IGCSE student in one house and the collisions are predictable enough to plan for. The Diploma internal deadlines land in the autumn of Grade 12, which is also when a Year 11 sibling's mocks are being set. The Diploma exam window sits in the spring; the IGCSE window sits in June, with a second one in late October and November. Results arrive at different times and from different bodies.

The less obvious collision is attention. A family can concentrate on one child's crisis at a time, and the Diploma generates more visible crises because its coursework is weighted and its deadlines are internal. The predictable result is a Year 10 student who drifts quietly for two terms while the household manages a Grade 12, and who then needs a more expensive intervention in Year 11 than they would have needed earlier.

The planning answer is to treat the younger child's Year 9 and Year 10 as the cheap window rather than the quiet one. Foundations in algebra, written method and scientific vocabulary cost very little to fix at Year 9 and a great deal to fix in the spring of Year 11. Al Mowaihat's early arrival times make a short twice-weekly session at that age genuinely sustainable, which is not true in most of this emirate.

sections.heading: The weekend plan for households whose weekdays are full
paragraphs: Some weeks cannot be made to hold two sessions, and forcing it produces two bad ones. Where a parent commutes, where the school run is long, or where one child has a sport commitment, the honest answer is to move one child's work to the weekend and leave four weekday evenings completely alone.

The weekend block is not simply a longer version of the weekday slot. Ninety minutes makes a full past paper under timed conditions possible, and that is a different exercise from a question group. A complete paper tests pacing, decision-making about which question to leave, and stamina through the long data questions at the end, none of which show up in a forty-five-minute session. Students who always lose marks on the last two questions have a pacing problem that only a full sitting reveals.

There is a scheduling advantage too. A weekend slot is far less likely to be cancelled, because it does not depend on traffic, a school test the next morning, or a parent arriving home. Across a term the difference between a slot that holds and a slot that is dropped twice a month is larger than the difference between two tutors.

What the weekend cannot do is substitute for regular contact in a subject that has genuinely broken down. Weekly rhythm matters for repair work; weekend blocks matter for performance work. Most households running both systems end up needing one of each, which is a different purchase from two of the same.

sections.heading: MYP, IGCSE, or both: the Year 11 decision in this school belt
paragraphs: Families in Al Mowaihat whose children are in an IB continuum school face a choice that families in a British-curriculum school never see: whether to continue the Middle Years Programme into Year 11 and go straight to the Diploma, or to sit IGCSEs first. Schools present this once, briefly, and parents are usually asked to decide on incomplete information.

The two routes produce different things. IGCSE produces separately certificated subject grades at 16, which are what UAE equivalency counts, what many employers recognise, and what a student carries if the family moves country or if the Diploma turns out not to suit. MYP produces no external certificate, and its criterion marks do not translate into a recognised grade set, but it prepares a student directly for the Diploma's internal assessment style and its command terms.

The equivalency point deserves stating precisely because it is where the decision has a concrete consequence. The published requirement on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB there is no points threshold published in the source used here, which means a family should confirm the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority rather than taking a figure from any tutoring page, including this one.

The table compares the routes on the dimensions that actually differ. It is a comparison, not a recommendation: both routes work and the right answer depends on the student and on how settled the family's next five years are.

sections.heading: Who is actually near you, and who only looks near
paragraphs: A near-me result is sorted by distance and by who paid to appear, and neither tells a parent whether the person has taught the syllabus. Around Al Mowaihat the local supply is genuinely better than in the coastal communities, because the district sits inside the school belt rather than outside it, and that makes the distinction between real and apparent proximity more important rather than less.

Three categories dominate the results. Agencies based in Dubai or Sharjah with a service area drawn generously, whose tutors would be driving 45 minutes each way in the evening. Individual tutors in the denser Ajman districts, frequently strong, usually teaching across a broad span of levels, and rarely able to name the paper structure of the specific qualification entered. And platforms that never mention the UAE, quote in dollars and route enquiries to a number outside the country.

Separating them takes four questions, all answerable in a sentence: which syllabus code did you last teach and when, which papers did your students sit, which topics did that cohort lose marks on, and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutor who answers all four quickly is worth considerably more than one who is eight minutes closer. A family running two systems has to ask all four twice, once per board.

sections.heading: What the Al Mowaihat school belt is short of
paragraphs: It is worth being specific rather than gesturing at scarcity. The Ajman school belt serves a largely British and Indian curriculum population, with a small IB continuum presence. That shapes which teachers live and work here, and therefore what is easy and what is nearly impossible to source locally.

Easy: Mathematics and the sciences at IGCSE level, English, and Arabic in the Ministry streams. These are taught in every school in the belt, which means several competent local tutors exist for each and the price stays competitive. Hard: Diploma Higher Level sciences, Economics with its internal assessment commentaries, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and any minority language. Each of those is taught by a very small number of people in the emirate.

There is a second constraint on the local pool that is rarely mentioned. In Abu Dhabi, the regulator's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document and should be verified against it, but the pattern is consistent: the best-placed local teacher is often the one person who cannot take the work.

The useful conclusion is not that local tutoring is inferior. It is that a household running both systems should expect to source the IGCSE side locally or online with equal ease, and the Diploma side online as a matter of course. Planning on that basis saves a term of searching for somebody who is not there. Everything below is written for that household rather than for a single student: two calendars lined up side by side, a route comparison between continuing the Middle Years Programme and sitting IGCSEs first, a coverage map of what this school belt can and cannot supply, a subject-by-subject account of the jump from Extended tier into a Higher Level course, and a template week with the prayer shift and Ramadan already built into it. Sources are named and dated throughout. Cambridge and Pearson positions come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026, and where a date has not been verified from the awarding body itself this page says so rather than guessing at it.

sections.heading: From IGCSE to the Diploma, subject by subject
paragraphs: Every two-board household eventually becomes a one-board household, and the transition from Year 11 to Grade 11 is where the most avoidable damage happens. A student who was comfortable at Extended level can arrive in a Higher Level course and spend a term confused, not because the content is beyond them but because the assessment expects something different: justification rather than answers, evaluation rather than description, and sustained independent work on an internal assessment.

The gaps are subject-specific and predictable. In Mathematics, the jump is from procedural fluency to proof and modelling, with Analysis and Approaches asking for algebraic manipulation that IGCSE never required. In the sciences, the jump is from recall and short calculation to data analysis, uncertainty and extended evaluation. In English, from comprehension and directed writing to argument about how a text works. In Economics and Business, from definition and application to diagram precision and evaluation under a word limit.

Each of those gaps is closeable in a defined number of weeks if it is named early. That is the argument for a short block in the summer between Year 11 and Grade 11, or in the first six weeks of the Diploma, rather than a reactive intervention in the spring after the first serious assessment has gone badly.

sections.heading: A worked week for two children in Al Mowaihat
paragraphs: This is the section nobody else in this market writes, and it is the one a two-board household actually needs: a plan on a page. The assumptions are an Al Mowaihat 2 household, a Grade 11 Diploma student and a Year 10 IGCSE student, buses arriving around 3:30pm, one parent commuting to Sharjah, and a term with no exams immediately ahead.

The shape that works is two stacked weekday slots on one evening, one longer weekend block, and three completely clear evenings. Stacking both children on a single evening sounds intense and is in fact the opposite: it concentrates the disruption into one night instead of spreading it across four, which is what makes the arrangement survive to the end of term. Three protected evenings are also what makes school homework possible without a fight.

The adjustments worth building in from the start are the predictable ones. In winter, Maghrib moves earlier and the second slot has to shift forward or shorten. During Ramadan, both slots move to post-Iftar, which an online booking absorbs and a travelling tutor usually cannot. In the twelve weeks before a series, the weekend block goes to whichever child is sitting papers and the other child steps down to fortnightly.
The table is a template rather than a prescription. The point is that a week designed once, in writing, at the start of term holds together far better than a week negotiated every Sunday night.

sections.heading: Academic honesty across both systems
paragraphs: A household running the Diploma and IGCSE together has two different honesty regimes to keep straight, and the Diploma one is stricter because so much more of its grade is internally assessed. Getting it wrong is not a billing dispute; the consequence falls on the student.

The permitted work is the same in both systems and worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain the assessment criteria and what each descriptor demands, help narrow a research question, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete an Internal Assessment, an exploration, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay, a personal project or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text for a student to paste in. A page found during research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is a straightforward malpractice trigger.

The materials rule applies across both boards. No tutor should reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads; the official source should be referenced and linked instead. That is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

Finally, nothing on this page claims any regulatory standing. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Describing what a regulator does is different from claiming its endorsement, and no tutor can promise a grade in either system, because boundaries are set after the series on the basis of that series' papers.

faqs.question: Can two children in Al Mowaihat have tuition on the same evening?
faqs.answer: In Al Mowaihat 1 and 2, usually yes. Buses reach the villa districts between 2:45pm and 3:45pm, which leaves roughly two and a half usable hours, enough for two back-to-back sessions starting around 4:15pm and 5:30pm. That only works if nobody has to travel, which is the practical argument for an online format here. Stacking both children on one evening also concentrates the disruption into a single night rather than spreading it across four, which is why the arrangement tends to survive the term.

faqs.question: Should my Year 11 child continue MYP or sit IGCSEs first?
faqs.answer: The honest comparison is about portability and preparation. IGCSE produces separately certificated subject grades at 16, which is what UAE equivalency counts and what a student carries if the family moves country or the Diploma turns out not to suit. MYP produces no external certificate but prepares a student directly for the Diploma's internal assessment style and command terms. Both routes work. The deciding factors are usually how settled the family's next five years are and how independent the student already is.

faqs.question: Do MYP criterion marks tell me how my child compares nationally?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and in Ajman less than most places. MYP subjects are marked on four criteria of 8 against levelled descriptors, which describe performance rather than rank it, and the local cohort for any one subject is small, so an internal position carries little information. That is a large part of why families in this school belt often want an outside diagnostic view in Year 10, before the Diploma or IGCSE decision is taken and while a term of work could still change the recommendation.

faqs.question: What should a household running both systems ask a prospective tutor?
faqs.answer: Four questions, twice, once per board: which syllabus code did you last teach and when, which papers did your students sit, which topics did that cohort lose marks on, and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutor who answers all four in a sentence each is worth considerably more than one who happens to live closer. For the MYP side, add a fifth: which subject guide do you work from, and can you name the criterion strands.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE Extended to IB Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Predictable and subject-specific rather than mysterious. In Mathematics the shift is from procedural fluency to proof, modelling and non-calculator manipulation. In the sciences, from recall and short calculation to data analysis, uncertainty and extended evaluation. In English, from comprehension to argument about how a text constructs meaning. Each gap closes in a defined number of weeks if it is named early, which is the argument for a short block in the summer before Grade 11 rather than a rescue in the spring.

faqs.question: Which subjects can I genuinely find locally around Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: IGCSE Mathematics and sciences, English, and Arabic in the Ministry streams are taught in every school in this belt, so several competent local tutors exist for each and pricing stays competitive. Diploma Higher Level sciences, Economics with its commentaries, Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, and minority languages are taught by very few people in the emirate. Plan on sourcing the IGCSE side either way and the Diploma side online as a matter of course.

faqs.question: Why might the nearest qualified teacher be unable to tutor my child?
faqs.answer: Because of where they work. In Abu Dhabi, the regulator's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the current policy document and should be verified against it. The pattern across sources is consistent, and it is why local supply is thinner than local advertising suggests.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a Year 10?
faqs.answer: It depends what the session is for. Repair work, where a topic sequence has broken down, needs weekly rhythm, so a weekday slot does more. Performance work needs full past papers under timed conditions, which require ninety minutes and therefore a weekend. A weekend slot also has the practical advantage of being the least cancelled slot in the week: it does not depend on traffic, on a school test the next morning, or on a parent getting home.

faqs.question: How do we handle a Diploma crisis without losing the Year 10?
faqs.answer: By protecting one fixed slot for the younger child before the crisis arrives. The predictable pattern in two-board households is that the Diploma generates visible deadlines, the household concentrates there, and the Year 10 drifts for two terms before needing a more expensive intervention in Year 11. A single protected weekday session, never used as the thing that gets cancelled when the Grade 12 has a deadline, costs far less than the repair it prevents.

faqs.question: Do the two systems have different academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: The permitted work is the same; the stakes differ, because far more of a Diploma grade is internally assessed. In both systems a tutor may teach content, explain criteria and descriptors, help narrow a research question, review a method and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. In neither may a tutor write, redraft or complete an assessment or supply text to paste in. A page found in research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is a malpractice trigger.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers us if one child studies in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Both, in different respects. Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, while Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Practically that means two inspection regimes, two sets of term dates and two fee-approval processes in one household. Request each school's latest inspection outcome directly rather than expecting to download a single report covering both.

faqs.question: What does UAE equivalency need from each of my children?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the IB, the source used here publishes no points threshold, so confirm that position on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. No tutoring provider performs or underwrites equivalency, and tuition is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both children to save money?
faqs.answer: Rarely well, once the older child is on a Diploma Higher Level subject. A tutor credible across Year 10 Cambridge 0580 and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches exists but is uncommon, and the rate follows the harder subject anyway, so the saving is smaller than families expect. What does save real friction is one provider, one slot pattern and one reporting rhythm across both children, with a different specialist teaching each of them.

faqs.question: How do we plan around Ramadan with two exam-year children?
faqs.answer: Move both slots to post-Iftar and decide it before the month begins. School hours shorten, the useful study window shifts late, and that is exactly when a travelling tutor is least available, so an online booking absorbs the change where an in-home visit usually cannot. Keeping the frequency and shortening the sessions works better than suspending the month, because a quietly abandoned Ramadan is where a pre-series plan most often slips in this emirate.

faqs.question: When do results arrive for each system, and why does the gap matter?
faqs.answer: The IGCSE dates are sourced: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November entry means waiting until January, which matters if a post-16 place depends on it. IB dates are deliberately absent from this page because none has been verified from the board itself; take any specific date from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org.

intro.heading: The deadlines a parent owns
paragraphs: Al Nuaimiya is one of Ajman's older, denser districts, minutes from the Sharjah boundary and within commuting distance of Dubai. Families here run a complicated administrative year: schools under two or three different authorities, exam entries made by centres, equivalency processes for university applications, and in some cases a private-candidate route. Tutoring sits inside all of that, and the mistakes that cost the most are administrative rather than academic.

Consider what a tutor cannot fix. A tier left as Core after the school's internal entry deadline has passed. A subject not entered at all. An equivalency file started too late for a university application. A private-candidate registration missed because nobody realised the centre's deadline sat months before the examination. Each of those is final, and each is a date a parent - not a student and not a tutor - is responsible for noticing.

Set against that, the academic calendar is relatively forgiving. Eight weeks before a written series, technique, timing and repeated errors can all be improved. An internal assessment can be rescued if the practical work was sound. A content gap found in DP1 costs a few sessions. None of that is comfortable, but all of it is recoverable, which is the opposite of an administrative deadline.

So this page is organised around the dates that close options. The school-entry calendar and who decides what. The Ministry of Education equivalency requirements, which are published and which one ranking competitor states incorrectly. The university application cycle, which runs ahead of the examination results it depends on. And the private-candidate route, which carries earlier deadlines and more responsibility for the family.

Where tutoring belongs in that picture is specific. Before a tier decision, a few sessions on genuine Extended or higher level material produce the evidence a school conversation needs. Before an application, predicted grades matter and so does the gap between a prediction and a realistic outcome. After a disappointing result, the resit decision should be made from the script. Those are academic jobs tied to administrative dates.

None of this requires a parent to become an expert. Almost every date on this page is obtainable with one email to an exams officer or an IB coordinator, and the equivalency requirements are published on a government site. The work is noticing in time, which is exactly the part a busy family loses when two or three schools' calendars are running at once.

Delivery, as on every one of our UAE pages: one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - which for a household with children at schools in two emirates is what makes a single supervised evening possible at all.

sections.heading: The entry calendar, and who decides what
paragraphs: Exam entries are the administrative deadline families most often misunderstand, because responsibility is split in a way nobody explains. The board publishes a final entries date for centres. The school sets an earlier internal date by which it needs decisions from families in order to meet the board's. The family's deadline is the school's, and it is usually announced once, by email, in a busy term.

What is decided in that window matters. Whether a Cambridge candidate is entered for Core or Extended, which caps the grade available. Whether a subject is entered at all. Which board, where a school offers more than one. For an IB student the parallel decisions are subject and level, taken at the end of the pre-DP year with consequences that run for two years and beyond.

The practical action is one email. Ask the exams officer for the internal deadline for entry changes, and for written confirmation of the board, code and tier for every subject. Both are facts the school already holds, and having them converts a vague anxiety into a dated plan. In a district like this one, where schools run several curricula, the confirmation is worth having in writing rather than from memory.

Then there is the zone detail, which is administrative and genuinely consequential. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. The zone belongs to the centre, not to the emirate, so the only timetable to work from is the one your school's exams officer issues.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: what is published
paragraphs: Equivalency is the administrative process that converts a foreign school certificate into something UAE institutions can use, and it is the single least well explained thing in this market. Zero of several competitor clusters in our research mention it at all, and one publishes the wrong subject count.

For the British track the published requirement is clear. Students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. A ranking tutoring site states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is incorrect and could change a family's subject choices for no reason.

For the American track the published requirements include an English proficiency score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, together with at least 450 in SAT mathematics before applying.

For the IB Diploma there is no points figure in the sources available to us, and we will not invent one. If your child is on the Diploma and you need the threshold, read it on the Ministry of Education's own site or ask the emirate attestation authority directly - and note that equivalency is a process families complete themselves through the official channel. IB Gram does not perform it, speed it up or guarantee it, and tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression.

sections.heading: Applications run ahead of results
paragraphs: The second administrative trap is the gap between when universities want information and when examination results exist. Applications are made on predicted grades, and the prediction is produced by the school months before the papers are sat.

That has two consequences a parent should plan around. The first is that a prediction matters as much as a result for the application itself, and predictions are based on the evidence the school has at the time - usually mock performance and assessed work. A student whose mock was unrepresentative has a specific, time-limited problem: produce better evidence before predictions are finalised. That is a legitimate reason to buy a short block of focused work, and the timing is dictated by the school's prediction calendar rather than by the examination.

The second is that a result arriving after an offer has conditions attached. For British-track candidates the published dates give a useful anchor: Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry can therefore produce a result in January, which is in time for some routes and not others - and that is a question for the receiving institution rather than for a tutoring site.

For IB candidates the equivalent dates come from the school's coordinator, because we publish none: the IB's own site could not be verified by us directly, and an application decision taken on a wrong date would be a serious error. Ask the coordinator for the cohort's dates in writing at the start of DP2 and keep them with the internal deadline calendar.

sections.heading: The private-candidate route
paragraphs: Some families in this part of Ajman end up outside the normal school-entry route: a student who has left school, one who is studying a subject the school does not offer, or one resitting after a move. That is the private-candidate route, and it shifts a large amount of administrative responsibility onto the family.

The mechanics are straightforward in principle. Entries are still made through a registered centre, so the first task is finding a centre that accepts private candidates for the subject and board you need. The centre's deadline for private entries is typically earlier than the one it applies to its own students, and fees are the family's responsibility. Some subjects with practical or speaking components are harder or impossible to enter privately, which is a question to resolve before anything else.

This is where families most often lose an entire series, because the sequence is unforgiving. Confirm the centre first, then the subject and component availability, then the deadline, then pay, then plan the teaching. Working in the opposite order - arranging tutoring and then discovering the entry cannot be made - happens more often than it should.

Our role here is limited and worth stating. We teach; we do not make entries, pay fees or act as a centre, and we have no premises in the UAE. What we can usefully do is work to the dates once they are fixed, and tell a family honestly when the time remaining is not enough for the subject they have in mind.

sections.heading: Term by term: what a parent should be doing
paragraphs: The administrative year has a rhythm, and almost all of it is one or two emails at the right moment rather than anything laborious. Written down, it stops being a series of surprises.

Early in the year, collect dates. The internal entry-change deadline, the mock window, and for an IB student the full internal deadline calendar - submission dates per subject, extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge deadline. Most schools provide these on request and very few families ask.

Mid-year, act on evidence. Mocks produce the first honest timed scripts and feed into predicted grades. This is the window for a tier or level conversation, for a short block aimed at the prediction, and for a frank question to the head of department about whether the current entry is right.

Late in the year, protect the sequence. Assessed work finished before revision, not during it. No new content in the final fortnight. And after results, the resit question answered from the script and from the receiving institution's position rather than from disappointment. The table sets the year out in the order the decisions actually arrive.

Keep all of it in one place - a note on a phone is enough. Households in this part of Ajman often deal with two schools under two authorities, and the single most common failure is not ignorance of a date but holding it in an email nobody can find in February. A list that both parents can see is worth more than any amount of good intention.

One more item belongs on that list: the dates of any external tests a university route requires, such as an English or mathematics proficiency test. Those are the only dates on the whole page a family schedules entirely themselves, which makes them the easiest to postpone until it is too late to resit.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the administrative year
paragraphs: The UAE calendar shapes the administrative year as much as the teaching one, and both effects are predictable enough to plan for.

Ramadan shortens school days and shifts usable working hours. Afternoons are low-energy; late morning at the weekend and after Iftar are productive. For a DP2 student with an internal assessment deadline inside the month, the plan should be rewritten before it starts rather than improvised, which usually costs two or three weeks. Because our lessons are online, moving a slot by two hours requires no renegotiation of anybody's journey.

Eid removes several days from a term at short notice. Where a school's internal deadline sits close to that break, the practical response is to bring the family's own checkpoint forward rather than to assume the school will move its date. Schools in different emirates handle these breaks slightly differently, which matters for a household with children in Ajman and Sharjah.

Administratively, the quietest periods are the best ones for paperwork. The long summer is when an equivalency file can be assembled without competing with term-time demands, when university requirements can be read properly, and when a private-candidate entry route can be investigated before deadlines tighten. Families who do that work in the summer rarely meet the administrative traps described on this page.

The teaching calendar follows the same logic. The long summer is the quietest working window of the year: an IB student can settle an exploration question or clear a backlog, and a British-track candidate can close the content gap that would otherwise surface in the final term. Because lessons are online, the slot follows a family travelling abroad, with the timezone adjusted.

sections.heading: Where tutoring genuinely helps a deadline
paragraphs: Having argued that administration matters more than teaching, it is worth being precise about where teaching does change an administrative outcome. There are four moments.

Before a tier or level decision, evidence is the thing in short supply. Two or three sessions attempting genuine Extended or higher level questions, marked honestly, give a family something to take into a conversation with the school. That is a cheap, finite purchase with a dated purpose.

Before predictions are finalised, a short focused block on the weakest paper can change the evidence the school is working from. This is a narrow window and it closes quietly, which is why knowing the prediction calendar matters.

Before an internal assessment deadline, coaching on criteria and planning is where marks are won - and it must happen early, because the practical work and the data collection cannot be redone later. And after a result, a session spent on the script tells you whether a resit is worth the autumn. In all four cases the tutoring is tied to a date, which is how we would rather sell it than as an open-ended weekly hour.

There is a fifth case, and it is the one families least expect to hear from a tutoring service: sometimes the honest recommendation is no teaching at all. If a tier is clearly right, predictions are already fair, assessed work is on schedule and the student is working steadily, the useful thing a parent can buy is nothing - and we will say so at the six-session review as readily as at the start.

Where a dated purchase does make sense, we keep it finite and write down what it is for. An arrangement with a purpose can be judged; an open-ended weekly hour gets renewed on impression, and impression in this market is driven by how pleasant a tutor is rather than by whether marks moved.

sections.heading: What we do not do
paragraphs: A page about administration should be unambiguous about the boundaries of our role, because several of the processes described here attract services offering to handle them for a fee.

We do not perform, expedite or guarantee Ministry of Education equivalency or attestation. Those are processes families complete themselves through the official channel, and we describe them and point you there. We do not make examination entries, pay fees, or act as a centre, and we have no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

We do not write, draft or edit assessed work of any kind - internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or coursework - and we do not sell completed work. Services that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice finding attaches to the student's diploma rather than to the seller. We also do not distribute boards' syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; your child's school is the proper route to current versions.

And we hold no approval, licence or accreditation from the Ministry of Education, SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education and Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. We can describe what those bodies do; none of them endorses us, and no tutoring service should imply otherwise.

Finally, we publish no statistic about our own results without the underlying data, and no grade guarantee of any kind. Nobody can know what a particular candidate will score, and a number offered in advance is a sales instrument rather than an educational commitment.

faqs.question: Which deadline should an Ajman parent actually diary first?
faqs.answer: The school's internal entry-change deadline. The board publishes a final entries date for centres, but your school needs decisions earlier in order to meet it, and that internal date is what constrains a tier change, a subject addition or a board switch. It is usually announced once, by email, in a busy term. Ask the exams officer for it in writing along with confirmation of the board, code and tier for every subject - both are facts the school already holds.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry of Education equivalency rule require?
faqs.answer: The published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring site states six subjects are required, which is incorrect. Verify your own case on the Ministry of Education's site or with the emirate attestation authority - families complete equivalency themselves.

faqs.question: Is there a published IB points threshold for equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not in the sources available to us, and we will not publish a number we cannot source. The British and American track requirements are documented in detail; no IB Diploma points figure appears alongside them. Read it on the Ministry of Education's own site or ask your school's IB coordinator, who handles this for a whole cohort annually. Treat any tutoring page quoting a confident IB figure without a government source the way you would treat any other unsourced claim about your child's future.

faqs.question: What does the American-track equivalency route require?
faqs.answer: The published requirements include an English proficiency score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, together with at least 450 in SAT mathematics before applying. Those are test thresholds rather than school grades, which means they are scheduled events a family can plan for - and the long summer is the sensible time to sit or resit them, away from term-time pressure. Verify the current position on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Why do predicted grades matter as much as results?
faqs.answer: Because applications are made before results exist. The school produces predictions months ahead of the papers, based on the evidence it has - usually mock performance and assessed work - and those predictions drive offers. A student whose mock was unrepresentative therefore has a narrow, dated opportunity: produce better evidence before predictions are finalised. Knowing your school's prediction calendar is what turns that from a missed chance into a short, well-aimed block of work.

faqs.question: Can a November resit result arrive in time to matter?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the sequence is what decides it. The November 2025 Pearson series results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a January return is realistic. Whether that is in time depends entirely on the receiving sixth form or university, which is a question for them rather than for a tutoring site. Confirm acceptance first, then the entry route with the school or a registered centre, then read the June script - a candidate two marks short needs different work from one thirty marks short.

faqs.question: How does the private-candidate route work and what are its risks?
faqs.answer: Entries still go through a registered centre, so the first task is finding one that accepts private candidates for your board and subject. Private-entry deadlines are typically earlier than those applied to the centre's own students, fees are the family's responsibility, and some subjects with practical or speaking components are difficult or impossible to enter privately. The sequence matters: confirm the centre, the components and the deadline before arranging any teaching. Families lose whole series by doing it the other way round.

faqs.question: Who supervises private schools in Ajman, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Dubai's by KHDA. It affects where you look for published school information rather than tutoring itself, which is governed federally through the MoHRE private tutor permit. For a household with children in two emirates, it means two sets of guidance and two internal deadline calendars to request.

faqs.question: What should we ask for at the start of DP2?
faqs.answer: The full internal deadline calendar in writing: internal assessment submission dates per subject, extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge essay deadline and the mock windows. Those dates bind your child and sit earlier than anything the board publishes. With the list in hand, the fortnight where several deadlines collide becomes visible months ahead and can be defused by finishing one piece early. Most schools supply it on request; very few families ask.

faqs.question: Does a tier change after mocks still make sense?
faqs.answer: If the internal entry deadline has not passed, yes - and the question is evidence rather than ambition. Extended carries the full grade range and includes content a Core candidate never meets, so the test is whether the student can access it and finish the harder paper in the time. Two sessions of real Extended past-paper questions, marked honestly, give you something to take to the head of department. After the internal deadline the realistic alternative is entering the other tier in the November series.

faqs.question: How do we handle two children at schools in different emirates?
faqs.answer: Request both internal deadline calendars and compare them side by side once a term. Schools under different authorities have different term dates and reporting cycles, and mock weeks can fall a fortnight apart, so one child's deadline will land in the other's revision week. Seeing that early lets you move a slot deliberately instead of cancelling under pressure. We sequence sessions by arrival time on one evening, since children crossing to Sharjah or Dubai get home later.

faqs.question: Does the summer have any administrative use?
faqs.answer: It is the best window of the year for paperwork. An equivalency file can be assembled without competing with term-time demands, university entry requirements can be read properly, a private-candidate entry route can be investigated before deadlines tighten, and test dates for English or mathematics proficiency can be planned. Families who do that work in the summer rarely meet the traps on this page. It is also the quietest time to settle an IB exploration question or clear a content backlog.

faqs.question: Can you help us with the equivalency or attestation paperwork?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should any tutoring service. Equivalency is a process families complete themselves through the official channel, and we describe the published requirements and point you to the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority. We do not perform it, expedite it or guarantee it, we make no examination entries and pay no fees, and we hold no approval or accreditation from any education authority. Tutoring is also not a requirement for equivalency, admission or progression.

faqs.question: What if we need teaching at short notice before a dated decision?
faqs.answer: Tell us the date and we will say honestly what is achievable before it. Evidence sessions before a tier decision, a short block before predictions, criteria coaching before an assessed deadline - those are all finite pieces of work we can usually place quickly. What we cannot do is reteach a course in a fortnight, and we will not substitute a generalist for an unavailable specialist during a dated block, because that costs exactly the window you were trying to use.

intro.heading: Proximity is the most expensive thing on the invoice
paragraphs: Ask three Al Rashidiya families what they pay for tuition and you will get three answers that cannot be compared. One is paying AED 120 an hour to a university student who supervises homework. One is paying AED 350 an hour to a visiting tutor who spends forty minutes of each booked hour in a car. One is paying AED 200 an hour online to somebody who has taught the exact Diploma course their child sits. All three describe themselves as paying for a tutor, and only one of them knows what they bought.

The word doing the damage in the search is 'near me'. Distance is a genuine cost in the Northern Emirates, but it is a cost to the tutor, and it is passed on. A visiting tutor crossing Ajman in evening traffic can serve two or three students a night, so the hourly rate has to carry the journey, the fuel and the dead time. Market quotes for in-home one-to-one visits in the UAE run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is not better teaching.

What proximity also buys is a smaller choice. The set of people within a short drive of Al Rashidiya who have recently taught Chemistry HL, or Additional Mathematics 0606, or Economics at the upper bands, is small. Paying a premium to select from a smaller pool is the opposite of value. IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, because lessons are delivered live over video, and the practical result is that the price of a specialist does not change with your postcode.

The rest of this page is arithmetic. It sets out the market bands by tier with sources, converts them into monthly figures for one, two and three subjects, compares the provider models an Ajman family can actually choose between, and then names the four ways money reliably disappears in this market: the cheap hour that teaches nothing, the premium hour that buys reputation rather than method, the generalist who prepares the wrong paper, and the coursework service that endangers the certificate it was bought to protect.

None of the figures below are IB Gram's price list. They are the market, published by the people who charge them, so that any quote you receive, including ours, can be judged against something external. Three of the strongest pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a family in Ajman transacts in.

Read it with a pen. The point of the tables is not to tell an Al Rashidiya family what to spend; it is to let them check a quote against something published before agreeing to it, and to see which part of a quoted hour is teaching and which part is transport.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-rashi.programmesIntro: An Al Rashidiya family budgeting for tuition is usually budgeting across two qualifications at once, because one child is mid-IGCSE while another starts the Diploma. The programmes below carry different hourly bands for the ordinary reason that teaching experience in them is differently scarce.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten externally examined subjects, with syllabus codes that determine the papers and often the tier. Rates for IGCSE support sit consistently below Diploma rates: one provider publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour against IB from AED 200. The differential reflects how many teachers are confident with the specification, not how hard the course is.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and many Al Rashidiya students are entered through Sharjah schools instead. The board is Cambridge or Pearson in either case, and the cheapest mistake to avoid is paying a tutor who has taught the other board's version of the same subject.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with three of the four rewarding process rather than recall. MYP support is often the best value purchase a family makes, because criterion technique transfers across every subject and a student who learns it in Year 9 stops losing marks in all of them simultaneously.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman Academy is the emirate's principal International Baccalaureate provider and several Sharjah schools take Al Rashidiya students into MYP. Families here commonly buy one MYP subject and find the gain shows up across the report card, which makes a single weekly hour go further than it does at Diploma level.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. This is where costs concentrate, because Higher Level teaching is scarce, internal assessment support is time-intensive, and most families increase from two sessions a week to three during DP2. Budget it as a two-year commitment, not a monthly one.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma is also where the in-home premium bites hardest in Ajman, because the local pool of Higher Level specialists is thin enough that proximity and specialism rarely coincide. Paying a travel premium to a generalist is the most expensive single configuration available to an Al Rashidiya family.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-IGCSE route most Northern Emirates students take, in three or four subjects. Rates sit alongside Diploma rates, with specialist bands quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. The first term of Year 12 is the period when families most often start tuition, because the step up from Extended is steeper than the school prospectus suggests.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published rule asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE subjects. That makes a weak A Level grade expensive in a way no tuition invoice shows.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-rashi.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Rashidiya families most often buy help in, across both qualifications. Each entry names what the money is buying, because a rate per hour is only meaningful once you know what has to happen inside the hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IB AA and AI; Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most purchased subject in this market and the one where cheap help is most tempting. Homework supervision at AED 120 an hour will not fix algebraic fluency. What moves a grade is marked work on unfamiliar multi-step problems, which requires a teacher who knows the paper.

subjects.name: Physics (IB HL and SL; Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and fields reliably produce the requests. The expensive part is uncertainty and error analysis for the Diploma internal assessment, and the alternative-to-practical technique at IGCSE. Both are teachable in a defined number of hours, which makes them worth buying as a block.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB HL and SL; Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and mole calculations dominate. A tutor who teaches curly-arrow notation as a claim about electrons rather than a diagram convention saves a term of confusion, and that is the difference a higher rate should be buying.

subjects.name: Biology (IB HL and SL; Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content volume invites memorisation and the papers reward command-term discipline. Cheap help tends to produce more notes; useful help produces marked answers to 'explain' and 'suggest' questions, where the grades actually sit.

subjects.name: Economics (IB HL and SL; Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and applied evaluation. The Diploma internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published articles, and article selection sets the ceiling before any writing starts. An hour spent choosing articles well is the cheapest hour in the subject.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study response under time pressure. Most lost marks are judgements never made: the theory is described accurately and the evaluation never arrives. That is a technique problem, which is why a small number of well-marked sessions outperforms a long general course.

subjects.name: English (IB Language and Literature; Cambridge 0500 and 0475)
subjects.description: Summary economy, quotation selection and the individual oral. English is the subject where families most often buy a long course and need a short one, because the gains come from a handful of repeatable techniques applied under time.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Additional and Further (Cambridge 0606, Pearson 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths entry by stronger cohorts. Local supply in Ajman is effectively nil, which makes this the clearest case in the whole subject list where paying for proximity means paying more for less.

subjects.name: Computer Science (IB HL and SL; Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Algorithm tracing by hand, pseudocode conventions and, for the Diploma, a documented solution assessed on planning and evaluation. Students arrive able to code and unable to document, and the documentation is where the marks are.

subjects.name: Arabic (IB Arabic B and ab initio; Cambridge 0508 and 0544)
subjects.levels: HL, SL, ab initio and IGCSE
subjects.description: Two or more genuinely different qualifications routinely confused when a family books. Paying for the wrong one is a pure loss. Confirm the entry code or the Diploma route before the first lesson is scheduled.
