sections.heading: What the market charges, with the sources attached
paragraphs: The table below is the band structure of this market in dirhams. It is assembled from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table, and each row names who publishes a figure in that band. Ajman rates for in-home work sit at or slightly below the Dubai figures, for the ordinary reason that local visiting tutors here charge less than those serving Downtown. Online rates do not vary by emirate at all.

Read it from the bottom upwards. The premium band above AED 500 exists and is published: one provider quotes AED 650 an hour. What it buys is a named individual with a reputation, and for the large majority of students it is not the constraint on the grade. The band that matters for an Al Rashidiya family is AED 150 to AED 300, where the only variable worth paying for is whether the person has taught that course at that level recently.

The bottom band deserves its own warning. AED 33 to AED 65 an hour buys supervision, not teaching. There is a legitimate use for it, which is making sure a Year 8 student actually does their homework in a quiet room with somebody checking. It is not a Diploma intervention, and buying it as one is the single commonest way money is wasted in this market, because the spend is small enough to continue for a year without anyone reassessing it.

One further caution about the bands themselves. They are as-of figures, collected in October 2026 from pages that may be revised, so treat them as a reference point rather than a current price list. What does not change quickly is the shape: a wide budget band, a narrow qualified-tutor band, an in-home band inflated by travel, and a thin premium band at the top priced on reputation. That shape is the useful part, and it is the part no competitor page in this segment publishes at all.

sections.heading: The monthly number, for one, two and three subjects
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead because nobody buys one hour. The commitment is monthly and it compounds with each subject added, which is why a family that starts with one subject in October can be surprised by the February invoice without anything having changed except the number of subjects.

The figures below convert the published monthly estimates into a one, two and three subject plan at a single weekly hour each. They use the mid-tier band of AED 600 to AED 1,200 per subject per month and the specialist exam-year band of AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more, both from Bestimate's published estimates, alongside the AED 799 monthly package for eight online sessions advertised in this market. These are market figures rather than ours, and they are deliberately shown as ranges because that is how they are published.

The useful conclusion for an Al Rashidiya family is that three subjects at specialist rates is a different category of decision from one subject at mid-tier rates, and should be treated as one. Where three subjects genuinely need help, the cheaper and usually better plan is two taught weekly and the third handled as a defined block before the series, rather than three open-ended weekly commitments running for a year.

One more line belongs in the arithmetic, and it is the one families forget: the cost of the plan that does not work. Six months at AED 800 a month spent on supervision for a Diploma student is close to AED 5,000 that bought nothing measurable. The same sum spent as two defined blocks on named weaknesses, each with a diagnostic at the start and the same paper type at the end, produces evidence either way. The expensive choice is rarely the higher hourly rate; it is the lower one left running unexamined for three terms.

sections.heading: The four places Ajman families lose money
paragraphs: The first is the cheap hour bought for the wrong job. Supervision at the bottom of the band is useful for a younger student and inert for a Diploma candidate, and because the monthly figure is small it survives review for far longer than it should. A year of AED 400 a month that produces nothing costs more than three months of AED 1,000 that produces a grade.

The second is the travel premium paid to a generalist. In-home quotes in the Northern Emirates run to AED 500 an hour at the top, and the increment over online delivery is journey time. Paying it for a specialist who could not otherwise be reached would be rational. Paying it to a person who has not taught your child's specification is paying extra for a smaller pool, which is the worst available trade.

The third is the premium rate bought as a proxy for method. Price signals scarcity, not pedagogy. A named tutor at AED 650 an hour may be excellent, and the question that should decide the purchase is the same one that decides a AED 200 purchase: which papers does my child sit, where do candidates lose marks in this syllabus, and what will you do about it. If the expensive answer is vaguer than the cheaper one, the price is doing no work.

The fourth is the worst. Services exist in this segment that sell completed Internal Assessments, with one publishing a price for exactly that. A family paying for written coursework has bought an academic-honesty breach, and the consequence for a Diploma candidate can reach the loss of the Diploma itself. The money is lost either way: if the work is detected the qualification goes, and if it is not, the student sits a written paper they were never taught to pass.

sections.heading: Provider models an Al Rashidiya family can actually choose between
paragraphs: Comparisons in this market are usually against an unnamed competitor, which tells a parent nothing. The honest comparison is between models, because each has a cost structure and a failure mode that follow from how it is built rather than from how well it is run.

A tuition centre spreads a teacher's hour across several students, which is why group rates are lower per head. The trade is pace: the group moves at its own speed and a student who is behind on one topic gets the same minutes as one who is ahead. A freelance independent tutor is often the cheapest one-to-one option and the hardest to replace mid-term, because there is no bench; illness or relocation ends the arrangement. An agency adds a margin and, in exchange, should add matching and replacement.

A platform like this one removes the geography and, with it, the travel premium, at the cost of requiring a student who can work on a screen for an hour. That suits most students from about Year 8 upward and does not suit all of them, which is why the trial exists. Where a child genuinely needs an adult in the room, a local in-home tutor is the right purchase and IB Gram is not, because we do not provide home visits in the UAE at all.

Two practical questions separate the models faster than any comparison table. Ask what happens if the tutor stops: a freelance arrangement ends, an agency or platform should propose a replacement who has taught the same specification. Then ask what happens if a lesson is cancelled a day out: a visiting tutor has committed an evening and will usually bill it, while an online slot can generally move to the next day. Those two answers tell you what the margin in an agency rate is actually paying for, and whether it is worth it for your household.

sections.heading: The permit is free, and that tells you something about the market
paragraphs: Families often assume that a licensed tutor costs more because the licence costs money. It does not. The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation lists the service as private tutor licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system, with no fee and a stated completion time of two working days.

Eligibility is wide: registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals providing private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and a figure circulating online could not be verified, so treat any page quoting a specific penalty amount as unreliable.

The pricing implication is straightforward. Nobody can justify a higher rate by pointing at the cost of their permit, because there is no cost. What a permit does tell you is that the person has registered to do this work, which is worth asking about and is not the same as evidence that they can teach your child's syllabus. No UAE authority certifies subject competence, and any advertisement claiming regulator approval for tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form. IB Gram holds no such approval and does not claim one.

One related point worth settling before you pay anybody. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is described as carrying a similar restriction. Treat that as press-reported rather than verified wording, and verify it against the current policy document if it matters to you. The general principle is sound everywhere in the UAE: a child's own class teacher taking private payment for tutoring that child is an arrangement to avoid, not to seek out.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context, next to the other things a family pays
paragraphs: A tutoring budget looks different beside the other lines in an education budget, and the comparison is worth making before deciding that AED 1,000 a month is a lot or a little. The Dubai regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the following academic year, under an economic incentives package, which is the nearest thing to a fixed point in the sector.

Scale is worth knowing too. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum schools accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Ajman's market is far smaller, which is precisely why its local tutoring supply is thin and why online delivery changes the choice available to a family here more than it does for a family in Dubai.

Against that, a defined tuition block is a modest and reversible expense, and an open-ended three-subject plan at specialist rates is not. The useful discipline is to decide in advance what the money is for, how you will know whether it worked, and when you will stop. Marked past-paper performance before and after a block answers all three. A general sense that things are better does not, and that is the gap most tuition spending disappears into.

There is also a timing cost that no rate table shows. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened in the previous year and enrolment rose by six per cent. A sector adding capacity that fast moves teachers between schools, and a tutor who was available on a Tuesday evening in September may not be in January. Booking a specialist slot early in the year costs the same as booking it late and is considerably more likely to be possible.

sections.heading: How to tell in six weeks whether the money is working
paragraphs: Most tuition decisions are reviewed on feeling, which is why so many of them continue past the point of usefulness. A student who likes their tutor and reports that things are clearer now is giving honest testimony about the hour and no information at all about the grade. The review that matters compares marked work under time against marked work under time, and it can be set up in advance for nothing.

The mechanism is simple. At the start, the student sits a past paper or a section of one under proper timed conditions, and the tutor marks it against the published scheme, recording the marks by question rather than as a total. Six weeks later the same paper type, a different series, under the same conditions, marked the same way. The comparison is per-topic, so it shows which part of the spend moved and which did not. A total alone hides exactly the information you need.

What to do with the result is where families hesitate. If the targeted topics moved and others did not, the plan is working and the scope was right. If nothing moved, the diagnosis was wrong rather than the tutor, and the next block should address something else. If everything moved slightly, the student was probably short of practice rather than teaching, which is a cheaper problem to solve. Stopping is a legitimate outcome of a review and the one almost nobody plans for in advance.
bullets: Record marks per question, not as a total
Same paper type, different series, same timed conditions
Compare per topic to see what the spend actually moved

process.title: Decide what the money is for
process.description: Name the gap before pricing anything: a specific topic, a paper type, a coursework stage or a study-method problem. A named gap can be bought as a block with a fixed total. An unnamed one becomes an open-ended monthly commitment that nobody reviews, which is how most tuition budgets drift.

process.title: Send the subject, level and board
process.description: Mathematics AA HL, or Cambridge 0580 Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher Tier. The level and the specification change who can teach it, and therefore what a fair rate is. A quote given without this information is not a quote for anything in particular.

process.title: Take the free trial before paying
process.description: One lesson at no charge, with no payment details collected first, on a topic your child is currently stuck on. Afterwards you get a short written note on what was done and what the priority should be. Judge the note, not the hour: it is the evidence that the person understands the examination.

process.title: Agree a plan with a stated end
process.description: Weekly teaching to a date, or a block of a defined number of hours, with the total cost known in advance. Open-ended arrangements are the ones that cost the most over a year, because nothing in them prompts a review.

process.title: Review against marked work, not impressions
process.description: At the end of the first half-term, compare marked past-paper performance with where the student started. That is the only check that distinguishes a plan worth extending from one worth stopping, and it is the review almost no family runs.

whyPoints.title: Published figures you can check
whyPoints.description: Every dirham band on this page names the provider or rate table that published it, including the ones that make our own band look expensive. In a segment where three of the strongest ranking pages publish no price at all, attribution is the differentiator.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium to pay
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered live online, so the AED 180 to AED 500 in-home band and the journey it pays for do not apply. The rate for a specialist is the same from Al Rashidiya as from anywhere else in the Gulf, because delivery cost does not change with distance.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with a fixed total
whyPoints.description: Where the gap is specific, you can buy eight or twelve hours with the total agreed in advance and a stated endpoint. That is the format most likely to produce a measurable result and least likely to turn into an unreviewed monthly standing order.

whyPoints.title: Matched on specification, not availability
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed because they have taught that course at that level, and if nobody has, you are told rather than offered a generalist. Paying a specialist rate for generalist teaching is the error this filter exists to prevent.

whyPoints.title: A refusal that protects the certificate
whyPoints.description: Coursework and internal assessments are taught, questioned and reviewed, never written. Services in this segment sell completed assessments at a published price; buying one risks the qualification the tuition was meant to protect, which makes it the most expensive purchase available.

whyPoints.title: No office, no claimed accreditation, no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram has no UAE premises and holds no regulator or examination-board approval. There is no satisfaction percentage or average-score figure on this page, because we could not produce the underlying data for one, and a number without a method is just decoration.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for a tutor in Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: Judged against published market figures rather than our own pricing: AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 180 to AED 500 for an in-home visit where the upper half is largely travel. Budget supervision runs from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour and is not exam-year teaching. The number that matters is monthly: one weekly hour with a mid-tier tutor is estimated at AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month in published rate tables.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home tutor cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is billable, even when the invoice does not itemise it. A visiting tutor crossing Ajman in evening traffic can teach two or three students a night, so the hourly rate carries the travel, the fuel and the dead time between bookings. Published bands show in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500 against AED 150 to AED 300 online for a qualified subject tutor. The extra buys physical presence, which helps some students a great deal and most students not at all.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. A student in Year 7 or 8 who does not do homework without supervision is well served by a lower-cost tutor whose role is to keep them at the desk and check the work. That is a real service and it is priced correctly. The error is buying it for a Year 11 or Diploma student with a specific syllabus gap, where the hour produces company rather than teaching, and the low monthly figure means nobody reviews it for a year.

faqs.question: What does a premium rate of AED 650 an hour actually buy?
faqs.answer: Scarcity and reputation. One provider in this market publishes that figure for a named tutor. It can represent genuine excellence, and it is not usually the constraint on a student's grade. The test is the same at any price: ask which papers the student sits, where candidates lose marks in that specific syllabus, and what the tutor will do about it. If the expensive answer is vaguer than a cheaper one, the price is not buying method.

faqs.question: Do online rates change because we live in Ajman rather than Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and that is one of the quieter advantages of the format for a Northern Emirates family. Delivery cost does not vary with distance, so the price of a specialist is the same from Al Rashidiya as from Jumeirah. In-home rates do vary by emirate, generally sitting a little lower in Ajman than in central Dubai, because local visiting tutors charge less. The gap between in-home and online, however, stays roughly constant, because it is mostly travel.

faqs.question: Does the tutor's permit add to the cost?
faqs.answer: It cannot, because it is free. The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted at no charge for two years, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation lists the service with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is mistaken. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no official fine amounts have been published.

faqs.question: Can two children in one Al Rashidiya household share an hour to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per head and it is usually a false saving where the children are at different levels or in different years. One-to-one exists because the hour follows one student's gaps. Two siblings in MYP and DP need entirely different teaching, and an hour split between them delivers two half-lessons. What does work, and is genuinely cheaper in time rather than money, is consecutive slots on the same evening so the household loses one evening instead of two.

faqs.question: How do group classes at a tuition centre compare on price?
faqs.answer: Lower per head, because a teacher's hour is shared. The trade is pace: the group moves at a single speed through a fixed syllabus plan, which suits a student whose gap matches the group's and wastes time for one whose gap does not. For broad content coverage early in Year 10 a group can be good value. For a specific weakness eight weeks before a series, one-to-one hours spent on exactly that weakness do more per dirham.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to get IB coursework support?
faqs.answer: Buy it early. A research question corrected in the second week of the process costs one session; the same correction in week ten means a rewrite that costs several. The expensive version is a late panic block of coursework coaching, and the ruinous version is paying somebody to write it, which risks the Diploma itself. Legitimate support is teaching, questioning and criterion feedback on the student's own draft, and it is cheapest when it starts before the first draft exists.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a full year or buy hours as we need them?
faqs.answer: Buy a block with a stated total and endpoint unless the gap is genuinely broad. Open-ended monthly arrangements are the ones that run for a year without review, because nothing in them creates a decision point. A twelve-hour block with a diagnostic at the start and the same paper type at the end produces evidence, and evidence is what tells you whether to extend. Our own plans are arranged this way for that reason.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes that look similar?
faqs.answer: Put the specification next to each. Ask both tutors which papers your child sits, their durations and weightings, and where candidates in that syllabus most reliably lose marks. A specialist answers without hesitation; a generalist talks about confidence and rapport. Then ask what each will refuse to do with assessed coursework. Two quotes at AED 220 an hour can differ completely in what they are selling, and none of that difference appears in the number.

faqs.question: Are there hidden extras in tutoring quotes?
faqs.answer: The common ones are travel added as a separate line for in-home visits, minimum session lengths that turn a sixty-minute need into a ninety-minute charge, cancellation windows that bill a lesson missed for a school trip, and materials fees. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per session, what happens if you cancel a day ahead, and whether anything is charged on top. On online delivery the travel line does not exist, which removes the largest of them.

faqs.question: Is private tuition required for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and any page implying it is creating false urgency about a regulatory process. Equivalency is assessed by the Ministry against published subject and grade requirements, and tutoring is not a condition of it. For the British track the published rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus an A Level at E or two AS Levels. IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: What should a first month of tuition realistically cost us?
faqs.answer: For one subject at one weekly hour with a mid-tier tutor, published monthly estimates put it at AED 600 to AED 1,200, and advertised packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Two subjects roughly doubles it. A specialist exam-year plan is estimated at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more per subject per month. Those are market figures, not ours; the point of publishing them is that you can hold any quote, including ours, against them.

The trial lesson costs nothing and collects no payment details, and the written note afterwards is the thing to judge. intro.heading: A small market behaves differently, and the pages ranking for this search do not know that
paragraphs: Al Rawda is a set of three villa sub-communities on the western side of Ajman, settled rather than transient, with buses running out towards Sharjah every morning. A parent here searching for a tutor sees the same results as a parent in Dubai Marina, and almost none of those results were written with a Northern Emirates family in mind. The neighbourhood lists at the bottom of agency pages name Dubai communities. The schools named are Dubai schools. The regulator named, where one is named at all, is Dubai's.

That is not just an irritation; it produces advice that does not transfer. A Dubai parent genuinely can find a Chemistry Higher Level specialist within a twenty-minute drive, because the emirate's private school market served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate students making up around seven per cent of that enrolment. A market that size supports specialists living inside it. Ajman's does not, and no amount of searching harder changes the arithmetic.

The second difference is regulatory, and it is simpler than it sounds. Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. For an Al Rawda family with one child at an Ajman school and another bussed into Sharjah, two of those apply at once.

The third difference is price, and it runs in the family's favour in one direction only. In-home tutoring quotes in Ajman sit at or slightly below Dubai levels, because local visiting tutors charge less than those serving Downtown. Online rates are identical everywhere, because the cost of a video lesson does not vary with distance. That single fact is what makes the small-market problem solvable: an Al Rawda family can buy from the same pool as a Dubai family at the same price, which is not true of anything delivered in person.

IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. What follows is the comparison itself: the emirates set against each other as tutoring markets, why market size determines specialist supply, what a Dubai family genuinely has that an Ajman family does not, the two qualifications compared for a household here, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules that are identical in every emirate, and the questions worth asking any tutor regardless of where they sit.

A parent who reads only one section should read the market comparison table. It explains why a reasonable search produces an unreasonable result here, and why the obvious response of searching harder locally does not work in an emirate this size.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely taught international route in the Northern Emirates, with syllabus codes that fix the papers and often the tier. programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with internal assessments carrying roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade. The cohort in Ajman is small, which is exactly why local Higher Level specialist supply is the thinnest part of the whole market here.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates at Ajman and Sharjah schools sit the May session. No specific examination or results date appears on this page, because the organisation's own site blocks automated retrieval and no date could be verified; your child's International Baccalaureate coordinator is the authority on all of them.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Continuous assessment against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. Criterion technique transfers across every subject, which makes MYP support unusually efficient: a student who learns what the descriptors require improves in several subjects at once rather than one.

For an Al Rawda family the practical consequence is that MYP help is the easiest IB support to justify locally and the hardest to find a specialist for nearby.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-IGCSE route taken by most Northern Emirates students who do not move into the Diploma. Entry requirements are expressed in IGCSE grades, which makes the August results day a real decision point and the Year 10 tier decision consequential two years later.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. subjects.description: Arabic teaching is abundant locally; teaching aimed at these specific syllabuses is scarce. The courses are genuinely different qualifications with different assumptions about fluency, and the wrong entry is discovered too late to fix.

sections.heading: Searching from Ajman is not the same as searching from Dubai
paragraphs: Run the same search from two addresses and the results barely change, which is the problem. The pages that rank for tutor searches in this country were written for the largest market in it, and they carry Dubai's assumptions inside sentences that look general. Advice to meet a tutor for coffee before booking, to check which nearby school they taught at, to compare three local agencies: all reasonable in a market with 227 private schools in one emirate, and all close to meaningless from a villa in Al Rawda.

The substantive difference is the number of candidates sitting any one course at any one level. Dubai's private schools served 387,441 students in 2024-25, with UK curriculum schools accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate about 7 per cent. Seven per cent of a market that size is still a large Diploma population, large enough that Higher Level teachers live in the emirate, commute within it and tutor in the evenings.

Ajman's equivalent figure is small, and the emirate's International Baccalaureate provision is concentrated in a handful of schools. Divide a small Diploma cohort across six subjects, two levels and a dozen Higher Level option combinations and the per-course demand in the emirate is a few students a year. No teacher builds an evening practice on that, so the specialists are not here, and a parent searching locally is not failing to find them; there is nobody to find.

There is one further asymmetry worth naming. Dubai is also adding capacity quickly: its 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened the previous year and enrolment rose by six per cent. A market growing at that rate pulls teachers towards it, which over time makes the supply difference between the emirates wider rather than narrower.

sections.heading: The emirates compared as tutoring markets
paragraphs: The table below compares what actually differs between the emirates from a tutoring point of view: who regulates the schools, how big the market is, what local supply looks like, and whether any of it changes the price of an online specialist. It is the comparison a Northern Emirates parent needs and that no page in this segment provides.

The regulator column is drawn from the UAE government's own published description of private school oversight. Dubai is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah is the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah is its Department of Knowledge, both of which also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

The last column is the one that resolves the page. Nothing in the regulator or market-size differences changes the price or availability of a tutor delivering live lessons over video, because that market is national and in practice regional. An Al Rawda family and a Dubai family choose from the same teachers at the same published bands. The emirate differences are entirely about what is available in person, which is the thing we do not sell in this country at all.

A note on the supply column, which is a judgement rather than a published figure. It reflects what families in each emirate report about finding subject-specific help in the evenings, and it will be wrong in individual cases: a Fujairah family with a chemistry teacher next door has better local supply than the row suggests. The regulator and the rate columns are sourced; the supply column is the pattern, not a promise about any one street.

sections.heading: Why market size decides who is available
paragraphs: The mechanism is worth spelling out, because once it is clear a lot of fruitless searching stops. A teacher who tutors in the evening needs enough students to justify specialising. If they can fill four evenings a week teaching Higher Level chemistry, they will teach Higher Level chemistry and get very good at it. If they can fill one evening a week, they will teach whatever is asked and remain a generalist, because that is the only viable practice in a thin market.

This is why the quality difference between a Dubai specialist and an Ajman generalist is not about the individuals. It is about how many students were available to each of them. The same teacher relocating from Ajman to Dubai would specialise within a year, and the same specialist relocating the other way would generalise. Blaming the local market's depth on the people in it mistakes a structural fact for a personal one.

It also explains the specific pattern of what is available locally. Mathematics at IGCSE level is findable in every Ajman community, because every school enters a large number of candidates for it. Biology is findable. English is findable. Additional Mathematics, Computer Science, Diploma Economics and Higher Level sciences are not, because the per-course demand within driving distance is a handful of students across an entire year.

The response is not to search harder but to change the search key. Replace distance with the course and the level, accept that the person may be teaching from elsewhere in the region, and the pool stops being a few people and becomes everyone teaching that course in this time zone. That is the only move available to a small market, and it costs nothing extra because online delivery does not price distance.

sections.heading: What a Dubai family genuinely has that an Al Rawda family does not
paragraphs: Being fair about this matters, because a page that claims the small market has no disadvantages is not credible. A Dubai family does have real advantages, and three of them are worth naming.

The first is in-person choice. If physical presence is what a particular child needs, a Dubai parent has a genuine market of visiting specialists and an Al Rawda parent has a much smaller one. For a young child, or a student who will not stay at a desk without an adult in the room, that is a material difference and it favours Dubai. In that situation a local visiting tutor is the correct purchase and we are not, since IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

The second is group and centre provision. Larger markets sustain tuition centres with real subject streams, and a well-run group class at IGCSE level can be good value for broad content coverage. Ajman has centres; it has fewer with deep per-syllabus streaming, for the same market-size reason as everything else on this page.

The third is school choice itself, which is upstream of tutoring. More schools means more curricula, more Diploma provision and more chance of a good fit without a long commute. Dubai confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the following academic year under an economic incentives package, which is a benefit that does not extend to families in a different emirate.

What a Dubai family does not have is any advantage in access to an online specialist, in the price of one, or in the information needed to choose well. Those three are national, and this page is an attempt to make the third of them available here rather than only in the market the ranking pages were written for.

sections.heading: IB or IGCSE: the comparison for a household here
paragraphs: Families in Al Rawda sometimes face the qualification choice directly, usually at a school transfer or when a child moves from Year 11 into post-16 study. The comparison below is practical rather than philosophical: what each qualification demands, what support it needs, and how each behaves in a market with thin local supply.

The decisive operational difference is the internal component. Diploma subjects carry internally assessed work worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge, all of which have deadlines spread through the two years and converge in the autumn of the second. IGCSE is overwhelmingly terminal, with coursework in a minority of subjects. That means the Diploma needs continuous, well-timed support and the IGCSE tolerates concentrated support late.

The second difference is repair. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, so an IGCSE grade has a structural second chance with results in January. The Diploma's internal components close on submission and its session is annual. In a household with limited hours, that asymmetry is the single most useful fact for deciding where the hours go.

The third is university positioning, and it should be checked rather than assumed. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track the published rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 plus post-16 qualifications; for the International Baccalaureate no points threshold is stated in the published clarification we worked from, so no figure should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one. Confirm with the Ministry and with the specific university.

sections.heading: Equivalency and permits: federal rules, identical everywhere
paragraphs: Two things in this market are genuinely the same across every emirate, and it is worth knowing which, because advertisements sometimes imply otherwise. The first is the Ministry of Education equivalency framework. The second is the permit that allows a person to tutor privately.

On equivalency, the published clarification sets out the British track as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. One ranking competitor states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is not what the published rule says.

On permits, an individual providing private lessons needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The service is listed as private tutor licensing, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted.

Neither of these is something IB Gram performs, guarantees or holds a status in. We hold no regulator or examination-board accreditation of any kind, and tutoring is not a requirement of equivalency. Any advertisement describing tutors as approved by a regulator is describing something that does not exist in that form, and that is as true in Dubai as it is in Al Rawda.

sections.heading: The five questions worth asking any tutor, anywhere
paragraphs: If distance stops being the filter, something has to replace it, and credentials are a weak substitute because they are easy to assert and hard to verify. The following five questions work on anybody, local or remote, and they take about four minutes.

Which papers does my child sit for this entry or this course, and how long is each? What is the weighting between the components? Where do candidates in this specific syllabus or subject most reliably lose marks, and how do you teach that? Which past series or paper type would you start from, and why that one? And what will you refuse to do if I ask you to help with coursework or an internal assessment?

The value is in the texture of the answers rather than their content, which is why a parent does not need to know the answers in advance. Someone who has taught Cambridge 0620 recently will say that mole calculations and ionic equations eat marks and will have a view about where to start. Someone teaching Diploma biology will mention command terms and statistical choice in the internal assessment. A generalist will talk about building confidence and rapport, which is pleasant and is not what decides a grade.

The fifth question is the one that should produce a refusal. A tutor who offers to write an internal assessment, complete coursework or supply text for submission has offered to put the student's certification at risk, and that market exists: one site in this search segment sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Hearing a clear no is the strongest signal available that the rest of what you are being told is honest.

process.title: Say which qualification and which level
process.description: IGCSE with a syllabus code and tier, or Diploma with the subject and level and, where relevant, the Higher Level option topic. In a thin local market this detail is what determines whether a specialist exists for you at all, so it is the first thing we ask for rather than a formality.

process.title: Tell us the honest evening window
process.description: The hour your child is genuinely home and able to think on an ordinary weekday in Al Rawda, which for a Sharjah bus route is later than the school timetable suggests. The slot is the one variable your address really does control, and a plan built on the wrong hour fails in a fortnight.

process.title: Free trial with a specialist, or an honest no
process.description: One lesson at no charge with no payment details collected, taught by someone who has taught that exact course. If nobody is free in your window this term, you are told that with a realistic date rather than matched to a generalist, which is the failure mode a small market produces by default.

process.title: Agree the format to the calendar
process.description: Continuous weekly teaching for a Diploma student with internal deadlines ahead, or a defined block for an IGCSE candidate with a specific weakness and a series approaching. The two qualifications want different shapes of support and buying the wrong shape is the commonest error here.

process.title: Review on marked work
process.description: At the end of the first half-term, compare marked timed work with where the student started, question by question. That is the check that distinguishes a plan worth extending from one worth stopping, and it is the review almost nobody runs because stopping is rarely planned for in advance.

whyPoints.description: The schools, the regulator, the commute and the supply picture on this page are Ajman's. Most pages ranking for this phrase carry Dubai assumptions inside sentences that read as general advice, and that advice does not transfer to a villa in Al Rawda.

faqs.question: Why do tutor searches from Ajman return Dubai results?
faqs.answer: Because the pages that rank for these phrases were written for the largest market in the country and list Dubai communities, Dubai schools and Dubai's regulator. The advice inside them assumes a market where specialists live within a short drive, which is true in an emirate whose private schools served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 and is not true in Ajman. The information is not dishonest; it simply does not transfer to a Northern Emirates address.

faqs.question: Is there really no Higher Level specialist in Ajman?
faqs.answer: For some courses, genuinely none available in the evenings, and the reason is arithmetic rather than anything about the emirate. A teacher who can fill four evenings a week with one Higher Level course will specialise in it; one who can fill a single evening will teach whatever is asked and stay a generalist. Divide a small Diploma cohort across six subjects, two levels and many option combinations and the per-course demand within driving distance is a few students a year.

faqs.question: Does an Ajman family pay less for tutoring than a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: For in-home visits, slightly less, because local visiting tutors in the Northern Emirates charge below those serving central Dubai; published bands run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour across the country. For online lessons, exactly the same, because delivery cost does not vary with distance. That second fact is the useful one: it means an Al Rawda family can buy from the same specialist pool as a Dubai family at the same published band.

faqs.question: Which regulator applies if our children attend schools in two emirates?
faqs.answer: Both. Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A child bussed into Sharjah is in a system regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee queries and complaints follow whichever body regulates that school.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to addresses in Al Rawda?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram provides only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Both IB and IGCSE lessons for Al Rawda families run live over video, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time. The page targets the near-me phrase because it is what parents type, and the honest answer is that in a thin local market the thing worth having is the specialist, and reaching them means dropping the distance requirement rather than compromising on the teaching.

faqs.question: Should a student here choose IGCSE and A Levels or the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student and on what their intended university expects, which should be checked with that institution. Operationally, the Diploma carries internal components worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of each subject grade with deadlines spread across two years, so it needs continuous well-timed support. IGCSE is almost entirely terminal and tolerates concentrated support late. In a household with limited hours, that difference matters more than any general claim about rigour.

faqs.question: Which qualification is easier to support in a small market?
faqs.answer: IGCSE, clearly. Local supply for the common IGCSE subjects exists in every Ajman community because every school enters large numbers of candidates. Diploma Higher Level support is the thinnest part of the local market in almost every subject. That is precisely why Diploma families here gain the most from an online arrangement, and why an IGCSE family can reasonably consider a local tutor for mathematics or biology if the hour suits.

faqs.question: What are the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: The published clarification sets out five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor page tells UAE parents six subjects are required, which the published rule does not say. Verify current requirements with the Ministry directly.

faqs.question: Is there a published equivalency figure for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not in the material we were able to verify. The published clarification we worked from sets out the British and American tracks and states no International Baccalaureate points threshold, which means any specific figure quoted on a tutoring page is unsourced. Check it with the Ministry of Education or the relevant attestation authority, and with the specific university, rather than relying on a tutoring provider. We neither perform nor guarantee any part of the equivalency process.

faqs.question: Do tutors in the UAE need a licence, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private lessons needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Are Ajman tuition centres worth considering?
faqs.answer: For broad content coverage early in an IGCSE course, a well-run group class can be good value, and Ajman has centres. What a smaller market supports less often is deep per-syllabus streaming, so a group may contain students on different boards and tiers moving at one pace. Eight weeks before a series, with a specific weakness identified from a mock script, one-to-one hours aimed at exactly that weakness do more per dirham than a general group course.

faqs.question: How do we judge a tutor we will never meet in person?
faqs.answer: On five questions, asked in four minutes. Which papers does my child sit and how long is each? What is the weighting between components? Where do candidates in this syllabus lose marks and how do you teach that? Which paper or series would you start from and why? What will you refuse to do with assessed coursework? The texture of the answers separates a specialist from a generalist, and the fifth should produce a clear refusal.

faqs.question: Does the growth of Dubai's school market affect families here?
faqs.answer: Indirectly and over time. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened the previous year and enrolment rose by six per cent. A market expanding that quickly draws experienced teachers towards it, which tends to widen rather than narrow the supply gap between emirates. It is another reason the useful search key for a family here is the course rather than the postcode.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for our subject this term?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic estimate of when a slot may open and an alternative evening if one exists. For a Higher Level option topic in a thinly taught subject at a popular hour, the honest answer in a given term is sometimes no. Being matched with a generalist instead costs six weeks and teaches the content without the assessment craft the grade turns on. No competitor page in this segment discloses a coverage limit; this one does.

intro.heading: Start with the invoice, not the brochure
paragraphs: A parent in Al Yasmeen typing "IB IGCSE tutor near me" into a phone is rarely curious about pedagogy. They have a Year 10 report in front of them, a grade that slipped, and a rough idea that this is going to cost money. The honest first answer is a number. Private tutoring across the UAE is advertised between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour, and the spread is not random: it tracks who is teaching, whether they travel, and whether they have ever marked the paper your child will sit.

Al Yasmeen sits in the newer residential belt of Ajman, inland from the Corniche and close to Al Mowaihat and Al Rawda. The practical consequence for tutoring is simple. The number of people within a short drive who have taught Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Paper 6 or IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is small. A parent searching locally is not choosing between specialists; they are choosing between whoever is close. That is the first place money gets wasted, and no amount of negotiation fixes it.

Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight rather than an emirate-level authority, which matters when you are comparing what you read about Dubai with what applies at home. The MoE supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Dubai's KHDA, Abu Dhabi's ADEK and the Sharjah Private Education Authority each run their own inspection and fee regimes, so a rate quoted in a Dubai article is not a rate set by anything that governs your child's school.

The second cost that goes unexamined is travel. Market figures for an in-home one-to-one visit in the UAE run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour inclusive of the tutor getting there, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is not a quality premium. It is fuel, Emirates Road at six in the evening, and a tutor who can fit three sessions into a day instead of five. You are paying for a car journey and receiving no extra teaching.

IB Gram's answer is to spend the difference on the teacher instead. Lessons for Al Yasmeen students are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own past-paper scripts on screen, and a recording they can replay before a mock. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. What a family here gains is a subject specialist chosen from the whole pool rather than from a twenty-minute radius of Al Yasmeen.

The rest of this page is a cost argument with the numbers shown. It sets out the market bands and where each came from, the four places tutoring budgets leak, how online, in-home and group formats compare per useful minute of teaching, and what the exam calendar does to the price of a late start. Every AED figure below is a market rate published by somebody else, cited as such, not a price list of ours.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-yasme.programmesIntro: Al Yasmeen households commonly run two curricula at once, with an older child on IGCSE and a younger one in a middle-years programme. These are the three programmes this page covers, with what each costs in tutoring hours rather than in abstract description.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and converts those criterion totals into a 1-7 grade. Parents find it opaque because there is no percentage anywhere. Tutoring here is cheap relative to Diploma work because the content load is lighter, but it is where the habit of writing to a criterion descriptor is built, and that habit is what decides Diploma grades two years later.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the MYP is the smaller of the two middle-years routes; most Al Yasmeen families are in a British-stream Year 9 or 10 instead. Where a child is in MYP, the live question is usually whether to carry on to the Diploma or move to IGCSE and A-Levels, and that choice changes which subjects are worth funding tutoring for now.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Edexcel runs a single tier with its own paper structure. Tutoring cost concentrates in Year 11 term two, when families buy hours for three or four subjects at once and the monthly figure triples without anybody planning it.
programmes.countryNote: Al Yasmeen students mostly sit Cambridge papers through their school as an internal candidate, which means the school handles entries and the zone timetable. Families who move mid-year, or who add a subject the school does not teach, become private candidates and pick up the entry fee themselves. That is worth knowing before you budget a tutoring block around an extra subject.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an internally assessed component. The Diploma is the most expensive programme to support because the work is spread across two years and three of the six subjects usually need help at different times, not the same time.
programmes.countryNote: There is no IB Diploma school in every Ajman neighbourhood, so Al Yasmeen Diploma students often travel to Sharjah or Dubai for school and arrive home late. Tutoring slots after 19:00 Gulf Standard Time are the ones that actually work, and a specialist who is physically elsewhere in the world can hold that slot more reliably than one driving across three emirates.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-yasme.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject is not uniform. The subjects below are the ones Al Yasmeen families most often buy hours for, with a note on what the marks are actually awarded for, because a tutor who does not know that is the most expensive kind.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry this course. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-question investigative paper worth a fifth of the grade that rewards students who can follow an unfamiliar structure. Marks are lost in method lines that are never written down, so the calculator cannot be the first thing a student reaches for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. It is not the easy option; the Higher Level paper expects confident graphical reasoning and matrix work. Students who chose it to avoid proof often find the modelling questions harder to start, because there is no single expected route and partial credit depends on stating assumptions.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Extended / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended runs two papers; Pearson 4MA1 splits across two equally weighted papers with a calculator throughout. Most lost marks sit in a narrow band: bearings, compound interest, histograms with unequal class widths, and surds. Six well-chosen past-paper sessions usually move more grade than a term of generic revision.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Extended, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways are where grades are made. Cambridge 0620 Paper 6 is the alternative-to-practical paper and is marked on experimental reasoning, not recall, which is why students who revise notes alone stall at a grade 6. The IB course adds data analysis under the same umbrella.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Extended, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest grade spread. Cambridge 0625 expects circuit reasoning in words as well as numbers, and the six-mark extended responses are marked against distinct points rather than general accuracy. Unit conversion errors cost more marks across a paper than any single topic gap.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.levels: IGCSE Extended, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem, not the difficulty. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance are the recurring weak points, and the command terms decide the mark: describe, explain and suggest want different answers. Diagram labelling and data-table interpretation are worth practising against real mark schemes.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language and English Language
subjects.description: Reading comprehension is scored on precision of retrieval; directed writing is scored on register and audience. Students in Ajman who speak excellent conversational English still lose marks for summary tasks that exceed the word count or paraphrase too loosely. This is a technique subject, and it responds quickly to tutoring.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.levels: IGCSE Extended, IB HL and SL
subjects.description: Both subjects reward applied answers tied to the case material rather than textbook definitions. IB Economics at Higher Level carries a quantitative paper that surprises students who chose it as an essay subject. The internal assessment asks for commentary on real published articles, which needs a method, not inspiration.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic alongside its licensed curriculum, and the grade still appears on the report. For non-Arab students the gap is usually script fluency and verb patterns rather than vocabulary. Short, frequent sessions work far better here than a long weekend block.

sections.heading: What an hour of tutoring in Al Yasmeen actually costs
paragraphs: Market rates for IB and IGCSE tutoring in the UAE run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor. The band that most Al Yasmeen families end up in is AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to AED 450 or above once you specify IB Diploma or IGCSE specialism. Those are published figures from providers advertising to UAE parents, not an IB Gram price list.

Reading them monthly is more useful than reading them hourly, because nobody buys one hour. A single weekly sixty-minute session at the mid band works out at roughly AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month on Bestimate's own estimates, with the budget end around AED 240 to AED 600 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more. Packaged offers in the market sit in the same territory: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four in-home double sessions.

The jump from the second row to the third row of the table below is the one worth staring at. It is almost entirely travel. An in-home one-to-one visit in the UAE is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour including the journey, and the teaching inside that hour is not different teaching. For a family in Al Yasmeen, where the pool of nearby subject specialists is genuinely thin, that premium buys proximity to a smaller choice.

Two figures are missing from almost every competitor page and both are free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted at no charge for two years, so a tutor quoting a licensing cost is adding something that does not exist. And no fine schedule for unlicensed tutoring has been published, so any page quoting a specific penalty figure is guessing.

sections.heading: The four places an Al Yasmeen tutoring budget leaks
paragraphs: Waste in tutoring is rarely the hourly rate. It is hours bought for the wrong thing, and it follows a pattern across Ajman households that is predictable enough to list. The first leak is the generalist hired for a specialist paper. A capable maths graduate can teach the content of Cambridge 0580 Extended; teaching a student how Paper 4 awards method marks when the final answer is wrong is a different skill, and a family paying AED 200 an hour for the first while needing the second is paying full price for half the job.

The second leak is group tuition bought as if it were one-to-one. A group of four at AED 100 a head looks like a saving against AED 250 alone. Inside a sixty-minute group session a given student gets a share of the teacher's attention measured in single-digit minutes, and the content is pitched at whoever is in the middle. For a child who is behind in one specific topic, that is a cheaper hour and a more expensive term.

The third leak is the late start. Families who begin tutoring in the final weeks before a written paper pay the exam-year specialist band and buy the least improvable time. The same money spread across the preceding two terms buys the same number of hours at a lower band and in a period where content can still be relearned rather than patched. Starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11 term two is the single largest cost saving available to an IGCSE family.

The fourth leak is the unbooked cancellation. In-home arrangements across Ajman routinely lose sessions to traffic, late school transport and a tutor stuck on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. Those hours are often still paid for, and they are hours of nothing. Online delivery removes the failure mode entirely, which is a cost argument before it is a convenience one.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tutoring compared on cost per useful minute
paragraphs: The comparison most pages make is price against price. The comparison that decides outcomes is price against teaching minutes actually received by your child. A sixty-minute one-to-one online session with a specialist delivers close to sixty minutes of directed teaching, with the student's own marked script on screen and the whiteboard saved at the end. There is no setup, no settling, and no part of the hour spent on the tutor arriving.

An in-home session in Al Yasmeen begins when the tutor reaches the door, which depends on the Ajman-Sharjah road and on whether the previous family overran. Families report the first ten minutes going to arrival, tea and finding the exercise book. The teaching inside the hour is the same teaching, bought at a premium of roughly AED 50 to AED 200 an hour over the online equivalent, and delivered by whoever was available within driving distance rather than by the person who knows the paper.

Group tuition changes the arithmetic again. At four students, each child's share of individual attention is a quarter of the session at best, and in practice less, because the pace is set by the group. That is fine for breadth revision in the weeks before a paper and poor for a specific gap. The honest use of group teaching is as a supplement to one-to-one work, not a replacement for it, and the cost comparison should be made on that basis.

For Al Yasmeen specifically, one more factor loads the comparison. The local pool of IB Diploma and IGCSE specialists within a twenty-minute drive is small. Choosing in-home delivery here does not mean paying more for the same teacher; it means paying more and choosing from a shorter list. That is why IB Gram delivers to Ajman over live video and spends the travel premium on the specialist instead.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and who regulates the tutor
paragraphs: Ajman's private schools, along with those in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. That is a different arrangement from the three emirates parents read about most. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge.

The distinction is not academic. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the emirate authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits locally. For Al Yasmeen families whose children attend school in Ajman, the relevant published guidance comes from the Ministry rather than from a KHDA circular, and a Dubai inspection framework does not describe their school.

Tutor regulation is federal and applies identically in Al Yasmeen and in Dubai Marina. Private tuition in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

Two things follow for a parent checking value. Ask whether the tutor holds the permit, because it costs nothing and there is no reason not to have it. And treat any claim of regulator endorsement with suspicion: a permit for an individual tutor is not an institutional approval, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a separate licence issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds no regulator endorsement and does not claim one.

sections.heading: The five-subject rule that decides which IGCSE subjects are worth funding
paragraphs: If the family plan includes a UAE university, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules change which subjects deserve tutoring money. For the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Those are the published requirements, clarified in July 2026 reporting on the Ministry's position.

The detail that reshapes a budget is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A family funding tutoring in Arabic for equivalency reasons is funding it for school-report reasons instead, which is a legitimate purpose but a different one. One competitor page tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and planning around the wrong number buys hours nobody needed.

For the American track the shape is different again: English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold should be taken from a tutoring website, including this one. Check it on the Ministry's own channel or with the school's IB coordinator, because an unsourced number here is a number a family would act on.

Equivalency is also not something a tutor performs. It is an administrative process run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authorities, and no amount of tutoring is required to complete it. What tutoring can do is make sure the five subjects a student is counting on actually clear the grade floor, which is a narrower and much cheaper objective than general improvement.

sections.heading: What a late start costs, counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate in Al Yasmeen sits June, with November as the resit lane. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. IB Diploma candidates in the UAE sit the May session.

Cost follows that calendar closely. A family that begins work three terms out buys standard-band hours across a long period and can afford one subject at a time. A family that begins six weeks out buys exam-year specialist hours for three subjects at once, which is where the AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 plus monthly figures come from. The hourly rate did not change; the number of hours needed in a short window did.

There is also an administrative trap that costs money rather than marks. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a private candidate that is a wasted entry fee and a wasted term of tutoring, so the zone should be confirmed with the centre rather than assumed.

Results timing shapes the resit decision. Pearson's November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. A family planning a resit should count backwards from the entry deadline, not from the exam, and link the live official timetable rather than trust a restated date.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA or coursework
paragraphs: This is the part of the market where money buys the most damage. One provider found in the UAE search results sells completed IB Internal Assessments outright. Under IB academic honesty rules, submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the website that took the payment. No family should spend money on that, at any price, and no tutor should offer it.

The legitimate version is well defined and it is cheaper. A tutor explains what each assessment criterion rewards, letter by letter, and what the marks within it are awarded for. The tutor reads what the student has written and says where it falls short of the descriptor. The tutor teaches the method: how to narrow a research question, how to structure a mathematical exploration, how to present data honestly. The student writes every word that is submitted.

In practice that means feedback with the criterion named. A comment such as "this does not yet meet the descriptor for personal engagement, because the chosen context is generic" is teaching. A rewritten paragraph handed back is not, and no amount of framing changes that. A tutor will not draft, complete or edit to completion an IB internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or an IGCSE coursework component.

The same boundary applies to past papers and syllabus documents. IB, Cambridge and Pearson materials are copyright, and a tutor should reference and link them rather than distribute copies. Al Yasmeen families are better served by a tutor who shows the student how to find the official document and read a mark scheme than by one who arrives with a folder of photocopies.
