sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies on top of the main curriculum
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed international curriculum. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects occupy real timetable space, and they appear on the report your child brings home.

The published requirements are specific enough to plan around. In Dubai, KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

For an Al Yasmeen family the tutoring consequence is about priority, not volume. These subjects do not count toward the five-subject equivalency total, so they are not where a university plan is won or lost. They do count toward the school report, promotion decisions and the child's own sense of whether they are coping. A short weekly session in Arabic as an additional language, focused on script and verb patterns, costs far less than letting the subject become the one the child dreads.

One constraint is worth knowing before buying material. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. A tutor should therefore work from what the school teaches, not from an imported syllabus, and should be able to say which textbook and scheme of work the sessions follow.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the board and the paper
process.description: Not "maths help" but "Cambridge 0580 Extended, Paper 4, loses method marks". The more precisely the request is framed, the shorter the match takes and the fewer hours get spent on diagnosis you have already done yourself. A recent marked script is worth more than any description.

process.title: See the match and the rate before you commit
process.description: You get the tutor's board and level experience, the papers they have taught, and the rate in AED per sixty-minute session in writing. Nothing is booked until you have both. If the honest answer is that no specialist is currently free for that subject, you are told that rather than offered a near-miss.

process.title: Take the trial lesson at no charge
process.description: One trial session per subject, with no card required and no obligation to continue. The point is diagnostic: the tutor works through a real question with your child and tells you what the actual gap is. If the match is wrong, say so and the next one is arranged.

process.title: Fix the slot around the Al Yasmeen school run
process.description: Sessions are booked in Gulf Standard Time at a repeating weekly slot, usually from 17:30 onwards for Ajman-based schools and later for students travelling back from Sharjah or Dubai. Timings shift during Ramadan to post-Iftar slots on request.

process.title: Review the spend every six sessions
process.description: After six sessions there is enough evidence to decide whether to continue, change subject or stop. That review is the control on cost. It is also when a block for an exam term should be set with an end date, so the monthly figure does not quietly become permanent.

whyPoints.description: The constraint on tutoring in Ajman is not price, it is choice. Al Zorah and Al Yasmeen have very few Diploma Higher Level specialists within twenty minutes. Remote delivery removes distance from the selection entirely, which is the one change that improves the teaching rather than the invoice.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reads drafts and gives criterion-referenced feedback. A tutor does not produce assessed work. That boundary is stated on the page because the alternative is sold openly in this search market, and a family should be able to see where a provider stands before the first conversation.

faqs.question: How much should an IB or IGCSE tutor cost for a family in Al Yasmeen?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for premium named tutors. Most Al Yasmeen families land between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor, rising to AED 200 to AED 450 or more once IB Diploma or IGCSE specialism is specified. Monthly, a single weekly session sits roughly between AED 600 and AED 1,200 at the mid band. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list; ask any tutor for their rate in AED per sixty minutes in writing.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor in Ajman worth the extra money over online lessons?
faqs.answer: On the published numbers, the in-home premium is roughly AED 50 to AED 200 an hour and it buys the journey, not better teaching. For an Al Yasmeen household there is a second cost: the choice narrows to tutors willing to drive there, which in practice excludes most Diploma Higher Level and IGCSE Extended specialists. Younger children who need physical supervision are the genuine exception. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, and delivers one-to-one lessons over live video instead, spending the travel premium on the subject match.

faqs.question: Which Ajman schools do Al Yasmeen students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Families in Al Yasmeen commonly name Ajman Academy, Pace British School Ajman, Our Own English High School Ajman, Habitat School Ajman, Woodlem Park School Ajman and Ajman Modern School. A sizeable group travels south instead, to schools in Sharjah such as Victoria International School of Sharjah, Delhi Private School Sharjah or Wesgreen International School. Programme offerings and boards change between academic years, so confirm the current curriculum with the school before planning tutoring around a particular syllabus. Schools are listed here as local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with my child in Ajman need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule has been published. Since the permit costs nothing, there is no good reason for a tutor not to hold one, and it is a fair question to ask.

faqs.question: Why is tutoring more expensive if we start six weeks before the exam?
faqs.answer: Because the number of hours needed in a short window rises, not because the hourly rate changes. Starting three terms before the June series lets a family buy standard-band hours for one subject at a time, around AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month. Starting six weeks out usually means two or three subjects at once in the exam-year specialist band, which is where monthly figures of AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more come from. The cheapest version of good tutoring is the early version, and in Al Yasmeen that means Year 10 rather than Year 11 term two.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Al Yasmeen actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page quoting it for a UAE student. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. IB Diploma students in the UAE sit the May session. Checkpoint tests for younger years are held in March, May and October. Always confirm the exact window against the official live timetable, because provisional timetables are revised before each series.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable problem and can it cost us money?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. For a private candidate in Ajman that means a lost entry fee on top of a lost paper, and a term of tutoring with nothing to show. Confirm the zone with the exam centre directly rather than reading a timetable found by search.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IB Internal Assessment without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor explains what each assessment criterion rewards and how many marks sit behind it, teaches the method for narrowing a research question or handling data, reads what the student has written, and says where the draft falls short of the descriptor. The student writes everything that is submitted. A tutor will not draft, rewrite or complete any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. Work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Published Ministry of Education requirements for the British track ask for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student also needs one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor page states six IGCSE subjects are required; the published figure is five. Verify the current rule through Ministry channels before making a subject decision on it.

faqs.question: Why do evening tutoring slots in Al Yasmeen start so late?
faqs.answer: Because a large share of households here work or school in Sharjah and Dubai. A child attending school in Ajman is usually home in time for a 17:30 start, but one travelling back from Sharjah or Dubai often is not free until 19:00 or later, and a parent who wants to be present arrives later still. Online delivery is what makes those slots usable at all, since a tutor does not have to be in the car at the same time. Ramadan timings shift to post-Iftar sessions on request.

faqs.question: Is group tutoring a real saving for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the problem is. A group of four at AED 80 to AED 120 a head looks cheap against AED 250 one-to-one, but each student receives roughly a quarter of the session at best and the pace is pitched to the middle of the group. For a child with a specific gap, such as electrolysis in Cambridge 0620 or histograms in 0580, that is a cheaper hour and a more expensive term. Group work earns its place as breadth revision close to a paper, alongside one-to-one sessions rather than instead of them.

faqs.question: Who oversees the private schools an Al Yasmeen family chooses from, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, as are those in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Dubai has KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. The practical effect is that Dubai inspection reports and KHDA circulars describe a different regime from your child's school. Tutor regulation, by contrast, is federal and identical across emirates, so the MoHRE permit question applies in Al Yasmeen exactly as it does in Dubai.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject an Al Yasmeen family needs?
faqs.answer: You are told, rather than offered a near-miss at the same rate. Thin coverage is real in narrow combinations such as IB Higher Level Further Mathematics or a minority second language, and placing a general tutor against a specialist paper is the most common way tutoring money gets wasted. Where no specialist is free immediately, the options are to wait for a named slot, to start with an adjacent subject that is covered, or to be given nothing until the right match exists. A free trial lesson is the test of whether the match is genuine.

faqs.question: How do we keep the monthly tutoring bill from creeping upwards?
faqs.answer: Two mechanisms do most of the work. First, review after every six sessions and decide explicitly whether to continue, change subject or stop; spend grows by default, not by decision. Second, buy any exam-term intensive as a block with a written end date, because that is the format that turns AED 600 a month into AED 2,000 without anybody choosing it. Sequencing subjects by paper date rather than by whichever report looked worst also prevents the Year 11 pattern of funding four subjects at thin coverage simultaneously.

faqs.question: Does the published AED rate include VAT or any extra charges?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask in writing. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees depends on the provider's circumstances and is not something a tutoring page should state as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation. What a parent can reasonably require is a single figure in AED per sixty-minute session, confirmation of whether that figure is inclusive, and a clear statement of what happens to a cancelled or missed session. Online delivery removes travel and material surcharges, which are the two extras most often added to in-home arrangements in Ajman.

intro.heading: The search says 'near me'. The real question is 'who knows this syllabus'
paragraphs: Type an IB IGCSE tutor near me query into a phone in Al Zorah and the results are mostly Dubai agencies with a radius setting switched on. Al Zorah is a low-density waterfront community on the northern edge of Ajman, built around mangrove creeks, lagoons and a golf course rather than around schools. There is no secondary school inside the development. Every family here already drives for the school run, and the same arithmetic that makes a 7:15am drop-off normal makes a 4:30pm tutor visit expensive in a currency parents rarely price: time.

The question behind the search is not really about distance. It is whether anyone reachable can actually teach this syllabus. Those are two different questions with two different answers. A graduate who lives in Al Nuaimiya and tutors general maths is nearby. A teacher who has worked through Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Paper 4 mark schemes, or taught IB Chemistry HL to the current syllabus, belongs to a far smaller group, and in the Northern Emirates that group is thin. Distance is easy to measure, which is why search engines sort by it. Syllabus fit is what moves a grade.

IB Gram answers the question by removing the radius. Tuition for families in Al Zorah is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and prayer times. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative, implying a tutor will appear at an Al Zorah villa, would be a promise nobody here could keep.

What replaces proximity is choice. Instead of the three or four people who can reach Al Zorah before traffic builds on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, a family picks from whoever teaches that subject at that level, wherever they are. For an Economics HL student in Grade 12, or a Year 11 candidate sitting Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended, that difference is the entire point of booking at all. A tutor eight minutes closer who has never seen the paper is not a better match; they are a more convenient one, and convenience is not what a grade responds to. The radius was never the thing standing between the student and the marks.

This page covers what a parent actually has to decide: what the Ajman market charges and why in-home rates sit higher, which regulator oversees Al Zorah's schools and what that means, how the Cambridge and Pearson calendars run backwards from the June and November series, what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment, and what the Ministry of Education needs to see for equivalency. Figures are attributed to whoever published them. Where a date is not verified, this page says so rather than guessing.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-zorah.programmesIntro: Al Zorah households split across two systems, and often inside one family: an older child on the IB Diploma at an Ajman continuum school, a younger one sitting Cambridge or Pearson IGCSEs. Here is what each stage demands, and what it demands specifically of a family living this far north.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around six transdisciplinary themes rather than subject periods, and it is assessed by teacher judgement rather than by papers. That makes a parent's usual signal, the test score, mostly unavailable. Tutoring at this stage is about fluency in the mechanics: number bonds, written methods, reading stamina and the habit of explaining an answer in a sentence.
programmes.countryNote: Al Zorah's primary-age children are usually driven to Ajman city or into Sharjah, which turns a 3:00pm finish into a 3:45pm arrival home. A 30-minute online session at 5:00pm, twice a week, fits that pattern far better than an hour-long visit nobody can schedule reliably.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marking runs on four criteria per subject, each scored out of 8, and the criteria reward process as much as the final answer. Students who have been rewarded for neat right answers suddenly lose marks for not showing a pattern, a justification or a reflection. The fix is reading the criterion strands and writing to them deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 11 is the year Al Zorah families most often start looking, because the choice between Diploma and IGCSE arrives at the same time as the first serious internal assessments. A specialist who has taught both routes can describe the difference honestly instead of selling one of them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, and those components have internal school deadlines that sit a long way before the exam window. The Diploma punishes drift more than it punishes weakness.
programmes.countryNote: There is no Diploma school inside Al Zorah, so the cohort a student belongs to is small and the subject teacher may be the only person in the emirate teaching that option. Online one-to-one is frequently the only way to get a second experienced voice on an HL paper.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is sat as separate subject qualifications, each with its own syllabus code and paper structure. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 has Foundation and Higher tiers. Knowing which code and which tier a child is entered for changes what practice is useful.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Zorah teenagers sit IGCSEs at a school in Ajman or Sharjah, and the two emirates are regulated by different bodies, so entry administration and term dates do not always align with the family's expectations. Ask the exams officer for the code and tier in writing before booking any tuition.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-zorah.subjectsIntro: The IB Diploma subjects below are the ones Northern Emirates students most often book, with the specific places marks go missing. Nothing here is a general promise about teaching quality; it is what the paper actually asks for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA rewards algebraic fluency and proof. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and far harder calculus. Marks are lost on Paper 1, the no-calculator paper, where students who can operate a GDC cannot manipulate surds or factorise a cubic by hand. The repair is timed non-calculator drilling, not more theory.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is modelling and statistics led, and the GDC is central rather than incidental. Students lose marks by reporting a regression output without interpreting the context, or by rounding mid-calculation. HL AI adds graph theory and matrices, which many schools teach late in Grade 12 under time pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The reliable losses sit in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, and in data-based questions where a student states a trend without naming the underlying cause. HL extends into transition metals and spectroscopic identification. Paper work has to be paired with reading the command term: state, describe, explain and deduce want different amounts of writing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics marks go on unit errors, on graph work where gradients are read rather than calculated, and on explanation questions answered with equations instead of sentences. HL adds rigid-body and quantum content that arrives when coursework deadlines are also arriving. Practice has to be against mark schemes, not against answers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology looks learnable and then punishes imprecision: a process named but not sequenced, a diagram labelled but not explained. The database and statistics questions catch students who have never calculated a standard deviation by hand. HL adds plant and animal physiology depth that rewards disciplined vocabulary.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry a large share of the marks and most students draw them without labelling the axes, the shift or the new equilibrium. HL adds quantitative questions and the theory-of-the-firm style calculation. The internal assessment commentaries need real, recent news articles and a word count that is respected to the letter.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks come from applying a tool to the specific case, not from describing the tool. A SWOT reproduced from memory scores little; one built from the case stimulus scores well. HL extends into operations and the pre-released case study, which rewards early, structured reading rather than last-week cramming.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Paper 1 guided analysis is where unprepared students write a summary instead of an argument about how the text works. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and two extracts that genuinely support it. HL adds the essay, which needs a line of argument rather than a tour of the novel.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: The Diploma language B papers assess reading comprehension, writing to a specified text type and a spoken component. Students who speak Arabic at home often lose marks on register and on text-type conventions rather than on vocabulary. Arabic A sits alongside the Ministry's own requirements for Arab students.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-zorah.igcseSubjectsIntro: For the Year 10 and Year 11 side of an Al Zorah household, the same honesty applies: the code and the tier decide what practice is worth doing.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge Core caps at grade C, Extended runs to A*. The most common wasted term is a student sitting Extended practice while entered for Core, or the reverse. Extended Paper 4 rewards method marks, so working has to be written out even when the answer is obvious.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the heaviest losses. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's entry, and the two demand different preparation: one tests handling apparatus, the other tests reading somebody else's experiment.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the recurring wall. Students who can balance equations still lose marks converting between mass, moles and volume under time pressure. Organic chemistry at Extended level needs the homologous series learned as patterns rather than as lists.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: The long-answer questions reward sequence and precision: naming a process is a mark, ordering its stages is the rest. Extended adds genetics problems where a Punnett square has to be drawn correctly rather than reasoned about verbally.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: The writing papers are assessed on content and language separately, and the task type is prescriptive. A strong writer who ignores the register of a report or an email loses content marks that fluency cannot recover. Listening practice has to be done at exam speed.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper. The common pattern is a student who knows the definitions and cannot use the business in the stimulus, which caps answers at the lowest band regardless of how much theory is produced.

sections.heading: What a 'near me' search actually returns in Al Zorah
paragraphs: A near-me search sorts by distance and then by whoever has paid to appear. Neither of those signals tells a parent whether the person on the other end has taught the syllabus. In Al Zorah the gap between the two is unusually wide, because the community was built as a resort and residential destination on Ajman's northern coast rather than as a school catchment, and almost nobody who teaches for a living lives inside it.

What the results tend to contain is three categories. First, Dubai and Sharjah agencies whose service area is drawn generously and whose tutors would be travelling 45 minutes each way in the evening. Second, individual tutors in the denser Ajman districts, often strong, often teaching across a wide range of levels, and rarely able to name the paper structure of the specific qualification your child is entered for. Third, international platforms that never mention the UAE at all, quote in dollars, and route enquiries to a number outside the country.

None of those is dishonest in itself. The problem is that a parent cannot tell them apart from a listing. The questions that separate them are specific: which syllabus code did you last teach, which papers did your students sit, which topics did that cohort lose marks on, and do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutor who answers those four quickly is worth more than one who is eight minutes closer.

This page is written to be checkable rather than persuasive. Every rate below is attributed to whoever published it, with the month it was read. Every regulatory statement links back to a federal or emirate source. Where a date has not been verified from the awarding body itself, that is said out loud.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus code and the paper numbers, in writing, before the first lesson.
Ask when the tutor last taught that exact qualification, not whether they can.
Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit.
Ask what happens in week three if the match is wrong.

sections.heading: How thin the local specialist pool really is
paragraphs: This is the part nobody in the SERP publishes, because it does not read as marketing. The supply of tutors in the Northern Emirates is heavily weighted towards widely taught subjects at the most common levels. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is taught in almost every private school in Ajman and Sharjah, so somebody competent is usually reachable. IB Chemistry at Higher Level, or Economics HL with its internal assessment commentaries, is taught by a handful of teachers in the whole emirate, and several of them are contractually barred from tutoring their own school's students.

That last point is worth stating clearly. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars the same thing. Reported as press coverage rather than quoted from the policy document, but the direction is consistent: the nearest qualified teacher is frequently the one person who cannot take the work.

Removing the radius changes the shape of the problem. A student in Al Zorah sitting Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL does not need the nearest maths teacher; they need somebody who has taught Paper 1 without a calculator to students who went on to score well, and who can diagnose in forty minutes whether the issue is algebraic fluency, exam timing or topic gaps. That person exists. They are unlikely to live in Ajman.

sections.heading: What families around Al Zorah pay, and what the drive adds
paragraphs: Start with the part of a quote that is not teaching. An in-home rate contains the tutor's travel, and in a community like Al Zorah the travel is real: a tutor based in Ajman city adds 30 to 50 minutes of round trip, one based in Sharjah closer to 90 minutes in the evening. That time is billed, either openly as a travel supplement or quietly as a higher hourly rate. The published bands make the pattern visible once you line them up.

The figures below were read in October 2026 from the providers named. They are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. Budget online tuition in the UAE starts around AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by the Bestimate rate survey, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring is quoted at AED 270 by TutorChase and AED 200 to 450 and above by Bestimate, and a premium named tutor at BartyED is published at AED 650.

Monthly packages are where the comparison becomes concrete for a household budget. Online packages of eight sessions a month have been advertised at AED 799. In-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions sit at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A family comparing AED 799 against AED 1,699 is, to a large extent, comparing a classroom against a car.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, and the reason is not coyness. The right rate depends on level, subject scarcity and how many weeks are left before the series, and a single number would be wrong for most readers. What is published is the market context above, so a parent can judge any quote, including ours, against something.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor at the door
paragraphs: This comparison deserves to be made properly rather than waved away, because in-home tuition has genuine advantages. A tutor in the room can see a child's body language, can take a book out of their hands, and cannot be muted. For a young or easily distracted student, that physical presence is worth paying for. Any page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising.

What it costs, in Al Zorah specifically, is reach and reliability. The pool of tutors willing to drive to a northern coastal community on a weekday evening is small, and it shrinks further once you require a particular syllabus at a particular level. A cancelled visit is a cancelled week, because there is no second person to call. And the session has to start after the drive, which in practice means 6:30pm or later for a tutor coming from Sharjah.

Online one-to-one trades presence for selection. The student gets the subject specialist rather than the nearest available teacher, the session can start at 4:45pm because nobody is in traffic, past papers can be annotated live on a shared screen and kept, and a replacement tutor is a scheduling question rather than a geographic one. For Diploma and IGCSE work, where most of the lesson is a paper, a pen and a mark scheme, the shared screen is arguably better than a kitchen table.

IB Gram offers the online format only in the UAE. In-home visits are an India-only service and no page on this site will tell an Al Zorah parent otherwise. The table sets out the trade honestly, including the places where the in-home option wins.

sections.heading: Who regulates Al Zorah's schools, and why it is not KHDA
paragraphs: Parents moving to Ajman from Dubai routinely look for a KHDA inspection report for an Ajman school and cannot find one, because KHDA's remit stops at the Dubai border. Al Zorah's schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which, in the words of the UAE government's own portal, plays a supervisory role for private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is a different inspection regime, a different publication habit and a different set of documents to ask for.

The practical consequence is that a parent in Al Zorah has to ask the school directly for its most recent inspection outcome rather than expecting to download it. If a child crosses into Sharjah for school, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates that school and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate authority.

None of this makes IB Gram a regulated education provider in the UAE, and this page does not suggest it. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, and any page claiming otherwise should be treated with suspicion. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; an individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Those are two different things and neither is a badge a matching platform can wear.
What a parent can reasonably verify is the tutor's permit position and the school's own inspection outcome. Both are questions the people involved should be able to answer in a sentence.

sections.heading: The exam calendar for an Al Zorah candidate, counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market names an exam series at all, which is strange, because the series is the only fixed point in the year. Everything else, the mocks, the coursework deadlines, the decision about whether to book tuition, is derived from it. Counting backwards is the only sensible way to plan.

For Cambridge, the two relevant series are June and November, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge's February/March series is offered in India only, so an Ajman candidate who reads an India-facing revision guide is reading the wrong calendar. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone; the board says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams run in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series, which is precisely why a page like this links the live official timetable instead of restating dates that can still be revised.

IB dates are deliberately absent. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the board itself. What can be said safely is that UAE schools sit the May session and that the November session exists as an alternative route. Any specific IB date should come from the school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and it should be checked rather than inherited from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch: the academic-honesty line
paragraphs: The IB Diploma is roughly a quarter internally assessed, which makes coursework the most commercially attractive and the most dangerous thing in this market. One page found in the research for this project sells completed Internal Assessments outright at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice, and the student, not the seller, carries the consequence, which can run as far as losing the Diploma.

The honest boundary is not complicated. A tutor may teach the underlying subject content, explain the assessment criteria and what each descriptor band actually asks for, discuss and narrow a research question, review a method for feasibility and ethics, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, a TOK essay or any assessed coursework, and must not supply text for the student to paste.

There is a second boundary that matters almost as much. No tutor may reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. The correct behaviour is to reference the official source and link to it, which is why this page carries no attachments. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

The third is honesty about outcomes. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any page that offers one is either misunderstanding how boundaries are set or hoping you do not ask. What tuition can reliably change is the quality and the quantity of deliberate practice, the student's grasp of what the command terms demand, and the gap between what they know and what they get onto the page.
bullets: Teaching the criteria, the command terms and the subject content: appropriate.
Feedback on a draft the student wrote, in writing, against the descriptors: appropriate.
Producing text, diagrams or data for the student to submit: never.
Supplying past papers or mark schemes as files: no; the official source is linked instead.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency for Al Zorah's IB and IGCSE leavers
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that turns an international school certificate into a document UAE universities and employers recognise, and it catches families late because schools talk about university offers rather than about attestation. It is worth understanding in Grade 10, not in the summer after Grade 12.

For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth knowing precisely, because a competitor page ranking for these queries currently tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required.

For the American track, English proficiency is met by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB, no points threshold is published here, because the source used for the British and American tracks does not state one, and an unverified figure on a page like this would be a liability rather than a help. Confirm the IB position on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tuition is not a requirement for it. What tuition can do is make sure the five subjects a student is counting on are actually passed at the grade the rule requires, which is a narrower and more useful claim.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB or IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every family on an international curriculum in the UAE also carries a set of mandatory national subjects, and they are the ones that get squeezed when Diploma coursework arrives. They are not optional extras. At federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule every emirate's version sits on top of.

The Dubai regulator publishes the most detailed version, and it is instructive even for an Ajman family because it shows how the requirement is structured. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary the lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

There is a constraint on tutoring here that nobody mentions. For the mandatory national subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor supporting Arabic as a first language or Islamic Education works within the prescribed material rather than importing their own, and Dubai schools must ensure that teachers of these subjects hold the relevant approval from the regulator to teach them. Support for these subjects should therefore be arranged carefully, with the school's own scheme of work in hand.

In practice the most common request from Northern Emirates families is Arabic as an additional language, where the issue is usually reading fluency and script confidence rather than grammar, and the most common mistake is leaving it until the year the grade starts to matter.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is specific: the syllabus code, the tier or level, the school and the series the child is working towards. Cambridge 0620 Extended in Ajman is a different request from Pearson 4CH1 in Sharjah, and the difference decides which tutors are worth proposing at all.

process.title: A diagnostic lesson, free of charge, with no card required
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. The tutor works through questions from the real paper to find out where marks are actually going: recall, method, command-term reading or timing. The family gets a written summary afterwards naming the first three targets, and no payment details are taken to get it.

process.title: A slot that survives the drive home from school
process.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time around the Al Zorah school run, not against it. For most families that means 4:45pm at the earliest and often 6:30pm or later when a parent commutes to Sharjah or Dubai. The slot is fixed weekly so the student stops negotiating it.

process.title: Weekly notes and a target, in writing
process.description: After each lesson the tutor records what was covered, what the student got wrong and why, and what the next session will attack. Progress is measured against the school's own assessment calendar, so a parent can see whether the work is landing before the next report arrives.

process.title: Change the tutor if the match is wrong
process.description: A tutoring match can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with competence. Say so early and a different tutor takes over with the notes already written, which is the one thing a geographic match cannot offer: in Al Zorah, a tutor who does not fit is often the only one who could reach you.

whyPoints.title: Selection instead of proximity
whyPoints.description: The constraint in the Northern Emirates is not willingness, it is the number of people who have taught a specific syllabus at a specific level. Teaching online over live video replaces a 30-minute radius with a subject panel, which matters most for exactly the HL and Extended subjects where a local option rarely exists.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can audit
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are attributed to the providers that published them and dated to the month they were read. That is deliberately different from the norm in this market, where three of six researched competitors publish no price at all and two quote in dollars.

whyPoints.description: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: yes. Producing any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay: never. The boundary is published because the alternative, found openly in this market, puts a student's Diploma at risk.

What is offered instead is a verifiable permit position for tutors and a clear account of what each regulator actually does.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for an Ajman evening
whyPoints.description: A large share of Ajman households work in Dubai or Sharjah, so evening schedules run later here than in Abu Dhabi. Slots are set accordingly, and lessons can move to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan rather than being quietly dropped for a month.

whyPoints.title: Honest coverage, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free for a niche subject at the level required, that is said rather than papered over with a generalist. The coverage table on this page exists so that a family can see the limit before paying for anything.

faqs.question: Is there really an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Al Zorah, or is that a Dubai agency with a map pin?
faqs.answer: Usually the second. Al Zorah has no school inside the community and very few resident teachers, so a near-me result is normally an agency in Dubai or Sharjah with a generous service area, or a generalist tutor in a denser Ajman district. Both can be fine. Neither tells you whether the person has taught the syllabus your child sits. IB Gram does not place a tutor at an Al Zorah address at all; lessons run one-to-one over live video, which is what lets a family choose by syllabus rather than by driving distance.

faqs.question: How much should an online IB tutor in Al Zorah cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Read against the market rather than against a single quote. In October 2026, budget online tuition in the UAE was advertised from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE rates were AED 270 at TutorChase and AED 200 to 450 and above in the Bestimate survey. A Diploma Higher Level subject with coursework support will sit at the upper end of that spread, not the lower.

faqs.question: Why would an in-home tutor quote more for Al Zorah than for Ajman city?
faqs.answer: Because the quote contains the journey. A tutor based in Ajman city adds roughly 30 to 50 minutes of round trip to reach the northern coast; one coming from Sharjah adds closer to 90 minutes in evening traffic. That time is billed either as an explicit travel supplement or as a higher hourly rate. The published bands show the gap: in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online.

faqs.question: Which schools do Al Zorah families actually use for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The practical catchment is the Ajman city cluster, 15 to 25 minutes inland depending on the hour, with Ajman Academy the best-known continuum school in the emirate. A meaningful number of families instead drive south into Sharjah, to schools such as Victoria International School of Sharjah, or as far as Deira. Students we support attend schools in both groups. No affiliation is implied by naming them, and any school name should be checked against the regulator's own listing before it affects a decision.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a MoHRE permit if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Ask the tutor directly.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my Year 11 child in Al Zorah sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, June or November. The February/March series is offered in India only, so an Ajman candidate following an India-facing revision calendar is working to the wrong dates. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams run in May/June and November. Ask the exams officer for the zone and the confirmed entry, in writing.

faqs.question: How much coursework help can an Al Zorah student accept before it becomes malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth stating precisely. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain each assessment criterion and what its descriptors actually demand, help narrow a research question, review a method for feasibility, and give written feedback on a draft the student has already written. A tutor must never write, redraft or complete the assessment, nor supply text to paste in. Work sold as a finished Internal Assessment is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start in Al Zorah on a school day?
faqs.answer: Most Al Zorah families land on 4:45pm at the earliest, because the school run comes in from Ajman city or Sharjah and the drive home absorbs the gap between the bell and the start of homework. Where a parent commutes to Dubai, 6:30pm or later is more realistic, and in Emirates City an 8:00pm start is common. Because lessons run online, no travel time has to be added to that. The slot is then fixed weekly so the student stops renegotiating it each week.

faqs.question: Which regulator inspects private schools in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government's portal describes as playing a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA regulates Dubai, ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge covers that emirate. This matters practically: an Al Zorah parent looking for a KHDA report on an Ajman school will not find one and should request the school's latest inspection outcome directly instead.

faqs.question: Is it five or six IGCSE subjects for UAE equivalency, and does Arabic count?
faqs.answer: Five. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. That precision matters, because a competitor page currently ranking for these queries states that six IGCSE subjects are needed. Confirm your own case with the Ministry or your emirate's attestation channel.

faqs.question: My child sits Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 - can the tutoring match the exact paper?
faqs.answer: That is the point of asking for the code. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core, which caps at grade C, and Extended, which runs to A*, and they sit different papers. A term spent on Extended practice by a Core candidate is a wasted term, and the reverse is worse. Confirm the tier with the exams officer in writing, then the work can be built around the specific papers entered, with Extended Paper 4 practice marked against the published scheme so method marks are not left on the table.

faqs.question: Does online one-to-one work for a student who has only ever had classroom teaching?
faqs.answer: For Diploma and IGCSE work it usually transfers well, because most of a useful session is a paper, a pen and a mark scheme on a shared screen, annotated live and kept afterwards. What changes is the student's share of the talking: in a class of 24 they can stay quiet, and in a one-to-one session they cannot. Younger or easily distracted students benefit more from a tutor physically in the room, and that is a fair reason to choose an in-home option instead.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's subject at the level we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, rather than handed a generalist. The honest position in the Northern Emirates is that supply is weighted towards widely taught subjects at common levels, and a rare Higher Level option or a minority language may have no specialist free in the window you need. Where that happens, the options are a later start date, a different format such as a short paper-focused block, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. Concealing a coverage gap costs a family a term, which is worse than losing an enquiry.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan for a family in Al Zorah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the practical arguments for an online format. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful study window moves to after Iftar, which is exactly the time an in-home tutor is least likely to be driving to the northern coast. Sessions can be rescheduled for the month and then returned to the usual slot, or held at the same frequency with shorter sessions. Set it before the month starts rather than cancelling week by week.

faqs.question: Do you cover Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB or IGCSE timetable?
faqs.answer: Arabic support is one of the most common Northern Emirates requests, usually for Arabic as an additional language where reading fluency and script confidence are the real issue. There is a constraint to respect: for the mandatory national subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so a tutor works within the school's prescribed material rather than importing their own. Dubai schools must also ensure teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education hold the regulator's approval for those subjects.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-zorah.closingBody: If your child is in Al Zorah and the honest problem is that nobody nearby teaches their syllabus, the first useful step is small: a free diagnostic lesson on the real paper, with a written summary of where the marks are actually going. Tell us the syllabus code, the tier or level, the school and the series being worked towards, and you will be matched with a subject specialist rather than with whoever is closest. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the drive home. If the match is wrong, say so in week two and it changes.

intro.heading: Pricing tuition like a household expense, not a rescue
paragraphs: A tuition decision taken in a panic costs roughly twice a tuition decision taken in October. That is the practical reason to look at the numbers early, and it is the reason this page leads with money rather than with pedagogy. Families in Emirates City are mostly in apartments, mostly with a parent commuting out of the emirate, and mostly paying school fees that already dominate the education line of the budget. Tuition has to fit next to that, not replace the thinking about it.

The published market spread is wide enough to confuse anyone. Budget online providers advertise from the mid forties per hour. Specialist exam-year tutors are quoted in the hundreds. A premium named tutor reaches AED 650. The spread is real, and it reflects genuinely different services, but it also hides a simpler truth: most of the variation in what a family eventually pays comes from how many hours they buy and how late they start, not from the hourly rate they negotiated.

So this page does the arithmetic the other way round. It starts from a monthly figure, works back to hours, and shows what each tier of the market publishes. It then lists the four ways money gets wasted in this market, because avoiding one of them saves more than shaving AED 30 off an hourly rate ever will.

The second half of the page handles the IB and IGCSE difference, which is where quotes stop being comparable. An IGCSE Extended hour and a Diploma Programme Higher Level hour are different products. Internal Assessment supervision is different again, and it is the component where the gap between legitimate support and malpractice is narrowest. All of that affects price, and a provider who quotes a single flat rate across the whole range has not thought about it.

There is also a question of what a household is buying at each tier. At the bottom of the published range sits a university student working through a syllabus they sat themselves three years ago, which is genuinely useful for a Year 8 catch-up and thin cover for a Diploma Higher Level paper. In the middle sits a qualified subject teacher who has taught the specification to a full cohort and knows the grade boundaries from experience. At the top sits scarcity: a tutor with a track record in one narrow component, priced because very few people can do that particular job. Deciding which of those three your child needs is a larger saving than any discount.

One structural note before the numbers. IB Gram is a matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service offered in India only, so no part of what follows includes a tutor arriving at a tower in Emirates City. That removes the travel premium from the equation entirely, which is itself a cost argument.

ajman/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-emirates.programmesIntro: Emirates City households often run two curricula at once, with one child on a British track and another in the IB. Here is what each programme implies for the tuition bill.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, graded 9-1 or A*-G, with a Core or Extended tier in most Cambridge subjects and Foundation or Higher in Pearson maths. The tier decision is a cost decision as well as an academic one: a Core entry caps the grade at C, and families who later want that door reopened pay for a rushed Extended conversion.
programmes.countryNote: Across Ajman and Sharjah both boards are in use, sometimes within one school. Published rates for IGCSE support sit lower than Diploma rates: Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour against IB from AED 200. Budget to the specification rather than to the word IGCSE, because a 0580 Extended hour is not the same work as a Year 9 catch-up hour.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across eight subject groups, with no external papers in most schools until the Diploma. Parents often misread a criterion score as a percentage and buy tuition they do not need, or miss a genuine gap because the report reads positively. Understanding the criteria is usually worth one session before committing to a term.
programmes.countryNote: MYP support is the cheapest intervention in the whole IB chain and the one families most often skip. A student who reaches Diploma Year 1 without algebraic fluency or lab-report discipline needs several times as many paid hours to repair it. Two years of a single weekly MYP session costs less than one panicked Diploma spring.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level hours are the most expensive in the market because the pool of tutors who have taught a specific HL subject to the grade boundaries is genuinely small. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words and the TOK essay to 1,600, and supervision of both is priced as its own block.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. The two-year total matters more than the hourly rate here: one HL subject at one session a week across both Diploma years is around 70 hours, so a AED 50 difference in the rate is a AED 3,500 difference in the plan. That is the figure worth negotiating, not the single lesson.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / IB DP)

subjects.description: Case-study application and evaluation marks are the recoverable ones. A short, well-targeted block of four to six sessions moves a grade here more reliably than a year of general support.

subjects.description: The Individual Oral and Paper 1 guided analysis are the components students under-rehearse. Priced in the mid band, and usually the subject where fewest total hours are needed if the work starts early.

sections.heading: What the word near costs you here
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor near Emirates City narrows the field to whoever lives within a reasonable drive and happens to be free at an evening hour. That constraint has a price, and it is paid twice. Once in the rate, because an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour and the upper part of that range reflects a car, fuel and forty minutes each way in the evening peak. Once in quality, because the specialist in the subject your child is failing may live in Abu Dhabi.

The teaching time is identical either way. Sixty minutes with a tutor on a screen and sixty minutes with a tutor on a dining chair contain the same sixty minutes of explanation. What differs is the travel premium, the cancellation risk, and the size of the pool you are choosing from. For a tower cluster on the edge of Ajman, the pool is the binding constraint.

There is one genuine benefit to presence worth stating honestly: a younger or very reluctant student may need an adult physically in the room to start work at all. For that child, in-home tuition does something online cannot, and a family should pay for it if that is the problem being solved. For a Year 10 or Diploma student who can already sit down with a laptop, it is a premium spent on logistics.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, so this is not a sales preference dressed as advice. Home visits are an India-only service. The reason to put the comparison on the page is that no competing page in this market publishes the in-home premium at all, which leaves parents paying for travel without ever seeing it itemised.

sections.heading: A year of tuition as a budget line
paragraphs: Convert the hourly rate into a monthly commitment before comparing anything. One session a week is four a month, allowing for a term break. Two sessions a week is eight. At the published band for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 150 to 300 an hour, one weekly hour lands between AED 600 and AED 1,200 a month, and Bestimate's Dubai table gives the same shape: AED 240 to 600 for budget tutors, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Then extend it across the period that matters. A single IGCSE subject supported from October of Year 11 to the June series is roughly eight months. A Diploma Higher Level subject supported across both years is closer to twenty months of term time. The second figure is the one that shocks families, and it is also the one where the hourly rate compounds: AED 50 an hour of difference across seventy sessions is AED 3,500.

Monthly packages advertised in this market give another reference point. Online blocks of eight sessions are offered around AED 799 a month, and in-home arrangements of four two-hour sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Those are the packages competing pages publish, read in October 2026; they are included here as market context rather than as an IB Gram offer.

sections.heading: The four places the money goes nowhere
paragraphs: The first is paying for content the student already holds. A tutor who begins by reteaching a topic from the start of the syllabus, rather than marking a recent paper to find where the method marks are vanishing, burns four to six hours before anything moves. Insist that the first session works from a marked script. If a tutor has no interest in seeing one, that is information.

The second is group tuition bought for a problem groups cannot fix. A centre class gives pace and practice volume at a lower price per hour, which is good value for a confident student. For a child who is two topics behind, it is the wrong instrument: the class cannot stop, so the gap persists while the invoice continues. Families often buy group sessions first because they are cheaper, then buy one-to-one anyway.

The third is the travel premium paid for a convenience the household does not actually need. A Diploma student who studies at a desk with headphones gains nothing from a tutor in the room, and the in-home rate carries between AED 30 and AED 150 of travel load depending on distance and timing. Across a year that is a second subject's worth of support.

The fourth is the late start. The same grade movement costs roughly twice as much in March as it does in October, because the same work has to be done in fewer weeks with more sessions and higher-priced specialist availability. Of every cost lever a family controls, the calendar is the strongest, and it is free to pull.

sections.heading: Why an IB hour and an IGCSE hour are not the same purchase
paragraphs: Published rates separate the two, and the reason is supply rather than prestige. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. The pool of tutors who have taught Cambridge 0580 Extended is large across the Gulf; the pool who have taken a student through Diploma Higher Level Chemistry, including the scientific investigation and the grade boundaries that follow, is small. Scarcity sets the price.

The structure of the work differs too. An IGCSE campaign is mostly syllabus coverage plus timed practice against a mark scheme, and it ends on a fixed day. A Diploma campaign runs across two years and carries components that sit outside the papers: the Internal Assessment in each subject, the Extended Essay at 4,000 words, and the TOK essay at 1,600 words with its exhibition. Those have internal school deadlines rather than board exam dates, and they cluster in Diploma Year 1 and the first half of Year 2.

That clustering is the budget trap families in two-curriculum households fall into. A Year 11 sibling needs hours in the spring; a Diploma Year 1 sibling needs hours in the same spring for an exploration deadline. Mapping both calendars in September is the cheapest planning anybody can do, and it usually reveals that one of the two campaigns can start earlier at a lower intensity.

On the Internal Assessment specifically, the price covers teaching and feedback and nothing else. A tutor explains the criteria, discusses method, reads a draft the student has written and says which paragraph does not meet the criterion. Nobody writes, completes or supplies the work. A provider offering a finished Internal Assessment at a price is selling a malpractice case, and one page in this market does exactly that.

sections.heading: Hidden extras: the six questions to ask before paying
paragraphs: Two quotes that look identical at AED 200 an hour can differ by a third once the terms are read. Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and what a lesson is: a 45-minute session billed as an hour is a 33 per cent increase that never appears in a comparison. Ask whether marking between sessions is included, because a tutor who marks a full paper outside the hour is doing unpaid work that eventually gets priced in or quietly dropped.

Ask about cancellation on both sides. A family that loses a paid session for a school event has lost money; a family whose tutor cancels twice a month has lost a plan. Ask what happens to a prepaid block if the match does not work in week two, and get the answer before paying for twelve weeks. Ask whether any VAT the provider charges is included in the figure quoted, and leave the broader tax question to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to a tutoring page.

Ask about the report. A short written note after each session is normal and costs nothing; a formal monthly report sometimes carries a fee. And ask what the rate becomes in the eight weeks before the exam series, because specialist availability tightens then and some providers price that period differently.

None of these are difficult questions. The reason they are worth writing down is that they are the ones families remember not asking. A provider who answers all six without hesitating is telling you something useful about how the service is run.

sections.heading: Deciding with marks instead of feelings
paragraphs: The decision about how many hours to buy should be made from marked work. Take the most recent full paper or test, and look at where the marks were lost rather than at the total. Three patterns justify different spending. Scattered single marks across every question usually mean technique: command words, working shown, units. That is cheap to fix and responds to a short block.

Whole questions left blank or abandoned halfway mean missing content, which is the expensive pattern because it needs reteaching before practice helps. One or two topics consistently failing while the rest holds is the best case: a targeted block of four to six sessions on those topics often moves a grade, and then the spending stops.

Review at six weeks on the same evidence. If the pattern of loss has not changed, something in the plan is wrong, and the answer is rarely more hours at the same thing. It is a different approach or a different tutor. A family that reviews on marked papers spends less over a year than a family that reviews on how the sessions feel, because feelings lag the mark scheme by about two months.

The last thing worth costing is the end. A good plan has a point at which it stops. Writing down what the exit looks like, a grade, a topic list cleared, a paper completed in time, prevents a weekly charge becoming a permanent household subscription that nobody re-examines.
