faqs.question: What should I budget each month for an IB or IGCSE tutor near Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Work from four sessions a month. At the published band for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 150 to 300 an hour, one weekly hour is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Bestimate's Dubai table gives AED 240 to 600 for budget tutors and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and northern-emirate rates sit at or just below Dubai levels. Diploma Higher Level hours price at the upper end because the specialist pool is small. Those are market figures from published pages read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; ours follow the free trial.

faqs.question: Why is Diploma tutoring priced higher than IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Supply, mostly. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, and the gap reflects how many tutors have actually taught each thing. Cambridge 0580 Extended is taught in hundreds of Gulf schools; Diploma Higher Level Chemistry with the scientific investigation and its grade boundaries is taught by far fewer people. The work differs too: a Diploma campaign runs across two years and includes the Internal Assessment, the 4,000-word Extended Essay and the 1,600-word TOK essay, all with internal school deadlines rather than exam dates.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to hire a tutor who lives near Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Usually not, once travel is counted. In-home one-to-one visits in the UAE are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the upper part of that range prices a car, fuel and forty minutes each way in the evening peak. The teaching time is identical to an online hour. What a local tutor adds is physical presence, which genuinely helps a younger or very reluctant child and adds little for a Year 10 or Diploma student who already works at a desk. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; that service runs in India only.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do most families here start with?
faqs.answer: One, and that is usually right. A single weekly hour held across the year is the cheapest pattern that actually moves a grade, because continuity catches a drift early. Two sessions a week makes sense for one subject that is badly behind, run for eight to twelve weeks rather than a year, with one session on content and one on timed questions. Families who start with two hours across three subjects almost always cut back by December, having paid for the lesson. Decide from a marked paper rather than from a general sense that things are slipping.

faqs.question: What are the hidden extras that change a quote?
faqs.answer: Six things. Whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson is, since 45 minutes billed as an hour is a third more than it looks. Whether marking between sessions is inside the rate. The cancellation terms on both sides. What happens to a prepaid block if the match fails in week two. Whether any VAT the provider charges is included in the figure. And whether the rate changes in the weeks before an exam series, when specialist availability tightens. A provider who answers all six without pausing is usually the better-run one.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates go up closer to the exams?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens and some providers price the pre-series weeks differently, so ask directly. The bigger effect is on your side of the ledger: the same grade movement bought in March costs roughly twice what it costs in October, because the work has to be compressed into fewer weeks at a higher session count. Of every cost lever a family controls, starting a term earlier is the strongest and the only free one. If you are already inside the final eight weeks, buy a defined block with a stated end date rather than an open monthly arrangement.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects to save money?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. A single tutor can reasonably cover maths and physics at IGCSE, or economics and business studies, and a two-subject arrangement saves a parent one relationship to manage rather than money on the rate. What does not work is stretching one tutor across the separate sciences at Diploma Higher Level, where each subject is its own specialism and a generalist costs more in wasted hours than a second specialist would in fees. Ask which specifications the tutor has actually taught before combining subjects.

faqs.question: Is a free trial really free, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: One session, no charge, and no card details taken beforehand. The condition worth stating is simply that it is one session per subject, not an open run of free lessons. Use it as a test rather than a demonstration: the tutor should work from your child's own marked paper and finish by naming two or three specific errors and what the first month would address. If the hour is spent on introductions and study-skills talk, the paid hours will be spent the same way and you have learned that at no cost.

faqs.question: How do I compare two providers when neither publishes a price?
faqs.answer: Make them quote a plan rather than an hour. Ask each for the total for the same brief: one named subject, one weekly hour, from now to the exam series, including marking. Then ask the six terms questions, about lesson length, marking, cancellation, prepaid blocks, VAT and pre-exam pricing. Three of the six pages examined in this market publish no figure at all and two quote in US dollars, so a direct rate comparison is often impossible. Plan totals with stated terms are comparable; vague hourly claims are not.

faqs.question: What does Internal Assessment or Extended Essay support cost, and what does it include?
faqs.answer: It is usually sold as a block of four to six sessions tied to milestones rather than as a monthly charge, which at mid-band rates is roughly AED 1,200 to 2,700. What it includes is teaching the skill the task assesses, explaining each assessment criterion, reading a draft the student has written and saying which section does not meet the criterion, and setting a timetable so the work does not land in one weekend. What it never includes is writing, completing, rewriting or supplying the piece. A provider selling a finished Internal Assessment is selling the student a malpractice case.

faqs.question: Do we pay for a session the school cancels with a sports day or a trip?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the terms, which is why the cancellation question belongs before the first payment rather than after the first clash. A reasonable arrangement gives both sides a notice period and allows a reschedule inside the same week. Because our tutor pool is not geographic, rescheduling an online session is usually straightforward: there is no travel to re-plan. An in-home arrangement is harder, since a replacement has to live nearby as well as teach the subject, which is one of the quieter costs of buying local.

faqs.question: Which subjects give the best return for the money in Year 11?
faqs.answer: The ones where marks are being lost to technique rather than to missing content. Business Studies and Economics respond quickly because evaluation and diagram marks are learnable in a short block. English reading tasks respond well for the same reason. Maths and the separate sciences take longer when whole topics are missing, because reteaching has to precede practice. Look at a marked paper: scattered single marks across many questions means a cheap fix, while abandoned whole questions means a longer and more expensive campaign. Spend where the pattern says the marks are recoverable.

faqs.question: Is the permit a tutor needs an extra cost added to our bill in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The tutor needs one; it costs you nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists the application with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. u.ae also states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts, so treat any figure you see online as unverified.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: When the thing you wrote down at the start has happened. A plan without a stated exit becomes a household subscription nobody revisits, and that is the most common way families overspend on tutoring. Define the end in advance: a grade on a school assessment, a topic list cleared, a full paper completed inside the time limit. Review on marked work at six weeks and again at twelve. If the pattern of lost marks has moved and the target is met, stop, and keep the option of a short block before the next series instead of a rolling monthly commitment.

ajman/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach MYP mathematics rather than general secondary maths: they mark against the four published criteria, know how a school converts criterion levels into a 1 to 7 grade, and can tell you which of the four is costing your child marks after reading one piece of work.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for when you buy MYP maths help in Ajman
paragraphs: Ajman is the cheapest emirate in the UAE to live in and one of the more expensive to buy specialist tutoring in, and both facts have the same cause. The private-school population is small, the pool of teachers trained in the IB Middle Years Programme is smaller still, and a large share of the families who want MYP maths support have children enrolled across the border in Sharjah or Dubai. A tutor who can mark criterion B properly is therefore a scarce commodity locally, and scarcity is priced.

That is the honest starting point for any conversation about cost. A parent ringing round Al Nuaimiya and Al Rashidiya will be quoted anything between AED 50 and AED 400 for what is described, in all cases, as maths tutoring. The quotes are not describing the same service. At the bottom of the range you are usually buying homework supervision from an undergraduate who has never seen an MYP criterion descriptor. Near the top you are buying a teacher who has marked MYP 5 work, knows what a level 7 in criterion D looks like against a level 5, and can work backwards from your child's report to the specific skill that is missing.

The second thing a quote hides is travel. A tutor driving from Sharjah to Al Jurf at five in the afternoon spends forty minutes in the car each way, and that time is in your hourly rate whether or not it is itemised. Published UAE figures bear this out: market in-home rates sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for the same calibre of teacher working online. You are paying a premium of roughly a third for a physical presence in the room.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and the Dubai commute. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature. It means an Ajman family in Al Yasmeen can work with a teacher who has taught MYP extended mathematics for a decade rather than whichever tutor is willing to drive up Emirates Road, and it means the travel third of the market rate does not appear in the price.

The rest of this page is built around the number. It sets out the published AED bands and who published them, the five local factors that move a quote up or down, how MYP mathematics is actually assessed so you can judge whether a tutor understands it, and what a term of weekly work looks like. There is no IB Gram price list here, because the right figure depends on the year group, the criterion in trouble and how many weeks remain. The free trial lesson exists so that conversation happens after someone has looked at your child's work.

ajman/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.programmesIntro: An Ajman MYP family is usually three or four years from the Diploma and one or two from the extended-versus-standard decision in MYP 5. These are the three IB programmes that bracket that window, with what each means for a household in this emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of concept-led study across eight subject groups, with mathematics assessed continuously against four published criteria rather than by a single end-of-year paper. Each criterion is marked out of eight and the school sets the boundaries that convert those levels into a 1 to 7 grade, which is why two Ajman schools can report different grades for identical work. MYP 5 splits mathematics into standard and extended routes, and some schools enter students for on-screen eAssessment.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's MYP provision is concentrated in a small number of schools, with Ajman Academy the best-known IB continuum option in the emirate. Many Ajman-resident MYP students actually attend IB schools in Sharjah or Dubai, which means the family is managing a cross-emirate commute as well as a curriculum. Private schools in Ajman sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so inspection reporting and mandatory-subject requirements follow the national framework.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two final years of six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Mathematics divides into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each available at both levels. The route a student can realistically take is largely decided by how far they got in MYP mathematics, which is why an MYP 4 grade matters more than it looks.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman families weighing the Diploma usually compare it against A Levels at a British-curriculum school in Sharjah, and the maths question decides it as often as the subject spread does. A student who finished MYP on the standard route and then chooses Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is taking on a very steep first term. Getting that call right in MYP 5 is cheaper than paying for remediation in the first DP year.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, finishing with the Exhibition in the final year. Mathematics is taught through units of inquiry rather than as a separate timetabled subject in the early years, which means arithmetic fluency varies widely between PYP leavers. The gap usually shows up in MYP 1 and MYP 2 as slow written method rather than weak understanding.
programmes.countryNote: The PYP-to-MYP transition is where most Ajman maths requests actually originate, even when the parent describes the problem as MYP underachievement. A child who arrives in MYP 1 without secure times tables and fraction work will lose criterion A marks for arithmetic rather than for the concept being tested. Six to ten weeks of targeted number work at this stage is markedly cheaper than the same intervention in MYP 4.

ajman/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP mathematics is organised into four branches that recur every year at increasing depth, rather than a list of discrete topics. These are the clusters an Ajman tutor is asked for most often, with what each actually tests and the point at which marks start leaking.

subjects.name: Number and operations
subjects.description: Integers, fractions, decimals, percentages, ratio, standard form, surds and index laws. The branch that quietly decides criterion A scores, because a student who is slow with fraction arithmetic runs out of time before the conceptual part of a question. Most MYP 1 and MYP 2 requests in Ajman are really number-fluency requests.

subjects.name: Algebra and equations
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, linear and simultaneous equations, inequalities, quadratics and rearranging formulae. Errors here are procedural rather than conceptual: a sign dropped during expansion, a denominator lost when clearing fractions. Marks are recovered faster in algebra than in any other branch, which is why it is where a first block of sessions usually goes.

subjects.name: Sequences, patterns and generalisation
subjects.description: Finding a rule, justifying it and then proving or testing it on new cases. This is the spine of criterion B, Investigating patterns, and the branch where the written justification earns more than the answer does. Students who can find the rule but cannot explain why it holds cap themselves at the middle bands.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry and graphs
subjects.description: Gradient, intercepts, parallel and perpendicular lines, distance and midpoint, plotting and interpreting non-linear graphs. The branch that bridges algebra and geometry, and the one that shows up in criterion D tasks because real-world data arrives as a graph. Axis labelling and scale choice are marked, not decoration.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, congruence and similarity, circle properties, Pythagoras, right-angled trigonometry and, on the extended route, the sine and cosine rules. Reasoning has to be written out: an unjustified angle is an unmarked angle. This is the branch where extended and standard diverge most visibly in MYP 5.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, box plots, scatter graphs and correlation, plus tree diagrams and conditional probability higher up. Heavily used in criterion D because a real-life context usually arrives as a dataset. Students lose marks for describing a correlation without commenting on its limits.

subjects.name: Functions and modelling
subjects.description: Function notation, domain and range, transformations of graphs, and fitting a model to data. The clearest preview of Diploma mathematics, and the branch that best predicts whether Analysis and Approaches is realistic. Weakness here rarely appears on a report card; it appears in the first DP term instead.

subjects.name: Discrete and extended-only topics
subjects.description: Logarithms, further indices, more demanding algebraic fractions, vectors in two dimensions and additional trigonometric work depending on the school's scheme. These are the topics that make the extended route feel like a different subject. A student moved onto extended mid-year usually needs a dedicated block on them.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside the Personal Project
subjects.description: Data handling, costing, scaling and statistical presentation used in service of a project in another domain. Mathematical quality is not separately graded, but weak numbers undermine the product and the report. Support here is process coaching and feedback only; the work and the writing must be the student's own throughout.

These are the areas we are asked about most, with the operational detail behind each.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense, central and close to the Sharjah boundary, so in-home tutors quote it as a short run and price accordingly. Households here often have both parents commuting to Dubai, which pushes workable session times to 6.30pm or later on weekdays.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Older established neighbourhoods near the Corniche with a mix of villas and flats. Reasonable in-home access from Sharjah, but an afternoon return along Al Ittihad Street adds a surcharge in practice. Online sessions commonly run at 4.30pm here, straight after the school bus.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Industrial and residential mix inland, with a long run from any Sharjah or Dubai tutor base. This is where travel loading on an in-home quote is most visible, and where families most often conclude that live video gives them the specialist instead of the driver.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Fast-growing villa districts popular with families whose children attend school in Sharjah. The school day finishes late once the bus route is counted, so a 5.30pm or 7pm slot works better than the standard 4pm. Weekend morning blocks are common for criterion-task work.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: Residential and well served by the Ajman ring roads, with a shorter effective commute to Sharjah schools than its distance suggests. Families here frequently run two children in the same household on alternating slots, which is simpler to arrange online than with a visiting tutor.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen
regions.note: Newer villa communities on the Ajman side of the Sharjah boundary, with limited local tutoring supply and almost no MYP-specific provision. Specialist requests from Al Yasmeen are the clearest case for remote one-to-one: the nearest MYP-trained maths teacher is usually not in the emirate.

regions.note: Developing residential district where most private-school families travel out of Ajman each morning. Evening sessions dominate and Friday mornings are heavily requested. In-home rates quoted here carry the longest drive of any Ajman area and the biggest implied travel charge.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Emirates City
regions.note: Apartment living along the waterfront and the towers inland, with a high proportion of short-term residents. Continuity matters more than price for these families, because a tutor who leaves mid-term costs a term. Remote delivery keeps the same teacher through a relocation.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman's own private schools
schoolClusters.note: A compact set of schools under federal Ministry of Education oversight, with IB provision concentrated in a small number of them and British-curriculum provision dominant. Students we support attend schools across this group; the mathematics requests skew towards MYP 4 and MYP 5, where the extended route and the Diploma decision arrive together.

The commute, not the curriculum, is what dictates when a weekday session can start for these households.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP Mathematics tutor in Ajman actually costs
paragraphs: Published UAE market rates for middle-years mathematics support run from about AED 45 an hour at the generalist end to AED 450 and above for an IB specialist, with in-home visits sitting at AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed into the hour. Those are market figures from the providers named below, not IB Gram's prices. MYP mathematics typically prices in the middle of that spread, below Diploma Higher Level work and above general Year 7 maths.

The reason MYP sits where it does is the marking. A general maths tutor can teach quadratics perfectly well and still cost your child criterion marks, because MYP mathematics is not assessed by a right answer. It is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and the communication and justification criteria reward things a conventional tutor never mentions. A tutor who has never read a criterion descriptor is cheaper for a reason, and the saving is real only if the problem is genuinely arithmetic.

The table below shows the bands with their sources. Treat the right-hand column as the useful one: it describes what each band buys for an MYP student specifically. The premium tier is included for completeness rather than as a recommendation, because at middle-years level there is rarely anything a AED 650 hour does that a well-matched specialist hour does not. We do not describe tutors as board examiners, since current examiner status is not something we can evidence.

What we will not do is publish an IB Gram rate card on this page. The honest figure depends on the year group, how many of the four criteria are in trouble, and whether you need a term of weekly work or four sessions before a deadline. The free trial lesson exists so that someone reads your child's marked work before a number is attached to it, and nothing is charged before that conversation happens.

sections.heading: Five things that move the Ajman number up or down
paragraphs: Two families in the same Ajman street can be quoted figures forty per cent apart for the same subject and year group, and the difference is almost always one of five variables. Knowing which ones apply to you is the fastest way to stop comparing quotes that are not comparable.

The first is travel, and in Ajman it is the big one. Specialist MYP teachers are concentrated in Dubai and Sharjah, so an in-home quote for Al Jurf or Al Helio is carrying a drive that an identical quote for Al Nuaimiya is not. The market gap between in-home and online bands, AED 180-500 against AED 150-300, is roughly the cost of that drive. Delivering over live video removes the variable entirely, which is why an Al Yasmeen family and an Ajman Corniche family pay the same.

The second is which criteria are in trouble. A student losing marks only in criterion A needs procedural fluency, which a competent generalist can supply. A student stalling in criterion B and criterion C needs someone who can teach mathematical justification and written communication, and that is a narrower skill set with a higher price. The third is session length: a 90-minute slot usually prices below two separate 45-minute slots, because set-up and review time is paid once rather than twice.

The fourth is timing in the school year. Availability is thinnest in the weeks before internal assessments and before the May examination period, and anything booked then costs more and offers less choice of teacher. The fifth is commitment shape. A standing weekly slot is the cheapest route to a grade change because the teacher is not re-diagnosing each week, while a four-session clinic around one deadline is cheaper in total but does not move a report card. Both are legitimate purchases; they are just not the same purchase.

sections.heading: MYP mathematics is marked against four criteria, not one score
paragraphs: This is the part most quotes assume you already know, and most parents reasonably do not. MYP mathematics has four assessment criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A task may address one criterion or several. The school then converts the pattern of criterion levels across the year into the 1 to 7 grade that appears on the report, using boundaries it sets itself.

That last point explains something Ajman parents ask constantly. Two children doing demonstrably similar work at two different schools can come home with different grades, because the conversion from criterion levels to a final grade is a school-level judgement rather than a fixed table. It also explains why a grade can fall without any single piece of work going badly: a student consistently reaching the middle bands in criterion C will drag the average even if criterion A is strong.

For tutoring, the practical consequence is that a diagnosis has to name a criterion. 'He is weak at maths' is not actionable. 'She reaches level 6 or 7 in knowing and understanding but level 3 in communicating, because she does not write the reasoning that justifies the steps' is actionable, and a first session with a marked piece of work in front of the teacher produces exactly that statement. Criterion C in particular is worth money, because it is the one where a confident mathematician loses marks for silence rather than for error.

The table sets out the four criteria, what each is called in the published guide and what a tutor can legitimately practise against it. The right-hand column is deliberately narrow: coaching method and reviewing a student's own drafting sits inside IB academic-honesty rules, and supplying content for an assessed task does not.

sections.heading: Where MYP maths marks leak between Year 7 and Year 11
paragraphs: The pattern in middle-years mathematics is remarkably consistent, and it is not the one most parents expect. Very few students are failing because the mathematics is too hard conceptually. They are losing marks in three repeating places: arithmetic that is slow rather than wrong, reasoning that is thought but not written, and context questions answered numerically without any interpretation.

In MYP 1 to MYP 3 the dominant loss is fluency. A student who computes with fractions hesitantly spends their working memory on the arithmetic and has nothing left for the structure of the question, so criterion A suffers even where the concept is understood. This is why so many Ajman requests that arrive labelled as an MYP problem turn out to be unfinished primary number work, and why six to ten weeks of drill plus method fixes more than a year of general revision does.

From MYP 3 onwards the losses shift to criterion C. Geometry is where this is most visible: an angle found correctly but without the reason named earns part of the available credit. Students who have been rewarded for right answers for years find it genuinely counter-intuitive that writing 'alternate angles, parallel lines' is worth marks. Changing that habit takes about four weeks of consistent correction on the student's own written work and holds afterwards.

In MYP 4 and MYP 5 the expensive loss is criterion D. A real-life task is set, the student calculates competently, and then stops. No comment on whether the model is reasonable, no mention of the assumption that makes it work, no sentence about what would break it. Those sentences are where the top bands live. The fix is a routine rather than a topic: every answer in a context gets one line on what it means and one line on what limits it.

sections.heading: Standard or extended mathematics in MYP 5, and the Diploma decision behind it
paragraphs: Somewhere in MYP 4 or at the start of MYP 5, a school will place your child on either standard or extended mathematics. In Ajman this frequently happens with minimal explanation to parents, and it is one of the few school decisions that has a direct financial consequence two years later.

The extended route covers the standard content plus additional material, which commonly includes logarithms, further index work, more demanding algebraic fractions, two-dimensional vectors and additional trigonometry depending on the school's scheme of work. It is not simply the same course taught faster. A student who finishes the standard route and then starts Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma begins with a genuine content gap as well as a pace gap, and closing it in the first DP term is both stressful and expensive.

This is where a clear-eyed view in MYP 5 saves money. If the ambition is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the extended route is close to a prerequisite in practice even where the school does not describe it as one. If the likely destination is Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, the standard route is perfectly adequate and pushing for extended may simply reduce the final MYP grade for no gain. The useful question to ask a tutor after a first session is not whether extended is better but whether your child's criterion B and criterion D work looks like a student who will enjoy Higher Level proof.

UAE universities matter here too, and the answer is less dramatic than it is often made to sound. Engineering and quantitative science admissions generally expect the Analysis and Approaches strand, while business, social science and health programmes commonly accept Applications and Interpretation. Check the specific programme page at the specific institution rather than any tutoring provider's summary, including this one, because entry requirements are revised and only the university's own page is current.

sections.heading: Ajman's schools and the federal Ministry of Education
paragraphs: Ajman does not have an emirate-level schools authority of the kind Dubai and Abu Dhabi operate. According to the UAE government's own guidance, the Ministry of Education plays a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi has the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge.

For a parent, the practical difference is where you look things up and who you escalate to. An Ajman school's inspection reporting and licensing sit within the federal framework rather than an emirate portal, so comparisons with a Dubai school's published rating are not strictly like for like. It also means the mandatory-subject requirements that apply across UAE private schools come from the national regulations rather than an emirate-specific circular. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the ministry's general regulations.

That matters for MYP families more than it sounds, because Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the IB programme rather than instead of parts of it. The timetable is therefore fuller than the IB subject list implies, and the week has less room in it than a parent planning three tutoring sessions might assume. One realistic weekly slot usually beats three aspirational ones.

None of this makes any tutoring provider an approved or licensed body. IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or relationship with the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation or any emirate authority, and any provider implying otherwise is worth questioning. What a parent can verify is the individual tutor's permit position, which the next section covers, and the quality of the marking, which the free trial lesson is there to show.

sections.heading: Scheduling an Ajman session around the Dubai commute and Ramadan
paragraphs: Scheduling is the quiet reason tutoring arrangements fail in this emirate. A large share of Ajman households have at least one parent working in Dubai or Sharjah and at least one child attending school outside Ajman, which means the family's real availability window is much narrower than the school day suggests.

Work backwards from the bus. A child at a Sharjah or Dubai school who boards at 6.30am is frequently not home before 4pm, and a child in Al Mowaihat or Al Helio later still. A 4pm session therefore becomes a 4.20pm session with a tired student, which is the worst hour of the day to attempt criterion B work. The slots that hold through a term are usually 5.30pm or 7pm on weekdays, or a longer weekend morning block. Friday and Saturday mornings are the most requested windows we see from Ajman and the first to fill.

Ramadan changes the shape of the week rather than cancelling it. School hours are shortened across UAE private schools and the productive part of the day moves, so sessions that worked in February do not work in Ramadan. Families generally either move to a late-morning slot while school finishes early, or to a post-iftar evening slot. The pattern worth avoiding is the mid-afternoon session during fasting, which produces attendance without learning. Planning the switch a fortnight ahead keeps the same teacher rather than losing the slot.

The UAE academic calendar also compresses revision into particular weeks, with winter and spring breaks falling where a British or Indian family may not expect them. The practical move for an MYP family is to map the school's own internal assessment dates in September, place the weekly slot where it survives those weeks, and treat the fortnight before each reporting point as the time for additional sessions rather than the time to start.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the task is a criterion B investigation
paragraphs: MYP mathematics is assessed substantially through work done in school time and at home, which puts tutoring directly next to a line that matters. IB academic-honesty rules require that assessed work is the student's own. A tutor who supplies the rule for an investigation, or hands over phrasing for a justification, has not helped; they have created a malpractice exposure that sits with the student.

The boundary is workable and worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach the underlying mathematics, work through unrelated examples of the same type, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin or the communication unclear. A tutor may not author any part of the submitted work, supply the generalisation, rewrite the explanation or edit a draft into something the student could not have produced alone. That distinction is the whole difference between teaching and the essay-mill model that circulates in this market.

Parents should also know that some providers in the UAE openly sell completed assessed work, including Diploma internal assessments at four-figure prices. That is an academic-integrity breach with consequences for the student rather than the seller, and it is worth treating any offer phrased as 'done for you' as a reason to walk away. The same applies to the MYP Personal Project in MYP 5: coaching on planning, process and reflection is legitimate, and producing the artefact or the report is not.

On the same principle, we do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past examination material or mark schemes. Those are the IB organisation's copyright and are properly accessed through your child's school and the official site. A tutor who offers you a folder of such material is offering something they are not entitled to supply, which tells you something about the rest of the service.

process.title: Send one piece of marked work
process.description: Before anything is quoted, send a recent marked MYP maths task and the latest report with its criterion levels. Reading real work takes about fifteen minutes and replaces a week of guessing. It is also what makes the trial lesson useful rather than introductory, because the teacher arrives already knowing which criterion to probe.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a named criterion
process.description: A full one-to-one lesson over live video at no charge and with no card details taken. The output a parent should expect from it is a specific statement: which of the four criteria is losing marks, what the underlying cause is, and roughly how many weeks of work it implies. If that statement does not arrive, the match is wrong.

process.title: Match on the criterion, not the postcode
process.description: Because delivery is remote, matching is done on teaching fit rather than on who lives nearest Al Nuaimiya. An MYP 5 extended student with weak algebraic fractions and an MYP 2 student with slow fraction arithmetic need different teachers, and neither of them needs the one who happens to be in the emirate.

process.title: Fix the slot around the commute
process.description: Agree one weekly slot that survives the school run, the Dubai commute and the UAE calendar, rather than the time that sounds convenient in September. Most Ajman families settle on a later weekday evening or a weekend morning block, with the Ramadan arrangement agreed in advance rather than improvised.

process.title: Review at six weeks against the school's reporting
process.description: Six weeks is long enough for criterion C habits to change and short enough to act if nothing has. The review compares the school's own criterion levels before and after, not a tutor's impression. If one criterion has moved and another has not, the plan changes; if nothing has moved, the teacher changes.

whyPoints.title: Prices quoted with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency an Ajman family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-level diagnosis, in writing
whyPoints.description: A first session produces a named criterion and a named cause, not a general impression. That is the difference between a plan you can check in six weeks and a standing order you cannot evaluate. The school's own criterion levels are the measure used, because they are the numbers that appear on the report.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the hour
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so the Al Jurf family and the Al Nuaimiya family pay for teaching time only. Published market data puts in-home rates roughly a third above online rates for comparable teachers, and in this emirate that gap is almost entirely drive time.

whyPoints.title: Specialist supply rather than local supply
whyPoints.description: The constraint in Ajman is not willingness to tutor, it is the number of resident teachers who have marked MYP mathematics. Remote delivery widens the pool to teachers who do this specific job, which matters most for criterion B and criterion D work and for MYP 5 extended content.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: We teach, review and give feedback on work the student has produced. We do not author assessed tasks, supply generalisations for investigations or distribute copyrighted syllabus and examination material. In a market where completed assessments are openly sold, saying so plainly is a practical differentiator.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no suitable MYP mathematics specialist is free at the slot you need, we say so at the trial stage rather than filling the hour with whoever is available. A mismatched teacher at the right time costs more than a short wait for the right one.

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP Mathematics tutor in Ajman charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates run from roughly AED 45-150 an hour for a generalist or university-student tutor working online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject teacher online, and AED 200-450 or above for an IB subject specialist. In-home visits sit at AED 180-500 because travel time is inside the hour. Those bands come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026; they are the market, not our price list. MYP mathematics usually prices in the middle, below Diploma Higher Level work and above general secondary maths, and the figure for your child depends on the year group and how many criteria need work.

faqs.question: Why does MYP maths tutoring cost less than IB Diploma maths in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Two reasons, and neither is that MYP matters less. Diploma Higher Level mathematics has a narrower supply of teachers who can mark it confidently, and the stakes of the final examination series push demand into a short window each year, so specialist hours are scarcer and dearer. MYP work also tends to be remediable in fewer sessions, because the losses are usually fluency and written communication rather than missing content. The gap is not large, though. An MYP 5 extended student working on logarithms and vectors is close to early Diploma material, and a tutor who can teach that will price near the specialist band rather than the generalist one.

faqs.question: Is a 90-minute MYP maths session better value than two 45-minute ones?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for a straightforward reason. Every session spends time settling in, reviewing the week's work and setting the next task, and in a 45-minute slot that overhead is a quarter of the lesson rather than a tenth. For an Ajman household where the child gets home late from a Sharjah or Dubai school, one longer slot also costs less in logistics than two. The exception is MYP 1 to MYP 3 arithmetic fluency, where short frequent practice genuinely beats long sessions. For criterion B investigation work, 90 minutes is close to a minimum, because finding a rule and then writing a justification does not fit in forty-five.

faqs.question: What does criterion B actually ask my child to do in MYP maths?
faqs.answer: Criterion B is called investigating patterns and is marked out of eight. The student is given a situation, finds a pattern in it, states a general rule, and then justifies or tests that rule on cases they were not given. The marks sit mostly in the last part. A student who spots the rule and writes it down without explaining why it must hold caps out in the middle bands, which is the single most common pattern we see in MYP 4 work. It is a teachable skill rather than a talent, and the practice is always on unrelated examples: a tutor who supplies the rule for a task being assessed has created a problem, not solved one.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 4 at school and his maths grade fell from 6 to 4. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with the criterion levels behind the grade rather than the grade. A two-band fall almost never means two bands of lost understanding; it usually means one criterion has collapsed and dragged the conversion down. The most common culprit in MYP 4 is communicating, where a student who reasons well in their head stops writing the justification, and the second is applying mathematics in real-life contexts, where answers arrive without interpretation. Send the marked work and the report, and a first session should name which one it is. If the answer is arithmetic fluency instead, that is six to ten weeks of specific practice rather than a general revision programme.

faqs.question: Should my daughter take standard or extended mathematics in MYP 5?
faqs.answer: It depends on where she is heading in the Diploma, not on ambition in the abstract. Extended covers the standard content plus additional material, commonly logarithms, further indices, harder algebraic fractions, two-dimensional vectors and extra trigonometry, depending on the school's scheme. If Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the likely destination, extended is close to a practical prerequisite even where the school does not call it one. If Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is more likely, standard is adequate and pushing for extended can lower the MYP grade for no benefit. Her criterion B and criterion D work tells you more about the right answer than her enthusiasm does.

faqs.question: Does a private maths tutor working with an Ajman family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the UAE government states that the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The government also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted with scepticism. Applications go through the ministry's own service page, app and e-services system.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ajman, and does it change how tutoring works?
faqs.answer: Ajman private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, alongside Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi has the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. For tutoring the difference is mainly administrative: inspection and licensing information for an Ajman school is found within the federal framework, so its reporting is not directly comparable with a Dubai school's published rating. The tutor's own permit obligation comes from the labour ministry and is the same in every emirate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my child's criterion B investigation before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin, where the notation is unclear and which part of the descriptor is not yet addressed. That is feedback, and it is both legitimate and useful. What a tutor must not do is supply the generalisation, rewrite the justification, or edit the draft into something the student could not have produced alone, because IB academic-honesty rules require assessed work to be the student's own and the consequence of a breach falls on the student. The practical test is simple: after the session, could your child explain every line of what they submitted without help? If not, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: We live in Al Nuaimiya and both parents work in Dubai. When can sessions realistically start?
faqs.answer: Count the bus rather than the bell. A child attending school in Sharjah or Dubai from an Ajman address is often not home before 4pm, and later from Al Mowaihat or Al Helio, so a 4pm slot in practice becomes a tired 4.20pm start. Slots that survive a full term from this part of Ajman are usually 5.30pm or 7pm on weekdays, or a longer block on Friday or Saturday morning. Weekend mornings are the most requested windows we see from Ajman households and the first to fill each term. Because lessons are over live video, no part of the arrangement depends on a tutor crossing the Sharjah boundary at rush hour.

faqs.question: Is it worth keeping MYP maths sessions running during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the slot moves. School hours shorten across UAE private schools during Ramadan and the productive part of the day shifts, so a timetable that worked in February will not hold. Families typically move either to a late-morning slot, taking advantage of the earlier school finish, or to a post-iftar evening session. The arrangement to avoid is the mid-afternoon session during fasting, which delivers attendance rather than learning. Agree the change a fortnight ahead so the same teacher keeps the slot rather than it being released. Reduced-intensity weeks are also a sensible time to work on written communication, which needs attention more than energy.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions does an MYP 3 student in Ajman usually need?
faqs.answer: One well-placed weekly session plus work done between sessions moves more than two sessions with nothing in between, and that holds across almost every MYP 3 case we see. The reason is that the losses at this stage are habits rather than gaps: slow fraction work, reasoning never written down, notation drift. Habits change through repeated correction on the student's own work, not through extra contact hours. Two or three sessions a week make sense in two situations: an internal assessment a fortnight away, or a student who has moved onto the extended route mid-year and has genuine content to cover. Otherwise the second session is usually buying reassurance rather than progress.

faqs.question: Does paying more per hour in Ajman actually buy a better MYP maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Up to a point, and then it stops. Moving from the AED 45-150 generalist band to the AED 150-300 qualified-teacher band buys something concrete: someone who marks against criterion descriptors rather than against right answers, which is where most MYP marks are actually lost. Moving into the AED 200-450 specialist band buys criterion B and criterion D expertise and MYP 5 extended content knowledge. Above that, the premium tier that publishes AED 650 an hour is paying for reputation rather than for a different marking skill at middle-years level. The useful question is not what the hour costs but whether the first session named a criterion and a cause.

faqs.question: Will MYP mathematics prepare my child for Maths AA or Maths AI in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Both, but not equally, and the MYP route matters. The Diploma splits mathematics into Analysis and Approaches, which leans towards algebraic technique and proof, and Applications and Interpretation, which leans towards modelling, data and technology. MYP extended mathematics, with its logarithms, algebraic fractions and additional trigonometry, is the natural run-up to Analysis and Approaches, particularly at Higher Level. The standard route prepares a student well for Applications and Interpretation and adequately for Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level. For UAE university entry, check the specific programme page at the specific institution, because quantitative degrees often expect the Analysis strand and requirements are revised.

faqs.question: If we take the trial lesson and then walk away, what have we paid?
faqs.answer: Nothing is charged and nothing is owed. The trial is a full one-to-one lesson over live video with no card details taken beforehand, and the point of it is to produce a specific diagnosis you can act on with or without us: which of the four MYP criteria is losing marks, what is causing it, and roughly how many weeks of work that implies. If the teacher is not the right fit, say so and we will either propose a different match or tell you plainly that we do not have the right specialist free at your slot. A mismatched tutor in a convenient hour is a worse outcome than a short wait.

ajman/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one marked piece of work
ajman/ib-myp-mathematics-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing quotes for an IB MYP mathematics tutor in Ajman, the most useful thing you can do costs nothing: send a recent marked maths task and the latest report with its criterion levels, and book the free trial lesson. A teacher who reads real work before the lesson can tell you in one session which of the four criteria is costing marks, whether the cause is arithmetic fluency or unwritten reasoning, and roughly how many weeks it implies. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the slot fits around the school run and the Dubai commute rather than around a drive to Al Nuaimiya or Al Jurf.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for in the middle years
paragraphs: Middle Years tuition is the hardest spend in the UAE market to judge, because the feedback loop is slow and opaque. A Diploma parent sees papers, weightings and a session in May. An IGCSE parent sees a syllabus code and a past paper archive. An MYP parent sees a report with numbers out of eight against letters, a comment about conceptual understanding, and no external benchmark anywhere. Many Ajman families respond by buying weekly hours in every subject and hoping, which is the most expensive version of the decision available to them.

The cheaper and more effective version starts with the structure. Each MYP subject is assessed against four published criteria, each marked from zero to eight, and those marks convert into a one to seven grade using boundaries the school applies. A student losing marks in criterion D of Sciences and a student losing marks in criterion A are two different problems with two different remedies, and no amount of general subject tuition addresses either until someone has read the actual descriptor.

Price follows from that diagnosis rather than from the subject name. Published market figures for middle-years support in this country run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 450 or more for specialist work, and the honest answer to where a given family lands is that it depends on whether the gap is coverage, skill or writing discipline. Coverage gaps are the cheapest to fix. Writing discipline against criteria takes longer and costs more, and nobody in this market tells you which one you have before you have paid for a term.

Ajman adds a local layer. Few families here are inside an IB continuum school in the emirate itself, so most MYP students travel into Sharjah or Dubai, or sit a national curriculum while a parent researches an eventual move to the IB. That means two of the most common enquiries we take from Al Nuaimiya, Al Mowaihat and Al Yasmeen are not about a subject at all: they are about whether a child entering the MYP late can catch up, and whether MYP marks will matter to anything later.

This page answers the money question in the open, with every figure attributed to the provider that published it, and then answers the questions behind it: what one criterion actually takes to fix, when the Personal Project needs paid help and when it does not, how the jump into the Diploma changes the bill in Year 12, and when the right advice is to spend nothing. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, and that limit is stated here rather than discovered later.

ajman/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to an Ajman family thinking about the middle years: the one before, the one in question, and the one it feeds. The money question looks different in each, because what is being assessed and who marks it changes completely between them.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led primary framework with no external assessment and no grades in the familiar sense. Reporting is against learning outcomes and the exhibition in the final year. Tuition at this stage is almost always about a specific literacy or numeracy gap rather than about the framework, and the market rate sits at the lower end accordingly.
programmes.countryNote: Few Ajman schools run the PYP, so most families who ask about it are considering a move into an IB school in Sharjah or Dubai. The useful spend at this age is a short diagnostic block on reading fluency or number facts, not a standing weekly commitment, and we say that even though it is the smaller sale.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each is assessed against four criteria marked from zero to eight, giving a maximum of thirty-two, which the school converts to a one to seven grade. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed against its own three criteria. Schools may enter students for on-screen eAssessment and ePortfolios leading to the MYP certificate.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the practical issue is that a child's MYP marks are generated entirely inside one school, usually across the Sharjah or Dubai border, with no external dataset to compare against. That makes the criterion descriptor the only reliable yardstick a parent has, and makes a tutor who ignores it close to useless regardless of subject knowledge.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus three core components, assessed through internal work marked at school and external papers sat in one session. This is where external marking appears for the first time for an MYP student, and where the cost of tuition in this market roughly doubles because the specialist pool narrows to subject and level.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 11 to Year 12 transition is the point at which Ajman families most often start paying real money, and the size of that bill is partly decided three years earlier. A student who left the MYP able to write to a criterion arrives in the Diploma needing content teaching; one who did not arrives needing both.

ajman/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: The MYP subjects below are described by which criterion usually costs the marks, because that is what a quote should be built around. A tutor who cannot tell you which criterion your child is losing marks in is quoting for hours rather than for a repair.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: Criterion A knowledge questions are rarely the problem. Marks go in criterion C, communication, where correct answers appear without the reasoning or notation that earns the band, and in criterion D, where a real-life application question is answered mathematically but never interpreted in context.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: The investigation criteria carry the risk. Hypotheses written without a scientific reason, method sections that do not control a named variable, and conclusions that restate the data instead of evaluating the method are the three recurring losses, and all three are fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: MYP Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis of writer's choices is the examined skill, not plot knowledge. Essays that summarise competently sit in the middle bands indefinitely until the student learns to anchor each paragraph to a technique and its effect, which is a writing habit rather than a content gap.

subjects.name: MYP Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Assessed across listening, reading, speaking and writing, with the phase rather than the year group setting the expectation. Students placed in a phase above their actual production level lose marks on accuracy for a year before anyone notices the placement was the issue.

subjects.name: MYP Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Source work and the investigation criteria decide the grade. Students who can describe a historical or geographical case well still lose marks when a question asks for evaluation of a source's origin, purpose and limitations and they offer content instead.

subjects.name: MYP Design
subjects.description: The design cycle is the assessment, and the written documentation carries most of the marks rather than the finished product. Students who build something good and document it thinly score lower than students whose outcome is modest and whose inquiry and evaluation are thorough.

subjects.name: MYP Arts
subjects.description: The process journal is assessed alongside the work. Marks are lost where developmental thinking was never recorded, which means the remedy is a documentation habit introduced early rather than extra practical tuition late.

subjects.name: MYP Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Marked against their own criteria and frequently the lowest marks on an MYP report, because students treat them as two subjects joined rather than as a single integrated question. Explicit coaching on synthesis fixes this faster than subject revision does.

subjects.name: MYP Personal Project
subjects.description: Assessed against three criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each marked from zero to eight. The product is not what is marked. Students who choose an ambitious goal and keep no process evidence lose marks that a modest, well-documented project would have earned.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Runs alongside the MYP in UAE private schools under federal requirements for Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. The written register is the usual gap for students who speak Arabic at home but have only been taught formal writing conventions at school.

ajman/ib-myp-tutor.regionsTitle: Ajman districts, and what the spend looks like in each
ajman/ib-myp-tutor.regionsIntro: What varies between Ajman districts is not the price per hour but the shape of the commitment: how many children are involved, how late a session has to start, and whether the school that sets the task sheets is in this emirate at all.

regions.note: Apartment-dense and close to the Sharjah line, with large day schools nearby. Enquiries from here are often for two children at once, so the comparison worth running is two short blocks against one standing weekly commitment.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa sub-districts with children travelling into Sharjah schools. Session start times here sit at 6.30pm or later, which rules out most in-home arrangements priced on a two-hour minimum.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central and older, mixing towers and villas near the Corniche. Families here tend to budget by term rather than by month, which suits a defined block with a measurable end point better than an open-ended monthly package.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Mixed residential and commercial blocks with fast access to Sharjah. The practical constraint is a late return home, so a fixed online slot costs less in cancelled sessions than any arrangement involving travel.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zahya
regions.note: Newer Emirates Road communities, often families who moved out from Dubai. These are the households most likely to be comparing an Ajman online rate against what they previously paid for in-home tuition in Dubai.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda

sections.heading: Why an MYP report resists being priced
paragraphs: A parent holding an MYP report has less information to act on than a parent holding an IGCSE mock result, and more than they realise. Less, because there is no percentage, no external cohort and no mark scheme in the public domain for a school's unit task. More, because the numbers are already diagnostic: four criteria per subject, each from zero to eight, which locates the problem far more precisely than a single aggregate ever could.

The reason families struggle to convert that into a decision is that schools report the band and not the descriptor. A five in criterion C of Mathematics is meaningless until you read what the band five descriptor asks for, and schools vary in how prominently they publish it. The first job in any honest quote is therefore to read the descriptors alongside the report, which takes one conversation and no money.

That one conversation routinely changes the size of the purchase. A student with sixes and sevens in criterion A and threes in criterion D does not need a subject tutor for a year; they need to learn to write an interpretation sentence after every calculation, which is a handful of sessions. A student with threes across all four criteria in Sciences has a genuine coverage gap and a different bill. Both sets of parents arrive asking the same question about hourly rates.

There is a second reason the middle years are hard to price, which is that the marks do not follow the student anywhere external. Nothing in an MYP report is seen by a university. Its value is entirely in what it predicts about readiness for the Diploma or for IGCSE, which means tuition at this stage should be judged on whether it builds a habit that survives into Year 12, not on whether a band moved from four to five this term.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in Ajman, in AED, with sources
paragraphs: Here is the market, as published rather than as estimated. The budget end of UAE online tuition is populated by platforms quoting from AED 33 to 52 and from AED 45 to 65 an hour for middle-school support. Qualified subject tutors online sit roughly between AED 150 and AED 300, with one provider publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist work including coursework and project supervision runs from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one named-tutor provider publishing AED 650.

In-home visits are a separate band because travel is inside the price. Published in-home figures for this market run from about AED 180 to AED 350, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly package rates seen include roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is the clearest single illustration of what travel costs a family.

None of those numbers is an IB Gram price list, and this page deliberately avoids inventing one. Our own figure follows the free trial lesson, because a four-session criterion repair and a year of weekly subject teaching are not the same purchase and quoting a single hourly rate for both would be misleading. What the table below does is let an Ajman parent see what a given shape of commitment costs at market rates before speaking to anybody.

One piece of context worth holding alongside these numbers: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. For families whose school fees are flat, tuition spend becomes the variable line in the education budget, which is exactly why it deserves to be bought in defined blocks with an end point rather than as a rolling monthly charge nobody reviews.

sections.heading: The six things that move an MYP quote up or down
paragraphs: Rate cards in this market hide the variables, so here they are in the open. The first and largest is whether the work needs a subject specialist or a capable generalist. Criterion writing discipline in Individuals and Societies can be taught by a strong humanities teacher; MYP Extended Mathematics heading into Analysis and Approaches cannot be taught well by a generalist, and the price difference between the two is most of the span in the table above.

The second is the number of criteria in scope. One criterion in one subject is a short, cheap, measurable job. Four criteria across three subjects is effectively a part-time teaching programme and should be priced and planned as one. The third is session length and frequency: a ninety-minute fortnightly slot often costs less per month than a weekly hour and produces more marked work, particularly for students from Year 9 upwards who can work independently between sessions.

Fourth is timing in the school year. Demand concentrates around report cycles and the final MYP year, and families booking in the week a report lands have less choice of tutor and slot than families booking a month earlier. Fifth is the sibling question, which matters in Ajman specifically because multi-child enquiries are common here; two children in one household sharing a tutor and a slot is cheaper per child than two separate arrangements, though only where the subjects align.

Sixth, and least discussed, is format. Online one-to-one sits below in-home at every level in the published figures, and the gap is not a quality discount. It is the travel that is no longer being paid for. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at all, since home visits are a service we run only in India, so for Ajman families the comparison is between our online delivery and someone else's in-home rate rather than between two of our own products.

sections.heading: The Personal Project: where the money is usually wasted
paragraphs: The final MYP year brings the Personal Project, and with it a predictable pattern of spending badly. Families buy weekly sessions for months, because the project feels large, and most of those hours go on the product rather than on what is assessed. The project is marked against three criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each from zero to eight. The thing the student makes is evidence, not the mark.

Knowing that changes the shape of useful support entirely. What helps is three to six sessions placed at the school's own milestones: one when the goal and success criteria are being set, because an over-ambitious goal with no measurable criteria is the most common structural failure; one in the middle, to check that process evidence is being recorded as the work happens rather than reconstructed afterwards; and one near the end, on reflection, which is the criterion students most often treat as a summary.

There is a hard line around this work and it needs stating plainly. The student chooses the goal, carries out the project, keeps the process journal and writes every word of the report. A tutor teaches research and documentation skills, asks questions about what exists, and points at a section that is describing rather than evaluating. A tutor does not supply text, set the goal or build the product. Providers in this market sell finished assessed work; buying it puts the student's own qualification at risk and we refuse the work outright.

The money argument is worth stating alongside the integrity one. Six well-placed sessions at specialist market rates cost less than a term of weekly tuition and address the criteria that are actually marked. Several Ajman families arrive in the final MYP year having already spent on a standing weekly commitment that never once looked at the planning criterion, which is the most avoidable overspend in the middle years.
bullets: Three criteria, each 0-8: planning, applying skills, reflecting
The product is evidence; the documentation is what carries the marks

sections.heading: From the MYP into the Diploma: the gap that creates the Year 12 bill
paragraphs: The cost of Diploma tuition is partly set three years earlier, and families who understand that spend differently in the middle years. The jump is not mainly about content. It is about external marking appearing for the first time, about papers with fixed command terms and mark allocations, and about internal work that is moderated outside the school. A student who has never written to a published descriptor meets all of that at once in Year 12.

The subject-by-subject gaps are predictable enough to plan around. MYP Extended Mathematics into Analysis and Approaches needs algebraic fluency and proof notation that MYP criterion C never really demanded. MYP Sciences into any Diploma science needs uncertainty treatment and formal evaluation language. MYP Language and Literature into the Diploma equivalent needs close textual analysis at a volume the MYP does not require. Each of those is a few weeks of focused work in Year 11, or a term of expensive remediation in Year 12.

That is the arbitrage available to an Ajman family, and it is a real one. Specialist Diploma tuition sits at the top of the published bands, from roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above per hour. Middle-years work sits lower. Closing a known transition gap at middle-years rates before the Diploma starts is cheaper than closing the same gap at Diploma rates in the middle of a coursework deadline, and the student arrives in Year 12 with the writing habit already formed.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every UAE private school teaches the mandatory national subjects regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. For an MYP student in Ajman, or in a Sharjah or Dubai school, those subjects run alongside the eight MYP groups and take real timetable space.

In Dubai the detail is published in unusual depth, and it is worth knowing even for an Ajman resident whose child attends school across the border. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The language-of-instruction rules follow from that. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes.

Two practical consequences for a tutoring decision. First, teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic in Dubai schools are required to hold the relevant KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential question to ask the school rather than a tutor. Second, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, so support in these subjects has to work from the school's own material rather than from an alternative programme bought elsewhere.

sections.heading: Who regulates the school setting your child's task sheets
paragraphs: An MYP mark is produced by a school, so the authority overseeing that school is part of the picture. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Dubai sits under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there.

Sharjah's Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same in its own. Both of those authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so their remit extends well beyond inspection. For an Ajman family whose child attends school in Sharjah, that is the body whose decisions shape the school calendar and the fee notice, not the Ministry covering their home address.

This matters to a tutoring plan in one specific way. Inspection reports and curriculum approvals are published by the authority that regulates the school, so a parent looking for the evidence behind a school's claims needs to look at the right register. Ajman families routinely search KHDA for a school that is not in Dubai, find nothing and conclude the information does not exist.

It also matters for what any tutoring provider may claim. No tutoring platform, including this one, is approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the Sharjah authority or the IB. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires an educational services permit for a training institute from KHDA, which is a specific thing issued to institutes with premises. Any provider implying regulator endorsement without holding that permit is making a claim a parent can and should test.
