sections.heading: When the honest advice is to spend nothing
paragraphs: Some middle-years enquiries should not end in a booking, and saying so is part of being worth hiring. A student scoring fives and sixes across all four criteria in a subject they dislike is not failing; they are a normal thirteen-year-old with a preference. Adding a weekly hour to that subject buys compliance, not learning, and the mark often does not move because there was no gap to close.

A second case is the student whose reports show low bands in criterion C across every subject at once. That is almost never six subject problems. It is a written-communication habit, and it is better addressed by one subject's tutor teaching the habit transferably, or by the school's own support, than by buying six separate tutors. Families who buy by subject in this situation spend several times what the repair costs.

A third case is timing. Six weeks before a major school report, a new weekly commitment in three subjects will not produce evidence of anything before the report lands, and the family will judge the spend against a deadline it was never going to meet. The better sequence is a diagnostic conversation now, one block starting after the report, and a decision based on the next cycle.

The fourth and bluntest case is availability. For a specific MYP phase in a minority language, or for a subject-and-year combination that is unusual, there may be no suitable specialist free in the window a family wants. We will say that rather than place a generalist, because a generalist in a specialist seat is how families end up paying twice. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is a reason to ask every provider about theirs.

process.title: Send the report and one task sheet
process.description: The criterion bands from the most recent report plus one marked unit task with the task sheet attached. Those two documents show whether the issue is a single criterion or a coverage gap, which is the difference between a five-session block and a year of weekly teaching.

process.title: Read the descriptors together, at no cost
process.description: One conversation comparing the band your child scored against what that band descriptor actually asks for. This is where most enquiries change size, usually downwards, and it happens before any quote exists so there is nothing to negotiate against.

process.title: A free trial lesson on the real task
process.description: One session at no charge, with no card details taken, working on the actual piece of work rather than on a generic exercise. You receive a written note afterwards naming the criterion in question and what the tutor would do about it.

process.title: Buy the smallest block that can be measured
process.description: A defined number of sessions ending in a re-marked task against the same criterion. Blocks are quoted as a total, not as a rolling monthly charge, so the commitment has an end date you chose rather than one you have to cancel.

process.title: Review the band, then decide
process.description: Compare the re-marked task against the opening diagnostic. Continue, change subject focus, change tutor or stop. Stopping on evidence is a legitimate outcome and the block is structured so that it is an easy conversation rather than an awkward one.

whyPoints.title: Priced by criterion, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A quote built around the specific criterion losing marks is usually smaller than a quote built around a subject name. We would rather sell a five-session repair that works than a year of weekly hours a family eventually resents paying for.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure on this page has a source
whyPoints.description: The bands quoted belong to named providers who published them, and none is presented as our rate. Our own figure follows the trial lesson, because the shape of the work changes the number more than the subject does.

whyPoints.title: Slots built for an Ajman evening
whyPoints.description: Later starts for families returning from Sharjah or Dubai, post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and no cancellation when the roads are bad. Over a term, a slot that holds produces more marked work than a better hour that does not.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: On the Personal Project and on unit tasks, the student owns the goal, the journal and every sentence. We teach skills, read what exists and ask questions. We do not supply text, and we turn down the work when that is what is being asked for.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from a small emirate
whyPoints.description: Because teaching is online, the pool for MYP Extended Mathematics or a specific language acquisition phase is national rather than whoever will drive into Ajman on a weekday evening. For unusual combinations that is the difference between a specialist and a substitute.

whyPoints.title: Advice that sometimes costs us the sale
whyPoints.description: Mid-band marks in a disliked subject, a communication habit showing up across six subjects, or an enquiry six weeks before a report are all cases where we will suggest spending less or nothing. It is the only way the recommendation means anything.

faqs.question: What does MYP tutoring cost per hour for a family in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for middle-years online tuition in this country run from roughly AED 45 at the budget end to AED 450 or more for specialist work. Platforms have published rates from AED 33 to 52 and from AED 45 to 65; a qualified-tutor provider published from AED 150; specialist bands run AED 200 to 450 and above, and one named-tutor provider published AED 650. In-home visits are quoted separately at roughly AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the price. Those are other providers' published figures. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson and depends on how much work the diagnosis actually calls for.

faqs.question: Why is my child's MYP report a number out of eight instead of a percentage?
faqs.answer: Because each MYP subject is assessed against four separate criteria, each marked from zero to eight, giving a maximum of thirty-two which the school converts into a one to seven grade using published boundaries. The structure is deliberately diagnostic: it shows which kind of thinking earned marks and which did not, rather than averaging everything into one figure. The practical consequence for a parent is that the number only becomes useful once you read the band descriptor beside it, because a five in a communication criterion and a five in a knowledge criterion call for completely different work.

faqs.question: Is paying for tuition in MYP Years 1 to 3 worth it at all?
faqs.answer: Often not, and that is worth hearing from a provider. In the early MYP years there is no external assessment, nothing a university will see, and plenty of time for a slow start to correct itself. The spend that does pay off is narrow: a genuine coverage gap after a curriculum change or a long absence, a diagnosed literacy or numeracy issue, or a transferable writing habit that will otherwise cost far more to fix in Year 11. A standing weekly commitment in a subject where the bands are mid-range usually buys attendance rather than learning.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to move one criterion band?
faqs.answer: For a single criterion in a single subject, four to six sessions is a realistic block, ending with a re-marked task against the same criterion so the change is visible rather than asserted. Communication and reflection criteria tend to move fastest, because the fix is a writing habit that can be practised on any content. Investigation criteria in Sciences and Design take longer, since the student has to produce a full piece of work to demonstrate the change. If a provider cannot put a number of sessions on it, they have not diagnosed it.

faqs.question: Does the Personal Project really need a paid tutor?
faqs.answer: It needs process discipline, which is not the same as weekly tuition. The project is marked against three criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, each from zero to eight, and the product itself is evidence rather than the mark. Three to six sessions placed at the school's milestones, on goal setting, on recording process evidence as the work happens, and on reflection, address what is assessed. Many families instead buy months of weekly hours that never examine the planning criterion. The student must set the goal, keep the journal and write every word themselves.

faqs.question: What actually makes one MYP quote higher than another?
faqs.answer: Six things, in rough order of weight. Whether the work needs a subject specialist or a capable generalist, which accounts for most of the span. How many criteria are in scope, counted across subjects. Session length and frequency, since a fortnightly ninety-minute slot often costs less per month than a weekly hour. When in the school year you book, because demand spikes at report cycles. Whether siblings genuinely share a subject and slot. And format, since published in-home rates sit above online rates at every level because the travel is inside them.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same Ajman household share one booking?
faqs.answer: Where the subject and level genuinely overlap, yes, and it is cheaper per child than two separate arrangements. Where they do not, a shared session usually means each child gets half an hour of attention at the price of an hour's convenience. Sibling enquiries are common in Al Nuaimiya and Al Mowaihat, so the question is worth asking properly: same subject and close enough in the programme to share a task, or different subjects that need separate slots. We will tell you which case you are in before quoting rather than after.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for MYP Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, and tuition centres in this market price group classes well below individual rates. The catch is that group teaching follows a fixed syllabus schedule, while a criterion problem is specific to one student's writing and reasoning. A group class is good value where the gap is coverage, because several students need the same content. It is poor value where a report shows strong knowledge marks and weak communication marks, since nobody in a group of eight is going to sit with your child's working and rewrite how it is set out.

faqs.question: Should we save the money now and spend it on Diploma tuition later?
faqs.answer: Partly, and it depends what the reports show. Specialist Diploma tuition sits at the top of the published bands, around AED 200 to 450 and above per hour, while middle-years work sits lower. Closing a known transition gap at middle-years rates in Year 11 is cheaper than closing the same gap at Diploma rates during a coursework deadline. So saving on broad weekly subject tuition in the early MYP years is sensible; saving on a diagnosed algebra or evaluation-language gap heading into Year 12 usually costs more in the end.

faqs.question: Will an MYP grade of five matter to a university later?
faqs.answer: No university sees it. MYP marks are generated inside the school, are not externally moderated in most years, and do not appear on any transcript a university assesses. Their value is predictive: they indicate whether a student is ready for the writing demands and the external marking of the Diploma or of IGCSE. That is the right basis on which to judge middle-years tuition. A band that moves from four to five this term matters far less than whether the student has learned to write to a published descriptor before Year 12.

faqs.question: How does the MYP to Diploma jump change what we pay in Year 12?
faqs.answer: It usually raises it, because external marking, fixed command terms and moderated internal work all arrive at once. The gaps are predictable: algebraic fluency and proof notation for Analysis and Approaches, uncertainty treatment and formal evaluation for the sciences, close textual analysis at greater length for literature. Each is a few weeks of focused work in Year 11 at middle-years rates, or a term of remediation in Year 12 at specialist rates during a coursework deadline. Families who treat Year 11 as the preparation year rather than a quiet year generally spend less overall.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit outside the MYP grades?
faqs.answer: They run alongside the programme and take real timetable space. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai schools, KHDA requires these subjects whatever the licensed curriculum, requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in the named subjects, and sets instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. Support in these subjects has to work from the school's own material, because additional or alternative content needs prior Ministry permission.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's unit task before it is handed in?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses and can read what the student has written and ask questions about it, including pointing out that a paragraph describes where the criterion asks for evaluation. What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a section into its final form or produce the analysis. The student writes every sentence and keeps the dated drafts. If the school asks what support was received, declare it accurately: honest tuition described honestly causes no difficulty, while work that appears from nowhere raises exactly the questions a family does not want.

faqs.question: Would a tutor travel to our home in Ajman, and what would that add to the price?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India, and UAE teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video. If you buy in-home tuition elsewhere, the published market rates sit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 45 to 450 online, and monthly packages have been published at around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits against about AED 799 for eight online sessions. The difference is the travel, which in Ajman means a forty-minute to two-hour round trip from most tutor bases.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to support an MYP student in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Read the band descriptors against the report yourself, identify whether one criterion or all four are low, and buy only for the narrow case. If one criterion is low, a block of four to six sessions ending in a re-marked task is the smallest unit that produces evidence. If communication marks are low across every subject, treat it as one writing habit rather than six subject problems. If the marks are mid-range in a subject your child simply dislikes, the cheapest option is genuinely to spend nothing this term and look again at the next report.

ajman/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Diagnose the criterion before you buy the hour
ajman/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IB MYP tutor in Ajman, the useful first step costs nothing: put the most recent report next to the band descriptors for the subject that worries you, and see whether one criterion is low or all four are. That single comparison usually decides whether you are buying a five-session repair or a term of teaching, and it is a far better basis for a budget than an hourly rate on a landing page. Send the report and one marked task with its task sheet, take the free trial lesson, and the quote that follows will be built on what the evidence actually shows rather than on the subject name.

ajman/ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named IB subjects one-to-one over live video, and each one works within the subject group whose internally assessed component they have marked repeatedly. Oral rehearsals are run live; written drafts are read and annotated before the session, never authored.

intro.heading: The internally assessed marks are the ones a screen is best placed to protect
paragraphs: Parents usually judge online tutoring by whether a screen can teach content. It can, and that is the least interesting part of the answer. The more useful question is which parts of a Diploma a video lesson handles better than a weekly appointment with whoever is locally available, and the honest answer is the internally assessed components and the orals — the pieces of the Diploma where marks are earned in private, months before any paper is sat, and where most Ajman students receive the least structured help.

Every Diploma subject carries a component marked inside the school and moderated externally. In the sciences it is a scientific investigation. In mathematics it is an exploration. In Group 1 it is an individual oral; in Group 2 an oral based on a stimulus; in economics a set of commentaries; in the arts a documented process. Theory of Knowledge adds an exhibition of three objects and a prescribed-title essay. Taken together these are a substantial share of the grade in every subject, and they are the marks a student has most control over.

They are also the marks most often lost on process rather than on ability. A student with an interesting investigation scores modestly because the research question could never have been answered with the data available. A mathematically capable student loses the reflection criterion entirely because reflection was read as a concluding paragraph. A fluent speaker under-performs the individual oral because the connective argument between the two works was never built. None of these is a knowledge problem, and all of them are visible in a draft three weeks before submission.

A screen is well suited to exactly this work. Drafts are shared, annotated and discussed. Orals are rehearsed live, recorded in the student's own voice, and played back so they can hear the pause where the argument went missing. Spreadsheets and graphic display calculator screens are shared directly, so a tutor watches the student operate the tool rather than describing it. The one thing a tutor cannot do remotely is touch the apparatus, and that limit is set out plainly in the section on Group 4.

Ajman makes this format more useful rather than less. The emirate's IB cohorts are small and its private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight, so the pool of local people who have marked a Higher Level investigation against its criteria is thin. Many households also have a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, which means the usable evening runs from about 18:30 to 21:00. A specialist who can hold that slot from anywhere is a better match than a generalist who can reach Al Rawda by seven. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that is an India-only service — and every lesson here is one-to-one over live video.

ajman/ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Each programme has its own internally assessed spine, and the work a tutor can usefully do over video changes with it. Establish which one your child is in before deciding what to buy.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each scored 1 to 8, with criteria describing different skills rather than levels of difficulty. The criterion that scores low is usually the one asking for evaluation or reflection. The programme closes with a personal project the student designs, carries out and documents, which is the first piece of extended independent work most students meet and a rehearsal for everything the Diploma will ask.
programmes.countryNote: Over video this stage works well because the artefacts are documents and process journals rather than physical objects. Ajman families most often arrive here in Year 10, after a report that read acceptably until Diploma expectations came into view. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the subject grade; the low criterion is what a session can target.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups at Higher or Standard Level, each carrying externally assessed papers plus an internally assessed component marked in school and moderated externally. The components differ by group: investigation, exploration, oral, commentary, documented process. Weightings are published in each subject guide and should be confirmed there rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's Higher Level groups are small, which has a specific consequence for internal components: one teacher may be supervising investigations across two or three courses at once, so individual feedback on a draft arrives late or thinly. That gap, rather than classroom teaching, is what most of our Ajman Diploma sessions are actually filling.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition built around three objects connected to a published prompt, plus an essay answering a prescribed title. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece supervised within the school. Both reward precision about how a claim is known and a question that can actually be answered, and both punish a late start more severely than any subject component does.
programmes.countryNote: The core arrives in the middle of DP1, exactly when two Higher Levels are at their hardest, and sequencing rather than ability is what fails. Over video the work is well suited to short, scheduled checkpoints: a question tested in week one, a plan in week three, a draft questioned in week six, all of it written by the student.

programmes.name: The year before the Diploma begins
programmes.description: The cheapest and least urgent place to intervene. A student entering DP1 who can manipulate algebra confidently, write a paragraph with a controlling idea, and work to a criterion rather than to a teacher's approval has access to the whole programme. One who cannot will meet all three demands at once in October of DP1, alongside new content in six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman this is also where video delivery is easiest to establish as a habit: the student is not yet under deadline pressure, so the routine of sending work ahead and receiving it marked gets built before it has to carry anything heavy. Families who start here rarely need the panic block later.

ajman/ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: What follows is organised around what the internally assessed component in each subject actually rewards, because that is where an online session makes the most difference and where the fewest students receive detailed help.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral traces a global issue through a literary and a non-literary work. Marks are lost on the connective argument rather than on knowledge of either text: students describe both works competently and never establish how the issue operates differently across them. Rehearsing aloud and playing the recording back exposes that gap in one session.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: An oral built from a stimulus the student sees shortly before speaking, plus productive writing marked on register, audience and text type. The usual loss is a well-written essay delivered where a blog, speech or letter was asked for. Over video this is drilled directly: a stimulus, a short preparation window, a recorded response.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The common failure is a question too broad to answer with achievable data, which is a problem that can only be fixed before the experiment, not after it. That makes a remote tutor most valuable three weeks earlier than most families call.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Quantitative investigations fail on uncertainty handling and on rounding too early; organic work fails on pathway recall. The investigation's evaluation criterion rewards specific, sourced limitations rather than general caution, and that distinction is teachable in a single session with the student's own draft on screen.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks exist for method as well as for answer, so working held in the head is unmarked. In the investigation the data-analysis criterion rewards correct treatment of uncertainty and a graph that earns its axes. Both are screen-friendly: the spreadsheet is shared and the tutor watches the student build the analysis.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is marked against five lettered criteria from presentation through to use of mathematics. Students lose the personal engagement and reflection criteria most often, because both are read as concluding paragraphs rather than as threads running through the piece. The graphic display calculator screen shares directly in a session.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology central rather than incidental. The usual loss is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence about what it means in context. Explorations here often start from real data the student can actually obtain, which makes the question-testing conversation shorter and more productive.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internally assessed commentaries reward one concept applied precisely to a current article, not a summary of the article. Diagrams are marked, and most are drawn from memory rather than labelled to the question. Both failures are visible in a shared document before anything is submitted.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The component's most expensive mistake is choosing an organisation the student cannot obtain information about, which turns into weeks of rescue work later. Testing that in week one costs twenty minutes and saves a term, and it is precisely the kind of check a scheduled online checkpoint delivers.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition requires three objects connected to a published prompt and justified individually. Marks follow the quality of the justification rather than the novelty of the object. A tutor's job is to question whether each object really does what the student claims, which is a conversation, and conversations work on video.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The experimental study is assessed on method and on the handling of results, and students lose marks for a design that cannot test what they set out to test. Command-term discipline carries the written papers. Neither element needs a shared room; both need a specialist who has marked the component.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Assessed on the comparative study and the process portfolio as much as on the exhibited work, which surprises families annually. Those two are documentation skills, photographed and shared easily, and they are where an online session adds more than it could in a studio.

ajman/ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Ajman district by district, and what the connection and the evening allow
ajman/ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: For an online arrangement the local variables are bandwidth, a quiet room and what time the household is genuinely free. These are the districts we hear from and what each one tends to need solving first.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Dense apartment living close to the Sharjah boundary. The room, not the connection, is usually the constraint: a session needs a door that closes, and families here often move the slot later so that a shared space is free.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central and well connected, with short internal journeys. Enquiries here cluster around internally assessed deadlines, and the useful arrangement is a short block of scheduled checkpoints rather than a weekly hour.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa households, frequently with several children. Headphones and a fixed desk matter more here than anywhere, because two siblings in adjacent rooms on two calls is the normal evening rather than the exception.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: A high share of DP1 and DP2 students, so demand concentrates in the 18:30 to 21:00 window. Families who fix a standing slot in September keep it; those who book in January take what is left.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial on the Sharjah side, with the longest commutes out of the emirate. Later starts are standard and shorter, sharper sessions work better here than a full hour at the end of a long day.

regions.name: Al Helio
regions.note: Newer housing and younger households, so Middle Years enquiries dominate. Establishing the habit of sending work ahead is the main thing a first block achieves, and it pays off two years later.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Zorah
regions.note: Lower density, shorter school runs and slightly earlier slots available. Group 4 investigations are the most common subject of enquiry, usually three weeks later than would have been ideal.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman
schoolClusters.note: IB provision in the emirate is concentrated rather than widespread, and private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight. Students we support attend schools across this group; supervision of every internally assessed component remains with the school.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the daily cross-boundary commute
schoolClusters.note: A meaningful number of Ajman households drive a child into Sharjah for school, which removes the early evening from the week and is the practical reason our Ajman sessions start after 18:30 rather than at four o'clock.

ajman/ib-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of online arrangement, chosen by what the component needs rather than by what is easiest to sell.

modes.title: Scheduled component checkpoints
modes.description: Four to six sessions spaced across the life of an internally assessed piece: test the question, agree the method, review the data, question the draft, check the criteria against the finished work. The spacing is the product. A single session two days before a school deadline can only tidy what exists, whereas a session in week one can prevent the question that was never answerable.
bullets: Criteria read together before anything is drafted
The research question tested against achievable data
The student's own draft annotated and questioned, never authored
A written note after each checkpoint saying what was and was not touched

modes.title: Live oral rehearsal with playback
modes.description: For the Group 1 individual oral, the Group 2 stimulus oral and any presented component. The student speaks to time, the session records only with the family's agreement, and the recording is played back so they hear the pause where the argument stopped. Most students improve more from hearing themselves once than from three conversations about structure.
bullets: Spoken to the real time limit from the first rehearsal
A stimulus or extract given with the real preparation window
Playback with the criteria open alongside
Recording only with explicit agreement, and deleted on request

modes.title: Weekly subject hour with marked work
modes.description: The standing arrangement for content and technique, with a timed task between sessions marked before the hour starts. This is what carries the externally assessed side of a subject while the component work runs in parallel, and it is the shape that produces a readable record across a term.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, one subject at one level
Timed task every week, marked against the assessment objectives
A criterion log that accumulates rather than resetting
Reviewed at week six against the marked evidence

sections.heading: The individual oral, rehearsed aloud and played back
paragraphs: In Group 1 the individual oral asks the student to trace a global issue through two works — a literary text and a non-literary one on the Language and Literature route — in a timed, recorded conversation with their own teacher, who then asks questions. Students prepare it as though it were an essay to be read, and the marks are not there. The assessment rewards an argument about how the issue operates differently in each work, maintained under questioning.

The failure is nearly always structural and it is audible rather than visible. A student talks for four minutes about the first text, four about the second, and never builds the bridge, so a listener learns about two works and nothing about the issue. On paper the plan looks balanced. Spoken aloud, the missing minute is obvious within the first rehearsal, and that is the whole argument for rehearsing it rather than discussing it.

Over video this is straightforward and the playback is what does the work. The student speaks to the real time limit with their extracts in front of them. The session records only with the family's explicit agreement. Then the recording is played back with the criteria open alongside, and the student marks their own performance before the tutor says anything. Almost every student hears the gap themselves on first listen, which makes the correction theirs and makes it stick.

Two practical notes. Confirm the current timings, extract limits and conditions with your child's coordinator rather than with any tutoring page, including this one, because those details are set by the school within the published requirements. And rehearse at least three times across three weeks rather than once the night before; the second rehearsal is where the argument is built and the third is where it becomes fluent under questioning.

sections.heading: Group 2: the stimulus you cannot see coming
paragraphs: A language-acquisition oral works differently from a Group 1 oral and the difference catches out exactly the students who are strongest in English. The student is given a stimulus a short time before speaking and must respond to it, then sustain a conversation. There is no opportunity to prepare content, so the thing being assessed is the ability to organise a response quickly in the target language and to keep going when the first idea runs out.

Bilingual Ajman students frequently assume this is easy and prepare nothing, then produce a fluent two minutes and an awkward four. Students whose spoken language is weaker but who have practised the shape of a response often do better, because the shape is what carries the time: describe what is in front of you, place it in a context, take a position, extend it with an example, acknowledge an alternative. That sequence can be rehearsed until it is automatic.

The productive written components fail for a related reason. Marks go to register, audience and the conventions of the text type the task specified, so an essay delivered where a blog or a speech was asked for loses conceptual marks before the language is read. Students who have never written a formal letter, a set of instructions or a speech in the target language are meeting the conventions for the first time in an assessment, which is an avoidable way to lose marks.

A video session suits both problems unusually well, because both are drills. The tutor supplies a stimulus and the real preparation window, the student speaks, the response is played back against the criteria. For the written side, the drill is three short pieces on the same content in three different text types, marked on whether each one sounds like what it claims to be. Four or five rounds of that transfers to anything the examination sets.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, when the tutor is not in the laboratory
paragraphs: This is the component where an online tutor's limits are real, and stating them precisely is more useful than hedging. The current DP sciences internal assessment is a scientific investigation assessed across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Two of those four live almost entirely in the planning and the writing; two depend on data that has to be produced somewhere. A remote tutor is strong on the first pair and can only support the second pair at one remove.

Research design is where most marks are won and lost, and it is won or lost before any apparatus is touched. A question that is too broad, or that depends on a variable the student cannot control, or that produces three data points when it needs eight, has already capped the piece. Reading the criteria and stress-testing the question in week one is twenty minutes of work that regularly saves a term. Almost nobody does it, because the exciting part is the experiment.

Data analysis and the evaluation criterion are also screen-friendly, because they are a spreadsheet and a piece of writing. The tutor shares the student's own data file, watches them build the graph, and asks why the uncertainty was handled that way. The evaluation criterion rewards specific, sourced limitations — this thermometer's resolution, this many repeats, this assumption — rather than general caution, and that distinction is teachable in a single session with the draft on screen.

What a remote tutor cannot do is handle the apparatus, supervise safety, or stand next to a student while a reading is taken. The school owns that, as it should, and any provider implying otherwise is misdescribing the component. The table sets out the division honestly, criterion area by criterion area.

sections.heading: The mathematics exploration and the calculator on a shared screen
paragraphs: The exploration is assessed against five lettered criteria, running from presentation and mathematical communication through personal engagement and reflection to use of mathematics. Confirm the current letters and mark allocations in the subject guide rather than from any tutoring page. The pattern we see in Ajman students' drafts is consistent: use of mathematics is reasonable, presentation is acceptable, and personal engagement and reflection score near the floor.

The reason is a misreading. Both of those criteria are treated as sections — a paragraph at the start about why the student chose the topic, a paragraph at the end about what they learned. Neither is a section. Personal engagement is evidenced by the choices made throughout: the data the student went and obtained, the method they adapted, the thing they tried that did not work. Reflection is evidenced at each turning point, where the student says why they are now doing something different. Written as threads rather than as bookends, both criteria move substantially.

The graphic display calculator is the other screen-specific advantage, and it is larger than it sounds. Students in Applications and Interpretation especially are examined on technology-assisted work, and most have learned the device by watching a teacher's hands from three metres away. In a video session the student shares their own calculator or software screen and the tutor watches the keystrokes, which exposes the habitual inefficiency that costs minutes in a paper. Nothing about that is better done in person.

The commonest expensive mistake is choosing a topic with no obtainable data behind it. A student who picks a question requiring information they cannot get spends three weeks discovering it and then starts again under deadline pressure. Testing the topic against available data in the first session is cheap, unglamorous and the single highest-return twenty minutes in the whole component.

sections.heading: Theory of Knowledge: three objects, questioned rather than supplied
paragraphs: The exhibition asks for three objects connected to one prompt from a published list, each justified in writing. Students choose objects that are interesting and then explain what they are. Marks follow the justification: why this specific object shows something about how knowledge works in relation to that specific prompt. An object chosen well and justified weakly scores below an ordinary object justified precisely.

A tutor's whole contribution here is questioning, and it is the kind of questioning that works better one-to-one than in a class of twenty. Does this object actually illustrate the prompt, or does it illustrate a neighbouring idea? Is the claim being made about the object, about the knowledge it represents, or about the student's own view? Could somebody disagree with the justification, and if not, is it saying anything? Four or five rounds of that produce a far stronger piece, written entirely by the student.

The prescribed-title essay fails differently. Students answer the title they wish had been set, usually a broader one, and write confidently past the question. The repair is mechanical: take the title apart word by word, identify what it actually commits you to, and build the essay against those commitments. It is a technique rather than an insight, and it transfers to the Extended Essay as well.

Two boundaries belong in this section. First, a tutor must never be the author of any part of either piece, and an offer in that direction should end the conversation with that provider. Second, word limits and current prompt lists are set in the published requirements and administered by the school, so confirm them with the coordinator rather than relying on a figure from a tutoring page. The thing we will not do is restate dates or limits we cannot source.

sections.heading: Where internally assessed marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Across the component drafts we read from Ajman students, six patterns account for most of the lost marks. None of them is about intelligence and all of them are visible early, which is the useful part: a component read in week two can be rescued cheaply, and one read two days before a school deadline can only be tidied.

The first is a research question that cannot be answered with achievable data. The second is reflection and engagement written as bookends rather than as threads. The third is evaluation expressed as general caution instead of named, specific limitations. The fourth is an oral with no connective argument between its two works. The fifth is a text type ignored, so the register is wrong before the language is read. The sixth is a component started so late that every other choice was forced.

Each has a repair cost and a deadline beyond which the repair is no longer available, and the table gives both. Read the final column hardest. Three of these six cannot be fixed at all once the data is collected or the recording is made, which is the entire case for buying checkpoints across a component rather than a rescue session at the end.

The practical move for an Ajman family is to ask the coordinator in September for the school's internal deadline calendar, then place three or four checkpoints against it. That single document is worth more than any tutoring plan built on guesswork, and it is free.

sections.heading: The authenticity trail that protects your child
paragraphs: Using an outside tutor on internally assessed work is entirely legitimate, and it becomes a problem only when nobody can show where the student's work ends and somebody else's begins. The protection is a record, and building one costs almost nothing if it is started at the beginning rather than assembled defensively at the end.

Four habits produce it. The student keeps dated drafts rather than overwriting one file, so a progression exists. The tutor's annotations stay as comments and questions on the student's text rather than as rewritten sentences. After each session a short note records what was discussed and what was not touched. And nothing is submitted that the student could not defend, sentence by sentence and choice by choice, to their own supervisor.

That last test is the whole of it. Schools ask students to confirm that submitted work is their own, and that confirmation is not a formality: awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice and the penalty can reach an entire entry rather than a single component. One operator researched in this market advertises finished internal assessments for a four-figure sum, which transfers every bit of that risk onto the student while the seller keeps the fee.

The table sets out, component by component, what the student owns, what a tutor may legitimately do and what evidence is worth keeping. It is also a reasonable thing to show a supervisor if they ask how outside support is being used, and in our experience that conversation goes better when the family raises it first.

sections.heading: Equipment, bandwidth and the Ajman evening
paragraphs: The setup is modest and the parts that matter are not the parts families worry about. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a stable connection, headphones, and paper and a pen on the desk. The camera matters because a tutor needs to see the student's written working as it happens; the headphones matter because in an Al Mowaihat or Al Nuaimiya household there are usually two other people within earshot.

Paper deserves its own sentence. Every externally assessed paper in the Diploma is handwritten under time pressure, and a student who has done a year of mathematics on a tablet will be slower and messier in the examination than their knowledge warrants. Our sessions ask for written working on paper, photographed and sent ahead. It feels old-fashioned and it protects marks.

On timing, the Ajman evening is narrower than a generic UAE page would suggest. With many households having a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, and some driving a child across the emirate boundary for school, the reliable window runs from about 18:30 to 21:00. Slots inside it are the first to fill in the second Diploma year. During Ramadan the usual adjustment is a shorter session after Iftar rather than a cancelled month, which keeps the rhythm and the marked-work record intact.

On recordings and data: sessions are recorded only with explicit agreement, recordings belong to the family and are deleted on request, and nobody needs a copy of a report card, a photograph of your child or a home address to arrange a lesson. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs how personal data is handled, and any provider should be able to say plainly what they collect, why, how long they keep it and how to have it removed.

sections.heading: What the first online session establishes, and the honest limits
paragraphs: The first lesson is free, no payment is taken beforehand, and its purpose is diagnosis rather than teaching. With the student's own marked work and any component draft on screen, a specialist should be able to say four things by the end of the hour: which subject and level this is being assessed at, which of the six loss patterns above are present, which of them are weeks of work and which are a calendar problem, and what the next three sessions will target.

That fourth answer is the one that separates people. A plan specific enough to be proved wrong — question stress-tested this week, data plan agreed next week, draft questioned in week four — can be judged by a parent without any subject knowledge. A promise to build confidence and support the student cannot be judged at all, which is why it is so often what gets said.

The limits belong here rather than in small print. A screen cannot supervise a student into starting work, cannot handle apparatus, and reads a reluctant seventeen-year-old less well than a person at the same table. Where supervision is the actual requirement, the in-home market option is the honest recommendation and we will say so at the diagnostic; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and steering around that would waste your time. We also publish no IB session or results date on these pages, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project — the coordinator holds the authoritative calendar.

The week-six review closes the loop. Parent, student and tutor look at the marked work and the component drafts and answer one question: has the targeted criterion moved? If it has, the next target gets chosen. If it has not, either the diagnosis was wrong, the work between sessions is not happening, or the match is poor, and each of those has a different remedy. Sometimes the right answer is to stop, and a provider who will not say that out loud has told you something worth knowing.

process.title: Send the component draft, not just the subject
process.description: A photograph of a marked paper plus whatever exists of the current investigation, exploration or essay tells a specialist more in two minutes than a description does. Add the subject, the level, the year group, the school's internal deadline if you have it, and the evening windows your household can genuinely hold.

process.title: We match on the component, not the city
process.description: Matching is done on who has marked that specific component at that level repeatedly, which is the whole point of delivering over video from a small emirate. You receive a named tutor, their subject and level coverage and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time, or a straight statement that we cannot cover it this week.

process.title: A free diagnostic hour
process.description: No payment beforehand. The tutor works from the student's own material and reports in writing: level, loss patterns present, which are repairable and which are calendar problems, and what the next three sessions will target. If the honest conclusion is that nothing should be bought, you hear it then.

process.title: Checkpoints placed against the school's calendar
process.description: Component work is scheduled backwards from the school's internal deadline rather than forwards from today: question tested, method agreed, data reviewed, draft questioned, criteria checked. Spacing is the product, because the question that cannot be answered has to be caught before the data is collected.

process.title: A written note after every session
process.description: Each note records what was discussed, what moved and, for component work, what the tutor did not touch. Those notes plus the student's dated drafts are the authenticity trail, and they are the thing that makes using outside support straightforward to explain to a supervisor.

process.title: The week-six review
process.description: Marked work and drafts on the table, one question: has the targeted criterion moved? If it has, choose the next target or stop. If it has not, the diagnosis, the plan or the match changes. The review exists so that a decision to stop is available and normal rather than awkward.

whyPoints.title: Built around the components, not around content delivery
whyPoints.description: The marks a student most controls sit in the investigation, the exploration, the orals and the core, and they are the marks that receive the least individual attention in a small cohort. Sessions are scheduled against those deadlines rather than spread evenly across a term.

whyPoints.title: Orals rehearsed and played back
whyPoints.description: Most students hear the missing minute in their own individual oral on first playback and correct it themselves, which is faster and more durable than being told. Recording happens only with explicit agreement and the file belongs to the family.

whyPoints.title: The authorship boundary written down
whyPoints.description: Annotations stay as questions on the student's own text, session notes record what was not touched, and dated drafts are kept. That record is what makes outside support easy to explain to a school, and it is the opposite of what the operators selling finished coursework in this market provide.

whyPoints.title: A specialist who has marked the component
whyPoints.description: Ajman's IB cohorts are small, so the local pool who have repeatedly marked a Higher Level investigation against its criteria is thin. Removing travel from the match means the subject decides it. That is the concrete reason for the format rather than a preference.

whyPoints.title: Slots that fit the real Ajman evening
whyPoints.description: Sessions run between roughly 18:30 and 21:00 because that is when households with a parent commuting to Dubai or Sharjah are actually free, and move later during Ramadan rather than pausing. A slot that cannot be kept produces no marked work.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated at the diagnostic, not afterwards
whyPoints.description: A screen cannot supervise, cannot handle apparatus and cannot rescue a component started too late. Where one of those is the real problem you will be told at the free lesson. IB Gram claims no accreditation from the International Baccalaureate or any UAE authority, and publishes no unverified IB dates.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help my child rehearse the Group 1 individual oral?
faqs.answer: This is one of the things video does best. The student speaks to the real time limit with their extracts in front of them, the rehearsal is recorded only with your explicit agreement, and the recording is played back with the assessment criteria open alongside so the student marks their own performance first. The common fault is structural: four minutes on each work and no bridge between them, which is invisible on a plan and obvious on playback. Rehearse three times across three weeks, and confirm current timings and extract conditions with the school's coordinator.

faqs.question: How does online tutoring work for a science investigation when there is no laboratory?
faqs.answer: By concentrating on the two criterion areas where most marks actually sit. Research design is decided before any apparatus is touched, and a question too broad or dependent on an uncontrollable variable has already capped the piece — stress-testing it in week one is twenty minutes that often saves a term. Data analysis and evaluation are a spreadsheet and a piece of writing, both shared on screen. What a remote tutor cannot do is handle apparatus, supervise safety or stand beside a student taking a reading. The school owns that, and any provider implying otherwise is misdescribing the component.

faqs.question: Is online support effective for the mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the two criteria it helps most are the two Ajman students most often lose. Personal engagement and reflection are repeatedly written as an opening paragraph about why the topic was chosen and a closing one about what was learned. Neither is a section: engagement is evidenced by the choices made throughout and reflection at each turning point. Rewritten as threads, both move substantially. Sharing the calculator or software screen also lets a tutor watch keystrokes, which exposes the habitual inefficiency that costs minutes in a paper. Confirm the criterion letters in the current subject guide.

faqs.question: What can a tutor see on a shared screen that a classroom teacher cannot?
faqs.answer: Three things, and all of them are diagnostic. The student's keystrokes on a graphic display calculator or in software, which reveal the slow habitual route they take through a calculation. The actual spreadsheet behind an investigation's analysis, rather than the finished graph that was pasted into the write-up. And their own voice played back on an oral rehearsal, which no classroom provides time for. A teacher with twenty students sees outputs; a one-to-one session over video sees the process that produced them, which is where the correctable errors live.

faqs.question: Which IB components rehearse well over video, and which genuinely do not?
faqs.answer: Well: the individual oral and the Group 2 stimulus oral, because they are spoken and can be recorded and played back. The mathematics exploration, because it is a document and a calculator screen. Economics commentaries, the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and the Extended Essay, because they are drafts to be questioned. Partially: the science investigation, where planning, analysis and evaluation work remotely but the practical does not. Badly: anything requiring apparatus, supervision of a reluctant student, or a studio. We say which category your child's situation falls into at the free diagnostic rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: How do I know an online tutor has not authored part of my child's work?
faqs.answer: Build a record from the beginning rather than assembling one defensively at the end. Four habits do it: the student keeps dated drafts instead of overwriting one file; tutor input stays as comments and questions on the student's own text rather than as rewritten sentences; a short note after each session records what was discussed and what was not touched; and nothing is submitted that the student could not defend sentence by sentence to their own supervisor. That last test is the whole of it. If they could not defend it, the work is not theirs and the consequence falls on them.

faqs.question: What evidence should we keep to show an internal assessment is my child's own?
faqs.answer: Dated drafts in sequence, so progression is visible rather than asserted. The raw data file or calculator file behind any analysis. Session notes recording what a tutor discussed and what they did not touch. Rehearsal recordings, where the family holds them and consent was given. And, for the Extended Essay, the record of supervisor meetings the school keeps anyway. None of this is onerous if it starts in week one. Showing a supervisor this trail unprompted generally makes the conversation about outside support easier rather than harder.

faqs.question: Does my child need their own graphic display calculator for online sessions?
faqs.answer: They need whatever device their school and the examination permit, and they need to be using it in sessions rather than watching a tutor use one. That is the point: the student shares their own calculator or software screen so the tutor can see the keystrokes and the route taken through a calculation. Most students have learned the device by watching a teacher's hands from three metres away, which produces slow habitual routes that cost minutes under time pressure. Confirm the permitted models with the school's coordinator, since that is set within the published examination requirements.

faqs.question: What equipment and connection does an online IB lesson in Ajman need?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect, and the parts that matter are not the glamorous ones. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a stable connection, headphones, and paper and a pen on the desk. The camera matters because the tutor needs to watch written working appear; the headphones matter because in most Ajman households there are two other people within earshot. Written work is photographed and sent ahead so it arrives marked. The one thing worth insisting on is paper: every Diploma paper is handwritten under time pressure, and a year of tablet-only work slows a student down.

faqs.question: Will our weekly slot survive Ramadan and the Ajman evening?
faqs.answer: It should, with one adjustment. The reliable Ajman window runs from roughly 18:30 to 21:00, because many households have a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah and some drive a child across the emirate boundary for school, which removes the early evening entirely. During Ramadan the school day compresses and family routines shift, and the arrangement that works is a shorter session after Iftar rather than a cancelled month. Keeping the rhythm matters more than keeping the length: a four-week gap costs more in lost momentum than four shortened sessions cost in content.

faqs.question: Should my child still write by hand if the lessons happen on a screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth being firm about. Every externally assessed Diploma paper is handwritten under time pressure, and a student who has spent a year typing mathematics or annotating texts on a tablet will be slower and less legible in the examination than their understanding warrants. Our sessions ask for working on paper, photographed and sent ahead. There is a second benefit: a photograph of handwritten working shows the tutor where the student stopped writing and started thinking in their head, which is exactly where method marks are lost.

faqs.question: Are online IB sessions recorded, and who has access to a recording?
faqs.answer: Only with your explicit agreement, and the file belongs to the family and is deleted on request. Recording is genuinely useful for oral rehearsal, where playback is the thing that produces the improvement, and it is also a file containing a minor's voice and image, so it should never happen by default. Ask any provider three questions: does recording happen, who can access the file, and how do we switch it off. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs personal data handling, and a provider should also state what they collect, why and how to have it deleted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor support the Theory of Knowledge exhibition without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the useful contribution is entirely questioning. Does this object actually illustrate the chosen prompt, or a neighbouring idea? Is the claim about the object, about the knowledge it represents, or about the student's own opinion? Could anybody disagree with the justification, and if not, is it saying anything at all? Four or five rounds of that produce a markedly stronger exhibition written entirely by the student. What a tutor must never be is the author of any part of it. Confirm word limits and the current prompt list with the coordinator rather than with any tutoring page.

faqs.question: What should the first online IB session actually establish?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing, by the end of the hour. The subject and level the work is being assessed at. Which loss patterns are present in the student's own marked work or component draft. Which of those are weeks of work and which are calendar problems that can no longer be fixed. And what the next three sessions will target, specified tightly enough that you can judge by session four whether it worked. A plan you cannot prove wrong is not a plan. The lesson is free and no payment is taken before it, so this judgement costs you nothing.

faqs.question: What are the honest limits of IB tutoring delivered over video?
faqs.answer: Three, stated plainly. A screen cannot supervise a student into beginning work, so where the real problem is that nothing gets started, weekly sessions become an expensive record of that fact. It cannot handle laboratory apparatus or supervise safety, which is why the practical half of a science investigation stays with the school. And it cannot rescue a component started so late that every choice was already forced. Where any of those is the actual situation, you will be told at the free diagnostic. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

ajman/ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Send the draft while it can still change
ajman/ib-online-tutor.closingBody: The useful first message is short: the subject, the level, the year group, a photograph of recent marked work, whatever exists of the current investigation, exploration or essay, and the school's internal deadline if you have it. We will arrange a free diagnostic hour with a specialist who has marked that component, and afterwards you will have a written note of the loss patterns present, which of them are still repairable, and what the next three sessions will target. Component work is scheduled backwards from the school's deadline, because the question that cannot be answered has to be caught before the data is collected. Nothing is taken before the first lesson.

intro.heading: An IB grade is not a measure of effort, and that is why the search starts
paragraphs: Most Ajman families who contact us about IB tuition have already noticed something odd. The child is working. The teacher says the work is coming in. The report still says 4. That gap between effort and outcome is almost always a gap between what the student is producing and what the examiner is marking against, and it is the single most fixable problem in the whole programme.

The International Baccalaureate marks against published assessment objectives and a published vocabulary of command terms. A paragraph that describes a process thoroughly will take the description marks and none of the explanation marks, however long it is. A laboratory write-up with perfect results and no evaluation of method loses the evaluation criterion entirely. A history essay that narrates the events of a period, accurately, scores in the lower bands because the question asked for an argument. None of these students has a knowledge problem.

So this page is organised around assessment rather than around reassurance. It goes through the three IB programmes and what a report means in each, through the six Diploma subject groups and what each group actually rewards, through the language routes in Groups 1 and 2 that quietly set a ceiling, and through the loss patterns we see most often in Ajman. Each of those sections ends in the same place: what a tutor can do about it, and in roughly how long.

Ajman is the smallest emirate by area, and its private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight rather than under an emirate-level authority as Dubai and Abu Dhabi do. A large share of Ajman households have at least one parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, which pushes the realistic start of a weekday session later than it would be in the capital. Those two facts shape the practical sections at the end of this page more than anything else about the city does. The emirate's IB cohorts are also small, which matters in a way parents only discover at option time: a Higher Level group of four or five, taught by a teacher who also carries two other courses, leaves less room for a student who has fallen behind to be caught inside the school day.

One thing stated at the top because it changes what to expect: every lesson for an Ajman family runs over live video, one-to-one. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which is a service we run only in India. The reason that works in Ajman's favour is supply. The number of people within driving distance of Al Nuaimiya who can mark a Higher Level Chemistry investigation against its criteria is small. The number who can do it over video at 19:30 on a Tuesday is not.

ajman/ib-tutor.programmesIntro: An IB report means something different in each programme, and so does the work a tutor can usefully do. Establish which programme your child is in before anything else; parents are often surprised by the answer in Year 10 and Year 11.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led programme with no external examinations. Work is assessed internally against learning outcomes, and the final year culminates in an exhibition that students plan and present themselves. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, which is why a parent can read a full PYP report and still not know whether their child is secure in written multiplication or in writing a paragraph with a controlling idea.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the practical use of tuition at this stage is narrow and worth stating honestly: arithmetic fluency, reading stamina and handwriting speed. Those three travel into every later programme. Paying for inquiry support in Year 4 generally buys enthusiasm the school is already generating.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each scored on a 1 to 8 scale, with the criteria describing different skills rather than different difficulty levels. A student can score 7 on knowledge and understanding and 3 on the criterion that asks them to evaluate or to reflect, and the overall grade hides that completely. The programme ends with a personal project that the student designs, carries out and documents.
programmes.countryNote: This is where Ajman families most often misread a report. A level 5 is not a predicted Diploma 5, and the two scales measure different things. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the subject grade, because that breakdown tells you which of four skills to work on and the single grade does not.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, one from each group in most cases, taken at Higher or Standard Level, plus three core requirements: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Every subject carries externally assessed papers and an internally assessed component marked by the school and moderated externally. The exact weightings differ by subject and are published in each subject guide.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman's IB cohorts are small, which has a specific consequence: option blocks are tight, and a student may be taking a subject at Higher Level in a group of four taught by a teacher covering two other courses. That is where external one-to-one support earns its place, and it is why most of our Ajman Diploma enquiries name a single subject rather than a general difficulty.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core is assessed differently from the six subjects. Theory of Knowledge is examined through an exhibition of objects and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is an independent piece of research supervised within the school; creativity, activity and service is a requirement rather than a graded component. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute additional points to the Diploma total.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman students usually meet the core in the middle of DP1, when they are also meeting the hardest content of two Higher Levels. The failure mode is almost never ability; it is sequencing. A tutor's job here is process coaching and questioning a draft the student has written, never authorship, and the distinction is one worth agreeing out loud in the first session.

ajman/ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: What follows is grouped the way the Diploma is grouped, because the technique that earns marks changes from group to group. These are the subjects Ajman families ask for most, with the place the marks are usually sitting.

subjects.name: Language A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed on analysis of how texts work rather than on what they say. Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis, and the usual loss is a response that summarises the extract before the first analytical sentence appears. The individual oral requires a global issue traced through two texts, and students under-prepare the connective argument rather than the content.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course, not a literature course, and the difference is the whole of the grade. Productive marks reward register, audience and text type, so an essay written where a blog was asked for loses conceptual marks before the language is even read. Receptive papers reward precise reading rather than broad comprehension.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The most common mark loss in the whole of Group 3: narrative where argument was asked for. Source questions have fixed shapes and reward a stated provenance and a judgement; essay questions reward a thesis maintained across paragraphs. Both are trainable in a handful of sessions once the pattern is named.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, and most students draw them from memory rather than labelling them to the question. Evaluation sits at the end of long answers and is the single most frequently unwritten set of marks. The internally assessed commentaries reward applying one concept to a current article precisely, not summarising the article.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Recall is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. Extended answers are marked against command terms, and data-based questions reward reading the axes carefully before reasoning. The scientific investigation is assessed on the quality of the question and the handling of uncertainty far more than on whether the experiment worked.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two separate failure modes. Quantitative work fails on units and on rounding too early; organic chemistry fails because reactions are memorised as isolated facts rather than as routes between functional groups. A tutor who treats both as one weakness repairs neither, which is why diagnosis comes before teaching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks are awarded for method as well as answer, so working done mentally is working unmarked. The common Ajman pattern is a student who understands the physics and writes two lines where five were available. Data analysis and uncertainty treatment carry criteria of their own in the investigation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, algebraic manipulation and calculus depth distinguish this route. Higher Level adds genuine content rather than harder versions of the same content, and students stepping up from a Middle Years course frequently meet formal proof for the first time. Method marks reward sequence written down, not sequence thought.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led work, with the graphic display calculator central rather than incidental. The usual loss is interpretation: a correct regression with no sentence saying what it means in context. The exploration rewards a genuine question with data behind it.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and the performing subjects
subjects.description: Assessed on process and on written reflection as much as on the finished work, which surprises families every year. The comparative study and the process portfolio are where marks are gained and lost, and both are documentation skills that can be taught directly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Marked on the quality of knowledge questions asked, not on the breadth of examples cited. The exhibition asks for three objects connected to a prompt and justified; the essay answers a prescribed title. Both reward precision about how a claim is known rather than confident assertion.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Mandatory federal requirements that sit beside the licensed curriculum rather than inside it. Teaching conditions, including the language of instruction and the separation of classes for Arab and non-Arab students, are set centrally. Ajman families tell us this is the hardest stream to resource locally.

regions.note: Dense apartment district close to the Sharjah boundary, with many households commuting out of the emirate. Sessions here typically start at 19:00 or later, and a quiet room is more often the constraint than the schedule.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central and mixed, with families who have moved between curricula more than once. Enquiries here are often about whether a Middle Years report translates into a Diploma prediction, which it does not.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa district, longer school runs, and households running several children through one evening. The usual question is sequencing: which child gets the standing weekly hour this term.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: Established residential area where our enquiries skew towards DP1 students carrying three Higher Levels. The conversation is usually about load distribution rather than about a single subject.

regions.name: Al Jurf

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Zorah

schoolClusters.city: Ajman
schoolClusters.note: Ajman's private schools run British, Indian and IB curricula under federal Ministry of Education oversight, and the IB provision in the emirate is concentrated rather than widespread. Students we support attend schools across this group.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and northern Dubai, within commuting distance
schoolClusters.note: A significant number of Ajman households drive a child across the emirate boundary for school, which is why a 16:00 session almost never survives the return journey and why our Ajman slots cluster after 18:30.

ajman/ib-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of arrangement, all delivered one-to-one over live video. Which one fits depends on whether the problem is content, technique or an internally assessed component with a school deadline.

modes.title: Weekly subject one-to-one
modes.description: A standing hour in one subject, held through the term. The session divides into reviewing work set since the last meeting, teaching the next piece of content or technique, and setting a timed task against the real command terms. This is the shape that produces a readable record, because eight marked pieces laid side by side show whether the same criterion is still scoring low.

modes.title: Internally assessed component support
modes.description: A short block around a school deadline for the scientific investigation, a mathematics exploration, an economics commentary or the Theory of Knowledge exhibition. The work is the student's throughout. The tutor's contribution is process: whether the question is answerable, whether the data can carry the argument, whether the criteria have been read, and what a weak paragraph is actually missing.

modes.title: Pre-examination technique block
modes.description: Six to ten hours concentrated in the weeks before the May session, aimed at command terms, timing across a paper and the specific marks a student repeatedly leaves on the table. It is the right purchase when content is broadly secure. It is the wrong purchase when a Higher Level syllabus is substantially missing, and we will say that at the diagnostic rather than afterwards.
