sections.heading: Which of the three IB programmes is your child actually in?
paragraphs: This sounds like a question with an obvious answer and it is routinely answered wrongly, because the programme names do not map neatly onto year groups and because Ajman families frequently move schools and curricula. A Year 11 student might be in the final Middle Years year, or in an IGCSE year at an IB school, or in the first Diploma year if the school runs an early start. Each of those means a different report, a different assessment model and a different job for a tutor.

In the Primary Years Programme there are no external examinations at all, and reporting is descriptive. In the Middle Years Programme each subject is assessed against four criteria on a 1 to 8 scale, where the criteria describe different skills rather than levels of difficulty. In the Diploma Programme, each subject has externally assessed papers plus an internally assessed component, and the grade is on a 1 to 7 scale with the total built from six subjects plus the core.

The consequence for spending is direct. A Middle Years criterion level of 4 in Criterion D tells you exactly what to work on, and the subject grade tells you nothing actionable. A Diploma 4 in a Higher Level science can mean a content gap or a technique gap, and the two take different amounts of time. Asking the school for the criterion breakdown, or for the component marks behind a Diploma prediction, costs nothing and changes what you buy.

The table sets the three programmes plus the core against what a report contains, what it hides and what a tutor can usefully move. Read the last column before agreeing to a weekly hour, because in one of the four rows the honest answer is that very little tutoring is required and the money is better left unspent.

sections.heading: The six subject groups, and what each one is actually marked on
paragraphs: The Diploma is built from six groups: studies in language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, the sciences, mathematics, and the arts. Students take one from most groups, at Higher or Standard Level. The useful thing about the group structure for a parent is that each group rewards a different skill, which means a tutor who is excellent in one group may add very little in another even if they know the content.

In Group 1 the skill is analysis of how a text works. In Group 2 it is control of register, audience and text type in a language being acquired. In Group 3 the skill is argument sustained across an essay and judgement applied to sources. In Group 4 it is precise use of command terms plus the handling of data and uncertainty. In Group 5 it is written method and, on the technology papers, interpretation of what a result means. In Group 6 the assessed object is as much the documented process as the finished work.

That is why our Ajman matches are made within one or two groups rather than across all six. A parent asking for help with a Diploma generally is asking a question we cannot answer usefully; a parent asking for Higher Level Chemistry, where Paper 2 long answers are scoring in the lower bands, is asking something a specialist can act on in the first hour.

The table names each group, the subjects Ajman students most commonly take in it, what the assessment actually rewards and where the marks typically go. It is also a reasonable checklist for a conversation with your child's coordinator, because the same question put group by group produces much better answers than one general question about progress.

sections.heading: Group 1 and Group 2: the language route that quietly sets a ceiling
paragraphs: In a household like many in Ajman, where more than one language is spoken at home and the school teaches in English, the Group 1 and Group 2 choices are the most consequential decisions in the whole option form, and they are usually made in forty minutes at a parents' evening. They determine what the student is marked against for two years.

The first fork is inside Group 1: Language A Literature or Language A Language and Literature. Literature works with literary texts and rewards sustained close reading. Language and Literature adds non-literary texts — advertising, journalism, speeches — and rewards analysis of how any text positions a reader. Students who read widely and dislike unseen non-fiction often do better in Literature; students who are sharp about rhetoric and less patient with long novels often do better in the other.

The second fork is between a Group 1 course and a Group 2 course in the same language. English B is a language-acquisition course with productive and receptive components, and for a genuinely bilingual student it can look like an easier grade. It is not automatically a better choice, because some university routes expect a Group 1 English and because a strong candidate in an acquisition course is still marked on register and text type, which is a discipline of its own. Some students also take two Group 1 languages and no Group 2, which is a legitimate route.

What a tutor can do here is honest and limited. We cannot advise on your child's university plans and should not pretend to. What we can do is look at a recent piece of writing in each candidate course and say what it is scoring on, which fork plays to the skills already present, and what the gap would be in either direction. That conversation is worth having before the option form, not after the first mock.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks actually go missing, pattern by pattern
paragraphs: Across the Ajman Diploma students we see, the same five patterns account for most of the gap between what a parent expects and what the report says. None of them is a knowledge problem, which is why more revision of content is the most common and least effective response.

The first is command-term blindness: answering the question that was recognised rather than the one that was set, which costs most of the marks on every extended answer in Groups 3 and 4. The second is unwritten method: a correct answer with the reasoning in the student's head, which is unmarkable in Group 5 and in the quantitative parts of Group 4. The third is unwritten evaluation, concentrated in Economics, Business Management and the sciences, where the final paragraph of a long answer carries marks that students simply never reach.

The fourth is time distribution across a paper: three immaculate answers and one blank, which no amount of subject knowledge fixes. The fifth is the internally assessed component treated as an essay rather than as a criterion-marked piece, so a student with a genuinely interesting investigation loses marks on the handling of uncertainty or on the quality of the research question.

Each has a different repair time, and the table gives them honestly. Two are matters of weeks. One is a matter of a term. One requires the student to change a habit, which no tutor can do on their behalf. A tutor who tells you all five are quick wins has not diagnosed anything.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary the examiner is marking against
paragraphs: The IB publishes its command terms and groups them by assessment objective, and the single highest-value hour a tutor can spend with a Diploma student is often the one that goes through them. Students treat describe, explain, analyse, evaluate and discuss as stylistic variations on the word write. The mark schemes do not.

The difference is structural rather than decorative. Describe asks for features, so a list of accurate features earns full marks. Explain asks for a causal chain, so the same features with no because earns part. Analyse asks for the components and how they interact. Evaluate and discuss ask for a judgement supported against alternatives, and a long answer with no judgement cannot reach the top band however accurate it is. To what extent is a judgement question wearing a disguise.

This is trainable fast, which is why it leads the technique sections of most of our Ajman plans. The method is unglamorous: take a six- or eight-mark question from the student's own subject, write the answer twice, once as the student instinctively would and once to the command term, and mark both against the published criteria. Three or four rounds of that in different subjects usually transfers.

The table gives the terms Ajman students most often meet, what each one actually requires and the answer shape that loses the marks. Print it and put it next to the desk; it is more use in the week before a paper than another set of flashcards.

sections.heading: Which subject to buy help in, when it is the total that matters
paragraphs: A Diploma total is built from six subject grades plus the core, and that changes the spending question in a way most families do not notice. The instinct is to support the lowest grade. The arithmetic often disagrees, because a grade already at 3 in a subject the student dislikes may be expensive to move, while a 5 that is one technique repair away from a 6 may be cheap.

Three tests sort this out quickly. First, is the gap technique or content? A 5 held back by unwritten evaluation moves faster than a 4 held back by a missing third of a Higher Level syllabus. Second, is the student's internally assessed component still open? Marks that are not yet submitted are easier to influence than marks already banked. Third, does any university route your child is considering name a specific subject or level? If it does, that subject is not negotiable regardless of where the cheap gains are.

The honest conclusion is often to buy help in one subject rather than two, and to ask the school for the component-level marks behind each prediction before deciding. Coordinators can usually supply them, and the breakdown converts a vague worry about the total into a specific list of movable marks.

What we will not do is build a plan around a points target and imply the plan delivers it. Nobody can promise a Diploma score, and a provider who prices a package against a predicted total is selling something they cannot control. What is honest is to identify the movable marks, work on them, and show you the marked evidence weekly so you can judge whether the work is landing.

sections.heading: What one weekly hour fixes, and what needs a term
paragraphs: One hour a week is thirty-odd hours across an academic year, and knowing what that buys prevents both over-spending and disappointment. It is comfortably enough to retrain command-term technique in one subject, to install the habit of written method, to teach how to close an evaluative answer, and to walk a student through criteria for an internally assessed component. All four are discrete skills with observable results inside a month.

It is not enough to rebuild a missing Higher Level syllabus. If a student has not secured the first year of Higher Level Chemistry, the content deficit is measured in dozens of teaching hours, and an hour a week spread across a year will be consumed by whatever is urgent that week. The honest options in that situation are narrower and worth naming: more hours over a shorter period, a decision to drop to Standard Level if the school allows it, or a decision to protect the other five subjects instead.

Nor can an hour a week supply motivation or supervision. A tutor on video can see the work, mark it, and tell you when it has not been done. They cannot make a seventeen-year-old sit down at eight o'clock. Where that is the real problem, the sessions become expensive weekly evidence of the same fact, and we would rather say so at the diagnostic than invoice around it for a term.

The practical test we use with Ajman families at week six: lay out the marked work and ask whether the criterion we targeted has moved. If it has, the arrangement is working and the next target is chosen. If it has not, either the diagnosis was wrong or the set work is not being done, and those have different remedies. That review is the point where an honest provider is willing to recommend stopping.

sections.heading: Ajman evenings, the federal regulator, and when a session can realistically start
paragraphs: Private schools in Ajman are overseen by the federal Ministry of Education, as are those in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, rather than by an emirate-level authority of the kind Dubai and Abu Dhabi operate. Across the country, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is what sits underneath every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

For a tutoring plan the oversight question matters less than the commute. A substantial share of Ajman households have a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, and a meaningful number drive a child across the emirate boundary for school. The result is that the weekday evening starts later here than in Abu Dhabi, and a 16:00 session booked optimistically in September is usually a 19:00 session by October. Our Ajman slots cluster between 18:30 and 21:00 for that reason.

Two further calendar facts worth planning around. Ramadan compresses the school day and shifts family routines, and the useful adjustment is usually a shorter, later session rather than a cancelled one; several families move to post-Iftar timing for the month and keep the weekly rhythm. And the final weeks before the May session collide with internal deadlines for the core, which is why the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work belongs much earlier in DP1 than most students schedule it.

The mandatory subjects deserve a note of their own. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed curriculum, with teaching conditions set centrally, including requirements about the language of instruction and about organising separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Any tutoring in those subjects has to work within what the Ministry permits, and material cannot be substituted freely, which is a real constraint rather than a formality.

sections.heading: How lessons are delivered, and the home-tutor question answered plainly
paragraphs: Every lesson for an Ajman family runs over live video, one-to-one, at a time set in Gulf Standard Time. The student needs a device with a camera, a reliable connection, paper and the same desk each week. Written work is photographed and shared before the session so the tutor has already marked it, which is what keeps the hour about the marks rather than about reading.

A good number of families start by asking for somebody to come round, and it is fairer to answer that directly than to steer around it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The market option genuinely exists, and the published bands for it are worth knowing: a 2026 Dubai cost survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors charging AED 200 to 500 once travel sits inside the rate, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200 and up for IB specialist work as published by Unitors.

What video delivery buys in Ajman is supply. The Diploma is a specialist programme and the emirate's cohorts are small, so the set of people who can mark a Higher Level Physics investigation against its criteria and the set of people who live twenty minutes from Al Rawda barely intersect. Removing the travel constraint changes which of those two sets you are choosing from.

The honest limits belong here rather than in a footnote. A screen is worse at supervision, cannot handle laboratory apparatus, and reads a room less well than a person at the same table. Where supervision is the actual requirement, a local visiting tutor from the market is the sensible recommendation and we will say so at the diagnostic. For the typical Ajman enquiry — one Higher Level subject, a grade below target, a May session ahead — the format is not a compromise at all.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the line a tutor works inside
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, and all of it must be the student's own. The boundary is clear and worth stating because this market contains operators who sell the other side of it: one advertises finished internal assessments for a four-figure sum, which is a malpractice trigger for the student and not a service any tutor should be near.

What a tutor may properly do is substantial. Read the criteria with the student. Question whether a research question can actually be answered with the data available. Ask what a paragraph is trying to establish. Point at a thin section and say why it is thin. Teach the subject skill the component is assessing. Mark a timed task. What a tutor may not be is the author of any part of the submitted piece, and a parent should treat an offer to help in that direction as disqualifying rather than convenient.

The test is whether the student could defend every sentence and every choice to their own supervisor. If they could not, the work is not theirs, and the consequence falls on them rather than on whoever supplied the text. Schools ask students to confirm authorship, and that confirmation is not a formality.

The same principle governs materials. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies; the right way to use them is to reference the official pages and work from what the school has legitimately issued. We also do not publish IB session or results dates on these pages, because those dates have not been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project. Confirm every date with your child's coordinator, who holds the school's own version of the calendar.

process.title: Name the subject and the level, not the programme
process.description: Higher Level Chemistry with Paper 2 long answers in the lower bands is a brief a specialist can act on in the first hour. Help with the IB is not. Send the subject, the level, the year group, a recent marked piece and the two evening windows that genuinely work for your household.

process.title: We match inside the subject group
process.description: Because the assessment objectives differ group by group, we match on the group and level rather than on general IB experience. You get a named tutor, their subject and level coverage, and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time — or a straight statement that we cannot cover it this week.

process.title: A free diagnostic hour
process.description: No payment taken beforehand. The tutor works from the student's own script and reports in writing: which loss patterns are present, which of them are weeks of work and which are a term, and what the first three weeks will target. If the conclusion is that tutoring is not the bottleneck, you will be told then.

process.title: Weekly timed work, marked before the session
process.description: A task every week against the real command terms, sat to time, photographed and sent ahead so it is marked before the hour starts. The session is spent on the marks. A written note follows naming the criterion targeted and whether it moved.

process.title: The week-six evidence review
process.description: Parent, student and tutor look at six marked pieces together and answer one question: has the targeted criterion moved? If yes, the next target is chosen. If no, the plan or the match changes. If the evidence says the money is better spent elsewhere, we say that.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the subject group, not to the city
whyPoints.description: Ajman's IB cohorts are small and its local specialist pool is correspondingly thin. Video delivery means the person who marks Higher Level Physics investigations weekly can take your 19:30 slot regardless of where they live, which is the concrete advantage of the format rather than a marketing line.

whyPoints.title: Assessment-led rather than content-led
whyPoints.description: The first session reads the script against the assessment objectives and names the loss pattern. Most Diploma grades that sit below expectation are held there by command terms, unwritten method or unwritten evaluation, and all three are visible in a single piece of marked work.

whyPoints.title: Evidence a non-specialist can read
whyPoints.description: Marked pieces, a criterion log and a written note after each hour. A parent does not need the subject guide to see whether the same criterion is still scoring low in week eight. Any claim about progress on this site is built from that record.

whyPoints.title: The authorship line agreed in the first session
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark and coach process. They are never the author of internally assessed work and they do not distribute board materials. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments; the distinction is worth making explicit before you start.

whyPoints.title: No regulator endorsement claimed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is not approved, accredited or endorsed by the International Baccalaureate, by the Ministry of Education or by any emirate education authority, and nothing on this site says otherwise. Regulators are named here to explain what they govern.

whyPoints.title: Slots that survive the Ajman commute
whyPoints.description: Sessions cluster between 18:30 and 21:00 because that is when households with a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah are actually free, and shift later during Ramadan rather than disappearing. A standing slot that cannot be kept is not a plan.

faqs.question: Which IB programme is my child in, and does it change what a tutor can do?
faqs.answer: It changes it completely. In the Primary Years Programme there are no external examinations and the useful tutoring targets are narrow: arithmetic fluency, reading stamina, handwriting speed. In the Middle Years Programme each subject is scored against four criteria on a 1 to 8 scale, so the actionable information is the criterion breakdown rather than the subject grade. In the Diploma, each subject has external papers plus an internally assessed component, and a grade below target can be a content gap or a technique gap, which take very different amounts of time. Ask the school which programme and, in the Middle Years, for the criterion-level detail.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma subject group mean when I am choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Each of the six groups rewards a different skill, so subject-group fit matters more than general IB experience. Group 1 rewards analysis of how a text works. Group 2 rewards control of register and text type in an acquired language. Group 3 rewards argument sustained across an essay and judgement on sources. Group 4 rewards command-term precision and the handling of data and uncertainty. Group 5 rewards written method and interpretation. Group 6 rewards documented process as much as outcome. A tutor strong in one group can add little in another even with good content knowledge.

faqs.question: Should my child take Language A Literature or Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: They are marked on different things. Literature works with literary texts and rewards sustained close reading of them. Language and Literature adds non-literary material — journalism, advertising, speeches — and rewards analysis of how any text positions its reader. A student who reads widely but dislikes unseen non-fiction often fares better in Literature; one who is sharp about rhetoric and impatient with long novels often fares better in the other. The practical way to decide is to look at a recent piece of the student's own analytical writing and see which skill it already shows, before the option form goes in.

faqs.question: For a bilingual Ajman student, is English B an easier grade than Language A?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is not automatically the better choice and the reasons are not only about difficulty. English B is a language-acquisition course assessed on receptive and productive skills, and a strong bilingual candidate is still marked on register, audience and the conventions of the text type the task asked for, which is a discipline of its own. Some university routes expect a Group 1 English. Two Group 1 languages with no Group 2 is also a legitimate route. Ask the coordinator what the school's leavers have found, and treat the decision as a route question rather than a difficulty question.

faqs.question: Where do IB Diploma students in Ajman most often lose marks?
faqs.answer: Five patterns cover most of it, and none is a knowledge problem. Answering the command term that was recognised rather than the one set. Leaving the method in the student's head, so a correct answer has one line of working above it. Stopping a long answer before any judgement, which forfeits the evaluation marks. Mismanaging time so three answers are immaculate and one is blank. And treating an internally assessed component as an essay rather than as criterion-marked work. The first three repair in weeks. Time management is a habit and takes a term.

faqs.question: If the Diploma total is what matters, which subject should we actually support?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily the lowest grade. Three tests sort it quickly. Is the gap technique or content, since a 5 held back by unwritten evaluation moves faster than a 4 missing a third of a Higher Level syllabus? Is the internally assessed component still open, because unsubmitted marks are easier to influence than banked ones? And does any university route name a specific subject or level, in which case that subject is not negotiable. Ask the coordinator for component-level marks behind each prediction first; it turns a worry about the total into a list of movable marks.

faqs.question: What can a single weekly hour of IB tutoring realistically repair?
faqs.answer: An hour a week is thirty-odd hours across a year. That is comfortably enough to retrain command-term technique in one subject, install the habit of written method, teach how to close an evaluative answer and walk a student through the criteria for an internally assessed component. It is not enough to rebuild a missing Higher Level syllabus, which is measured in dozens of teaching hours, and it cannot supply supervision or motivation. If the real problem is that the work is not being started, weekly sessions become expensive evidence of that rather than a remedy.

faqs.question: What are IB command terms, and why do they decide the grade?
faqs.answer: They are the published verbs that open examination questions, grouped by assessment objective, and each one specifies a different answer shape. Describe asks for features. Explain asks for a causal chain, so an accurate description with no because in it takes part marks. Analyse asks for components and their interaction. Evaluate and discuss ask for a judgement supported against an alternative, which is why a balanced, accurate answer with no judgement cannot reach the top band. To what extent is a judgement question in disguise. This is trainable in a few sessions and is usually the highest-value hour available.

faqs.question: How late can a tutoring session start in Ajman on a school night?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect, and that is usually a feature. A large share of Ajman households have a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, and a number drive a child across the emirate boundary for school, so a 16:00 slot booked in September tends to become a 19:00 slot by October. Our Ajman sessions cluster between 18:30 and 21:00 for that reason. During Ramadan many families move to a shorter session after Iftar and keep the weekly rhythm rather than pausing, which works better than cancelling a month and restarting.

faqs.question: Who oversees private schools in Ajman, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which also supervises private schools in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, rather than an emirate-level authority of the kind Dubai's and Abu Dhabi's regulators provide. Private schools across the country are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For a tutoring plan the direct effects are two: the mandatory subjects run alongside the licensed curriculum with centrally set conditions, and school-level inspection information is less granular than a Dubai parent would expect.

faqs.question: Does a Middle Years level 5 mean my child is on track for a Diploma 5?
faqs.answer: No, and reading it that way causes real problems in Year 11. The Middle Years scale scores four criteria from 1 to 8 within each subject, and the criteria describe different skills rather than levels of difficulty. A student can score 7 on knowledge and understanding and 3 on the criterion that asks for evaluation or reflection, and the reported subject grade averages that away. The Diploma uses a 1 to 7 subject scale built from external papers and an internally assessed component. Ask for the criterion breakdown; the low criterion is the thing worth working on.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB tutor to our home in Ajman, or is everything over video?
faqs.answer: Everything for UAE families is one-to-one over live video, at times set in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The in-home market exists and the published bands are worth knowing — a 2026 Dubai cost survey puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel is inside the rate. What video delivery buys in a small emirate is supply: the specialist who marks your child's component weekly rarely lives nearby.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and the prescribed-title essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can read the assessment criteria with the student, question whether the three objects genuinely connect to the chosen prompt, ask what a paragraph is trying to establish, and say why a justification is thin. What a tutor must never be is the author of any part of the submitted work, and an offer in that direction should end the conversation with that provider. The practical test is whether your child could defend every sentence and every choice to their own supervisor. Schools ask students to confirm authorship, and that confirmation is not a formality.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does an Ajman Diploma student actually have spare?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a tutoring plan usually assumes. Six subjects, two or three at Higher Level, plus the core and a creativity, activity and service commitment, already fill most weekday evenings, and a cross-emirate school run removes another hour from each end of the day. This is why we rarely recommend more than one or two tutored subjects at a time: adding three weekly hours does not add three hours of capacity, it displaces homework. The better question is which single subject has the most movable marks, and then protecting the rest with the school's own support.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no IB specialist free for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is more than this market usually does. Mathematics, the three sciences, English A and B, Economics, Business Management and Psychology are generally coverable within a few days at both levels. Less common requests take longer: some ab initio languages, the arts subjects at Higher Level, and Arabic as a first language. Where we cannot cover something, the useful thing we can still do is say where the gap is so you look in the right place rather than waiting on a maybe. No IB session or results date is published on these pages, because those dates are not confirmed for this project.

ajman/ib-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one subject and one marked script
ajman/ib-tutor.closingBody: The quickest route to a useful plan is narrow. Send the subject, the level, the year group, a photograph of a recent marked piece and the two evening windows that genuinely work in your household, and we will arrange a free diagnostic hour with a tutor who works in that subject group. You will get a written diagnosis afterwards: which loss patterns are present, which are weeks of work and which are a term, and what the first three weeks will target. If the honest conclusion is that the school's own support or a different subject is the better place for the money, we will tell you that instead. Nothing is taken before the first lesson.

ajman/ib-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named Diploma subjects at a named level. Each works inside one or two subject groups, because the Higher Level material and the internally assessed component in each group reward different things, and a tutor who has marked one of them has not thereby marked the others.

intro.heading: A near-me search is a supply question, and in Ajman the supply is subject by subject
paragraphs: Search for a local IGCSE tutor in most UAE cities and you get a long list. Search for a local IB Diploma tutor in Ajman and the list collapses, which surprises parents who assume the difference is advertising. It is not. The Diploma is a specialist programme, Ajman's IB provision is concentrated rather than widespread, and the set of people within driving distance who have taught Higher Level Chemistry to examination and marked an investigation against its criteria is genuinely small.

That makes the near-me question a different question than it first appears. It is not really about distance. It is about whether the subject and level your child needs can be staffed at all inside a twenty-minute radius, and the answer varies enormously across the six subject groups. Mathematics and Biology are usually coverable locally. Higher Level Chemistry, Psychology, Computer Science and anything in Group 2 beyond the common languages frequently are not, at any price.

So this page is organised by subject rather than by geography. For each of the scarce ones it states what the Higher Level material actually adds, where the marks go, what one session can fix fastest and what no session can fix. That is more useful to an Ajman parent than a map, because a map tells you who is nearby and tells you nothing about whether they have ever marked the component your child is about to submit.

Two local facts do matter, and they are not the ones usually published. The first is the evening: with many Ajman households having a parent working in Dubai or Sharjah, and some driving a child across the emirate boundary to school, the window in which a weekday session reliably happens runs from roughly 18:30 to 21:00. The second is the examination centre, which is a genuinely local matter and is discussed below, because it affects a Diploma candidate in a way a tutor's postcode does not. A third fact sits behind both: private schools in Ajman are overseen by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate-level authority, so the school-level information a Dubai parent takes for granted is less granular here, and questions put directly to the coordinator carry more weight than anything a listing can tell you.

One thing said plainly at the top. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Ajman family is one-to-one over live video. That is why the subject rather than the postcode decides the match, and it is the reason this page can be honest about which subjects are thin locally instead of pretending the radius is irrelevant or that it is everything.
bullets: Local supply is thick in Mathematics and Biology, thin in HL Chemistry, Psychology and Group 2
The teacher at your child's own school is the one local option to avoid
The examination centre is the local fact that actually affects a candidate
Ajman's reliable weekday window is roughly 18:30 to 21:00
Coverage is stated per subject and level, including where we cannot help

ajman/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Supply varies by programme as well as by subject, and the three programmes fail a near-me search in different ways. Establish which one your child is in before judging whether a short local list is a problem.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, scored 1 to 8, with the criteria describing different skills rather than levels of difficulty. The programme closes with a personal project the student designs and documents. The teaching demand is wide rather than deep, which is why local supply here is reasonably good: a strong secondary teacher in the subject can work to the criteria once they have read them.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman a near-me search at this stage usually succeeds, and that is worth knowing because it tells you something about the Diploma result later. If a local list is short for Year 9 Mathematics, the problem is advertising. If it is short for Higher Level Mathematics, the problem is supply.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Standard Level
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, with Standard Level courses carrying external papers plus an internally assessed component. A capable teacher from a British or Indian curriculum background can often cover Standard Level content competently, which is why local lists are longer at this level than at Higher Level and why many quotes you receive will quietly be for a tutor whose Diploma experience stops here.
programmes.countryNote: The question to ask any local candidate is specific: which level have you taught to examination, and have you marked the internally assessed component in this subject? A Standard Level answer to a Higher Level problem is the most common mismatch in this emirate, and it is invisible until the first draft comes back.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, Higher Level
programmes.description: Where the near-me search fails hardest. Higher Level courses add genuine additional content rather than harder versions of the same material, carry heavier internally assessed demands, and are examined on depth. The pool of people who have taught a specific Higher Level course to examination is small nationally and smaller still inside one small emirate.
programmes.countryNote: This is the level at which most of our Ajman enquiries arrive, and it is the level at which proximity is least able to deliver. A household in Al Rawda choosing between a nearby generalist and a remote specialist in Higher Level Chemistry is not choosing between convenience and quality; it is choosing between two different subjects.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Assessed through an exhibition of three objects with written justifications, a prescribed-title essay, and a supervised independent research piece. Supervision stays with the school. The outside contribution is questioning: whether a research question can be answered, whether an object illustrates the prompt it is attached to, whether a justification could be disagreed with.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is the one area where local supply is almost irrelevant, because the work is documents and conversations. It is also the area Ajman students most often leave too late, since the core arrives in the middle of DP1 at exactly the point two Higher Levels get hard.

ajman/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Below, the subjects an Ajman near-me search handles well and the ones it does not, with what the Higher Level material actually adds in each case. Treat the thin ones as a reason to widen the search rather than to lower the specification.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.levels: HL and SL · usually coverable locally at SL
subjects.description: Standard Level is the best-supplied Diploma course in the emirate. Higher Level is not, because it adds proof, deeper calculus and content that exists nowhere else, and a tutor from an A Level background meets some of it for the first time. The marks go to method written down rather than held in the head.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.levels: HL and SL · thinner locally than Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Technology is central rather than incidental, so a tutor has to teach the graphic display calculator as an instrument rather than mention it. The lost marks are interpretive: a correct regression with no sentence saying what it means in context. Fewer local tutors have taught this route than the Analysis one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: HL and SL · reasonably coverable locally
subjects.description: The best-supplied of the three sciences, because the content maps onto A Level and IGCSE teaching more closely than Chemistry or Physics. Marks go to command-term discipline in extended answers and to the handling of uncertainty in the investigation, both of which need marked practice rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: HL · genuinely scarce in the northern emirates
subjects.description: Higher Level adds substantial material and two separate failure modes that need two different drills: quantitative work failing on units and early rounding, organic work failing on pathway recall. The investigation's evaluation criterion rewards named instrument limits, not general caution. Few local candidates have marked it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mark loss is cheap to fix once named — method unwritten, so a correct answer sits above one line of working — and the Higher Level extension material is where a generalist stalls. Data analysis and uncertainty carry criteria of their own in the investigation, and that is specialist marking rather than general science teaching.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.levels: HL and SL · rarely available locally
subjects.description: Reads accessibly and is assessed severely, which is why families underestimate it. Marks sit in precise terminology, in command-term discipline, and in an experimental study whose design has to be able to test what the student set out to test. Very few teachers in a small emirate have taught the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: HL and SL · moderate local supply
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked and most are drawn from memory rather than labelled to the question. Evaluation sits at the end of long answers and is the single most frequently unwritten set of marks in the subject. The commentaries reward one concept applied precisely to a current article.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.levels: HL and SL · moderate local supply
subjects.description: The expensive mistake is an internally assessed component built around an organisation the student cannot get information from, which turns into weeks of rescue work. Testing that in week one takes twenty minutes. Content is accessible; the marks are in application and evaluation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Two halves that fail separately. Theory needs exact terminology; programming work can run correctly and still lose marks because it was never explained. The Higher Level case study has a hard internal timeline, and starting late here is more costly than in any other subject.

subjects.name: English A and English B
subjects.levels: HL and SL · reasonable local supply
subjects.description: Group 1 rewards analysis of how a text produces its effects, and the individual oral rewards a connective argument between two works. Group 2 rewards register, audience and text type. Local supply is decent, but a tutor used to IGCSE English frequently marks Group 1 work for fluency rather than against the criteria.

subjects.name: Group 2 ab initio languages
subjects.description: Spanish, French or Mandarin from the beginning, assessed on productive and receptive skills in a language the student has had for two years. The pool is small nationally and almost nil inside Ajman. When a family needs this, a remote match is not a convenience, it is the only route.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Governed federally, with centrally set teaching conditions including the language of instruction and the requirement that classes for Arab and non-Arab students be organised separately. Families tell us this is the hardest stream to resource locally, and material cannot be substituted freely by a private tutor.

ajman/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: What "near me" actually covers from each part of Ajman
ajman/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The districts below are the ones we hear from. The note on each is about what the local pool and the household's evening really permit, rather than about distance in kilometres.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Closest to Sharjah and therefore to the largest nearby pool of teachers, which makes a local list longest here. It is also the district where a quiet room is hardest to find, so the constraint moves from supply to space.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central, with reasonable access from both Sharjah and central Ajman. A local Standard Level Mathematics or Biology match is realistic here; a local Higher Level Chemistry match generally is not, whatever a listing suggests.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Spread-out villa district where internal drives are long enough to narrow the pool by a further step. Households here often need two subjects at once, which compounds the problem: two local specialists is a much harder ask than one.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: A high share of DP1 and DP2 students, and the district from which we receive the most Higher Level science enquiries. Demand concentrates in the same evening window, so a standing slot fixed in September is worth more than a shorter drive.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: On the Sharjah side, with long approaches from central Dubai and a correspondingly thin local field in specialist subjects. Later starts are normal, which removes the early-evening hour a visiting tutor would need to make a trip worthwhile.

regions.name: Al Helio
regions.note: Newer housing with younger families, so Middle Years enquiries outnumber Diploma ones and the near-me search usually succeeds. That changes abruptly at Year 12, which catches households out when a sibling reaches the Diploma.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Zorah
regions.note: Lower density and shorter school runs, so slightly earlier sessions are workable. Group 4 investigation enquiries dominate, and they arrive about three weeks later in the component's life than would be ideal.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman
schoolClusters.note: IB provision in the emirate is concentrated rather than widespread, and private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight. That concentration is exactly why a Diploma near-me search returns a short list. Students we support attend schools across this group.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah, inside the daily commute
schoolClusters.note: Many Ajman households cross the boundary for school, which enlarges the nearby teacher pool slightly and removes the early evening entirely. The second effect is larger than the first, which is why our Ajman slots sit after 18:30.

ajman/ib-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Three ways an Ajman family uses a specialist who is not local, chosen by what the subject needs rather than by what is nearby.

modes.title: Weekly Higher Level subject hour
modes.description: A standing slot in one named subject at one named level, with a timed task between sessions marked before the hour starts. This is the arrangement for a Higher Level course where the content extension is the problem, and it is the one that produces a readable record: eight marked pieces show whether the targeted criterion is still scoring low.
bullets: One subject, one level, the same tutor throughout
Timed task every week, marked against the assessment objectives
A written note naming the criterion targeted and whether it moved
Held between 18:30 and 21:00 to survive the commute

modes.title: A scarce-subject block
modes.description: For Psychology, Computer Science, an ab initio language or anything else with effectively no local pool. These are usually bought as a defined block rather than as an open-ended weekly arrangement, because the specialist's time is the constrained resource and because the target is normally a named component or paper rather than general improvement.
bullets: A named target and an end date agreed before the block starts
Scheduled against the school's internal deadline, not from today
Coverage and match time stated honestly before you commit
No automatic continuation when the block ends

modes.title: Marking and feedback only
modes.description: The arrangement for a self-directed student in a well-supplied subject. They sit a paper to time, send it, and the session is spent entirely on the marked script and the criterion log. It costs a fraction of weekly teaching because the teaching hours belong to the student, and it is a waste of money if the independent work is not already happening.
bullets: One script a fortnight, sat to the real time limit
Marked against the published assessment criteria
A criterion log that accumulates across the block
Early, honest warning when the set work is not being done

sections.heading: The Higher Level problem: what the extra material actually is
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume that Higher Level is Standard Level with harder questions, and a tutor who knows the subject can therefore handle either. In several Diploma courses that is wrong in a way that matters. Higher Level adds content that does not appear at Standard Level at all, plus a heavier internally assessed demand and examination papers that test depth rather than range. A tutor who has taught Standard Level to examination has not met a meaningful part of the Higher Level course.

In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches the additional material includes formal proof and substantially deeper calculus, which is where a tutor from an A Level background can be competent and still be working from unfamiliar ground. In Chemistry and Physics the Higher Level extensions are the subject's hardest sections and the ones most likely to appear in the questions a struggling student cannot start. In Computer Science the Higher Level case study has an internal timeline of its own.

This is the single most useful filter available to an Ajman parent, and it is one question long: which level have you taught to examination, and have you marked the internally assessed component in this subject? Not which levels can you teach. Which have you taught to examination. The answer is checkable, it is specific, and the most common local mismatch in this emirate — a Standard Level answer to a Higher Level problem — becomes visible before any money is spent instead of in week five.

The table below sets out, subject by subject, what the Higher Level material adds, where the marks actually go and why the local pool is thin. Thin local supply is not a reason to accept a generalist; it is a reason to stop treating distance as the filter.

sections.heading: Group 2 and the ab initio problem
paragraphs: Language acquisition is where a near-me search in a small emirate fails most completely, and the failure is quiet because families assume a language tutor is a language tutor. A Group 2 Diploma course is not a conversational language course. It is assessed on receptive and productive skills against published criteria, with an oral built from a stimulus the student sees shortly before speaking, and productive writing marked on register, audience and the conventions of the text type the task specified.

An ab initio course compounds this. The student has had the language for two years, which means the marks available are tightly bounded and the technique matters more than the vocabulary. A native speaker with no teaching background will have an excellent conversation with your child and leave the marks exactly where they were, because the thing being assessed is the ability to organise a response quickly inside a known structure, not fluency.

What a session fixes fastest here is the shape of a spoken response: describe what is in front of you, place it in a context, take a position, extend it with an example, acknowledge an alternative. That sequence can be rehearsed until it is automatic, and it carries the time limit when the content runs out. For the written side, the drill is the same content written three times as three different text types, marked on whether each sounds like what it claims to be.

The honest position on coverage is that the common Group 2 languages are usually matchable within a week or two, and some ab initio courses are not matchable at all at short notice. When that is the case we say it rather than holding the enquiry open, because a parent who knows the gap can go and look in the right place — starting with the school, which may be able to arrange additional support internally for a course it chose to offer.

sections.heading: The teacher at your child's own school: the one local option to avoid
paragraphs: This is the most tempting near-me option and the one to leave alone. The appeal is obvious: the teacher knows the course, knows the school's internal deadlines, and knows your child. The problem is that the arrangement sits directly against the conditions attached to private tutoring in the UAE, and the exposure falls partly on a teacher who may not have read them closely.

The framework is this. Private tutoring is regulated by permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories that include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The permit carries a code of conduct, and that code has been reported as barring a permit holder from serving students affiliated with their own school. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have separately been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school.

Both of those are press-reported rather than read from the current policy documents, so verify the detail against the authority's own publication before relying on the exact wording. Ajman's private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education oversight rather than under the Abu Dhabi regulator, so the emirate-level ethics rule is not the operative one here — the permit's own conditions are. The direction of travel is clear enough in both cases that a provider marketing your child's own teacher privately is a reason for real caution rather than a convenience.

The table sets out the categories a parent actually encounters, the permit position for each, and how to check. Note the last row: a business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs its own educational services permit from the relevant authority. IB Gram holds no such permit and is not approved, accredited or endorsed by the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or any emirate authority, and claims none of those things.

sections.heading: The local fact that actually matters: where the papers are sat
paragraphs: If you are going to let geography drive a decision, let it be this one rather than the tutor's address. A Diploma candidate sits papers at a centre, under conditions set by the examination administration, on a timetable administered through the school. For a family in Ajman that is a real logistical question with real consequences, and it is the piece of local information most worth establishing early.

Ask the coordinator three things, in writing, in the first term of DP1. Where will the candidate physically sit the papers. What the arrangements are if the student is entered as a private candidate for anything. And what the school's internal deadline calendar looks like for every internally assessed component, because those deadlines sit months before anything external and are the dates that actually shape a tutoring plan.

A related point for families who move boards. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any date on a page like this should be treated as indicative and the official timetable consulted instead. For IB sessions specifically, this page publishes no date at all, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project.

The practical reason to settle all of this early is that it changes the shape of a tutoring plan rather than its content. A candidate with an internal component deadline in late January needs checkpoints in November, not a weekly hour that arrives at the deadline alongside them. The school's calendar is free, authoritative and the single most useful document in the whole arrangement.

sections.heading: What a session fixes fastest in each of the scarce subjects
paragraphs: The useful thing about specialist scarcity is that it concentrates the problem. When a parent cannot find a local Higher Level Chemistry tutor, what they actually need is rarely a complete course; it is one or two specific repairs that the school's small group has not had time to make. Knowing which repair you are buying turns an open-ended search into a defined purchase.

In Physics the fastest repair is written method: a student who understands the physics and writes two lines where five marks were available recovers those marks in weeks, not months. In Chemistry it is the separation of the two failure modes, so that unit handling and pathway recall get different drills instead of one vague revision plan. In Psychology it is command-term discipline plus a study design that can actually test the claim being made. In Computer Science it is explaining code rather than producing it.

In Group 2 it is the shape of a spoken response under time pressure. In Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation it is the interpretive sentence after a correct calculation. In Economics it is how to close an evaluative answer, which is the most frequently unwritten set of marks in the subject and takes two or three sessions to install.

The table pairs each scarce subject with its fastest repair, a realistic time, and the thing a session genuinely cannot fix. That last column is the one worth reading twice, because it is where families are most often sold something undeliverable: a short block repairs technique and cannot install a missing Higher Level syllabus, and no tutor can promise a grade or a points total.

sections.heading: What proximity genuinely buys, stated fairly
paragraphs: It would be dishonest to write a page arguing that distance never matters, so here is the fair version. A person in the room can do four things a screen cannot, and for some students one of those four is the whole problem.

They can supervise. A reluctant student who will not begin work alone is a different proposition when an adult is sitting at the table, and no amount of video quality substitutes for that. They can read a room: the sideways glance that means the explanation landed, the fidget that means it did not. They can handle physical material directly. And they can be an anchor in a household's week in a way an appointment on a screen is not.

Against that, for a Diploma Higher Level subject, the nearby candidate is drawn from whoever can reach your district by seven on a weekday, and in Ajman that pool frequently does not contain anyone who has taught the course to examination. The choice is therefore not between quality and convenience; it is between a specialist in the right subject and an adult in the right room. For a student whose problem is a missing extension topic, the first wins easily. For a fifteen-year-old who does not open a book, the second does.

Where the honest recommendation is a local visiting tutor, we say so at the diagnostic. The published market bands for that option are worth knowing: a 2026 Dubai cost survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel is inside the rate, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which is why the comparison can be made without a stake in the answer.

sections.heading: Credentials, examiner claims and what a listing cannot tell you
paragraphs: Local listings in this market compete on adjectives, and two claims in particular are worth treating carefully because they are easy to assert and hard to check.

The first is examiner status. A tutor described as an examiner for the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson may well be one, and a provider should be able to evidence it for the individual rather than for the company. We do not describe tutors as examiners on these pages unless that status can be shown, and we never use it to imply access to marking, to grade boundaries or to paper content, because that implication is false and the suggestion of it is a reason to walk away.

The second is regulator approval. No tutoring platform in this market holds approval, accreditation or endorsement from the International Baccalaureate, the Ministry of Education or any emirate education authority, and "approved tutors" is the single most misleading phrase available on these pages. IB Gram claims none of it. A business with premises and staff needs its own educational services permit, which is a specific thing issued to training institutes and is not the same as an individual's tuition permit.

What a listing genuinely cannot tell you is the only thing that matters: which level this person has taught to examination, whether they have marked the internally assessed component in this subject, who marks the practice work and against what, and what the plan for the next three weeks is in terms specific enough to be proved wrong. Those four questions take ten minutes and they sort a short local list faster than any amount of reading.

sections.heading: How coverage is disclosed, and what happens when nobody covers the subject
paragraphs: No competitor researched in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign telephone number. The disclosure here is straightforward. Mathematics at both routes and both levels, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, English A and English B, Economics, Business Management and Psychology are generally matchable within a few days. Computer Science at Higher Level, the arts at Higher Level, some ab initio languages and Arabic as a first language take longer, and occasionally cannot be matched at all at the moment you ask.

When that happens you will be told, with the reason, rather than left on a list. That is more useful than it sounds, because a parent who knows the subject is nationally scarce can do three things we cannot: go back to the school and ask what internal support exists for a course it chose to offer, ask the coordinator whether another family is in the same position and whether a small group is possible, and widen the search knowing that distance was never the constraint.

Where we can cover the subject, the sequence is short. You send the subject, the level, the year group, a photograph of recent marked work and the two evening windows that genuinely work. We come back with a named tutor, their subject and level coverage, and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time. The first lesson is free, nothing is taken before it, and its purpose is a written diagnosis rather than a sales conversation.

And there is a version of this answer that recommends spending nothing. If the diagnostic concludes that the real problem is supervision, or that the student is carrying three Higher Levels they cannot carry, or that a component has passed the point where it can be repaired, you will hear it at the free lesson. The week-six review exists to produce the same answer later if the marked evidence supports it.

faqs.question: Does it actually matter whether an IB tutor is near me in Ajman?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma subject, far less than the search implies, and for one reason: the nearby candidate is drawn from whoever can reach your district by seven on a weekday, and in a small emirate that pool frequently contains nobody who has taught the course to examination. What proximity genuinely buys is supervision, reading a room, handling physical material and being an anchor in the week. If your child's problem is that they will not start work alone, those matter enormously. If the problem is a missing Higher Level extension topic, the specialist in the right subject wins easily.

faqs.question: Why are Higher Level science tutors so hard to find in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Because Higher Level is not Standard Level with harder questions. It adds content that does not appear at Standard Level at all, a heavier internally assessed demand, and papers that test depth. The pool of people who have taught a specific Higher Level course to examination and marked its investigation against the criteria is small nationally and smaller inside one emirate with concentrated IB provision. Biology is the best supplied of the three sciences, because it maps most closely onto existing A Level and IGCSE teaching. Chemistry and Physics at Higher Level are genuinely scarce locally.

faqs.question: Can I find an ab initio language tutor near me in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Realistically, no, and it is better to know that at the start. The pool is small nationally and close to nil inside the emirate. It is also the subject where a wrong match does the least good: a native speaker with no teaching background will have an excellent conversation with your child and leave the marks where they were, because the assessment rewards organising a response quickly inside a known structure rather than fluency. If we cannot cover a specific ab initio course we say so, and the first place to go back to is the school that chose to offer it.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from my child's own IB school privately?
faqs.answer: It is the most tempting local option and the one to leave alone. Private tutoring is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and the permit carries a code of conduct that has been reported as barring a holder from serving students affiliated with their own school. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have separately been reported as prohibiting it outright. Both are press-reported rather than read from current policy documents, so verify the wording with the authority. Ask the school's own written policy first.

faqs.question: Where will my child actually sit the IB examinations if we live in Ajman?
faqs.answer: At a centre, under conditions administered through the school, and that is the one genuinely local fact worth establishing early. Ask the coordinator three things in writing during the first term of the first Diploma year: where the candidate will physically sit the papers, what the arrangements are for any private-candidate entry, and what the internal deadline calendar looks like for every assessed component. That last document matters most for planning, because internal deadlines sit months before anything external. This page publishes no IB session or results date, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site for this project.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects can you cover at short notice, and which can you not?
faqs.answer: Matchable within a few days, usually: Mathematics on both routes at both levels, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, English A and English B, Economics, Business Management and Psychology. Slower or sometimes not matchable at all: Computer Science at Higher Level, the arts at Higher Level, some ab initio languages, and Arabic as a first language. When we cannot cover something you are told, with the reason, rather than left on a list — which lets you go back to the school, ask whether a small group is possible, or widen the search knowing distance was never the constraint.

faqs.question: What does a local tutor give us that a remote specialist cannot?
faqs.answer: Four things, and for some students one of them is the whole problem. Supervision, because a student who will not begin work alone is a different proposition with an adult at the table. Reading a room, which is the sideways glance that means an explanation landed. Handling physical material directly. And being an anchor in a household's week in a way a screen appointment is not. Against that, the nearby pool in a Higher Level Diploma subject often contains nobody who has taught the course. Where supervision is the real need, we recommend the local market option at the diagnostic.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Ajman a reasonable alternative for Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the centre teaches that specific course at that specific level, which is worth asking directly rather than assuming. Group classes cover syllabus broadly and cost less per head — the published budget band in this market runs AED 33 to 65 per hour, researched October 2026 — and they cannot diagnose one student's loss pattern. For a Higher Level extension gap a group class rarely reaches the material. Note also that a business with premises needs its own educational services permit rather than an individual tuition permit; ask which one it holds.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a Higher Level tutor for an Ajman family?
faqs.answer: For the well-supplied subjects, usually a few days, and the binding constraint is the slot rather than the subject: the reliable Ajman weekday window runs from roughly 18:30 to 21:00, and those slots fill first in the second Diploma year. For scarce subjects it can be a week or more, and occasionally it is not possible at the moment you ask. You get a straight answer either way. Families who fix a standing slot in September of the first year keep it; those who start looking in January take what is still open.

faqs.question: What single repair moves a Higher Level Physics grade fastest?
faqs.answer: Writing method down in sequence. The most common pattern we see is a student who understands the physics perfectly and writes two lines where five marks were available, because the reasoning stayed in their head. Marks exist for the method as well as for the answer, so unwritten reasoning is unmarked reasoning. Three to six weeks of marked timed work usually recovers it, and the evidence is readable by a parent without any physics: the same questions, with more lines of working and more marks. What that cannot repair is a missing half of the extension content.

faqs.question: My child takes Psychology — why can nobody locally teach it?
faqs.answer: Because very few schools in a small emirate have run the course, so there is little local teaching history to draw on. The subject also reads more accessibly than it is assessed, which is why families underestimate the hours. The marks sit in precise terminology, in command-term discipline across extended answers, and in an experimental study whose design has to be capable of testing the claim the student set out to test. That last one has a hard deadline: it can be fixed before the data is collected and not afterwards, which is why an early session is worth several late ones.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a UAE permit if they teach my child from outside the country?
faqs.answer: This is a reasonable question and it deserves a careful answer rather than a confident one. The published position is that individuals providing private tutoring need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and that those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The published material addresses tutoring in the UAE rather than setting out a cross-border rule, and we are not going to invent one. What we will do is tell you plainly where a tutor is based, which is more than a foreign telephone number in a footer does.

faqs.question: What should we do if you cannot cover my child's subject at all?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. Go back to the school and ask in writing what internal support exists for a course it chose to offer, because a department with four Higher Level students has options a parent cannot see. Ask the coordinator whether another family is in the same position and whether a small group or a shared arrangement is possible. Then widen the search knowing that distance was never the constraint, and judge any candidate on which level they have taught to examination and which component they have marked rather than on how near they live.

faqs.question: Is a generalist IB tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth saying so. For Middle Years work, where the demand is wide rather than deep, a strong secondary teacher who reads the criteria properly can do good work across several subjects. For Standard Level courses in well-mapped subjects the same can be true. Where it stops being true is Higher Level, because the extension material is specific content a generalist may never have taught, and the internally assessed component is marked against criteria that need to have been seen before. Ask which level they have taught to examination; the answer settles it.

faqs.question: How do we check a local tutor's claim to be an examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask for it to be evidenced for the individual rather than asserted for the company, and treat vagueness as an answer. Then listen for the second half of the claim, because that is where it becomes a problem: any suggestion that examiner status gives access to marking, to grade boundaries or to paper content is false and is a reason to end the conversation. We do not describe tutors as examiners on these pages unless the status can be shown, and never to imply that kind of access. More useful questions are which level they taught and who marks the practice work.

intro.heading: What IGCSE tuition actually costs in Ajman, and why the range is so wide
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency an Ajman household budgets in. So start with the numbers. Across the UAE, a budget online tutor is advertised from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs about AED 180 to 500, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and on home-tutor listings at AED 200 to 500. A recognised IGCSE or A-Level specialist is AED 200 to 450 and upwards; TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the top, BartyED lists AED 650.

Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and each is attributed above to whoever published it. That matters because a rate quoted with no source is not information. It also matters because the ranges overlap: the same human being can be worth AED 150 online and AED 300 at a door, and the difference is not teaching quality. It is forty minutes of driving each way, fuel, and an opportunity cost the tutor has to recover from somebody.

Ajman has a specific version of this problem. The emirate is compact, but the subject specialists are not evenly spread across it. A Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 teacher or an Edexcel 4CH1 chemistry specialist is far more likely to be living in Sharjah or Dubai than in Al Rawda, which means an in-home arrangement in Ajman usually prices in a cross-emirate drive during the worst part of the evening. Households in Masfout or Manama face a version of this that no amount of money solves cleanly, because the drive is simply too long to be weekly.

This is the reason IB Gram runs UAE tuition one-to-one over live video rather than at an address. It is not a cost-cutting device presented as a philosophy; the arithmetic is just better for the family. The travel line disappears, so the money that was paying for a car on Emirates Road pays for a tutor who marks the exact paper your child sits. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any address in Ajman, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Saying that plainly is more useful than letting you discover it after a deposit.

The rest of this page is arithmetic. What moves a quote and by how much, how monthly packages are actually constructed, what a realistic two-year IGCSE run costs for one child in Ajman, and where tutoring sits against the rest of the education bill. None of it contains a promised grade, because a price can be stated honestly and an outcome cannot.
