ajman/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four funding shapes cover nearly every Ajman enquiry. Which one you are buying changes the total far more than the hourly rate does, and most families only discover that halfway through.

programmes.name: Year 9 pre-IGCSE groundwork
programmes.description: The cheapest hour a family will ever buy, because it is bought before anything has gone wrong. Year 9 work is about algebraic fluency, scientific notation, data handling and writing in paragraphs, and it is usually fixed in a single term of fortnightly sessions rather than a weekly commitment. Funded here, the same outcome costs a fraction of the Year 11 version.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman schools make tier decisions for Mathematics and the sciences early in Year 10, and those decisions are made on Year 9 attainment. A family that spends modestly in Year 9 is often buying access to the Extended or Higher tier, which no amount of Year 11 spending can retroactively open up once entries have closed.

programmes.name: The two-year Cambridge IGCSE run
programmes.description: Weekly or fortnightly support across one to three subjects for the full two years. This is the largest single education purchase most families make outside school fees, and it is the one most often bought without a budget. The sensible structure is a small number of subjects funded properly rather than every subject funded thinly, because an hour spread across four papers teaches nobody anything.
programmes.countryNote: Across the two years, Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Multiply by twenty-two months of term time and the two-year figure is a number worth looking at before the first session, not after the twentieth.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the sciences, 4EA1 for English Language A. Tiering is Foundation and Higher. Practical understanding is examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate component, which slightly narrows what tutoring needs to cover and occasionally narrows the fee with it.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel's November series is the quietly useful one for an Ajman budget. A single weak subject can be re-sat in November without repeating a year, which converts what would have been a full extra year of fees into a dated block of sessions. The entry window closes months earlier, so the saving is only available to families who plan in the autumn.

programmes.name: Single-subject re-entry and resits
programmes.description: The narrowest and most cost-efficient purchase on this list: one paper, one error log, a fixed number of sessions, a stated finish date. Because the content was covered once already, the work is almost entirely technique and timing, and technique moves faster than content. Open-ended arrangements make no sense here and should be refused.
programmes.countryNote: A resit candidate in Ajman normally sits as a private candidate through an approved centre, and centres set their own administrative charges on top of the board's entry fee. Ask the centre for the full figure in writing before planning the tutoring budget, because that cost lands in the same month as the sessions.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Rates are not uniform across subjects. The driver is scarcity of people who can mark the paper, not difficulty of the content, and the two are often unrelated. Here is where the premium sits in the Ajman market and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The deepest supply pool in the emirate, so the most competitive rate. Expect to find qualified maths tutors across the whole published band rather than only at the top, and expect a wide quality spread at the lower end. The price signal here is weak; ask for marked evidence instead.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A genuine scarcity premium. Few tutors in the northern emirates teach 0606 regularly, and those who do often sit at the specialist end of the band. If a quote for 0606 comes in at a budget rate, the likely explanation is that the tutor has not taught the syllabus rather than that you found a bargain.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Mid to upper band. The written practical component on the Cambridge route narrows the pool further, because teaching it needs familiarity with how experimental skills are examined on paper. Tutors who can do that part credibly price accordingly, and it is usually worth it.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Similar to physics, with the organic pathways and electrolysis content concentrating demand in the months before the series. Rates on chemistry visibly firm up in the spring term, which is one of the few places where seasonality genuinely shows in a quote.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Broad supply, moderate rate. The risk is paying a general science tutor a biology rate: the extended-response marking in biology is a specific skill, and a tutor who cannot show marked examples of it is being paid for the subject label rather than the capability.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Rates vary more than any other subject, because almost anyone can present as an English tutor and very few can mark directed writing against the published bands. The useful filter is a marked sample with band references on it, and that filter removes most of the lower end of the market.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Widely available at mid-band rates across Ajman and Sharjah. The pitfall is being sold 0500 technique at a 0510 price, or the reverse. The two are assessed on different criteria and confirming which code your child is entered for is the single cheapest thing you can do before agreeing a rate.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Competitive rates, thin specialist depth. Many tutors can teach the content and fewer can train case-study application, which is where the grade is decided. Ask for a marked extended answer showing where the application and evaluation marks were awarded before you accept a rate at the upper end.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Upper-mid band, with scarcity driven by diagram marking. A tutor who corrects axes, titles and shift arrows on a student's own diagram is doing the job; one who presents finished diagrams is not, and that distinction is worth more than a hundred dirhams an hour of nominal seniority.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: The clearest scarcity premium after 0606. Paper 2 algorithm design and pseudocode tracing needs a tutor who has marked it, and that pool is small in the northern emirates. Online delivery widens the pool enormously, which is where the price advantage of video becomes concrete rather than theoretical.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Mid band, with a short seasonal spike. Format discipline carries most of the marks, so sessions are heavy on timed practice and light on explanation, which means fewer total hours are usually needed than families budget for. That is a saving worth taking.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Lower-mid band and broadly available. Case-study specificity is what moves marks, and building it is more about structured recall work between sessions than about hours in the session, so a fortnightly arrangement often delivers the same result as a weekly one at half the cost.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: In an in-home arrangement, your address is a line item. The notes below are about distance and evening traffic rather than community character, because those are the two things that change what a visiting tutor has to charge.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: Central and quick to reach from Sharjah, so in-home quotes here sit at the lower end of the travel premium. The trade-off is that evening parking and lift access in the denser blocks eats ten minutes a tutor still has to be paid for.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Close to the city core with reasonable access from the Sharjah side. Households running two children on different boards often find the in-home model prices badly here, because two subjects means either two visits or one tutor pretending to cover both.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Long internal roads and an awkward run to the Emirates Road junctions. Quotes reflect it. Families here report the widest gap between a tutor's advertised rate and the figure finally agreed once travel was discussed honestly.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Mowaihat 1, 2 and 3 are villa areas with a real cross-emirate drive for most specialists. This is where the in-home premium is largest in Ajman, and where replacing it with video changes a budget most visibly.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer Emirates Road developments with decent access, which keeps the travel premium moderate. These are also the households most likely to be funding an IGCSE child and an IB child at once, which is a different budgeting problem altogether.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Established areas with short local journeys, so a second weekly session is cheaper to add here than almost anywhere else in the emirate. That matters in the term before a November entry when hours need to concentrate.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche and Al Rumailah
regions.note: Seafront apartments where the constraint is a quiet room rather than a quote. Evening noise pushes timed paper practice to weekend mornings, and weekend slots occasionally carry a premium in the local market.

regions.name: Emirates City and Al Alia
regions.note: The longest evening drives in Ajman and the latest realistic start times. An in-home tutor pricing a 8.30pm session here is pricing a journey home at 10pm, and the quote shows it.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen and Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density villas with easy parking but a longer approach. Families here tend to buy one longer weekly session rather than two short ones, which is the right call economically as well as practically.

regions.name: Masfout and Manama
regions.note: The inland exclaves, where a weekly in-home specialist is not a pricing question but a logistics impossibility. Delivery over live video is the only route to a 0606 or 0478 tutor at any price.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman city schools: the established cluster
schoolClusters.note: Fee levels and tutoring demand both concentrate here. Enquiries from this cluster are most often about Mathematics and the sciences, and most often arrive after a Year 10 report rather than before one.
schools: GEMS Our Own English High School, Ajman
Ibn Seena English High School, Ajman

schoolClusters.city: The Emirates Road belt
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools serving the villa developments, with a wider board mix. Budget questions from this belt lean towards funding two curricula in one household and towards sixth-form entry requirements.

schoolClusters.city: Cross-border enrolment in Sharjah and Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Where an Ajman child is enrolled outside the emirate, the school day finishes further away and the in-home tutoring window narrows at both ends. That compression is the hidden cost in a cross-border enrolment.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways to buy, priced on different logic. All three run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so none of them carries a travel component.

modes.title: Single diagnostic hour
modes.description: One session, free, spent on a past-paper question set rather than on introductions. It exists because the commonest budgeting mistake in this market is committing to a month before anyone has established what the problem is. A diagnostic hour tells you whether you are buying a technique fix of three weeks or a content rebuild of a term, and those have very different prices.

The reason to avoid long prepaid packages is simple: a package creates a reason to keep teaching after the problem is solved. A monthly review creates a reason to stop. Published monthly packages elsewhere in this market run from around AED 799 for eight online sessions to AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

It is the most expensive format per month and the cheapest per mark recovered, because the content is already in place and the work is pure execution. It has a fixed finish date, which is the whole point: the calendar ends the spending rather than a conversation.

sections.heading: What the Ajman and northern-emirates market charges for IGCSE tuition
paragraphs: An IGCSE hour in the UAE is sold at between roughly AED 45 and AED 650, and the first job of this section is to show you which band you are being quoted from. The bands are real and the boundaries between them are about who the tutor is rather than what they teach. A university student revising alongside your child is a different product from a teacher who has marked the paper, and both are legitimate purchases at the right price for the right problem.

Every figure in the table is attributed to the provider that published it, with the date of the research. That is not a formality. Three of the six strongest-ranking pages in this search publish no price whatsoever, and one of them asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. A sourced number is checkable; an unsourced one is marketing. If a provider will not tell you which band they sit in before a call, you already know something useful.

Read the band against the problem rather than against your budget. A Year 9 fluency gap in algebra is genuinely well served at the lower end, because what is needed is supervised practice and someone to notice when a method is wrong. A Year 11 student losing evaluation marks on Economics 0455 extended questions is not, because the person at that rate has probably never marked one. Paying specialist money for a fluency problem is as wasteful as paying budget money for a marking problem, and families do both.

One structural point about the in-home band. The AED 180 to 500 range for a one-to-one visit includes travel, and travel is not a service. It is a cost that has to be covered before any teaching happens, and in Ajman, where most subject specialists live in Sharjah or Dubai, it is a large one.

sections.heading: Eight things that move the number on an IGCSE quote
paragraphs: Once you know the bands, the useful question is what pushes a specific quote up or down inside them. There are eight common variables and they are not equally important. Subject scarcity and delivery format do most of the work; session length and payment terms do almost none, despite being the two things families negotiate hardest.

Scarcity is the big one and it is counter-intuitive. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 cost more in the northern emirates than Physics 0625 does, not because they are harder but because fewer people in reachable distance have marked them. That is precisely the premium that disappears when delivery stops depending on reachable distance, which is the single strongest financial argument for video in a market like Ajman.

Timing is the second. Chemistry and Mathematics rates visibly firm up in the spring term as the June series approaches, and a family that starts in October is buying at a different price from a family that starts in March. The honest version of this is not that providers raise prices opportunistically; it is that the available specialists fill their evenings, and what is left is priced as scarcity. Starting early is a discount nobody advertises.

The table below sets out all eight with a rough direction and size. The sizes are indicative percentages of the base rate from the published bands above, not a tariff, and any provider who quotes you a precise multiplier for any of them is inventing it.

sections.heading: The travel line nobody itemises, and what it costs an Ajman household
paragraphs: In-home quotes in the UAE are almost always presented as a single hourly figure with travel folded in, which conceals the most interesting number in the whole arrangement. Work it out and the picture changes. A specialist based in Sharjah coming to Al Mowaihat for a one-hour session is committing somewhere around ninety minutes to two hours of total time in the evening peak. The teaching is one hour of that. The rest is a cost the family pays for without receiving anything.

That is why the in-home band sits at AED 180 to 500 while the same tutor delivering online sits at AED 150 to 300. The gap is not a premium for presence; it is a reimbursement for a drive. And the gap is wider in Ajman than in central Dubai, because the specialist pool is further away. A household in Masfout or Manama cannot buy the service at all on a weekly basis, at any price, because there is no rate at which a twice-weekly inland round trip is rational for a tutor.

There is a second, less visible cost: the session gets worse. A tutor arriving at 7.15pm after fifty minutes on Emirates Road is not at their best, and a student who has been told to wait at home rather than get on with homework has lost the same fifty minutes. Whatever the merits of face-to-face teaching in principle, the version being sold in this corridor is frequently a tired adult and a restless teenager at the end of a long drive.

None of this makes in-home tutoring a bad product. For a Year 7 child who needs supervision as much as instruction, for a student who genuinely cannot work on a screen, or where a local tutor happens to live three streets away and teaches the right paper, it can be exactly right. It is just rarely the right answer for an Ajman Year 11 student who needs a specialist on a specific component, and the honest reason is geography rather than ideology.
bullets: An in-home hour in Ajman commonly costs the tutor 90 to 120 minutes of evening
The AED 180-500 in-home band against AED 150-300 online is largely that drive
No weekly in-home rate is rational for Masfout or Manama, which is a logistics limit
A tired tutor and a waiting student are a quality cost on top of the money

sections.heading: Monthly packages, and the arithmetic providers do not show you
paragraphs: Monthly packages are the normal way this market sells, and they are worth reading as arithmetic rather than as offers. The published shapes in the UAE include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Divide those out and the effective hourly rates are very different from the headline, which is the point of packaging.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions give a cleaner comparison: roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A family funding two subjects at the specialist end during Year 11 is therefore looking at a four-figure monthly commitment, and that is a number to see in October rather than to discover in March.

The structural risk in a package is not the price. It is the incentive. A prepaid three-month block gives a provider a reason to keep delivering sessions after the problem has been fixed, and gives the family a reason to keep attending in order not to waste the money. Both reasons are bad. A monthly arrangement with a written review at week six creates the opposite pressure, which is why that is how this works here, and why there is no joining fee or prepaid term to recover.

sections.heading: Two years, nine subjects: a worked IGCSE budget for one Ajman child
paragraphs: Families budget per hour and spend per year, which is how a modest-sounding rate becomes a surprising annual figure. Work the whole thing through once, in advance, and most of the stress comes out of it. Take a typical Ajman student carrying nine IGCSE subjects across Years 10 and 11, roughly twenty-two months of term time once holidays are removed.

Nobody funds nine subjects and nobody should try. The realistic shape is one to three subjects supported at any one time, with the selection changing as error logs close. A workable plan looks like this: Year 10 carries one subject weekly, usually Mathematics, because it underpins the sciences. Year 11 autumn adds a second, chosen from the mock results. The spring term before the series runs two subjects with a dated intensive on the weakest paper. Total funded subject-months across the two years come to somewhere between twenty-five and forty, not one hundred and ninety-eight.

Apply the published monthly bands to that and the arithmetic is tractable. Thirty funded subject-months at the mid band of AED 600 to 1,200 is a two-year total in the region of AED 18,000 to 36,000, and the same plan at the budget band is materially less while buying materially less. An in-home version of the same plan costs more because of the travel component, and in Ajman specifically it also costs availability, since the specialist for the weakest paper may simply not be drivable.

The number worth writing down is the one per recovered mark rather than per hour, and it cannot be calculated in advance. What can be done is to spend the first six weeks establishing whether this is a technique problem or a content problem, because the two have completely different durations and therefore completely different totals. That is exactly what the free first lesson and the week-six review exist to establish, before the big number is committed.

sections.heading: Why this is delivered over video, and what that does to the bill
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers UAE tuition one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; those are offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because the phrase you searched for was a home tutor and you are entitled to know exactly what is on offer before you read another word about price.

The financial effect is straightforward. Removing the drive removes the component that pushes the in-home band to AED 180-500 and keeps the online band at AED 150-300. More importantly for Ajman, it removes distance as a constraint on who can teach your child. The 0606 specialist, the 0478 algorithm marker, the person who has actually marked Cambridge written practical papers: none of them need to be within forty minutes of Al Rawda. That is not a cost saving dressed up as a benefit. It is the reason the saving exists.

The trade-offs are real and worth naming. A screen is worse for a young child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task. It needs a stable connection and a quiet room, which is harder in a shared Corniche apartment than in a Zorah villa. It requires a tablet or laptop and, for maths and sciences, ideally a writing surface the tutor can see. Where those conditions cannot be met, in-home tuition from a local provider is the better purchase and we will say so rather than sell around it.

What video does not compromise is the evidence. Marking happens on a shared screen in front of the student, scripts are saved rather than left in a notebook, and the raw-mark log is a document a parent can open at any time. An in-home session in a kitchen produces none of that unless the tutor chooses to build it, and most do not.

Removing travel is why the online band sits below the in-home band
Distance stops deciding which specialists your child can reach

sections.heading: Tutoring in the context of the rest of the education bill
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little in isolation. It sits alongside school fees, transport, exam entry and the various administrative charges that arrive in the same months, and the only sensible way to judge it is against that whole bill. For families in the northern emirates with a child enrolled in Dubai, there is useful public context: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Scale is worth knowing too. Dubai's private school sector in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, American 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. That is the market Ajman families are competing in for sixth-form places, and it is why IGCSE grades carry weight beyond the certificate itself.

Exam costs belong in the budget and cannot be stated here, because they are set by the board and by the centre rather than by us, and a private candidate's administrative charge varies between centres. Ask the school exams officer, or the approved centre if your child is sitting privately, for the full figure in writing. It lands in the same month as the heaviest tutoring and families are regularly caught by that overlap.

The last item is the one nobody budgets: repeating a year. An extra year of private school fees dwarfs any plausible tutoring spend, which is the honest commercial case for funding a weak subject properly in Year 10 rather than hoping. It is also the case for the November re-entry route, which converts a lost year into a dated block of sessions.
bullets: KHDA confirmed no private school fee increase in Dubai for 2026-27, in May 2026
Dubai held 387,441 private school students across 227 schools in 2024-25
Exam entry and private-candidate centre charges land in the heaviest tutoring month

sections.heading: Ten questions to ask before you accept an IGCSE quote
paragraphs: A quote is a document you are allowed to interrogate, and in this market the answers are more informative than the number. Ten questions cover almost everything, and three of them tend to end conversations quickly.

Ask which band the rate sits in and why. Ask which syllabus code and component the tutor has marked, and for a redacted sample of that marking. Ask whether travel is included and how long the journey to your area takes, because an honest answer tells you whether the rate is sustainable or will quietly rise. Ask what happens if you cancel after one session. Ask whether the figure includes VAT; providers should be able to state the position on their own pricing in writing, and nobody should be inventing a general tax ruling for you. Ask who is actually delivering the session, because agencies sometimes quote at a specialist rate and allocate at a general one.

Then the three uncomfortable ones. Ask for the circumstances in which they would recommend stopping. Ask what evidence you will receive and when. And ask whether they are promising an outcome, because any answer that commits to a specific grade or an improvement figure is a reason to end the conversation: no tutor can commit to a mark on a results slip, and offering to is either a misunderstanding of the examination or a deliberate one.

One Ajman-specific check. The UAE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee. A quote that itemises a licensing or permit cost is charging you for something that is free. That is a small amount of money and a large amount of information about who you are dealing with.
bullets: Which band is this rate, and which component has the tutor actually marked?
Is travel included, and how long is the journey to my area in the evening?
What evidence will I receive after each session, and when?
Under what circumstances would you tell me to stop paying?

process.title: Say what you are solving
process.description: Send the subject list with syllabus codes from the school's entry statement, the tier your child sits in, and what the last report or mock said. A rate quoted without that information is a guess, and guessed rates are the ones that move after a month.

process.title: Take the free hour
process.description: One full session at no cost, spent on a past-paper question set. It produces a marked script and a written view of whether this is a three-week technique problem or a term-long content problem. Those two have very different totals, and you should know which you are funding.

process.title: Price the plan, not the hour
process.description: Work out how many subject-months you are actually buying across the rest of Year 10 and Year 11, then apply a monthly band to it. Most families discover the plan is smaller and the total larger than they assumed, which is a better thing to discover in October than in March.

process.title: Start monthly, review at six weeks
process.description: Billed monthly with no joining fee and no prepaid term. At week six you receive a written review with a recommendation that may be to change subject focus or to stop. Reschedules inside the month are not charged, because Ajman evening traffic is not something you control.

process.title: Add a second subject only on evidence
process.description: A second subject is added when the first one's error tally is visibly closing, not when the term starts. Funding two subjects thinly from the outset is the most common way an IGCSE budget gets spent without a grade moving.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED number on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was researched. Three of the strongest pages in this search publish no price at all, and one asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the quote
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video, so nothing in the price is paying for a car on Emirates Road. In Ajman, where most subject specialists are based in Sharjah or Dubai, that is the largest single component removed from an in-home rate.

whyPoints.title: Specialists regardless of distance
whyPoints.description: A household in Masfout or Al Mowaihat reaches the same 0606 or 0478 specialist as one in Al Nuaimiya. Distance stops being a filter on who can teach your child, which is where the real value of video delivery sits.

whyPoints.title: Monthly, with a reason to stop
whyPoints.description: No joining fee, no prepaid block and a written review at week six that can recommend stopping. Prepaid packages create an incentive to keep teaching after the problem is solved; monthly billing creates the opposite one.

whyPoints.title: Market rates, not our price list
whyPoints.description: The bands here describe what the UAE market charges, attributed to their sources. For what a specific plan would cost, the free first lesson and the follow-up conversation give you a figure based on your child's actual papers rather than a tariff.

whyPoints.title: Nothing promised about grades
whyPoints.description: No session, block or intensive carries a promised grade, score or improvement figure. What is committed to is the evidence, the review dates and an honest recommendation, including the recommendation that a tutor is the wrong purchase.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Ajman charge per hour in 2026?
faqs.answer: Across the UAE market, an in-home one-to-one visit with travel included is published at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and home-tutor listings at AED 200 to 500. In Ajman the figure tends to sit in the upper part of that band for anything specialist, because most subject specialists are based in Sharjah or Dubai and the quote has to cover the drive. The same teaching delivered over live video is published at AED 150 to 300. Those are market figures, attributed to their sources, not a price list.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home rate in Ajman higher than the same tutor online?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for a journey as well as a lesson. A specialist travelling from Sharjah to Al Mowaihat for a one-hour evening session commits roughly ninety minutes to two hours in total, of which only one hour is teaching. That unpaid time has to be recovered somewhere, and it is recovered in the hourly rate. The published gap between the AED 180 to 500 in-home band and the AED 150 to 300 online band is largely that recovery. In Ajman the gap widens, because the specialist pool sits further away than it does in central Dubai.

faqs.question: Is a monthly IGCSE package cheaper than paying session by session?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and the saving is usually smaller than the risk. Published UAE packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which work out at roughly AED 100 and AED 200 to 225 an hour respectively. The discount against a per-session rate is real but modest. The problem is the incentive: a prepaid block gives a provider a reason to keep delivering sessions after the problem is fixed, and gives you a reason to keep attending so the money is not wasted. Monthly billing with a review avoids both.

faqs.question: Should I be paying for a tutor's travel time to Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: If someone is driving to Al Mowaihat in the evening peak, then yes, somebody has to pay for it, and pretending otherwise just means the rate rises later. The honest question is whether you want to buy it at all. For a Year 7 child who needs an adult present, it can be worth every dirham. For a Year 11 student who needs a specialist on Cambridge 0606 or a written practical paper, you are paying a large travel premium for a smaller pool of available tutors. Over live video the travel line disappears and the pool stops depending on distance.

faqs.question: How much should two years of IGCSE support cost for one child?
faqs.answer: Work it in subject-months rather than hours. A realistic plan across Years 10 and 11 funds one to three subjects at a time, totalling roughly 25 to 40 funded subject-months rather than every subject for twenty-two months. At Bestimate's mid monthly band of AED 600 to 1,200 for weekly one-hour sessions, thirty subject-months lands somewhere around AED 18,000 to 36,000 across the two years. The budget band is materially less and buys materially less. The exam-year specialist band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above per month moves the total upwards sharply.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor charge more for Physics than for Business Studies?
faqs.answer: Usually a little, but the bigger gaps are elsewhere. The driver is scarcity of people who have marked the component, not difficulty of the subject. In the northern emirates, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 carry the clearest premiums, because very few reachable tutors teach them regularly. Physics 0625 sits mid to upper band partly because of the written practical component. Business Studies 0450 looks competitive on price but has thin specialist depth, so the risk there is paying a fair rate to someone who cannot train case-study application.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Ajman climb as the June series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes, and not because providers raise prices opportunistically. Specialist evening slots fill through the spring term, so a family starting in March is choosing from what is left rather than from the whole pool, and what is left prices as scarcity. Chemistry and Mathematics show this most visibly. The practical consequence is that starting in October is a discount nobody advertises: the same tutor at the same nominal rate, chosen from a wider set, with more weeks to work with. Late starts cost more and deliver less for structural reasons rather than commercial ones.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student tutor a false economy at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not always. For a Year 9 or early Year 10 fluency problem, where the need is supervised practice and someone to notice a wrong method early, the budget band of AED 45 to 150 is a sensible purchase and the alternative is overpaying. It becomes a false economy at the point where the problem is mark-scheme technique on a specific component. Somebody who has not marked Economics 0455 extended responses cannot teach the evaluation marks, however well they understand economics. Match the band to the problem rather than to the budget, and expect to change band as the problem changes.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE tutoring fees in the UAE subject to VAT?
faqs.answer: That depends on the provider's own tax position, and this page will not state a general ruling for you. What any provider should be able to do is tell you in writing whether their quoted figure includes VAT, and show a tax registration number if they hold one. If a quote is silent on the point, ask before you agree it, because the difference is material on a four-figure monthly commitment. For the treatment of education services in general, the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance is the only source worth relying on, not a tutoring company's summary of it.

faqs.question: Should a tutor's quote include a charge for the MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: No, and if it does, that is useful information. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. A quote itemising a permit cost is charging you for something that costs nothing.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can one Ajman family realistically fund?
faqs.answer: One to three at any given time, and fewer than families expect. The failure pattern is funding four subjects thinly, where each gets a fortnightly half-hour of attention, nothing closes, and a year's budget is spent without a grade moving. The alternative is to fund one subject properly until its error tally is visibly closing, then rotate the money to the next. Mathematics is usually first, because it underpins the sciences. The second subject should be chosen from mock results rather than from a feeling about which teacher your child dislikes.

faqs.question: What is a fair price for a 90-minute IGCSE session in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Take the hourly band the tutor sits in and expect a small discount per hour for the longer slot, because setup and settling time is amortised across more teaching. A qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour should therefore price ninety minutes somewhat below one and a half times the hourly figure. The ninety-minute slot is worth buying where a full structured paper is being worked through, since a 60-minute session cannot contain an attempt and its marking. For technique drills, two shorter sessions usually beat one long one.

faqs.question: Do two siblings sharing one IGCSE session halve the cost?
faqs.answer: The cost per child falls, and so does the attention per child, in roughly the same proportion. It works where both children are on the same board, the same subject and a similar level, which in practice means twins or a tight year gap. It works badly where one is sitting Cambridge 0580 and the other Edexcel 4MA1, because the papers and mark schemes differ and the session becomes two half-sessions. Two separate marked records still have to come out of it. Tell us both sets of codes and we will say honestly whether one session fits.

faqs.question: Who pays the IGCSE exam entry fee for a private candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The family does, through the approved centre that enters the candidate, and the total has two parts: the board's entry fee for each syllabus and the centre's own administrative charge. Centres set the second part themselves, so the figure varies and no honest page can quote it for you. Ask the centre for the full amount in writing before you build a tutoring budget, because entry money and the heaviest tutoring month usually arrive together. Entry deadlines also sit months ahead of the papers, so this is an autumn conversation rather than a spring one.

faqs.question: What does the first month of IGCSE tutoring in Ajman actually cost?
faqs.answer: The first lesson costs nothing. After that, a single subject at one session a week sits inside the published monthly bands: roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, on Bestimate's estimates. There is no joining fee and no prepaid term, so the first month is also the smallest commitment available. What you should have at the end of it is four marked scripts, an error tally and enough information to decide whether month two is worth buying.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get a figure based on your child's actual papers
ajman/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The bands on this page describe the UAE market with sources attached. What a specific plan costs depends on which subjects, which codes and how many months, and that is a short conversation rather than a tariff. Start with the free first lesson: one full session on a past-paper question set, a marked script at the end of it, and a written view of whether you are funding a three-week technique fix or a term of content. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, billed monthly, with no joining fee and nothing prepaid.

intro.heading: The year is decided before the papers are sat
paragraphs: An IGCSE year has four decision points and only one of them is the examination. The entry is submitted months in advance and fixes the board, the code and the tier. The tier sets a ceiling that cannot be lifted afterwards. The centre's administrative zone determines which version of the timetable is correct. And the series chosen determines when results arrive, which in turn determines whether a post-16 place can wait for them.

None of those four is a teaching decision, and all four are usually made while a family is thinking about revision. That ordering is why so many households arrive at tuition in the spring of Year 11 with a problem that was created in the previous autumn. Counting the year backwards from the series makes each decision visible while it is still open.

Ajman Corniche gives a family one real advantage in all of this: time in the afternoon. The seafront towers sit inside the old city's school catchment, so runs are often fifteen minutes and a session can start at 4:00pm, which is earlier than almost anywhere else in the emirate. The counterweight is space. A flat with siblings needs an agreed quiet room for a live video lesson, and that is a week-one conversation rather than a week-five improvisation.

Delivery is stated plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The phrase in this page's address is the one parents search, and it is answered honestly: what in-home tuition is quoted at in this market, what the travel premium consists of, and why a Corniche household usually gets more teaching per dirham from a specialist on a screen.

The dates below are sourced and dated, which is unusual in this market. Cambridge and Pearson positions come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026. Past dates keep their year because the year is what makes them checkable; future series are named by month only, because a page that dates itself to one year is wrong the next without anybody touching it.

One correction worth making loudly, because other pages in this market get it wrong. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to candidates in India. A centre in Ajman enters the June and November series. A revision calendar built on the India dates is a revision calendar for a different country, and a parent who acts on it books leave, cancels travel and sets a revision schedule against a window their child will never sit. That is the kind of error a tuition page can cause without ever teaching a lesson, which is why the series named here are the ones an Ajman centre actually enters and why the official timetable is linked rather than copied out.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a Corniche household working towards IGCSE, and the decisions that set the ceiling are taken in the first two rather than the last two.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, before the course begins
programmes.description: No external papers and therefore no entry deadlines, which makes this the cheap window. Algebraic fluency, written method, scientific vocabulary and reading speed are built here or repaired expensively two years later. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for schools that choose to use them.
programmes.countryNote: The Corniche's short school runs make a 4:00pm half-hour session sustainable at this age in a way it is not at Year 11, when school homework alone consumes the window. Families who use Year 9 rarely need an emergency in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Each subject is its own qualification with its own code. Mathematics 0580 splits into Core, capped at grade C, and Extended, which runs to A*. Sciences such as Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 offer Core and Extended papers, with the practical route decided by the centre rather than the student.
programmes.countryNote: The zone detail matters here. Cambridge states that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Separate codes and a different assessment shape: 4MA1 Mathematics A with Foundation and Higher tiers, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Practical knowledge is assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical route, so Cambridge past papers are not a substitute.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson exams run in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables for future series which it then revises, so the live official PDF is the only version worth revising from.

programmes.name: After Year 11
programmes.description: The grade set decides which routes stay open: A Levels, the IB Diploma or a vocational pathway. Mathematics and the sciences are where doors close quietly, because a Core or Foundation entry can rule out a Higher Level or A Level course regardless of how strong the result was inside that tier.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency on the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-ajman-corniche.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects most often requested from the Corniche, each with the code and the point in the year where the work has to happen.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier recommendation forms in the spring of Year 10, which is the moment to intervene rather than the spring of Year 11. Extended Paper 4 rewards method marks, so working has to be written out even when the answer is obvious.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves carry the heaviest losses and both are taught early, which means a Year 10 gap persists quietly until the mocks. Confirm whether the centre entered the practical or the alternative-to-practical paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall and they sit in the first year of the course. Students who balance equations confidently still lose marks converting between mass, moles and volume under time pressure.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Long answers reward ordering as much as naming. Genetics problems at Extended need a Punnett square drawn correctly, and that is a technique fixable in a fortnight once somebody has named it.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level Diploma course. It introduces calculus and trigonometric identities early, and it is where a weak Year 9 algebra foundation stops being hideable.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Writing is marked on content and language separately and the task types are prescriptive. Listening practice has to be done at exam speed, which is a habit built across a term rather than a skill taught in a session.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses move the grade. Students lose marks by retelling the passage instead of analysing how it works, and by writing more than the time allows rather than planning for four minutes first.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the entire paper. Theory reproduced from memory caps an answer at the lowest band, which is why timed case practice matters more here than content revision.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries disproportionate weight and most students draw curves without labelling axes, shifts or the new equilibrium. Data-response marks come from quoting the figure in the extract.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Running alongside the international timetable. For the mandatory national subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support works inside the school's prescribed material.

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards
paragraphs: Read the year in reverse and the sequence makes sense. At the end sit the papers, in June or in the late-October to November window. Before them, the final weeks of timed practice, which is the only activity that should be happening by then. Before that, the mock window, whose job is to generate information rather than a grade. Before that, the final entry, which fixes the board, the code and the tier. And before all of it, the tier recommendation, which forms in the spring of Year 10 on the basis of internal assessment.

That last point is the one worth dwelling on, because it inverts the usual assumption. Most families treat Year 11 as the year that matters and Year 10 as preparation. In practice the ceiling on the final certificate is set in Year 10, when the school decides which tier to recommend, and a term of targeted work before that recommendation is worth more than two terms after it.

The sourced dates give a Corniche family some fixed points for the past, which is how the future shape can be estimated without publishing something that might be revised. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

The table gives the sequence with the span rather than inventing a future calendar. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then revises them, so the correct habit is to link the live official timetable and to check the centre's own version rather than a copy found online.

sections.heading: Why the entry deadline sits months before the exam
paragraphs: Parents are regularly surprised that an entry closes long before anybody feels prepared, and the reason is administrative rather than academic. A board has to print papers, allocate them to centres, build timetables for six administrative zones, arrange invigilation and prepare scripts for marking, all of which has to be finalised before a single candidate sits down. The deadline is a logistics date, not a readiness date.

The consequence is that the entry is a forecast. A school submits a tier based on what it knows in the autumn, and the student then has months to become somebody that entry no longer suits. Both directions are possible: a student entered for Core who improves sharply, and a student entered for Extended who does not. Neither can be fixed after entries close, which makes the autumn conversation with the subject teacher far more consequential than it feels.

A worked illustration of the gap, using the sourced Pearson dates: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A family thinking about a November entry is therefore making a decision in the summer about a result that will not arrive until the following January. Any post-16 application has to be told about that gap rather than discovering it.

The practical advice is short. Ask the exams officer, in writing and in the autumn, for the board, the codes, the tiers, the paper numbers and the centre's zone. Then ask when entries close and whether a tier change is still possible. Those two messages are the highest-value administrative work of the year.

sections.heading: The zone trap almost nobody mentions
paragraphs: This is a small operational detail with a large consequence, and it appears on virtually no tutoring page in this market. Cambridge states that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that the board cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

What that means in practice is that a timetable found through a search engine, or borrowed from a cousin in another country, may list a paper on a different day from the one your child's centre is sitting it. The failure mode is not academic. A student who revises the right content and arrives on the wrong day has lost the paper, and the board's position on responsibility is explicit.

The fix is to get the timetable from the centre, in writing, and to check it against the paper numbers on the entry. Then build the revision schedule from that document rather than from any other. For Pearson candidates the equivalent discipline is to use the live official timetable rather than a provisional version, because provisional timetables are published well ahead of a series and then revised.

A tutor can help with this in a way that costs nothing: the first session should include a check that the student knows their own paper dates, in their own centre's version, and that somebody at home has a copy. It is a five-minute conversation that occasionally saves a year.
bullets: Ask the centre which of the six Cambridge zones it sits in.
Get the centre's own timetable in writing and revise from that copy.
Check paper numbers on the timetable against the paper numbers on the entry.
For Pearson, use the live official timetable rather than a provisional one.

sections.heading: November: a resit route, or a plan in its own right?
paragraphs: The second window is usually described as a resit route and that undersells it. For some students a November entry is the better primary plan: a candidate who joined the course late, who missed a term, or who is sitting a subject outside the school's normal timetable may be better served by the later series than by being pushed into June.

The trade is the results gap. For Pearson, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, against 20 August 2026 for the June 2026 series. Four to five additional months of preparation are bought at the cost of a result arriving in January, and whether that trade works depends entirely on what is waiting for the grade. A post-16 place that cannot wait makes the trade unavailable; a gap year, a repeat year or an internal progression frequently makes it sensible.

For Cambridge, June is the main sitting and November is the resit route, and the February and March series that appears in some revision material is offered to candidates in India rather than to a centre in Ajman. A family planning around those dates is planning around a different country's calendar, and this is a mistake that has been published on tutoring pages in this market.
The decision should rest on a component breakdown rather than on a feeling. The table sets out the question to ask at each step, because the sequence is stable even when the dates change.

sections.heading: Results in August, results in January
paragraphs: The results gap between the two windows is the single most practically useful fact on this page, and it is the one families most often learn too late. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Five months separate those two experiences.

That gap has three consequences. First, a November candidate cannot use their grade in a post-16 application that closes in the autumn, so the receiving institution has to be told in advance rather than asked to accommodate it later. Second, a November candidate spends the autumn term in a kind of limbo, often already enrolled somewhere on a conditional basis. Third, the January arrival means any subsequent decision, including a further resit, is being taken in the middle of the following academic year.

None of that makes November wrong. It makes it a plan that needs the receiving end organised first. The sequence that works is to establish what the grade is for, ask whether that destination can wait until January, and only then choose the series. Families who choose the series first and ask the question second are the ones who end up with a good grade that arrived too late to be useful.

One more operational note for Corniche households: private candidate entries are arranged through a centre rather than through a school, with fees and deadlines set by the centre and the board. Ask the centre directly. This page does not quote entry fees, because they are not ours to quote and they change.

sections.heading: What each term of the two years has to deliver
paragraphs: A two-year course has four terms that matter and each has a different job. Treating all four the same is the commonest planning error, and it produces the familiar pattern of a quiet first year followed by a frantic second.

Year 10 autumn is for foundations and for establishing whether the student can access the harder question types at all, because that is what the tier recommendation will be based on. Year 10 spring is when the recommendation forms, so it is the last term in which a change of trajectory can change the ceiling. Year 11 autumn is for completing content and for the mock window, whose output is information rather than a grade. Year 11 spring is for timed practice marked against real schemes, and for nothing else.

A tuition plan that respects that shape costs less and achieves more than a flat weekly arrangement across both years. One weekly session in Year 10 in the genuinely weak subject, a short block before the tier recommendation, a mock-review session, and an eight-week pre-series block is a smaller total spend than two years of weekly hours, and it puts each hour where the calendar can use it.

The table sets out the four terms with what each should deliver and the signal that it has. Two things follow from reading it as a whole. The first is that no term's job can be done by a later one: foundations cannot be laid in the spring of Year 11, and timed practice is wasted on a student whose content is still missing. The second is that the cheapest hours in the two years are the earliest ones, which is the reverse of how most households spend, and the reason is simply that nothing else is competing for attention in a Year 10 autumn.

sections.heading: Private candidates, and what the centre controls
paragraphs: Not every IGCSE candidate sits through their own school. A student taking a subject the school does not offer, a home-educated student, or somebody resitting after leaving may enter as a private candidate through an examination centre instead. That changes who holds the administrative responsibility, and it is worth understanding before relying on it.

A centre controls the entry, the fees, the timetable version, the practical route in the sciences where one applies, and the invigilation. A tuition provider controls none of those. So the questions that decide whether a private entry is viable are centre questions: does it accept private candidates for this code, in this series, with this practical route, and by what date does the entry have to be in. Those answers should be obtained before any tuition is booked around them.

For sciences in particular the practical route question is decisive. Where a Cambridge centre enters candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, the assessment is entirely written and a private candidate can prepare for it fully. Where a practical paper is required, laboratory access has to be arranged through the centre, and not every centre offers it. Pearson assesses practical knowledge within the written papers, which is why the two boards are not interchangeable for a private candidate.
This page quotes no entry fees and no centre deadlines, because they belong to the centre and the board and they change. Ask directly, in writing, and get the answer before the plan is built.

sections.heading: The honesty line, and who may teach at all
paragraphs: Two boundaries belong on every page in this market and they are rarely both present. The first is academic. A tutor may teach content, explain what a command term demands, work through past questions and give feedback on the student's own answers. A tutor must never produce work that will be submitted, nor supply text for a student to copy, and the honest version of coursework support is feedback on a draft the student wrote.

The second is the materials rule. No tutor should reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The correct behaviour is to reference the official source and link to it, which is why there are no attachments on this page. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

The third is who may tutor. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

The fourth is claims. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after a series on the basis of that series' papers. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none; describing what a regulator does is not the same as being endorsed by it.

process.title: Get the four administrative facts
process.description: Board, syllabus code, entry tier and the centre's administrative zone, in writing from the exams officer, plus the paper numbers. Those four decide which past papers matter and which timetable is correct, and everything else on a plan is downstream of them.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis with no card details taken. It establishes whether marks are going on content, method, command-term reading or timing, and it includes a check that the student knows their own paper dates from their own centre's timetable.

process.title: Place the work where the calendar can use it
process.description: Weekly work in Year 10 while the tier recommendation is still open, a mock-review session in Year 11 autumn, and an eight-week block of timed papers in the spring. That is a smaller total spend than two flat years and it puts each hour where it earns most.

process.title: Fix the slot and settle the room
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and end before Maghrib rather than against it. The Corniche's short school runs make a 4:00pm start realistic; the thing to settle in week one is which room in the flat is the quiet one and what the rest of the household does during the session.

process.title: Use results week properly
process.description: Ask the school for the component breakdown before deciding anything, then take one diagnostic session on it. A narrow shortfall on one paper is a different problem from a broad one across all of them, and only the first is reliably closed by a short block before the next series.

whyPoints.title: Sourced dates, and no invented ones
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson positions come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026, and past dates keep their year because that is what makes them checkable. Future series are named by month, so the page does not go stale without anybody touching it.

whyPoints.title: The India correction, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's February and March series is offered to candidates in India. A centre in Ajman enters June and November. Pages in this market have told UAE parents otherwise, and a wrong date a family acts on is worse than a thin page.

whyPoints.title: The zone warning passed on
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, states that the correct version of the timetable must be used, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. That belongs on a tuition page and is on almost none.

whyPoints.title: Year 10 treated as the decisive year
whyPoints.description: The tier recommendation forms in the spring of Year 10 and sets the ceiling on the certificate. A term of targeted work before it is worth more than two terms after it, which is the opposite of how most families spend.

faqs.question: Why does the IGCSE entry close so long before the exams?
faqs.answer: Because it is a logistics date rather than a readiness date. A board has to print papers, allocate them to centres, build timetables for six administrative zones, arrange invigilation and prepare scripts for marking, and all of that has to be finalised before any candidate sits down. The consequence for a family is that the entry is a forecast: the tier is submitted on what the school knows in the autumn, and the student then has months to become somebody that entry no longer suits.

faqs.question: When will my child in Ajman Corniche actually get their results?
faqs.answer: It depends on the series, and the gap is larger than most families expect. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November entry buys four to five extra months of preparation at the cost of a result arriving in January, which matters a great deal if a post-16 place depends on it. Tell the receiving institution in advance rather than asking it to accommodate the gap later.

faqs.question: Is the February or March Cambridge series available to a centre in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to candidates in India. A centre in the UAE enters the June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. This matters because revision material and tutoring pages written for an India audience circulate freely here, and a family planning around a February exam window and a late-autumn entry deadline is planning around a different country's calendar entirely.

faqs.question: Could my child in Ajman be revising from the wrong Cambridge timetable?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. The board states that it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. A timetable found online or borrowed from another country may list a paper on a different day. Ask your centre which zone it is in and revise from the centre's own copy.

faqs.question: Which term really decides my child's IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: Year 10 spring, which is when the school's tier recommendation forms on the basis of internal assessment. The tier sets a ceiling on the certificate that cannot be lifted after entries close, so a term of targeted work before the recommendation changes more than two terms afterwards. Most families invert this, treating Year 10 as preparation and Year 11 as the year that matters, which is why so much spring-of-Year-11 tuition arrives at a problem created a year earlier.

faqs.question: Can a November entry be the main plan rather than a resit?
faqs.answer: For some students, yes, and it is undersold as an option. A candidate who joined the course late, missed a term, or is sitting a subject outside the school's normal timetable may do better in the later window than by being pushed into June. The trade is the results timing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Whether that works depends entirely on what is waiting for the grade, so establish the destination's deadline before choosing the series.

faqs.question: How do I enter my child as a private candidate from Ajman?
faqs.answer: Through an examination centre rather than through a school, and the centre controls almost everything that matters: whether it accepts private candidates for that code and series, the entry deadline, the fees, the timetable version, the practical route in the sciences, and invigilation. Ask those questions in writing before building any tuition plan around the entry. This page quotes no entry fees or deadlines because they belong to the centre and the board and they change.

faqs.question: How is science practical work handled for a private candidate?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route the centre enters. Where a Cambridge centre enters candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, the assessment is entirely written and a private candidate can prepare for it fully: identifying controlled variables, spotting a flaw in a method, reading a scale, plotting and interpreting results. Where a practical paper is required, laboratory access has to be arranged through the centre and not every centre offers it. Pearson assesses practical knowledge within its written papers instead.

faqs.question: What should we do with the mock papers rather than just the mock grade?
faqs.answer: Read them by cause rather than by topic, within a fortnight, while the student remembers their thinking. Four questions: which marks were lost to content never securely learned, which to method where the knowledge was present and the working did not earn it, which to the command term where a different question was answered, and which to time. Those four need four different responses and only the first needs teaching. Write the result down as an error log.

faqs.question: Can a session start at 4pm for a family on the Corniche?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the few parts of Ajman where it is straightforward. School runs from the seafront towers are among the shortest in the emirate, often around fifteen minutes, so after food and a short break a 4:00pm start works. Because lessons run online, no travel is added at either end of the slot. The real constraint here is space rather than time: a flat needs an agreed quiet room for forty-five uninterrupted minutes.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor on Ajman Corniche worth the extra cost?
faqs.answer: It buys physical presence, which matters for a younger or easily distracted student, and the premium is real. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, while in-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, read October 2026. For IGCSE paper work, where most of a session is a question, a mark scheme and a shared screen, that premium buys relatively little.

faqs.question: Can one Ajman student sit some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson?
faqs.answer: That is a centre and school question rather than a tutoring one, and in practice it happens: a student may sit most subjects with one board and one or two with another, particularly where a subject is taken privately. What it means for preparation is that past papers, paper structures and practical routes do not transfer between the boards, so each subject has to be prepared against its own code. Confirm the full list of codes with the exams officer in writing.

faqs.question: How much of the final eight weeks should be full papers?
faqs.answer: At least one a fortnight per subject, and more in the sciences. A full paper tests pacing, the decision about which question to leave, and stamina through the long data questions at the end, none of which appear in a forty-five-minute session. The rest of the block is best spent on question groups attempted under time and marked to the published scheme in the session, so the student reads the marker's wording rather than the answer.

faqs.question: Is there a permit a private tutor must hold before teaching my child?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Why will you not reprint the next series timetable on this page?
faqs.answer: Because boards revise them. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of a series and then issues final versions, and Cambridge timetables differ by administrative zone, so any date reprinted here could be wrong for your centre or out of date by the time you read it. The sourced past dates on this page keep their year because that is what makes them checkable. For anything forward-looking, the live official timetable and your centre's own copy are the only versions worth using.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Helio costs you, in money and in minutes
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic a search engine will not do for you. An in-home IGCSE tutor visiting Al Helio charges for the hour taught and, indirectly, for the hour spent getting there and back. Market rates collected across the UAE in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180-350 on Bestimate's own rate table, with independent home tutors quoting as high as AED 500. The same qualified-subject-tutor tier delivered online sits at roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. The gap between those two bands is not a quality gap. It is a car.

Al Helio sits inland, off Sheikh Ammar bin Humaid Street, with Al Nuaimiya to the north-west and Al Mowaihat and Al Rawda on either side. A tutor living in Sharjah or Dubai who agrees to a 5pm session in Al Helio is committing to the late-afternoon run up Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road, and will price that commitment in. A tutor living in Ajman itself avoids the drive but belongs to a far smaller pool: Ajman's private-school sector is modest, and the number of adults in it who have taught Cambridge Physics 0625 Extended to a Year 11 class is smaller still.

That is the comparison worth making before any money changes hands. If your child needs help with Mathematics 0580 at Core level, a competent generalist within fifteen minutes' drive may be entirely adequate. If your child needs Chemistry 0620 Extended, where marks turn on titration calculations and ionic-equation balancing, the question is not who is close. It is who has marked that paper and knows which of the six command verbs on it actually demands a comparison rather than a description.

Move the same question one neighbourhood over and nothing changes. A family in Al Nuaimiya has the same short local tutor list and the same long drive-in list. A family in Al Jurf or Emirates City has a slightly different commute and an identical shortage of Extended-tier science specialists. This is the honest finding of this page: in Ajman the binding constraint is the depth of the subject pool, not the distance to it, and distance is the only one of those two that a car solves.

So here is what IB Gram does and does not do. Lessons for Al Helio students are delivered one-to-one over live video, on a screen the student and tutor both write on, timed to Gulf Standard Time around the Ajman school day. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Al Helio or anywhere else in the UAE; door-to-door visiting is a service we run only in India. What that buys you is choice of teacher rather than choice of postcode, and it is why the rest of this page is about syllabus codes, exam series and permits rather than driving times.
