sections.heading: Coursework and controlled assessment when the deadline is close
paragraphs: Fewer IGCSE subjects carry coursework than used to, but where a component exists it is usually the one causing the panic, because it has a fixed date and cannot be revised for. That pressure is exactly when families get offered help of the wrong kind.

The boundary is the same across every board and qualification. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain what the mark criteria require in specific terms, question whether the evidence actually supports the conclusion, and help the student decide what to fix with the hours remaining. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to a finished state, or supply text for submission. Work that is not the student's own puts the certification itself at risk, which is a far larger loss than a weak component mark.

It is worth knowing that an active market in exactly this exists in the same search results a parent is reading. One site in this segment sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. The same logic applies to any paid writing of an IGCSE coursework piece: the detection route is mundane, because a teacher who has read a student's work all year notices a change in voice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

Where a component is genuinely beyond repair in the time left, the honest advice is to submit the best version the student can produce and redirect the remaining hours to the written papers, which carry more marks. That is a less comfortable conversation than an offer to fix it, and it is the one that leaves the qualification intact.

process.title: Get three facts from the school
process.description: The board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier entered, and which timetable version applies to your centre. Those three facts determine everything a tutor can usefully do, and almost no family has them written in one place before February of Year 11. The examinations officer can supply all three.

process.title: Say where you are in the calendar
process.description: Year 10 with the tier still open, Year 11 before mocks, the eight weeks after mocks, or a resit decision after results. Each of those is a different purchase with a different realistic scope, and naming it prevents the commonest disappointment in this market, which is buying the wrong format for the wrong month.

process.title: Free trial on real material
process.description: One lesson at no charge with no payment details taken, spent on a past-paper question from the correct board and tier rather than on a general assessment. You get a short written note afterwards naming the priority, and the note is what to judge, because it shows whether the tutor is reading the examination or the student's mood.

process.title: Agree a block with an endpoint
process.description: A stated number of hours aimed at named weaknesses, with a diagnostic at the start and the same paper type at the end. Open-ended weekly arrangements run for a year without review. A block forces a decision point, and a decision point is what turns spending into evidence.

process.title: Re-plan on the mock scripts
process.description: After mocks the plan is rewritten from what the scripts show, marked question by question against the published scheme, with each loss tagged as content, retrieval, method or timing. That is the one point in the year when the evidence is good enough to justify changing course, and the point most families instead use to work harder at the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the board's timetable
whyPoints.description: The schedule starts from the published series and the school's own dates, not from a generic revision chart. That ordering is what tells a family in February whether they are buying technique, content or a resit plan, and the three are not interchangeable.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation handled with evidence
whyPoints.description: Marked work at both tiers under timed conditions, with a written summary for the subject teacher. It is the cheapest intervention in the whole sequence and it happens at the only point when the answer still changes the grade ceiling.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts used as diagnosis
whyPoints.description: Marks recorded question by question and each loss tagged. Timing losses need timed practice, retrieval failures need recall testing, and only genuine content gaps need teaching. In most scripts the content gaps are a minority of the marks lost.

whyPoints.title: Dates quoted with sources and framing
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own pages, with historical results dates keeping their years so they can be checked. Future series are named by month only. The February and March series is identified as offered to India, not the UAE.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan and holidays planned in advance
whyPoints.description: The month is scheduled around deliberately, either shifting after Iftar or pausing with an intensive block afterwards, and holiday weeks are used for the full timed papers that a single weekly hour cannot accommodate.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals, no invented figures
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation, has no UAE premises, and publishes no success percentage, because we could not produce the data behind one. The permit relevant to private tutoring here is a labour authorisation, not a quality mark.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE candidates in Al Jurf sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The exact dates depend on your centre: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Work from the timetable your school's examinations officer issues, not from a version found online.

faqs.question: How far ahead does the exam entry actually close?
faqs.answer: Months ahead of the paper. Boards have to produce and distribute materials, allocate centres and build timetables across several time zones, so entries close well before the series. Once they do, the subject, tier and board are fixed for that candidate. The practical consequence is uncomfortable: problems usually become obvious in the autumn of Year 11, after the window for changing anything about the entry has closed, which leaves teaching and technique as the only remaining levers.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth entering after a weak June result?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding factor is usually timing rather than ability. Pearson's November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a resit result arrives in January, which may fall after a sixth-form or university deadline. Check that first. Also check what re-entry involves: the full paper set for the subject is sat again, not the single paper that went badly, which means carrying it alongside the start of Year 12.

faqs.question: Can the school still change my child's tier in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and certainly not after the entry closes. Tier is set by the school, generally during Year 10, and it caps the grades available. If you believe the decision is wrong, the time to produce evidence is while it is still open: two or three sessions of marked tier-appropriate past-paper work under timed conditions give you a document to take to the subject teacher instead of an impression. Sometimes that evidence confirms the school's view, which is also worth knowing early.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to Al Jurf homes?
faqs.answer: No. In-home tutoring is a service IB Gram provides only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for Al Jurf families run live over video, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers and data tables annotated on a shared screen. We target the home-tutor phrase because it is what parents search, and then answer it honestly. Families who need an adult physically present with a younger child should hire a local visiting tutor instead.

faqs.question: We are eight weeks from the series. What is realistic?
faqs.answer: Paper technique, timing discipline, command-term accuracy and two or three named topic gaps. That is genuinely worth marks. Reteaching a two-year syllabus is not realistic and any plan claiming it is not reading the calendar. The most effective shape is a block of eight to twelve sessions aimed at whatever the mock scripts show as the most expensive failure types, with a re-test on the same paper type at the end so the result is visible rather than felt.

faqs.question: What should we do with the summer between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Fix the Year 10 content that was never secured, which is cheaper and calmer in a quiet month than in February. Mole calculations in chemistry, algebraic fluency in mathematics and recall volume in biology are the usual candidates, because each compounds through Year 11. Two or three sessions a month through the summer costs a fraction of the emergency block it prevents, and a student starting Year 11 without last year's gaps has a materially different year.

faqs.question: How do we read mock results properly?
faqs.answer: Ignore the percentage on the front and read the script. Mark it against the published scheme, record marks by question rather than as a total, and tag each loss as content not known, content not retrievable, method abandoned, or time run out. Those four need completely different responses and only one of them is fixed by more revision. Two papers are normally enough to show the pattern, and the pattern is what the next block of sessions should be aimed at.

faqs.question: Is Ramadan a problem for a Year 11 revision plan?
faqs.answer: Only if nobody plans for it. School days shorten, fasting afternoons are low-energy, and the productive hours move to after Iftar. Two patterns work: shift sessions to roughly 9pm onwards, which suits timed papers better than new content, or pause the month and book an intensive block afterwards. Decide in advance, because late-evening slots fill quickly across the Gulf and a preferred tutor may not be free at short notice.

faqs.question: Why does the timetable version matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, and its guidance states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. A date found online can be entirely real and belong to a different zone or a different series. Take the timetable from your school's examinations officer, and build any revision plan or travel arrangement around that document only.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an IGCSE coursework component?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain what each mark criterion requires, question whether the evidence supports the conclusion and help the student prioritise with the hours left. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to a finished state or supply text for submission. Work that is not the student's own risks the qualification, not just the component mark. If a component is genuinely beyond repair in the time left, redirect the hours to the written papers.

faqs.question: My child has mocks next month and has not finished the syllabus. What now?
faqs.answer: Triage rather than coverage. Find out from the subject teacher which topics the mock will examine, secure the ones that carry the most marks, and accept that the untaught material will cost marks in the mock without that being a prediction about the series. A mock is a diagnostic, not a verdict, and its most valuable output is the breakdown of how your child fails under time, which is still produced even when the content coverage is incomplete.

faqs.question: Do holiday intensive blocks actually work better than weekly hours?
faqs.answer: For some things, yes. A holiday week is the only realistic window in the year for sitting three full papers under proper timed conditions and having them marked, and that exercise is worth more than several isolated weekly hours. Weekly teaching is better for building content across a term. The error is using holidays for content coverage and term time for timed papers, which is the way round most families default to and the less effective of the two.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are riskiest to leave until the final term?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606, because the content is new rather than extended and cannot be compressed. Chemistry, because organic chemistry is often taught late and a student can reach mocks never having been examined on a third of the Extended content. Biology, because recall volume takes weeks. English, by contrast, responds relatively well to a short late block, since its gains come from a few repeatable techniques applied under time.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.closingHeading: Tell us where you are in the series
ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-jurf.closingBody: One message does it: the subjects, the board and syllabus code, the tier entered, and whether you are in Year 10 with the tier still open, in Year 11 before mocks, in the weeks after them, or deciding about a November resit. We will reply with what that position makes realistically achievable, whether a tutor who has taught that specification is free in an Al Jurf evening slot, and what shape of block fits the weeks remaining. The trial lesson runs on a real past-paper question from your child's own board and tier, and the written note afterwards is the thing worth judging.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mowaihat.tutorsIntro: Al Mowaihat families are matched with subject teachers who name the syllabus code and the papers before anything else, and who will take a slot that starts within an hour of the school bell rather than one that suits them.

intro.heading: The window is about two and a half hours wide
paragraphs: Al Mowaihat's three villa districts sit along Sheikh Ammar Road, which is the single most useful fact on this page. The road runs Al Mowaihat into Ajman's school belt in ten to twenty minutes depending on the hour, which is short by the standards of this emirate and the reason a mid-afternoon session is actually achievable here. Families in Al Zorah or Al Rawda do not have that option, and the plans they make look different as a result.

Work the day forward. Most private schools in Ajman finish between 2:00pm and 3:00pm, with buses arriving back into the villa districts between 2:45pm and 3:45pm. There is then a real need for food, a change of clothes and twenty minutes of nothing. That puts the earliest honest start at around 4:00pm, and the window closes at roughly 6:30pm for a Year 10 or 11 student who still has school homework, Maghrib prayer and a family dinner to fit in.

Two and a half hours is not much, and this is where the delivery format becomes a timetable decision rather than a preference. An in-home tutor driving in from Sharjah or from central Ajman consumes 30 to 50 minutes of that window before anybody opens a book, and in evening traffic rather more. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, which means the session can begin at 4:15pm because nobody has to arrive. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India.

The second half of this page is about the specifics of IGCSE in this particular school belt. Which board a school is entered with changes the syllabus code, the paper structure and sometimes the tiering, and parents are frequently unsure which of Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel their child is sitting. That is not a failure of attention: schools talk about subjects, not about codes. But the code is what decides which past papers are worth the two and a half hours.

Everything factual below is sourced and dated. Cambridge and Pearson positions come from the boards' own exam-administration pages, read in October 2026. Where a figure or a date is not verified, this page says so instead of filling the gap. That matters more than it sounds: an earlier version of this project's research offered the Cambridge February and March key dates as its worked example, and those dates apply to candidates in India rather than in the Gulf. A date a parent plans around has to be right for their country, so the series named here are the ones an Ajman centre actually enters, and the official timetable is linked rather than reprinted because boards revise provisional versions. Nothing on this page should be the last thing you check before an entry deadline; it should be the thing that tells you which question to ask your exams officer.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mowaihat.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to an Al Mowaihat household running an IGCSE timetable, and each one takes a different share of the weekday window. The entry decisions that affect the final grade are taken a year earlier than most families expect.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: No external papers, which makes this the cheapest and most effective place to fix foundations. Algebraic fluency, written method, scientific vocabulary and reading speed are built here or they are repaired expensively in Year 11. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for schools that use them.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where Al Mowaihat's short school run pays off most. A 4:00pm half-hour session twice a week is easy to sustain at Year 8 and almost impossible to sustain at Year 11, when school homework alone fills the window.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Each subject is a separate qualification with its own syllabus code. Mathematics 0580 splits into Core, which caps at grade C, and Extended, which runs to A*. Sciences such as Physics 0625 and Chemistry 0620 offer Core and Extended papers plus a practical route decided by the centre. Knowing the code and the tier decides which practice is worth doing.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge's zone system is the detail nobody in this market mentions. Every centre sits in one of six administrative zones and the board states that using the correct version of the timetable for the zone is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSEs carry their own codes: 4MA1 for Mathematics A with Foundation and Higher tiers, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology. The assessment structure differs from Cambridge's in the number of papers and in how practical skills are examined, so past-paper practice does not transfer between the two boards.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson exams run in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always use the live official PDF.

programmes.name: What follows Year 11
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade set determines which post-16 routes stay open: A Levels, the IB Diploma, or a BTEC pathway. Mathematics and the sciences are where doors close quietly, because a Core entry or a Foundation tier result can rule out a Higher Level or A Level option regardless of how well the student performed within that tier.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. Worth knowing in Year 10, not after results.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mowaihat.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones most often requested from the Al Mowaihat school belt, with the code, the usual failure point, and what fits into a two-and-a-half-hour weekday window.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most common wasted term in this subject is practising the wrong tier. Extended Paper 4 rewards method marks, so working has to be written out even when the answer is obvious. A 45-minute weekday session is enough for one paper section plus marking.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the heaviest losses. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's entry, and the two need different preparation: handling apparatus against reading somebody else's experiment.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall. Students who balance equations confidently still lose marks converting between mass, moles and volume under time pressure. Organic chemistry at Extended needs the homologous series learned as a pattern, not a list.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Long answers reward sequence and precision: naming a process earns a mark, ordering its stages earns the rest. Extended adds genetics problems where a Punnett square must be drawn properly rather than reasoned about aloud.

subjects.name: Mathematics - Additional and Further
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Maths or a Higher Level Diploma course. It bridges to calculus and trigonometric identities early, and it is the subject where a weak Year 9 algebra foundation becomes unmissable.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Writing papers are marked on content and language separately and the task types are prescriptive. A fluent writer who ignores the register of a report or an email loses content marks fluency cannot recover. Listening practice must be done at exam speed.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses are where marks move. Students lose them by retelling the passage instead of analysing how it works, and by writing more than the time allows rather than planning for four minutes first.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the entire paper. The usual pattern is a student who knows every definition and cannot use the business in the stimulus, which caps answers at the lowest band regardless of how much theory appears.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries disproportionate weight and most students draw curves without labelling axes, shifts or the new equilibrium. Data-response questions reward quoting the figure from the extract rather than describing it vaguely.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Running alongside the international timetable rather than instead of it. For the mandatory national subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support works inside the school's own prescribed material.

sections.heading: What time the school day actually ends around Al Mowaihat
paragraphs: Every tuition plan in this emirate fails or holds on this single number, and almost nobody writes it down. Private schools in Ajman generally finish between 2:00pm and 3:00pm, earlier than the Dubai pattern many families arrive expecting. Bus routes then add twenty to forty-five minutes depending on which of the Al Mowaihat districts a household sits in and how many stops come first.

What follows is not negotiable and is usually underestimated: food, a change out of uniform, and a short period of doing nothing at all. A fifteen-year-old pushed straight from the bus into a tutoring session produces an hour of compliance rather than an hour of learning, and the family pays for both at the same rate. Building in forty minutes of decompression is the cheapest performance intervention available.

That arithmetic puts the earliest honest start at around 4:00pm for Al Mowaihat 1 and nearer 4:30pm for Al Mowaihat 3. The far end of the window is set by school homework, Maghrib prayer and dinner, and for a Year 11 student with three subjects of homework it closes at about 6:30pm. Weekends and the pre-series period are where anything longer than an hour has to live.

Confirm the finish time with your own school rather than inheriting it from this page, because timings vary by section and change between terms, and a primary sibling frequently finishes at a different hour from a Year 11. The table below is a framework for the calculation rather than a published schedule, and it is worth filling in once with your own numbers at the start of the year.

sections.heading: What actually fits inside two and a half hours
paragraphs: Once the window is measured, the planning question changes from how many hours to buy into what can be completed inside one sitting. Forty-five minutes is enough for a defined, finishable task. It is not enough for a full Extended Paper 4, which runs well beyond that and cannot usefully be split across two weeks because the point of a full paper is the stamina.

So the weekday session should be built around a section rather than a paper. One question group, attempted under time, then marked against the published scheme in the same sitting, with the student reading the marker's wording rather than the answer. That cycle takes thirty to forty minutes and produces something concrete: a specific, named reason a mark was lost. Four of those a month is a diagnosis; a term of unstructured hours is not.

Full papers belong at the weekend or in the pre-series block, and sciences in particular need the longer slot because the data questions at the end of a paper are where time pressure bites. A student who always runs out of time on the last two questions has a pacing problem that only shows up in a full sitting.

The practical consequence for an Al Mowaihat family is a split week: a short weekday slot for diagnosis and repair, and one longer weekend block during the twelve weeks before a series. That shape costs less than two weekday sessions and achieves more, because it matches the work to the time available rather than to the invoice.

sections.heading: Which board is your child actually entered with?
paragraphs: This is the most common source of wasted practice in the Northern Emirates, and it is nobody's fault. Schools talk about Maths, Physics and Biology. Awarding bodies issue codes, and the codes decide which past papers exist and what shape they take. A family downloading Cambridge 0580 papers for a child entered with Pearson 4MA1 is practising a different examination.

The two boards differ in more than branding. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits candidates into Core and Extended, with different papers and a grade ceiling of C on Core. Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 uses Foundation and Higher tiers. In the sciences, Cambridge centres choose between a practical paper and the alternative-to-practical paper, which examine genuinely different skills; Pearson assesses practical knowledge within its written papers. None of that is apparent from a school report.

Both boards also run different session structures. Cambridge offers June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with a warning that the correct zone timetable must be used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, publishes provisional timetables in advance, and revises them, which is why this page links the live official timetable rather than reprinting dates.

The fix takes one email. Ask the exams officer for the board, the syllabus code, the tier or entry level and the paper numbers for every subject, in writing. Then the two and a half hours a week can be spent on the right examination.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision taken a year early
paragraphs: The tiering decision is the quietest high-stakes choice in an IGCSE course. It is usually made by the school in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the basis of internal assessment, and it sets a ceiling on what the final certificate can say. A Cambridge Core entry caps at grade C. A Pearson Foundation entry caps lower than Higher. Neither cap can be lifted after entries close.

There is a genuine argument for the lower tier, and it is not the one families fear. A student entered above their level spends a year meeting questions they cannot attempt, loses confidence, and often ends with a worse grade than the lower tier would have produced. Secure performance inside Core is more useful than a scattered performance across Extended. The mistake is not choosing a tier; it is choosing it without knowing what it closes.

What it closes matters at the post-16 stage. A Core or Foundation result in Mathematics or a science can rule out an A Level or a Diploma Higher Level option regardless of how strong the result was within its tier, because the course assumes content that only the higher tier covered. That is the conversation to have in Year 10, while the entry is still open and while a term of targeted work could still change the recommendation.

It also matters for equivalency. The published requirement on the British track is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E. Tiering does not affect that threshold, but it affects which five subjects are safe to count on.

sections.heading: Practical science when the lab is at school and the tutor is on a screen
paragraphs: This is the honest objection to online tuition in the sciences, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a deflection. A tutor on a screen cannot hand a student a burette. What a tutor can do, and what the examination actually rewards, is a different and larger set of things.

Start with what the paper asks. Where a Cambridge centre enters candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, the examination is entirely about reading somebody else's experiment: identifying the variable that was controlled, spotting the flaw in a method, reading a scale correctly, plotting and interpreting results, and suggesting an improvement. Every one of those is a written skill and every one of them is better taught with the paper on a shared screen than with apparatus on a bench.

Where the centre enters candidates for a practical paper instead, the laboratory work is done at school with school equipment, as it must be. The tuition contribution is the write-up and the thinking around it: planning, tabulating, uncertainty, and the evaluation that students habitually write as a list of mistakes rather than as an argument about which error mattered most. Pearson assesses practical knowledge within the written papers, which makes the same written skills decisive there too.

The table sets out which paper examines what, so a family can confirm the centre's entry and then stop worrying about the part that is not being examined. Confirm the entry with the exams officer; it is a centre decision rather than a student one.

sections.heading: Building the week around prayer, sport and homework
paragraphs: A tuition slot does not fail because it was badly taught. It fails because it was placed in the one part of the week that was always going to break. The fixed points in an Al Mowaihat week are school, the drive, prayer times, school homework, and whatever sport or activity the family has already committed to, and a tuition session has to be fitted between them rather than on top of them.

Prayer times shift through the year, which means a slot set in September may collide with Maghrib by November. Building the session to end before the prayer rather than butting against it removes a recurring source of cancelled sessions. During Ramadan the pattern changes more sharply: school hours shorten, the useful study window moves to after Iftar, and an online session can simply move with it where an in-home visit usually cannot.

The other predictable collision is the school's own assessment calendar. A tuition session the evening before a school test is almost always better spent on that test than on the tutor's planned sequence, and a tutor working from the school's assessment dates can plan around it. That is an argument for telling the tutor those dates at the start of term rather than discovering the clash each week.

The last point is the one families resist: fewer, better-placed sessions beat more, badly placed ones. A single 4:15pm Tuesday slot that never moves builds more over a term than three slots that are each cancelled twice a month.
bullets: Set the session to end before the prayer, not to run up against it.
Give the tutor the school's assessment dates at the start of term.
Move to post-Iftar timing for Ramadan rather than cancelling the month.
One slot that never moves beats three that are frequently cancelled.

sections.heading: The November route and the results gap nobody plans for
paragraphs: Most families treat the summer series as the only series, which makes a disappointing result feel final when it is not. Both boards run a second window, and understanding how it works changes what a family does in the week results arrive rather than three months later.

For Cambridge, the resit route is the November series, with June as the main sitting. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, exams are available in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The gap that catches people out is the results timing: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry therefore means waiting until January, which matters if a post-16 place depends on the grade.

The decision in results week is a diagnostic one, not an emotional one. A grade that missed by one mark on one paper is a different problem from a grade that missed across every paper, and only the first is reliably fixed by a short resit block. Asking the school for the component breakdown before entering a resit is the step most families skip, and it is the step that decides whether the entry fee is well spent.

Private candidate entries work differently from school entries, with fees paid through a centre rather than through the school. Ask the centre directly about entry deadlines and charges; they are set by the centre and the board, not by anybody selling tuition, and this page does not quote them.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with IGCSE work
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less internally assessed weight than the IB Diploma, which makes the honesty line simpler but not less important. The boundary is that a tutor teaches, explains and gives feedback on the student's own work, and never produces work that will be submitted.

The second boundary concerns materials. No tutor should reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. The correct behaviour is to reference the official source and link to it, which is why there are no attachments on this page. Reproducing assessment material is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material a malpractice exposure.

The third is honesty about outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, because boundaries are set after the series on the basis of that series' papers. What tuition reliably changes is the volume and quality of deliberate practice, the student's reading of command terms, and the gap between what they know and what reaches the page. Any provider offering a promised grade or money back against a result is either misunderstanding how boundaries work or hoping the question is not asked.

A note on who may tutor at all. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

process.title: Send the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Ask your exams officer for the awarding body, the syllabus code, the entry tier and the paper numbers, in writing, and send those. Cambridge 0620 Extended is a different request from Pearson 4CH1, and the difference decides which past papers are worth the weekday window.

process.title: Tell us when the bus actually arrives
process.description: The useful detail is not the school finish time but the time your child walks through the door, which district you are in and whether a parent is still commuting. That is what sets the slot. In Al Mowaihat it usually allows a 4:00pm to 4:30pm start, which is rare in this emirate.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is a diagnosis rather than a sales call, with no card details taken. The tutor works through real paper questions to find whether marks go on recall, method, command-term reading or timing, and you keep the written summary naming the first three targets.

process.title: Fix one slot and protect it
process.description: A single weekday slot that never moves builds more across a term than three that are cancelled twice a month. We set it to end before Maghrib rather than against it, and we take the school's assessment dates at the start of term so the session can flex around a school test.

process.title: Add a weekend block only before a series
process.description: Full papers need ninety minutes and cannot be split across two weeks, so they belong at the weekend during the twelve weeks before mocks or a series. Outside that period the weekday slot alone is usually the right purchase, and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Built around the clock, not around the tutor
whyPoints.description: Sessions start within an hour of the bus arriving because nobody has to travel to Al Mowaihat first. An in-home visit consumes 30 to 50 minutes of a two-and-a-half-hour window before a book is opened, and in evening traffic rather more.

whyPoints.title: Codes before promises
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and 0625, Pearson 4MA1 and 4PH1: the tutor names the syllabus and the papers they have taught before quoting anything. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the entire seven-page competitor area cluster researched for this project.

whyPoints.title: The zone warning passed on
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. That belongs on a tuition page, and it is on almost none of them.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer on practical science
whyPoints.description: A tutor on a screen cannot hand a student a burette. What the alternative-to-practical paper examines is reading somebody else's experiment, which is a written skill better taught with the paper on a shared screen than with apparatus on a bench.

whyPoints.title: A plan with an end date
whyPoints.description: Pre-series blocks finish on a stated date rather than becoming a permanent subscription, and weekly work steps down once the diagnosed gap closes. A provider that never proposes reducing the frequency is managing revenue rather than marks.

whyPoints.title: Nothing borrowed, nothing promised
whyPoints.description: No promised grades, no self-published ratings, no claim of approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and no syllabus documents or mark schemes supplied as downloads. The official source is linked instead.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a tuition session can realistically start in Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: Around 4:00pm for Al Mowaihat 1 and nearer 4:30pm for Al Mowaihat 3. Work it forward: schools in Ajman generally finish between 2:00pm and 3:00pm, buses reach the villa districts between 2:45pm and 3:45pm, and then thirty to forty-five minutes are needed for food and decompression. Pushing a fifteen-year-old straight off the bus into a lesson buys an hour of compliance rather than an hour of learning. Because lessons run online, no travel time is added at either end of that slot.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Pearson in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, in writing, for the awarding body, the syllabus code, the entry tier and the paper numbers for every subject. Schools talk about Maths and Physics; boards issue codes, and the codes decide which past papers exist. A family practising Cambridge 0580 for a child entered with Pearson 4MA1 is preparing for a different examination. It is one email and it is the highest-value email of the year.

faqs.question: Is 45 minutes after school long enough to be worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the session is built around a finishable task rather than a whole paper. One question group attempted under time, then marked against the published scheme in the same sitting, with the student reading the marker's wording rather than the answer, takes thirty to forty minutes and produces a specific named reason a mark was lost. Full papers need ninety minutes and belong at the weekend, because the stamina across a complete paper is itself part of what is being tested.

faqs.question: Which schools does Al Mowaihat feed, and what time do they finish?
faqs.answer: Sheikh Ammar Road puts Al Mowaihat within a short drive of most of Ajman's larger private schools, including Ajman Academy, Ajman Modern School, The City School Ajman, Habitat School Ajman, Pace British School Ajman and Al Ameer English School. Finish times generally fall between 2:00pm and 3:00pm but vary by section and change between terms, so confirm with your own school rather than relying on this page. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; no affiliation is implied by naming them.

faqs.question: Can online tuition handle IGCSE practical science properly?
faqs.answer: It depends on which paper the centre has entered, and that is worth checking. Where candidates sit the alternative-to-practical paper, the examination is entirely about reading somebody else's experiment: identifying controlled variables, spotting a flaw in a method, reading a scale, plotting and interpreting results. Those are written skills, and a shared screen suits them better than a bench. Where a practical paper is entered, the laboratory work happens at school and tuition contributes the planning, tabulation, uncertainty and evaluation.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core and wants an A. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Core caps at grade C, and that cap cannot be lifted after entries close, so the conversation has to happen while the entry is still open. Moving up to Extended means covering content the Core class did not teach, which is a defined block of work rather than an impossible one if there is a year to do it in. A diagnostic session establishes whether the student can reliably access the harder question types, which answers the question faster than waiting for the next mock.

faqs.question: Does a Core or Foundation entry close off A Levels or the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: It can, and this is the part of the tiering decision families most often discover too late. A Core or Foundation result in Mathematics or a science may rule out an A Level or a Diploma Higher Level option regardless of how strong the result was within that tier, because the post-16 course assumes content only the higher tier covered. Ask the post-16 coordinator which entries their courses require, in Year 10, while a term of targeted work could still change the recommendation.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change an Al Mowaihat tuition schedule?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten and the useful study window moves to after Iftar, which is exactly when an in-home tutor is least likely to be driving anywhere. An online session moves with the month: rescheduled to post-Iftar timing, or kept at the same frequency with shorter sessions. Set the arrangement before the month begins rather than cancelling week by week, because a quietly abandoned month is where a term's momentum is most often lost and where a pre-series plan slips.

faqs.question: Should the session move if there is a school test the next day?
faqs.answer: Almost always, yes. An evening before a school assessment is better spent on that assessment than on a tutor's planned sequence, and a tutor who has the school's assessment calendar can plan around it instead of colliding with it each time. Send those dates at the start of term. The broader principle is that one weekly slot which never gets cancelled builds far more across a term than three slots that each get dropped twice a month.

faqs.question: When will my child get November IGCSE results, and does that matter?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, whereas June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. So a November entry means waiting until January, which matters a great deal if a post-16 place depends on the grade. Factor that gap into any resit decision, and tell the receiving school about it rather than assuming they will allow for it.

faqs.question: Is a resit worth entering after a disappointing summer result?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the component breakdown before deciding. A grade that missed by one mark on one paper is a different problem from a grade that missed across every paper, and only the first is reliably fixed by a short pre-series block. That breakdown is the step most families skip and the one that decides whether the entry fee is well spent. Private candidate entries are arranged through a centre, with fees set by the centre and the board rather than by any tuition provider.

faqs.question: Why does this page keep mentioning Cambridge zones?
faqs.answer: Because the board does, and almost no tuition page passes it on. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A family revising from a timetable found online rather than from the centre's own version is taking a risk nobody mentioned to them.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Maths and Physics for a Year 11 in Al Mowaihat?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE level this is a reasonable pairing and worth asking about, because the mathematical technique in Physics overlaps with the Extended or Higher Maths content and a single tutor can reinforce both. Test the claim with specifics: which codes, which papers, and when each was last taught. The saving is usually in scheduling rather than in the rate, since one relationship means one slot pattern, one set of notes and one reporting rhythm instead of two.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers and mark schemes for Cambridge and Pearson?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutor should. Reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure. The correct approach is to reference the official source and link to it, which is why there are no attachments here. Work is done against material the student legitimately holds through their school, marked against the published scheme in the session.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a permit to teach IGCSE in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

intro.heading: Comparing three emirates from one address
paragraphs: Al Nuaimiya is one of Ajman's older, denser districts, close enough to the Sharjah boundary that daily life crosses it constantly. Children attend school in Ajman, in Sharjah and in Dubai. Parents work across all three. So a tutoring decision here is a cross-emirate comparison whether a family intends it to be or not.

Three things genuinely differ across that boundary, and the first is regulatory. Ajman's private schools, along with those in Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's fall under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Abu Dhabi's under the Department of Education and Knowledge. If your children attend school in two emirates, you are dealing with two sets of published information and two sets of processes.

The second difference is supply and price. Dubai has the deepest tutoring market in the country - the emirate recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25 - and prices to match. Sharjah has a long-established market concentrated around Al Majaz and Al Qasimia. Ajman's local market is smaller than either, which means a family here searching by distance gets a short list of generalists, and a tutor travelling from Dubai prices the journey.

The third is the school run, which decides what hour a session can start. A child at an Ajman school may be home by half past three. A child crossing into Sharjah or Dubai may not be home until five or later, and that is the single most important number in any tutoring plan.

Then there is everything that does not differ. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates wherever they sit. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The mark scheme for 0620 has no Ajman edition. The command terms mean the same thing on both sides of the boundary. The tutor permit is federal. Those facts are why we match on the board and the code rather than on the emirate, and teach one-to-one over live video - IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that service exists only in India.

One practical note on how to use this. If your child is young and the real need is an adult beside them to stay on task, local Ajman help is both cheaper and better suited than anything online, and we would say so rather than take the booking. The comparisons here are aimed at families whose problem is course-specific - a tier decision, a weak paper, an unfamiliar board - because that is where the local list runs out.

What follows is the regulator map, the three-emirate comparison on supply and cost, the school-run arithmetic, the board identification problem in a multi-curriculum district, and the list of things that are identical everywhere.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nuaimiya.subjectsIntro: The subjects Ajman families ask for most, with the codes that decide the match. None of this content varies by emirate, which is the point.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The highest-volume request here as everywhere. Bounds, algebraic rearrangement under time pressure and multi-step problems abandoned one operation early account for most lost marks, and all three respond to timed papers with immediate marking.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
subjects.description: Electricity and graph-gradient work dominate the losses. The Cambridge route's alternative-to-practical paper is a separate skill - named instruments, variables, sources of error - and is teachable in three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole ratios, electrolysis products and organic conditions, plus the language problem: the scheme wants the observation, not the conclusion. Precision recovers marks the student has already earned.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content is memorisable, so marks go on command words and diagram work. Genetic crosses, transport in plants and experimental design are where an hour converts most directly into marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics for curriculum crossovers
subjects.description: Ajman has a large Indian-curriculum school population, and students moving into IGCSE entries meet different question phrasing and stricter expectations about showing method. The content overlap is wide; the examination behaviour is not.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and reading analysis carry the grade. Summarising when asked to analyse effect is the standard loss, and timed writing annotated against the mark scheme moves this subject faster than reading more.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Widely taken in Ajman and Sharjah schools where English is the language of instruction but not of the home. Note-making, summary word limits and register shifts are formulaic enough to coach precisely.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward define, apply to the case, evaluate with a judgement. Economics diagram accuracy is a cheap source of marks that schools often leave to the student to sort out alone.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables cost more marks than programming ability, and the subject is among the hardest to staff locally at a weekday hour in any of the northern emirates.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, and why an Ajman family needs to know
paragraphs: This is the comparison nobody in this market publishes, and it is the one that affects an Ajman household most directly, because so many of them have children in schools under two different authorities.

The map is settled. The Ministry of Education plays a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods - so curriculum and fee approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate body there. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools.

What that means practically is about where to look for information. If your child's school is in Ajman, published guidance and processes come through the federal ministry. If it is in Sharjah, SPEA's framework applies to fees, curricula and assessment methods. If it is in Dubai, KHDA publishes a great deal - including its mandatory-subject requirements and its school inspection outcomes - which is useful reading even for families outside Dubai, because the federal baseline behind it is the same.

One federal rule underlies all of them: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is why your child's international programme shares its week with lessons that belong to none of it, whichever emirate the school sits in.

A final point on us, because regulator names in tutoring copy are often used to imply something. IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from the Ministry of Education, SPEA, KHDA, ADEK or any education authority, and we have no premises in this country. We can describe what these bodies do; we would never suggest any of them endorses us.

sections.heading: Ajman, Sharjah and Dubai compared for tutoring
paragraphs: With the regulatory picture settled, the practical comparison is about supply, price and journey - the three things that actually change when you cross a boundary.

Ajman's local tutoring market is the smallest of the three. There is general support available, and there are capable people, but the pool of tutors who have taught a specific syllabus code to grade standard for years is thin. A family filtering by distance from Al Nuaimiya gets a short list that skews heavily towards generalists, which is a supply fact rather than a comment on anybody's ability.

Sharjah is deeper, with its established districts around Al Majaz and Al Qasimia, and close enough that in-home arrangements from there into Ajman are common. The journey is priced into the rate, and in the eight to ten weeks before a series those tutors are committed to families nearer to them.

Dubai is deepest and most expensive. The emirate recorded 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, so the specialist population behind it is the largest in the country. In-home from Dubai into Ajman sits at the top of the market band once travel is absorbed. Online, that same specialist costs no more to reach than somebody in Al Rashidiya - which is the single most useful arbitrage available to a family at this address.

There is a seasonal footnote to all three. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series, and the denser markets fill first, so an Ajman family searching in that window finds the Sharjah and Dubai specialists committed to families nearer to them. Booking a scarce course early, even fortnightly, is what avoids choosing from the residue.

sections.heading: The cross-boundary school run
paragraphs: A large share of Al Nuaimiya students attend school outside Ajman, and the journey is the number that decides a tutoring plan. Everything else is negotiable; the time a child walks through the door is not.

For a child at an Ajman school, arrival home between half past two and half past three is normal, which makes a four o'clock session genuinely workable - the earliest slot available to almost any family in the northern emirates. For a child crossing into Sharjah, the afternoon return is slower than the morning journey and arrival between four and half past is typical. For a Dubai school, five o'clock or later is common.

Add a tutor's own journey and the arrangement starts to decay. A tutor coming from Sharjah or Dubai into Ajman is travelling in the same traffic, after their own working day. A session nominally at five begins at twenty past, ends early because another family is waiting, and is cancelled outright on the evenings when something goes wrong on the Emirates Road or the Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road. Families absorb that as the price of living here, and it is avoidable.

The online version is simply arithmetic: take the real arrival time, add thirty minutes for food and decompression, and that is the slot. If the bus is late the lesson moves by the same amount instead of disappearing. For a household with children at schools in two emirates, slots are then sequenced by arrival time, which turns four supervised evenings into one.

sections.heading: Which board, in a district with several curricula
paragraphs: Ajman has a large Indian-curriculum school population, and several schools enter some cohorts or subjects for Cambridge or Pearson papers. The practical consequence is that families here are less likely than most to know which board their child is sitting, and every tutoring decision depends on it.

The codes settle it. Cambridge uses four digits: 0580 mathematics, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English, 0510 English as a second language. Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a 4: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Both appear on the statement of entry and in the exam information the school circulates, and the exams officer can confirm board, code and tier in one reply.

Why it matters: the paper structures differ, the question phrasing differs, and the preparation differs accordingly. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended and its sciences include an alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson's maths sets two equally weighted papers. A tutor fluent in one board will give confident and wrong guidance about the other, and a student who has practised the wrong board's papers for a term usually finds out in a mock.

For crossover students the gap is examination behaviour rather than content. A capable candidate from a CBSE or ICSE background can lose marks because method is not shown and because command terms are treated as general invitations to write. Two to four board-specific sessions working through past papers, marked against the published scheme, close that gap faster than any amount of additional content teaching.

sections.heading: The cost comparison, with the premiums named
paragraphs: Prices in this market are rarely published, so a family here comparing three emirates is usually comparing anecdotes. The bands below are from published UAE rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026 - market figures rather than our price list.

Budget online tutoring, generally delivered by university students, advertises from about AED 45 an hour. A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300. An in-home one-to-one visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 or more. Monthly packages seen in the market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

There are two premiums inside those numbers and both are worth naming. The travel premium pays for a journey, and for an Ajman address served from Sharjah or Dubai it is at the higher end. The brand premium pays for reputation, often attached to an examiner claim that is rarely evidenced and never transfers to your child's paper. Neither changes what happens inside the hour.

Against that, there is a genuine Ajman advantage. Local general tutoring here tends to be priced below the Sharjah and Dubai equivalents, which makes it good value for exactly the jobs general tutoring does well: supervision, routine, working through practice questions a teacher has selected. The sensible combination for many households is cheap local help for discipline plus a small number of specialist online hours for direction.

sections.heading: What is identical across all three emirates
paragraphs: Having compared what varies, here is the list that does not - and it is the longer one, which is the whole argument of this page.

The examinations. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level papers in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any page telling northern-emirates parents to prepare for a February sitting is describing another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Entries are made by the school's centre, and the administrative zone that determines the timetable version belongs to that centre.

The marking. There is no Ajman edition of the 0625 mark scheme, no local variant of a command term, and no regional difference in the three topics where candidates lose the most marks in each subject. That is precisely why a tutor's course experience is the variable worth optimising and their emirate is not.

The permit and the honesty rules. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published. And a tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work in every emirate, and may never write any part of assessed coursework.

sections.heading: A decision checklist for an Al Nuaimiya family
paragraphs: Comparisons are only useful if they end somewhere, so here is the order we would suggest from this address.

First, establish the board, code and tier, and ask for the school's internal entry-change deadline in writing. In a district where schools run several curricula this is genuinely uncertain for many families, and it governs everything downstream, including whether a tier change is still possible.

Second, decide what kind of problem you have. Supervision and routine, which local Ajman help supplies cheaply and well. Or course-specific technique, triage and script analysis, which it generally cannot, and for which the emirate of the tutor is irrelevant once delivery is online.

Third, do the arithmetic on the school run and set the slot from the real arrival time plus thirty minutes. Fourth, test with a marked script rather than a conversation: a free trial lesson built around a recent paper resolves in an hour what weeks of discussion will not. And fifth, if you have children at schools in two emirates, compare both calendars once a term, because mock weeks and internal deadlines will collide and it is better to see it coming.

Two things are worth writing down while you do this: the board and code for each subject, and the arrival time for each child. Those two lines brief any tutor in this market accurately, and they are the facts most enquiries omit, which is why most enquiries get a generic reply.

And if the answer at the end of all that is that local general help plus disciplined past-paper work is enough, that is a good outcome. The point of comparing properly is to buy the right thing, not to buy more.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel into Al Nuaimiya for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Local Ajman tutors will, and tutors from Sharjah or Dubai will at a price that includes the journey - published UAE rate cards put in-home visits at roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once travel is absorbed. IB Gram does not: we run no home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that service exists only in India. For course-specific work the online format is also the better deal here, since a Dubai-based specialist costs no more to reach than somebody in the next district.

faqs.question: Who regulates our school if it is in Ajman rather than Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, along with Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods; Dubai has KHDA and Abu Dhabi has ADEK. If your children attend school in two emirates you deal with two sets of published information. None of these bodies regulates private tutoring, which is federal through the MoHRE permit.

faqs.question: Is tutoring cheaper in Ajman than in Sharjah or Dubai?
faqs.answer: Local general tutoring usually is, which makes it good value for the jobs general tutoring does well - supervision, routine, working through practice questions. What Ajman has least of is course-specific depth: the pool of people who have taught a particular syllabus code to grade standard for years is small. Published market bands put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300 an hour with no travel component, so the sensible combination is often cheap local help for discipline plus a few specialist online hours for direction.

faqs.question: Our child goes to school in Sharjah. When can a session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Take the real arrival time and add thirty minutes. A child at an Ajman school is often home by half past three, so four o'clock works. Crossing into Sharjah, arrival between four and half past is typical, which makes five realistic. For a Dubai school, five-thirty or later. The published school finish time is not a useful input: dismissal, loading, the bus route and afternoon traffic add up. One week of noting when your child walks in gives you the number.

faqs.question: How do we find out whether our school uses Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Look for the code. Cambridge uses four digits - 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500 - and Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a 4: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Both appear on the statement of entry and in the exam information the school circulates, and the exams officer can confirm board, code and tier in one reply. This matters especially in Ajman, where several schools run Indian or mixed curricula and enter some cohorts for British-board papers in particular subjects.

faqs.question: My child moved from a CBSE school into IGCSE entries. What actually needs to change?
faqs.answer: Examination behaviour more than content. The subject overlap is substantial, but IGCSE questions are phrased differently, the expectation that method is shown is stricter, and command terms are treated as precise instructions rather than general invitations to write. A capable student can lose marks for reasons unrelated to knowledge. Two to four board-specific sessions working through past papers, marked against the published scheme, usually close that gap faster than more content teaching.

faqs.question: Do Ajman students sit the same exam series as Sharjah and Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Exactly the same. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates - the February/March series is offered in India only - and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Entries are made by your school's centre, and the administrative zone that determines which timetable version applies belongs to that centre rather than to the emirate. For Pearson, the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January.

faqs.question: Is a November resit possible, and when would results arrive?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the sequence matters. First confirm the receiving sixth form or university accepts a January result - the November 2025 Pearson series results reached students on 22 January 2026. Then confirm the entry route with the school, or with a registered centre if your child has left, since private-candidate entry carries earlier deadlines. Then read the June script: a candidate two marks short needs a short targeted block, while one thirty marks short should reconsider whether the same subject is the right use of the autumn.

faqs.question: Does the tutor permit work differently in Ajman?
faqs.answer: No, it is federal. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it costs nothing, asking a prospective tutor is entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: We have children at schools in two emirates. How do we manage two calendars?
faqs.answer: Compare them side by side once a term. Two schools under different authorities will have different term dates, different reporting cycles and mock weeks that can fall a fortnight apart, and an internal deadline for one child will land in the other's revision week. Seeing that in advance lets you move a slot deliberately rather than cancelling under pressure - which, left to itself, always happens to the younger child. We sequence sessions by arrival time on a single evening.

faqs.question: Are group classes in Ajman worth it before the exams?
faqs.answer: For a shared content weakness, yes, and they are the cheapest paid teaching per student. For an individual problem, no: a group cannot keep one candidate's error log, review the script they wrote, or decide that this student should abandon one topic and drill another. That is why group revision courses often feel productive and move little - the candidate who needed three sessions on electrolysis spent six hours covering everything. Match the purchase to whether the weakness is shared or individual.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons apply in Ajman too?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools across the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations - that federal baseline sits behind every emirate's requirements. The practical effect is a full school day with homework from two curricula, so an evening tutoring session needs to be short and specific. We can support Arabic as an additional language where a student arrived mid-school and sits below their year group.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with assessed coursework in IGCSE subjects that have it?
faqs.answer: With the teaching and the feedback, yes; with the writing, never. A tutor may explain what the task requires, question a plan, teach the skill involved and explain why a paragraph does not answer the question asked. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework. Services selling finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: What if the right specialist is booked when we need them?
faqs.answer: We offer a different hour with the right person, or a named date when one frees up. Demand concentrates in the eight to ten weeks before a series and narrow courses - Additional Mathematics, computer science, a specific board's business paper - sometimes have nobody free. What we will not do is substitute a generalist into a deadline block and leave a family to discover the mismatch over six weeks, because that costs exactly the weeks you were trying to buy.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nuaimiya.closingBody: Ajman, Sharjah and Dubai differ in regulators, supply and price. They do not differ in the paper your child sits, the scheme it is marked against, or the permit a tutor needs. So start with the facts that travel: the board, syllabus code and tier, your child's real arrival time, and a recent marked script. Send those and we will mark the script against the published scheme, match a tutor who has taught that exact course, and run a free trial lesson over live video at no cost - with no journey priced into anything.
