ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-a.tutorsIntro: Each tutor profile below names a board and a syllabus rather than a subject label. That is deliberate: a teacher fluent in Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and a teacher fluent in Pearson 4CH1 are teaching overlapping content through different papers, and the difference shows up in the final month.

intro.heading: The question is not 'can you teach maths', it is 'which syllabus'
paragraphs: A parent in Al Rashidiya who wants IGCSE help usually starts by asking around the building, then on a community group, then on Google. The replies arrive quickly and they are nearly all the same shape: an experienced teacher, flexible hours, all subjects, reasonable rates. What almost none of them contain is a four-digit number. Yet that number is the thing that decides whether the hour helps.

Your child's school has entered them for a particular syllabus with a particular board. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580, with an International variant numbered 0607 at some schools; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1. Cambridge Chemistry is 0620, Physics 0625, Biology 0610, Coordinated Sciences 0654, English as a First Language 0500 or 0990 depending on the version. Those codes sit on the statement of entry and often on the exam timetable the school sends home. They determine the number of papers, the length of each, whether there is a practical paper or an alternative to practical, and whether the subject is tiered.

A tutor who has taught the other board's version of the same subject is not useless, but they are working from the wrong map. They will prepare a student for a structured written paper that does not exist on that entry, or miss that the Pearson paper is sat in two parts of equal weight where Cambridge splits a short-answer paper from an extended one. In the last six weeks before a series, when preparation becomes paper-shaped rather than topic-shaped, that mismatch costs grades.

This page answers the proximity question honestly. The pool of people within a short drive of Al Rashidiya who have recently taught a named syllabus in a named subject is small, and for the less common subjects it is empty. IB Gram does not run in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, because the service is delivered live online, one tutor and one student over video. That removes the radius from the search, and the radius is the only reason the syllabus question was hard to answer in the first place.

What follows is the information a parent needs in order to interview anybody, including us. Where to find the syllabus code. How Cambridge and Pearson differ on the same subject. What Core and Extended actually mean for a grade ceiling. What the Northern Emirates market charges, in dirhams, with the figures attributed. How the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules treat an IGCSE certificate. And how science practical work is handled when the lessons are on a screen.

None of it requires a parent to become an examinations officer. It requires one piece of information, held by the school, that almost nobody asks for before paying a tutor. A family in Al Rashidiya who sends that code in a message has already done more to protect the grade than a family who spent a fortnight comparing hourly rates, because the rate only matters once the person on the other end is teaching the right examination.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-a.programmesIntro: An IGCSE entry sits inside a longer route, and the route matters for how tutoring is planned. Al Rashidiya students arrive at Year 10 from Cambridge Lower Secondary, from a British national-curriculum primary, or from a transfer out of CBSE or an American programme, and each start leaves a different hole.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Three years of staged curriculum frameworks in English, mathematics, science and increasingly computing, with optional Checkpoint tests at the end. Checkpoint results are diagnostic rather than certificated, and they are the earliest reliable signal of whether a student is on track for the Extended tier at IGCSE. Schools use them to set tiers, which means a weak Year 9 can quietly decide a grade ceiling two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October windows, so an Ajman school may run them at a different point from a neighbour in Sharjah. Families in Al Rashidiya who want a tier decision reconsidered should ask for the Checkpoint breakdown by strand rather than the overall score, because the strand data shows whether the gap is algebra, number or problem-solving.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, examined externally with syllabus codes in the 0400 to 0700 range. Most subjects offer Core and Extended routes with different papers and different grade ceilings. Assessment is almost entirely terminal, with coursework retained in a minority of subjects, so paper technique carries as much weight as content knowledge by the final term.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman private schools sit under federal Ministry of Education supervision, and a large share of Al Rashidiya students cross into Sharjah schools regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Either way the board is Cambridge or Pearson rather than the regulator, and the entry decision, including tier, is made by the school. Ask for it in writing at the start of Year 10.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other major international route, with codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics Specification A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry and 4BI1 for Biology. Papers are structured differently from Cambridge: Mathematics Specification A is two papers of equal weight, and the sciences use a single-paper or two-paper model depending on specification, with practical skills assessed in the written papers rather than in a separate practical examination.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the June 2026 series reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the lag a resit candidate in Ajman should plan around.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The two-year route most IGCSE students in the Northern Emirates follow next, in three or four subjects, with AS assessed separately or as part of a staged A Level. Subject content steps up sharply from IGCSE, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, and the first term of Year 12 is where students who coasted through Extended discover the gap.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement includes one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE or GCSE subjects. Verify the current rule with the Ministry before relying on it for a university application.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-a.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Al Rashidiya families ask about most, with the Cambridge code in each case and the Pearson equivalent where there is one. The description says what the papers demand rather than restating the subject title.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Pearson Foundation and Higher Tier
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics. Extended adds functions, vectors, more demanding trigonometry and harder algebraic manipulation. Marks go missing in multi-step problems where the method is right and a sign or a unit is wrong, which is a correctable habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger cohorts as a bridge to A Level. Calculus, logarithms, series, matrices and kinematics appear here first. Students who manage 0580 by pattern recognition struggle immediately, because 0606 rewards algebraic fluency and offers far fewer structured scaffolds.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Motion, forces, energy, waves, electricity, magnetism and atomic physics. Electricity is the reported sticking point in nearly every cohort, usually because circuit reasoning was learned as formula selection. The practical component differs by board, and the alternative-to-practical paper has its own technique.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Particles, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, periodicity, organic and analysis. Mole calculations and ionic equations account for a disproportionate share of lost marks. Extended adds electrolysis depth and organic reaction detail that Core candidates never meet.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Characteristics of organisms, cells, transport, respiration, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. The content volume invites memorisation and the papers reward command-term discipline. Experiment-design questions and graph interpretation are the two areas most students have never practised separately.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics taught as one award, with reduced depth per discipline. Students moving from Coordinated Science into A Level sciences need the gap closed deliberately, because the omitted content is assumed rather than retaught in Year 12.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing, plus composition. The reading paper is a comprehension and summary exercise with a strict economy of expression, and summary marks are lost by students who paraphrase rather than select. Composition is marked on structure and control as much as on content.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475 / 0992)
subjects.description: Poetry, prose and drama, assessed through passage-based and essay questions. The decisive skill is quotation selection under time pressure. Students who learn whole essays and reproduce them score worse than those who learn fifteen quotations well and respond to the question asked.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Business activity, people, marketing, operations and finance, assessed through short answers and a case study. Evaluation marks require a judgement supported by the case, and most candidates describe the theory correctly then stop before the judgement, leaving the top band untouched.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, international trade. Diagram accuracy is worth real marks and axis labelling errors are the commonest avoidable loss, followed by answers that explain a concept without applying it.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Data representation, networks, hardware, software and algorithm design with pseudocode. The second paper rewards students who can trace an algorithm by hand, a skill that coding practice alone does not build. Pseudocode conventions must match the board's published style.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 First Language / 0544 Foreign Language)
subjects.description: Two very different qualifications often confused by parents. First Language assumes fluency and assesses literary and directed writing; Foreign Language assesses functional reading, writing and communication. The right entry depends on the student's background, and a wrong entry is a very expensive mistake to discover in Year 11.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-a.regionsTitle: Where syllabus-specific IGCSE help is hard to find in Ajman
ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rashidiya-a.regionsIntro: The proximity problem is not evenly distributed. Some Ajman communities are close to schools with large British-curriculum cohorts, and some are not close to anything. The notes below describe the local supply of subject-specific IGCSE teaching rather than the commute.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Central and well connected, with a mixed curriculum population and no large single-school cohort nearby. Core subject help is findable locally; Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and Arabic First Language are not.

regions.name: Al Nuaimiya
regions.note: The densest residential district in the emirate and the one with the most informal tutoring activity. Supply is genuine but almost entirely generalist, and very few advertisements name a board, let alone a syllabus code.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa communities nearest the newer schools to the west of the city. More teachers live here than in the older districts, which makes maths and science cover plausible and leaves the humanities thin.

regions.name: Al Rawda
regions.note: Family housing with a strong pull towards Sharjah schools, so the cohort is split across Cambridge and Pearson entries in the same street. A tutor serving three houses here may be working from three different specifications.

regions.name: Al Jurf
regions.note: Mixed residential and institutional, with longer distances between households. In-home tutoring economics work poorly here because a visiting tutor can fit fewer students into an evening, which pushes quoted rates up.

regions.name: Al Zorah
regions.note: Low-density waterfront housing on the northern lagoon. Almost no local tutoring supply, and the distances make a visiting specialist unrealistic for a single weekly hour.

regions.name: Emirates City
regions.note: Tower blocks with a transient, multi-curriculum population. Cohorts change year to year, so word-of-mouth recommendations age quickly and a tutor recommended two years ago may now be teaching a different board.

regions.name: Ajman Corniche
regions.note: Seafront apartments with a notable share of teaching households, which makes it one of the better local markets for English and humanities support and no better than anywhere else for the sciences.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools in Ajman
schoolClusters.note: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and the British-curriculum cohort in the emirate is concentrated in a handful of schools. Students we support from Al Rashidiya are entered through these schools for Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE.

schoolClusters.note: Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which the UAE government notes also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. modes.title: Syllabus-led weekly teaching
modes.description: One subject, one syllabus, one evening a week through the school year. The tutor works from the board's published syllabus content list and tracks coverage against it, so a parent can see at any point which topics have been taught, which have been examined in practice and which are outstanding. Most Al Rashidiya families run this in two subjects.

modes.description: A short diagnostic block for families unsure whether Core or Extended, or Foundation or Higher Tier, is the right entry. The tutor works through tier-appropriate past-paper material at both levels and reports what the evidence shows. The decision stays with the school, but the parent goes into that conversation with marked work rather than an impression.

sections.heading: Does anyone near Al Rashidiya actually teach your child's syllabus?
paragraphs: Answer first: for Mathematics 0580 and the three separate sciences, probably yes, if you are willing to accept whoever is free. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, Arabic First Language 0508, Economics 0455 or English Literature at a high band, almost certainly not within a short drive of Al Rashidiya, and asking the question that way is what reveals it.

The reason is arithmetic rather than anything about Ajman. A neighbourhood tutoring market needs enough students in one subject at one level on one board to sustain a specialist. Al Rashidiya's IGCSE population is split across at least two boards, two tiers in most subjects, and schools on both sides of the Sharjah border. Divide a modest total by all of those and the per-syllabus demand within walking distance is a handful of students a year.

What happens next is predictable. A generalist takes the work, because the alternative is turning away a paying family. The teaching is often decent on content. The student arrives at the series having practised the wrong paper structure, or having never seen an alternative-to-practical paper because the tutor's experience was with a board that assesses practicals differently. The parent never finds out that this was the problem, because a grade does not come with a diagnosis.

IB Gram's answer is to delete the radius. Lessons are delivered live over video, one to one, so the search covers everybody teaching that syllabus in this time zone rather than everybody living near your building. We do not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and we say so before you ask. What you get instead is a tutor who can name your child's papers, their durations and their weightings before the first session.
bullets: Common subjects are locally findable; the specialist ones are not
Two boards times two tiers times two emirates fragments the local market
A generalist rarely tells you they are working from the wrong specification
Online delivery makes the syllabus the search key instead of the postcode

sections.heading: Find the code before you book anything
paragraphs: The syllabus code appears on your child's statement of entry, on the school's examination timetable, and usually on the subject information sheet handed out at the start of Year 10. If none of those are to hand, the subject teacher will confirm it in a sentence. It is a two-minute enquiry that changes who you should be hiring.

The table below sets out the pairs that matter most in Ajman. Note that the two boards are not simply different names for the same examination. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended runs two papers, a shorter structured paper and a longer one, while Pearson 4MA1 runs two papers of equal length and weight. In the sciences, Cambridge entries typically include either a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper, whereas Pearson International GCSE science specifications assess practical skills within the written papers.

The second thing the table shows is that tiering is board-specific. Cambridge uses Core and Extended with different papers and different grade ceilings. Pearson Mathematics Specification A uses Foundation and Higher Tier, also with different ceilings. A tutor who assumes the wrong model will pitch the work at the wrong level for an entire term, which is worse than pitching it slightly too hard.

Take the code to any tutor you are considering, including us, and ask three things: which papers does that entry sit, how long is each, and what is the weighting. A specialist answers without looking it up. Anybody who deflects to a general statement about experience with the British curriculum has told you what you needed to know.

sections.heading: Core and Extended decide the ceiling, not the difficulty
paragraphs: Parents often read Core as the easier version of the same examination. It is more accurate to treat Core and Extended as two qualifications sharing a name. They have different papers, different content lists in several subjects, and different grade ranges, and the entry is made by the school rather than by the family.

The practical consequence is that a tier decision taken in Year 10 constrains options in Year 12. A student entered for Core in a science cannot reach the upper grades in that subject, and a sixth-form place or an A Level entry requirement expressed as a grade may therefore be out of reach before Year 11 begins. That is not a reason to push every student towards Extended; it is a reason to make the decision on evidence and to revisit it while it is still reversible.

The evidence that matters is performance on tier-appropriate past-paper questions, not an impression from classwork. A student can look comfortable in lessons and still miss the algebraic fluency that Extended assumes, and a student can look disengaged and turn out to be well inside the Extended range once the questions are unfamiliar enough to require thought. Marked past-paper work separates those cases in two sessions.

Where a family in Al Rashidiya wants that evidence, the tier review block above produces it: sampled questions at both tiers, marked against the published scheme, with a written summary for the subject teacher. The school still makes the entry. The parent simply stops arguing from feelings.

sections.heading: Five questions that identify a syllabus-fluent tutor
paragraphs: Credential lists are easy to assemble and hard to verify, and years of experience correlate loosely with knowing a current specification. The following five questions take four minutes on a phone call and separate a specialist from a generalist without requiring the parent to know any of the answers in advance.

First: which papers does my child sit for this entry, and how long is each one? Second: what is the weighting between them? Third: what is the single topic in this syllabus where candidates most reliably lose marks, and how do you teach it? Fourth: which past series would you start from, and why that one? Fifth: what will you not do, if I ask you to help with coursework or a controlled assessment?

The answers are revealing in their texture rather than their content. A teacher who has recently taught 0620 will say that mole calculations and ionic equations eat marks, will have a view about which series to start from, and will describe a method rather than an attitude. A generalist produces warm, general sentences about building confidence. Neither is dishonest; one of them is going to help your child in the final term and the other is not.

The fifth question matters more than it looks. The correct answer involves a refusal. A tutor who offers to produce coursework, write up an investigation or supply material to submit has offered something that puts the student's certification at risk. Hearing a clear no is a reason to continue the conversation, not to end it.
bullets: Ask which papers, how long, and what weighting
Ask where marks are lost in that specific syllabus
Ask which past series they would start from
Ask what they will refuse to do with assessed work

sections.heading: What IGCSE support costs in the Northern Emirates
paragraphs: Prices in this segment are badly published. Of the stronger pages ranking for these searches, three carry no figure at all, and the two that quote numbers quote US dollars. The bands below are market rates in dirhams, taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table, and attributed so that you can check them. They are not our price list.

Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the commitment. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run from AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 for a mid-tier tutor, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four in-home visits of two hours.

IGCSE rates sit below IB rates almost everywhere, and one provider makes the gap explicit: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. That differential is real and it is about scarcity of teaching experience rather than difficulty. It also means an Ajman family running two IGCSE subjects is looking at a smaller monthly number than a Diploma family, which changes what is affordable in the final term.

The in-home premium is the part worth examining before paying it. Market quotes for in-home one-to-one visits run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The difference is a journey across Ajman in evening traffic. For a family in Al Rashidiya buying syllabus-specific teaching, that is money spent on transport rather than on the thing that moves the grade.

sections.heading: Five accredited subjects: what the Ministry of Education asks of an IGCSE certificate
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step families discover late, usually when a UAE university asks for it. For the British track, the published requirement is that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches people is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. That is a meaningful planning point for a student in Ajman carrying both as school requirements, because it means the five have to come from elsewhere in the timetable. One competitor page ranking in this segment tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is not what the published rule says.

On the American track the same clarification sets out English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No International Baccalaureate points threshold is stated in that source, so any figure quoted for IB equivalency should be checked directly with the Ministry rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation. The process belongs to the Ministry and the relevant attestation authority, and tutoring is not a requirement of it. What a tutor can do is make sure the five subjects a student is relying on are the ones they are strongest in, which is a timetable conversation best had in Year 10 rather than Year 13.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the lessons happen on a screen
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online science tutoring is the practical work, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Practical skills are taught in the school laboratory, and no tutor, visiting or online, substitutes for that. What a tutor works on is the assessment of those skills, which is a written exercise in both boards and a distinct discipline from doing the experiment.

For Cambridge entries that include the alternative-to-practical paper, the work is specific and highly teachable: reading a scale correctly, tabulating with consistent significant figures, plotting with sensible axes, identifying the dependent and independent variables, naming a control, spotting the anomalous point, and writing an improvement that is actually an improvement rather than a repetition of the method. These questions are predictable in form and most students have never drilled them.

For Pearson International GCSE science specifications, practical skills are assessed within the written papers, which changes the shape of preparation rather than removing it. The same competencies appear embedded in longer questions, and a student who has practised them in isolation recognises them when they arrive in a different wrapper. This is one of the places where a tutor working from the wrong board's materials leaves a visible hole.

The screen helps more than it hinders here. A shared document with the student's own tabulated data, annotated live by the tutor, is a better teaching surface than two people leaning over a notebook. Graphs can be marked up, misread scales can be zoomed, and the finished annotated page is saved for revision. None of that is available across a dining table.
bullets: Laboratory skills come from school; assessment technique comes from practice
Alternative-to-practical questions are predictable in form and rarely drilled
Pearson embeds the same skills inside the written papers
Annotated shared documents beat paper for data and graph work

process.title: Send the syllabus code
process.description: The code from the statement of entry, the school timetable or the subject teacher. With it we can name the papers, durations and weightings and match a tutor who has taught that specification. Without it, any match is a guess dressed as a service, which is the ordinary state of this market.

process.title: Say which tier the school has entered
process.description: Core or Extended for Cambridge, Foundation or Higher Tier for Pearson Mathematics. If you are not sure, or you think the decision is wrong, say that too: the tier review block exists for exactly that situation and produces marked evidence rather than an opinion.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a real topic
process.description: One lesson, no charge, no payment details collected first, spent on something your child is currently stuck on in that syllabus. You get a short written note afterwards naming what was done and what the tutor thinks the priority is. That note is the thing to judge, not the warmth of the hour.

process.title: Set the coverage plan against the syllabus
process.description: We map the remaining syllabus content against the weeks left before the series and agree what is taught, what is practised and what is accepted as a gap. For a Year 11 student in the second term, that document is more useful than any amount of general revision promise.

process.title: Switch to paper-shaped work eight weeks out
process.description: From roughly two months before the series, sessions move to timed papers from the correct board and series, marked against the published scheme. The syllabus code you sent at step one is what makes this step possible, which is why it is step one.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the specification, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed because they have taught 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher Tier, not because they teach maths. That is the single most useful filter available in this market and almost nobody applies it, because applying it means sometimes saying no.

whyPoints.title: Both boards treated as different qualifications
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson papers differ in count, weighting and the handling of practical assessment. We keep them separate in matching and in past-paper work, so a student never practises a paper structure they will not sit.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can audit
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, including the ones that make online tuition look expensive. Three of the strongest pages in this search segment publish no price at all, which is its own kind of answer.

whyPoints.title: A clear refusal on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coursework, controlled assessments and investigations are taught, questioned and reviewed, never written or completed for the student. The refusal is the product. A service willing to cross that line is selling a certification risk alongside the lesson.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If no tutor for your syllabus is free in the evening slot you need, you hear that with a realistic date. Being told no in week one is cheaper than discovering in week six that the person teaching your child is working from the wrong specification.

whyPoints.title: No UAE premises, no claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: IB Gram has no office or centre in the UAE and holds no regulator or board accreditation. The permit relevant to private tutoring here is a labour authorisation issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it certifies the right to work, not teaching quality.

faqs.question: Where do I find my child's IGCSE syllabus code?
faqs.answer: On the statement of entry the school issues before the series, on the examination timetable sent home, and usually on the subject information sheet given out at the start of Year 10. If none of those is to hand, the subject teacher will confirm it in a sentence. Codes look like 0580 for Cambridge Mathematics or 4MA1 for Pearson Edexcel Mathematics Specification A. It takes two minutes to establish and it determines which tutor is actually able to help, so it is worth the message.

faqs.question: Is a Cambridge tutor able to teach a Pearson Edexcel entry?
faqs.answer: Often, but not without preparation, and you should ask rather than assume. The content overlaps substantially; the papers do not. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 Extended runs a shorter structured paper and a longer one, while Pearson 4MA1 runs two papers of equal weight. In the sciences the handling of practical assessment differs. A tutor who has taught both will say so plainly and will name the differences. One who waves the question away is likely to prepare your child for the wrong paper shape in the final term.

faqs.question: Can we change my child from Core to Extended in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the school and how late in the cycle the request comes. Entries are made by the school, and there are deadlines after which a change is not practical. The useful move is to produce evidence early: marked past-paper work at both tiers, under time, against the published scheme. That turns a disagreement into a conversation with the subject teacher. If the evidence supports the school's existing decision, you have learned something worth knowing before Year 11 rather than after it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a local tutor for in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, Arabic as a First Language 0508, Economics 0455 and English Literature at the upper bands. These have small per-syllabus demand in any single neighbourhood, and Al Rashidiya's cohort is already split across two boards and schools in two emirates. Mathematics and the separate sciences are findable locally if you are willing to accept whoever is available. For the rest, removing the travel requirement is what makes a specialist reachable at all.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes in Al Rashidiya for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. In-home tutoring is a service IB Gram offers only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for Ajman families run live over video, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own papers and a shared annotation surface on screen. We target the home-tutor search term because it is what parents type, and then answer it honestly: the teaching you want is delivered without a journey. Families who need an adult physically present should hire locally instead.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child have tutoring in?
faqs.answer: One or two at a time, in the subjects where the gap is specific rather than general. A student receiving help in five subjects has no time left to do the work that makes the help stick, and the cost becomes a four-figure monthly commitment. If the difficulty genuinely spans most subjects, the problem is usually study method, reading speed or attendance rather than content, and a single well-chosen subject plus a study-skills focus does more than five parallel courses.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE candidates in Ajman actually sit their exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one. Always work from the timetable your school's examinations officer issues.

faqs.question: How long after the November series do results arrive?
faqs.answer: For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November series results reach students in January: the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. June series results arrive much sooner, with June 2026 results going to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. That gap matters if a resit is being used to repair a grade for a university application, because a January result may arrive after some application deadlines have passed.

faqs.question: Which subjects can an Ajman student count towards the five the Ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification of the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. For a student in Ajman carrying both as school requirements, the five accredited subjects must therefore come from elsewhere in the timetable. One ranking competitor page tells UAE parents that six subjects are needed; the published rule says five at no less than E or grade 3. Verify with the Ministry before relying on it.

faqs.question: How is practical science handled if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Laboratory work stays at school, where it belongs. What a tutor teaches is the written assessment of practical skills, which is a separate discipline: reading scales, tabulating to consistent significant figures, plotting sensible axes, identifying variables and controls, finding the anomaly and proposing a real improvement. Cambridge entries may include an alternative-to-practical paper where these questions appear directly; Pearson specifications embed the same competencies inside the written papers. Annotating the student's own data table on a shared screen is a better teaching surface than paper.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a controlled assessment or coursework task?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain the mark criteria, question a draft and point out where the evidence does not support the claim. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it to a finished state, or supply material for submission. That boundary is not negotiable and it is in the student's interest: work that is not the student's own puts the certification itself at risk. Any service that offers to produce assessed work is selling you a problem alongside the lesson.

faqs.question: What is a realistic monthly cost for two IGCSE subjects in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Working from published market figures rather than our own pricing: a mid-tier tutor at one weekly hour per subject is estimated at AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month per subject by Bestimate's rate table, and advertised package pricing in this market includes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Two subjects at one hour a week is therefore a four-figure monthly commitment in most configurations. In-home delivery at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour raises that materially, and most of the increase is travel.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with one term left. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a changed plan. A single remaining term is not enough to reteach a two-year syllabus, so the work becomes triage: identify the highest-value gaps using marked past-paper evidence, drill the paper types that carry the most marks, and accept named gaps rather than pretending to cover everything. That is a different service from syllabus-led teaching and should be bought as one. A tutor who promises full coverage in a term is either not reading the calendar or not telling you the truth.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Cambridge International variant of Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics, syllabus 0607, is a separate course from 0580 with a different emphasis on investigation and technology use, and some schools in the region enter students for it specifically as preparation for the International Baccalaureate. It needs a tutor who has taught that variant, not a 0580 teacher adapting. Tell us the code on the entry and we will say whether we can cover it for your slot this term, or tell you plainly that we cannot.

faqs.question: Which regulator oversees IGCSE schools in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The qualification itself is not regulated by any emirate authority; it is awarded by Cambridge International or Pearson. If your child attends school across the border, private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are listed by board and syllabus rather than by location, which is the point of this page: the useful filter at IGCSE is the specification, and the specification does not change between one Ajman villa community and the next.

intro.heading: Two neighbourhoods, one answer
paragraphs: Al Rawda is three villa sub-communities set west of the older part of Ajman, numbered one, two and three, with Sheikh Ammar Bin Humaid Street carrying the morning traffic towards Sharjah. Al Mowaihat is the next cluster over, closer to the schools on the western side of the city. Al Nuaimiya is denser and nearer the centre. A parent on any of these streets types essentially the same thing into Google, and the results are essentially identical, which raises a fair question: does the street matter at all?

For some things it genuinely does. The commute differs by fifteen or twenty minutes, which changes the earliest workable session time. Local in-home quotes differ a little, because a visiting tutor can fit more students into an evening in some communities than others. The proportion of teaching households differs, which affects how much informal help circulates. Those are real differences and this page sets them out honestly rather than pretending the emirate is uniform.

For the things that decide an IGCSE grade, the street changes nothing. The syllabus code on your child's entry is the same whichever villa they live in. Core or Extended is set by the school, not the postcode. The June and November series, the six Cambridge administrative zones, the entry deadline months ahead of the paper: all identical. And the supply of people within a short drive who have recently taught Additional Mathematics 0606 or Arabic as a First Language is thin in all three communities, because the per-syllabus demand in any single Ajman neighbourhood is a handful of students a year.

That is why the honest answer converges. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service for us. Lessons for Al Rawda families run live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. Once travel is removed from the arrangement, the comparison between neighbourhoods collapses into one remaining variable, which is the hour of the evening that works in your particular household.

The rest of this page does the comparison properly: the three communities side by side, what proximity buys and does not buy at IGCSE level, why two neighbours can be sitting different boards, how rates vary across the emirate and how they do not, the regulator picture that is identical across all of Ajman, and the one thing that genuinely varies street by street and nobody mentions, which is whether the student has somewhere quiet to work between lessons.

A parent reading this from Al Mowaihat or Al Nuaimiya will find the comparison runs the other way round and arrives at the same place. That is the test of whether an argument is real: it should hold when you stand on the other street and look back. The one thing worth optimising is the hour, and the one thing worth checking is the code on the entry.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.programmesIntro: The route through to IGCSE and beyond is the same in every part of the emirate, and the decision points are the same too. These notes name where each stage can be influenced and where it cannot.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Staged frameworks in English, mathematics and science with optional Checkpoint tests at the end, available in March, May and October windows. Results are diagnostic rather than certificated, and schools use them to set IGCSE tiers, which makes Year 9 the stage where a grade ceiling is quietly established without anything appearing to have happened.
programmes.countryNote: Al Rawda and Al Mowaihat children often sit Checkpoint at different schools in different windows, so neighbouring families compare results that are not comparable. The useful thing to request is the breakdown by strand rather than the overall mark, since the strand data shows whether the gap is number, algebra or problem-solving.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, eight to ten subjects, externally examined with codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology and 0500 English as a First Language. Most subjects split into Core and Extended with different papers and grade ceilings. The entry, including tier, is made by the school.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June and a November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Specifications including 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology, with paper structures that differ from Cambridge. Mathematics A runs two papers of equal weight, and practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson examinations run in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects over two years with a sharp step up from Extended IGCSE in mathematics and the sciences. Entry requirements are expressed in IGCSE grades, which is the mechanism by which a Year 10 tier decision reaches forward and closes a door two years later.
programmes.countryNote: The published Ministry of Education requirement on the British track includes five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Verify current requirements with the Ministry.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.subjectsIntro: The list below notes, for each subject, whether local supply in an Ajman villa community is realistic or not. That is the comparison this page is making, applied subject by subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher Tier
subjects.description: The one subject where local supply exists in every Ajman community, because demand is high enough to sustain it. The quality varies and the board question still applies: 0580 Extended and 4MA1 Higher Tier are different paper structures for overlapping content.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Locally findable in Al Mowaihat and Al Nuaimiya more readily than in Al Rawda, simply because more teaching households sit nearer the western schools. Whether that local tutor has taught the specific entry, including alternative-to-practical technique, is a separate question.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Available locally in principle, though organic chemistry and electrolysis depth at Extended level narrow the field considerably. Mole calculations recur through the whole course, so a tutor who treats them as a topic rather than a foundation leaves the gap in place.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The science with the widest local supply and the one where content volume makes the timing of revision critical. Experiment-design and graph-interpretation questions need separate practice and are rarely what a local generalist works on.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Local supply is reasonable across all three communities, with Ajman Corniche and Al Jurf households contributing a number of English teachers. Summary economy and composition control are the skills that move marks, and both respond to short targeted blocks.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Effectively unavailable locally in any Ajman community. Content is new rather than extended, so a student cannot be carried by a 0580 tutor adapting, and the number of candidates per neighbourhood is far too small to sustain a specialist within driving distance.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Another subject where the street makes no difference because the answer is the same everywhere: almost nobody locally. Algorithm tracing by hand and the board's pseudocode conventions are the specific skills, and coding experience alone does not supply them.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Thin supply across the emirate. Diagram accuracy and applied evaluation are what the papers reward, and a tutor from a general business background will teach the concepts and miss the diagram discipline where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Somewhat more available locally than economics. The case-study paper rewards judgements supported by the stimulus, and most candidates describe a tool correctly and never make the judgement, which is a technique problem with a short fix.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 First Language / 0544 Foreign Language)
subjects.description: Local supply of Arabic teaching is good across Ajman; local supply of teaching aimed specifically at these two syllabuses is not. The two are genuinely different qualifications and the wrong entry is an expensive discovery in Year 11.

sections.heading: Al Rawda or Al Mowaihat: does the street change the answer?
paragraphs: Take the question literally and test it. Two Year 10 students, both entered for Cambridge 0580 Extended and 0620 Chemistry, one living in Al Rawda 2 and one in Al Mowaihat. Same board, same tier, same papers, same series. What differs between them?

Three things, measurably. The Al Mowaihat student is likely home from school fifteen to thirty minutes earlier, because the western schools are closer, which means a 5pm session is realistic there and a 6pm start is more honest in Al Rawda. Local in-home quotes are slightly lower in Al Mowaihat, because a visiting tutor can serve more households per evening in a tighter cluster. And more teaching households sit near the western schools, so informal recommendations circulate more readily there.

Nothing else differs. Not the syllabus, not the tier, not the entry deadline, not the paper structure, not the Cambridge zone their centre belongs to, not the November series behind the June one, not the content either student has to know. The things that determine the grade are identical, and the things that differ are logistics.

That is the whole argument of this page, and it has a practical consequence. If the only real variables are the hour of the evening and the travel economics of a visiting tutor, then removing travel from the arrangement removes the difference between the two addresses entirely. What is left is a slot time, which the family sets, and a specification match, which is the same requirement in both communities.

Read the bottom half of the table rather than the top. The first rows are the genuine differences and they are all logistical: arrival time, local quotes, supply of informal help. The later rows are the ones that decide outcomes, and they are constant across the emirate. A parent who spends effort optimising the first group while ignoring the second has optimised the wrong variables, which is what a neighbourhood-based search encourages.

One row deserves a note. Local supply of informal help is highest in Al Nuaimiya and it is also the least specific, because volume in an informal market comes from generalists rather than specialists. That is not a criticism of the people doing the work; it is a structural fact about how a dense residential market with many curricula and two boards allocates teaching. A parent in Al Nuaimiya has the most options and the hardest filtering job.

Two caveats keep the table honest. The arrival times are what families in these communities report rather than published figures, and a single closure on the Sharjah approach can add twenty minutes to any of them on a given day. And the in-home quote levels describe a small local market where a single tutor changing their schedule moves the average, so treat them as a direction rather than a measurement. sections.heading: What proximity buys at IGCSE, and what it does not
paragraphs: Proximity has genuine value in a small number of cases, and it is worth naming them rather than dismissing the whole idea. A younger student who will not stay at a desk without an adult physically present benefits from a visiting tutor. A student with specific additional needs may need in-person support. A household with unreliable connectivity has a practical constraint. In those cases a local in-home tutor is the right purchase, and IB Gram is not, because we do not offer home visits in the UAE at all.

What proximity does not buy is specification fluency, and that is what decides an IGCSE grade. The chance that the nearest available tutor has recently taught your child's exact syllabus, at the right tier, and knows the paper structure and the practical assessment model, is a function of how many such teachers live within a twenty-minute drive. In an Ajman villa community that number is small for the common subjects and zero for several others.

Proximity also does not buy continuity, which matters more over a two-year qualification than most families expect. A local arrangement ends when the tutor moves, changes job or takes on a fuller schedule, and in a dense informal market that happens often. A student who has three different tutors across Year 10 and Year 11 has effectively had none, because each one spends their first sessions discovering what the last one did.

And proximity costs money. Published in-home bands run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and the increment is a journey across the emirate in evening traffic. Paying that to reach a specialist who could not otherwise be reached would be rational. Paying it to reach a generalist, which is the usual outcome in these communities, is paying more for a smaller choice.

sections.heading: Why two houses on the same street sit different boards
paragraphs: One of the quieter oddities of this part of Ajman is that two neighbouring families with children in the same year can be preparing for different examinations. The reason is the Sharjah border: Al Rawda sends children both to schools within the emirate and to schools a short drive into Sharjah, and the board a school uses is a school decision rather than a regional one.

This has a practical effect on the most common way families find tutors, which is asking a neighbour. A recommendation that worked brilliantly for the house opposite may be a recommendation for a Pearson specialist when your child sits Cambridge, or for an Extended tutor when your child is entered for Core. The recommendation was honest and it may be the wrong match, and nothing in the conversation surfaces that unless somebody asks for a code.

It also explains why the per-syllabus market in any one community is thinner than the apparent number of IGCSE students suggests. Divide a modest cohort by two boards, then by two tiers in most subjects, then by ten subjects, and the demand for any specific combination within walking distance is a handful of students across a whole year. No specialist can build a practice on that, which is why the specialists are not there.

The response is simple and it is the same on every street. Get the syllabus code from the statement of entry, the examination timetable or the subject teacher, confirm the tier, and use those as the search key instead of the neighbourhood. That is a two-minute enquiry and it is the single most useful thing a parent in any of these communities can do before paying anybody.

sections.heading: Rates across the emirate: what varies and what does not
paragraphs: In-home rates do vary across Ajman, for ordinary reasons of travel economics, and they vary within a narrow band. Online rates do not vary at all, because the cost of delivering a video lesson does not change with the distance between two addresses. The table below sets out the published market bands with their sources, which is something three of the strongest pages ranking for these searches do not do at any price.

The bands are market figures rather than ours, collected from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table. Ajman in-home quotes generally sit at or slightly below the Dubai figures, since local visiting tutors here charge less than those serving central Dubai. The monthly view is more useful than the hourly one: published estimates for a single weekly hour run from AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The comparison that matters for this page is the last row. A specialist teaching a named syllabus online costs the same from Al Rawda as from Al Mowaihat, Al Nuaimiya or anywhere else in the Gulf time zone. That is the one row where a neighbourhood-based search actively costs a family money, because the alternative to it is paying a travel premium for a smaller pool of teachers.

One honest note on the budget band. Rates from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour buy homework supervision rather than syllabus teaching, and there is a legitimate use for that with a younger student. Bought as Year 11 examination preparation it produces company rather than progress, and because the monthly number is small it tends to survive unexamined for far longer than it should.

sections.heading: The regulator picture, identical across the emirate
paragraphs: Parents sometimes assume that a different part of the emirate means a different oversight arrangement, particularly where children cross into Sharjah for school. The emirate-level picture is actually simple, and it is the same in Al Rawda, Al Mowaihat and everywhere else in Ajman.

Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not just inspection sits with the emirate regulator there.

What varies for an Al Rawda family is therefore not where they live but where their child goes to school. A child at an Ajman school is in a federally supervised system; a sibling at a Sharjah school is in an emirate-regulated one, with a different route for a fee query or a complaint. That is worth knowing and it is not a tutoring variable.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and identically across the country. An individual giving private lessons needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

sections.heading: The thing that genuinely varies street by street
paragraphs: There is one variable that does differ house by house and that nobody discusses, because it is not a service anybody sells. It is whether the student has somewhere quiet to work for two hours between lessons, and it predicts progress better than almost anything a tutor controls.

In the villa communities of Al Rawda and Al Mowaihat this is usually straightforward: a room with a door and a desk. In the apartment density of Al Nuaimiya or the towers of Emirates City it can be genuinely hard, with shared rooms, younger siblings and a television in the only available space. A student in that position is not lazy when the independent work does not get done; they are working in a room that makes it impossible.

This matters for tutoring because an hour a week with no work behind it moves very little, whatever the subject and whoever teaches it. A student with four hours of independent practice between sessions progresses several times faster than one with none, and the gap between those two students is larger than the gap between a good tutor and an average one. Where the space does not exist, the honest fix is to find somewhere it does, which may be a library, a quieter hour of the day, or a reallocation of the household's rooms for two years.

It also changes what a session should be used for. Where independent work genuinely cannot happen, the session has to carry the practice itself: timed questions attempted inside the lesson rather than set for later. That is a less efficient use of a paid hour and it is better than setting work that will not be done, which is the default and the reason many arrangements quietly fail.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not the neighbourhood
process.description: The code from the statement of entry, the examination timetable or the subject teacher, plus the tier. That pair is the search key that actually matters, and it is identical whether you are in Al Rawda, Al Mowaihat or anywhere else in the emirate.

process.title: Tell us the observed arrival time home
process.description: Not the school end time but the hour your child is genuinely through the door on an ordinary weekday. This is the one variable your community really does change, and it is what determines whether a 5pm, 6pm or 7pm slot will survive past the second week.

process.title: Say where you are in the two years
process.description: Year 10 with the tier still open, Year 11 before mocks, the weeks after them, or a resit decision after results. Each is a different purchase with a different realistic scope, and naming it prevents buying the wrong format for the month you are in.

process.title: Free trial on a real past-paper question
process.description: One lesson at no charge with no payment details collected, worked on material from the correct board and tier. The short written note afterwards names the priority, and the note is the evidence: it shows whether the tutor is reading the examination or the student's mood.

process.title: Fix the study space before the schedule
process.description: Agree where and when the independent work between sessions will happen. In a villa this is usually easy and in an apartment it is often the binding constraint. Where it cannot be solved, we build the practice into the session instead of setting work that will not get done.

whyPoints.title: The comparison made honestly
whyPoints.description: This page says what genuinely differs between Ajman communities, including the things that favour a local tutor, rather than pretending the emirate is uniform. The conclusion happens to favour online delivery; the reasoning is available for you to check.

whyPoints.title: Specification, not postcode
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched on the syllabus code and tier your child is entered for. That requirement is identical in every community, and it is the filter that a neighbourhood search structurally cannot apply.

whyPoints.title: The slot set by observed arrival time
whyPoints.description: The one real local variable is when your child is actually home, and it differs by fifteen or thirty minutes between these communities. We set the slot from what you observe over a normal week, not from the school's timetabled end of day.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium in any community
whyPoints.description: Published in-home bands run to AED 500 an hour and the increment over online delivery is a journey. From Al Rawda, where sub-community travel alone costs a visiting tutor twenty minutes, that premium buys nothing a student can use.

whyPoints.title: Continuity across two years
whyPoints.description: An IGCSE is a two-year qualification and three tutors across it is effectively none. A platform arrangement has a replacement bench matched on the same specification, which a local informal arrangement by its nature does not.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals or invented numbers
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation, has no UAE premises, and publishes no satisfaction or success statistic, because we could not produce the data behind one. The permit relevant to private tutoring here is free, and it authorises work rather than certifying quality.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IGCSE tutor in Al Mowaihat than in Al Rawda?
faqs.answer: Marginally, and only for the common subjects. More teaching households sit near the schools on the western side of the city, so informal recommendations circulate a little more readily there and local quotes sit slightly lower. For Mathematics, Biology and English that produces a small real advantage. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478, Economics or Arabic as a First Language, the local answer is the same in both communities, which is that there is effectively nobody.

faqs.question: Why do my neighbours' children sit a different exam board?
faqs.answer: Because the board is a school decision and Al Rawda sends children both to schools within Ajman and to schools a short drive into Sharjah. Two houses on the same street can therefore be preparing Cambridge and Pearson specifications in the same subject. It matters when you ask a neighbour for a tutor recommendation: the recommendation may be genuine and still be for the wrong specification, and nothing in that conversation surfaces it unless somebody asks for a syllabus code.

faqs.question: Does living further from school change what tutoring we need?
faqs.answer: It changes when, not what. A student arriving home at 4.30pm cannot seriously work at 5pm, so the slot moves later and the session has to fit a shorter usable evening. The content, the papers, the tier and the technique required are identical to those of a student living ten minutes from the same school. Where the commute is long, holiday weeks and Saturday mornings carry more of the load, because weekday evenings simply have fewer usable hours in them.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram come to Al Rawda villas for lessons?
faqs.answer: No. In-home tutoring is a service IB Gram offers only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for Al Rawda families run live over video, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers annotated on a shared screen. We target the home-tutor phrase because that is what parents type, and the honest answer is that the substance you want is delivered without a journey across three villa sub-communities.

faqs.question: Are tutoring rates lower in Ajman than in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In-home rates are, modestly, because local visiting tutors in the Northern Emirates charge less than those serving central Dubai. Published bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 with specialists quoted higher. Online rates do not differ at all, because the cost of delivering a video lesson does not change with distance, which means an Al Rawda family pays the same for a specialist as a family in Jumeirah and chooses from the same pool.

faqs.question: Who regulates schools in Ajman compared with Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which the UAE government describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. For an Al Rawda family with children at schools on both sides of the border, that means two different routes for a fee query or complaint.

faqs.question: Should we pick a tutor our neighbour recommends?
faqs.answer: Start there and then check two things: which board and syllabus they last taught, and which tier. A recommendation from a satisfied family is genuine evidence about reliability and manner, and no evidence at all about specification match, which is what decides the grade. Ask the recommended tutor which papers your child sits, how long each is and what the weighting is. A specialist answers immediately; a generalist talks about rapport, which is pleasant and not the thing you are buying.

faqs.question: How much does a long school commute actually cost in study time?
faqs.answer: For an Al Rawda student bussed into Sharjah, typically between sixty and ninety minutes a day, which over a school week is most of a full study day. The practical consequence is not that the student needs more tutoring but that their usable evening is shorter, so the plan has to be realistic about what fits. Families in this position get disproportionate value from holiday blocks and Saturday morning slots, where the time is not already spent.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Ajman a better option than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per head and the trade is pace. A group moves at one speed through a fixed syllabus plan, which suits a student whose gap matches the group's and wastes time for one whose gap does not. For broad content coverage early in Year 10 a centre can be good value. Eight weeks before a series, with a specific weakness identified from a mock script, one-to-one hours aimed at exactly that weakness do more per dirham spent.

faqs.question: What if we have no quiet place for our child to study?
faqs.answer: Then say so, because it changes what the session should do. An hour a week with no independent work behind it moves very little, and in a shared room with younger siblings and a television the independent work usually does not happen. The honest options are finding another space or another hour, or building the practice into the lesson itself with timed questions attempted during the session. That is a less efficient use of a paid hour and better than setting work nobody can do.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge timetable differ between Ajman and Sharjah centres?
faqs.answer: It can, because Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each. Two children at schools either side of the emirate border may therefore be working from different documents. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Take the timetable from your school's examinations officer.

faqs.question: How many tutors will my child have across Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: Ideally one per subject, and that is harder to achieve in an informal local market than families expect. Arrangements end when a tutor moves, changes job or takes a fuller schedule, and a student with three tutors across the two years has effectively had none, because each spends the first sessions discovering what the previous one covered. Continuity is worth paying for, and where a tutor does have to change, the replacement should be matched on the same specification.

faqs.question: Is the November series available to candidates at Ajman schools?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply here. The timing caveat on November is the results lag: Pearson's November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026, which may fall after some sixth-form or university deadlines, so check that before entering a resit.

faqs.question: What is the single best thing to do before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: Get three facts from the school in writing: the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier your child is entered for, and which timetable version applies to your centre. It takes one message to the examinations officer and it determines whether any tutor you hire is working from the right map. Almost no family has these written down in one place before February of Year 11, and they cost nothing to obtain in Year 10.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.closingHeading: The address is not the variable
ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rawda.closingBody: Send the subject, the syllabus code, the tier and the hour your child is genuinely home on a weekday in Al Rawda. We will tell you whether a tutor who has taught that specification is free in that window this term, what the honest earliest start time is given your bus route, and what the weeks remaining can realistically achieve. If a visiting tutor would suit your child better, because they are young or need an adult in the room, we will say that too, since home visits are not something we provide in the UAE at all.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.tutorsIntro: These are the IGCSE specialists most requested by families in Al Yasmeen and the villa districts around it. Rates move with subject and with how close the exam series sits, so a quote follows the free trial rather than preceding it.

intro.heading: The expensive decisions are made before anyone is hired
paragraphs: Al Yasmeen is a villa district inland from the Ajman coast, with wide plots, settled households and a school run that mostly stays inside the emirate. Two features of that make it a distinctive place to buy tuition. There is usually a spare room, so a student has somewhere quiet to work. And the afternoon is short rather than swallowed by a drive back from Sharjah, which means the cheaper early-evening slots are genuinely available to families here.

Before any of that matters, though, two decisions have already set most of the eventual bill, and neither involves a tutor. The first is the tier: Cambridge Core caps the available grade at C, and a family that accepts a Core entry for comfort in Year 10 and then wants an A Level route in that subject pays for a rushed conversion or an extra year. The second is the start date. The same grade movement bought in October costs roughly half what it costs in March, because the work has to be done either way and compression means more sessions at scarcer, dearer availability.

Only after those come the questions families usually ask first. Which tutor, at what hourly rate, for how many subjects. Those matter, but they are smaller levers. A household can save AED 30 an hour by negotiating and lose three times that by hiring in February for a subject where whole topics are missing.

What this page does is show the arithmetic. It costs a full Year 10 to Year 11 plan rather than an hour. It ranks subjects by how many marks a paid hour tends to recover, because that is the real return calculation. It publishes the AED bands providers in this market print, with the month they were read, since three of six pages examined in this market publish no price at all. And it says plainly when to stop, which almost nobody in this business writes down.

A point on delivery before the numbers, because it changes the arithmetic. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE and sends no tutor to any UAE address. Home visits are a service offered in India only. For a family in Al Yasmeen that removes the travel component from the price entirely: an in-home hour in this market is quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 and part of that pays for a car on the Ajman ring road rather than for teaching.

Read it with a recent marked paper next to you. The single most useful cost control available to a household is looking at where marks were actually lost before deciding how many hours to buy, and that costs nothing at all.
