ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.programmesIntro: Al Yasmeen families run several British-track routes across siblings. These are the stages where money is spent, with what each one implies for the total.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years where the tier decision is quietly made. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and give the school a benchmark rather than a certificate. Support here is the cheapest in the whole British track and the stage families most often skip.
programmes.countryNote: The economics are stark. A single weekly session in Year 9 that keeps a student eligible for the Extended tier costs a fraction of the catch-up block a Core-entered Year 11 student needs when the family realises the grade is capped at C. Earlier slots are easier to book in Al Yasmeen because the school run stays inside Ajman.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, graded 9-1 or A*-G, with Core and Extended tiers in most subjects. Core is capped at C. Extended is where almost all the paid tuition in this market goes, and the papers reward mark-scheme literacy as much as content knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Rates for IGCSE support sit below Diploma rates across this market: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour against IB from AED 200. Within IGCSE, the separate sciences and Extended maths price higher than Business or Economics, because the specialist pool is smaller and the content load is heavier.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board in use around Ajman and Sharjah, with codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics and 4EA1 for English Language A. Calculator rules and paper structures differ from Cambridge, so a tutor matched to the wrong board wastes hours on the wrong habits.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November route is a genuine budget option: a resit in one subject costs far less than a repeated year.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE grade becomes an entry requirement. Most schools set a threshold, often a 6 or 7 in maths and the sciences, for A Level entry in that subject, which is why a Year 10 tier decision reappears as a cost two years later.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education equivalency rule for this track names five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Protecting five solid passes is a cheaper plan than repairing four.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-yasmeen.subjectsIntro: The notes below are written for a budgeting decision: what each subject costs in hours and how recoverable its lost marks tend to be.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: High volume, so competitively priced, but slow to move when whole topics are missing. Extended requires fluency without a calculator, and rebuilding that takes weeks rather than sessions. Budget a term, not a fortnight.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: A calculator is permitted in both papers, which shifts the work towards method and structure. Marks lost to rounding when an exact answer is required are among the cheapest to recover in any subject.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Priced at the upper end of IGCSE support because the tutor pool is thinner. The alternative-to-practical paper is the best value target: apparatus reasoning, graph work and error sources respond quickly to focused hours.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations are a contained, teachable block that often moves a grade on its own. Organic chemistry takes longer. A tutor who starts with the calculations is spending your money in the right order.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Large content load but a wider tutor pool, so mid-band pricing. Most recoverable marks sit in data-response questions and in precision of wording, both of which respond to marking practice rather than reteaching.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: The best return per paid hour in this list. Evaluation and application marks are learnable in a short block, and a four to six session campaign targeted at case-study technique frequently moves a grade.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy earns marks before a word of analysis, which makes it another fast-return subject. The data-response structure is a pattern a student can learn in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers covering reading and directed writing. The summary question is the single most recoverable component, because students lose marks copying phrasing rather than compressing it.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Steady progress rather than quick gains, so budget across terms. The syllabus variant decides whether speaking is endorsed separately, which determines how much oral practice is worth buying late on.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal and data representation are reliable, cheap marks that students neglect. Programming confidence takes longer and is the part worth starting in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

sections.heading: The Core entry is the most expensive decision in Year 10
paragraphs: Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in most IGCSE subjects, and the Core route caps the grade available at C. That is not a prediction about performance; it is a ceiling written into the entry. A student who sits Core and answers everything correctly still cannot be awarded above a C in that subject.

The cost appears two years later. Most schools set an entry threshold for A Level in a subject, commonly a 6 or 7 at IGCSE in maths and the sciences, and a Core-capped grade does not reach it. The family then pays for one of three repairs: an intensive conversion to Extended inside the school's own entry deadline, a resit in the November series, or a changed sixth-form plan that closes a university route. Each of those costs more than the support that would have kept the Extended tier open.

Why does a Core entry get made? Usually for sensible-sounding reasons. The student is anxious, the Extended paper looks harder, a teacher recommends the safer option, and nobody states the ceiling plainly to the parent. The decision is reversible only within the school's entry deadlines, which sit months before the exam, so the window closes long before anyone feels the consequence.

The question to ask the head of department in Year 10 is specific: what tier is my child entered for, what is the deadline to change it, and what grade would they need in a school assessment to justify Extended? That conversation is free and it is the highest-value thing on this page.

sections.heading: Cost per grade: where an hour buys the most marks
paragraphs: Families usually allocate tuition by anxiety, buying hours in the subject that worries them most. A better allocation is by recoverability: how many marks a paid hour tends to return in that subject, given the pattern of loss on a recent paper. The two rarely point to the same place.

Technique losses are cheap to fix. Marks going missing because a command word was misread, working was not shown, units were omitted or an evaluation lacked a justification respond to a short block of marking practice. Content losses are expensive, because reteaching has to happen before practice helps, and that is measured in weeks. A paper with scattered single marks missing across many questions is a cheap problem; a paper with whole questions abandoned is not.

Subject matters too. Business Studies and Economics respond quickly because evaluation structure and diagram accuracy are learnable patterns. The summary question in English First Language is a contained skill. Extended maths without calculator fluency, and organic chemistry, are slow. That ordering is not about difficulty; it is about how concentrated the recoverable marks are.

One more variable belongs in the calculation: how long the student has. A technique problem can be fixed six weeks before a paper and still show up in the mark. A content gap discovered six weeks out cannot be fully closed, so the spending there should target the highest-yield topics rather than the whole syllabus, and the honest version of that conversation is one a tutor should initiate without being asked.

sections.heading: The three quotes an Al Yasmeen family usually gets
paragraphs: Ask around in a villa district and three kinds of quote come back. A neighbour's recommendation of a university student at the bottom of the market, often informal and cash-based. An agency rate in the middle. And an in-home arrangement with a tutor who will drive over, quoted at a premium that is rarely itemised.

Published figures let you place each one. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In the middle, Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, while TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai cost table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The in-home premium deserves a sentence of its own because nobody itemises it. A tutor crossing from Sharjah or central Ajman to a villa in Al Yasmeen spends real time and fuel doing it, and that cost is inside the hourly rate. The student receives the same sixty minutes of teaching. What the premium buys is physical presence, which genuinely matters for a younger or very reluctant child and matters much less for a Year 10 student who already works at a desk.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so the comparison here is not a sales device. Home visits run in India only. The figures are published because this market hides them: three of six pages examined print no price, and two of those that do quote in US dollars.

sections.heading: What a villa household actually needs to buy
paragraphs: The equipment conversation is short and it saves money. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, a pair of headphones, a desk with a wall behind it rather than a corridor, and a stable connection. That is the whole list. Families sometimes buy a graphics tablet or a subscription platform before the first session; neither is necessary, and a tutor who requires one should explain why.

What a villa in Al Yasmeen does provide, which an apartment often does not, is a room with a door. That is worth more to an hour of tuition than any device. A student working at the kitchen table with siblings nearby loses ten minutes of every session to interruption, which at mid-band rates is a meaningful share of what the hour cost.

The second thing worth organising is the paper. Have the most recent marked script, the school's topic list and any mock timetable ready for the first session. A tutor who spends session one diagnosing from real marked work is working on the right problem by session two. A tutor who has nothing to look at starts by reteaching from the beginning, and that is four to six hours spent on content the student already holds.

Finally, agree who talks to whom. A short written note to the parent after each session is standard and costs nothing. A formal monthly report sometimes carries a fee. Ask which you are getting, because a family that reads a note each week catches a stalling plan early, and catching it early is the cheapest correction available.
bullets: A quiet room with a door beats any equipment purchase

sections.heading: Exam entry, resits and the private candidate route
paragraphs: Exam entry is a cost that sits outside tuition and catches families by surprise. Where a student is enrolled at a school, the school enters them and charges the entry fees, which vary between centres and between boards. There is no single published national figure, so ask the school's exams officer for the per-subject cost in writing rather than relying on a number quoted online.

A private candidate, meaning a student not entered through their own school, registers through a centre that accepts external candidates and pays that centre's fees, which differ from the in-school rate. Families consider this route for a resit, for a subject the school does not offer, or after a move between curricula. The practical constraint is that private entry has its own deadlines, usually months before the exam window, and some practical or coursework components are harder to arrange externally.

The November series is the budget tool most families overlook. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November, and Pearson International GCSE in May/June and November, so a single weak subject can be retaken in one series rather than triggering a repeated year. That is a far smaller cost, in fees and in time, than any alternative. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so it is not a route for a UAE candidate.

Build the dates in before you build the budget. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and the live timetable on the board's own site is the only version to plan from. A page like this one should not be your source for a date a family acts on.

sections.heading: The calendar is the cheapest lever you have
paragraphs: Of all the ways to reduce what tuition costs, the one that works most reliably is free: start earlier. The same grade movement needs roughly half the hours in October that it needs in March, for three compounding reasons. There are more weeks, so the work can be spread at one session rather than two. Content can be retaught before it is practised, instead of both at once. And specialist availability is wider, so you are not paying the scarcity premium that appears in the final eight weeks.

The pattern in this market is predictable. Enquiries cluster after the mock results come back, which is exactly when the hours cost most and the useful slots have gone. Families who book in September or October pay mid-band rates for the slot they want. Families who book in February pay the upper band for whatever is left, usually late in the evening.

There is a second calendar effect inside the year. Ramadan shifts the school day and the household rhythm, and a plan that ignores it loses weeks. Sessions often move to a post-Iftar slot during that period, and families who agree the change in advance keep continuity while those who improvise lose a month. Mock weeks, school trips and the end-of-term crush do the same thing on a smaller scale.

Write the year on one page in September: term dates, mock windows, the school's internal deadlines, the exam series, and Ramadan. Then place the tuition hours where they can survive. That single sheet of paper is worth more than any rate negotiation, and it is the thing almost no family does before hiring.

sections.heading: When to stop paying
paragraphs: Almost nothing in the tutoring business is written about stopping, which is why so many families end up with a monthly charge nobody re-examines. A plan that cannot describe its own ending is not a plan; it is a subscription. Decide the exit at the start, in terms somebody could check.

Useful exits are concrete. A named grade on a school assessment. A topic list cleared, with the student able to complete past questions on each item unaided. A full paper finished inside the time limit with the mark above a stated threshold. Vague exits such as feeling more confident are not testable, and a plan without a test runs forever.

Then review on marked work at six weeks and again at twelve. If the pattern of lost marks has moved towards the target, continue. If it has not moved at all, more of the same is the wrong purchase: change the approach or change the tutor. If the target has been met, stop, and keep a short block in reserve for the weeks before the series rather than carrying a weekly charge through a quiet term.

One honest caveat. Stopping and restarting costs a little more per hour than continuity, because a tutor has to re-establish where the student is. For a subject that is genuinely fixed, that cost is smaller than months of unnecessary sessions. For a subject where the student is still fragile, continuity is cheaper. The marked paper tells you which case you are in, and it is the only thing that does.

faqs.question: What is the total cost of IGCSE tutoring in Al Yasmeen for one subject?
faqs.answer: Cost the plan rather than the hour. One weekly session from October to the June series is about eight months, or roughly 32 sessions. At the published band for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 150 to 300, that is AED 4,800 to 9,600 across the campaign, or AED 600 to 1,200 a month. A targeted block of four to eight hours for one diagnosed problem is far less. Those are market figures from pages read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does a Core entry cost us money later?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge Core caps the awarded grade at C, whatever happens in the exam. Most schools require a 6 or 7 at IGCSE for A Level entry in maths and the sciences, so a Core-capped grade does not reach the threshold. The family then pays for an intensive conversion inside the school's entry deadline, a November resit, or a changed sixth-form plan. Ask the head of department in Year 10 which tier your child is entered for and what the deadline to change it is.

faqs.question: Which subject should get the first block of paid hours?
faqs.answer: The one where a marked paper shows recoverable marks, not the one causing the most worry. Scattered single marks across many questions means a technique problem that a short block fixes. Whole questions abandoned means missing content, which needs weeks of reteaching before practice helps. Business Studies, Economics and the English summary question tend to move in four to six hours. Extended maths without calculator fluency and organic chemistry take a term. Spend where the marks are concentrated and recoverable.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who drives to our villa worth the extra cost?
faqs.answer: Only if presence is the problem being solved. In-home one-to-one visits in the UAE are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the upper part of that prices travel, fuel and evening traffic rather than teaching. The hour contains the same sixty minutes either way. For a younger or very reluctant child who will not start without an adult in the room, that premium buys something real. For a Year 10 student with a desk and headphones, it does not. IB Gram does not offer UAE home visits in any case.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE exam entries themselves cost in Ajman?
faqs.answer: There is no single published figure, and any page quoting one should be treated carefully. Where a student is enrolled at a school, the school enters them and charges its own fee per subject, which varies by centre and by board. A private candidate registers through a centre that accepts external entries and pays that centre's rate, which is usually higher. Ask your school's exams officer for the per-subject cost in writing, and ask about the deadline at the same time, since entry deadlines sit months before the papers.

faqs.question: Can a November resit save money compared with repeating a year?
faqs.answer: Substantially, yes, and it is the option families overlook most often. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November, and Pearson International GCSE in May/June and November, so one weak subject can be retaken in a single series instead of triggering a repeated year of school fees. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not a route for a UAE candidate. Check the live timetable on the board's own site and the school's entry deadline before planning a resit campaign.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy any software or equipment for online lessons?
faqs.answer: No. A laptop or tablet with a working camera, headphones, a desk with a wall behind it and a stable connection is the entire list. Families sometimes buy a graphics tablet or a platform subscription before the first session, and neither is necessary; a tutor who insists on one should explain what it adds. The thing that genuinely improves an hour is a room with a door, which most villas in Al Yasmeen already have and most apartments do not.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we realistically afford to support at once?
faqs.answer: One properly, usually. Spreading two hours a week across three subjects is the commonest way a tuition budget disappears without any grade moving, because no subject gets enough continuity to shift a pattern. A better sequence is one subject at a time with a short block, reviewed on marked work, then the next. If two subjects genuinely need support, consider one weekly hour in each rather than splitting an hour, and expect the campaign to run longer.

faqs.question: Does the rate go up in the weeks before the June series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens and some providers price that period differently, so ask directly. The bigger effect is on your side: the same grade movement bought in March takes roughly twice the hours it takes in October, because the work compresses into fewer weeks at a higher session count. Demand spikes right after mock results, which is also when the good slots have gone. Booking in September or October buys a mid-band rate and the hour you actually want.

faqs.question: What happens to our money if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: Ask that question before paying for anything, and get the answer in writing. A reasonable arrangement lets a family change tutor early without losing a prepaid block, and proposes an alternative specialist rather than leaving you to start again. Because our tutor pool is not geographic, a replacement does not have to live near Al Yasmeen as well as teach the subject, which is one of the quieter advantages of online delivery. Changing in week two costs a fortnight; leaving a poor match until March costs a grade.

faqs.question: Does the Ramadan timetable change what we pay for or when lessons run in Al Yasmeen?
faqs.answer: Agree the change in advance rather than improvising. The school day and the household rhythm both shift, and sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot for that period. Families who settle the new time before the month starts keep continuity; families who cancel week by week usually lose a month of progress and then buy it back later at a higher intensity. Put Ramadan on the same sheet as term dates, mock windows and the exam series when you plan the year in September.

faqs.question: Is group tuition a cheaper way to get the same result?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour and it solves a different problem. A group class gives pace and practice volume, which suits a confident student who needs more reps. It cannot stop for one child, so a student who is two topics behind stays behind while the invoices continue. Families frequently buy group sessions first because of the price, then buy one-to-one anyway, having paid twice. Decide from the marked paper: missing content needs one-to-one diagnosis, while missing practice can be bought in a group.

faqs.question: What should the first six weeks produce for the money?
faqs.answer: Three visible things. A named list of where marks are being lost, taken from marked work rather than impressions. A short written plan with the school's deadlines and the exam series on it. And at least one measurable improvement, a component score up, a timed section completed, a topic cleared. If none of those exists after six weeks, the purchase is not working, and the answer is a different approach or a different tutor rather than more hours of the same thing.

faqs.question: When is the right time to stop paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: When the exit you wrote down at the start has happened: a named grade on a school assessment, a topic list cleared with unaided past questions, or a full paper completed inside the time limit above a stated threshold. Then stop, and keep a short block in reserve for the weeks before the series rather than carrying a weekly charge through a quiet term. Restarting costs slightly more per hour than continuity, so if a student is still fragile, continuity is the cheaper choice. The marked paper decides.

intro.heading: The honest answer first
paragraphs: Al Zorah is a new development on Ajman's coast: low density, still filling in, built around a marina, a golf course and villa and apartment plots. It is a pleasant place to live and an extremely thin place to find a tutor. There is no school inside the development, the resident population is small, and the informal network that produces tutoring recommendations in an older district has not had time to exist.

So the honest answer to 'is there an IGCSE tutor near me' is that the nearest ones are in Ajman's older districts or across the boundary in Sharjah, that almost all of them are generalists, and that the chance of one of them having taught your child's specific syllabus to grade standard is close to zero. That is not a criticism of anybody; it is a consequence of population density and of how specialist teaching experience accumulates.

It is worth separating two different needs at this point, because they have different answers. If your child is young and needs an adult sitting beside them to keep them on task, presence is what you are buying and a local arrangement - even a general one - is the right choice. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so we are not the provider for that.

If your child is in Year 10 or 11 and losing marks on Cambridge 0620 Paper 4 or Pearson 4MA1, presence is not the problem. What is needed is somebody who has taught that paper, marked it against the published scheme, and can say in one session which three things are costing marks. Those people exist in quantity; none of them lives in Al Zorah, and over live video that does not matter.

The rest of this page is therefore about verification rather than geography: how to read a tutor's claims, what questions reveal course experience in two minutes, how to identify which board your child is on in a district where schools run several curricula, what the realistic options are when nobody local fits, and what the market charges so that any quote can be judged.

It also covers cost, because a family with no local market has nothing to compare a quote against. The bands quoted later come from published UAE rate cards and from a Dubai tutoring cost survey read in October 2026, and they are the market's figures rather than ours - published so that any quote, including ours, can be measured against something checkable.
Delivery here, as on all our UAE pages, is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run - which from this development is a real journey in its own right.

sections.heading: Why a new development has no tutoring market
paragraphs: It is worth explaining the mechanism, because it is not obvious and it affects how a family should search. Tutoring markets form around schools and around established residential density. Teachers live near the schools that employ them. Independent tutors build a client base by word of mouth within a neighbourhood. Both processes take years.

Al Zorah has neither input yet. No school inside the development means no resident teaching population. A small and recently arrived resident population means no word-of-mouth network - and the parents who would normally supply recommendations are themselves new and asking the same question. So a distance-sorted search returns either nothing or a handful of names from Ajman's older districts who are willing to make the drive.

Those names are not bad tutors. They are, however, almost certainly generalists, because that is what the broader northern-emirates market mostly consists of: capable people who teach several subjects across several year groups. The population of adults who have taught one specific syllabus code to grade standard for years is small everywhere and concentrated nowhere near a new coastal development.

The useful conclusion is not to search harder locally but to change the filter. If the examination is national - and it is - then the right question is who has taught the paper, not who can reach the house. Over live video the answer to that question is a real choice rather than a short list, and nothing in the rate pays for a journey across Ajman.

sections.heading: Reading a tutor's claims
paragraphs: Because a family here is choosing from listings rather than from reputation, it helps to know how listings are written. The language is designed to maximise enquiries, which means it is broad where you need it to be specific.

'All subjects, all levels' means a willingness to teach anything, not experience of everything. 'Ten years' experience' may describe ten years of general tutoring, with no particular syllabus taught twice. A degree in the subject proves the subject, not the examination - a chemistry graduate knows more chemistry than 0620 requires and may not know that the mark scheme wants an observation rather than a conclusion. 'Examiner' is a claim rarely evidenced and never transferable to your child's paper.

The replacement questions are short and cannot be answered from a listing. Which board and code is my child entered for, and how do you know? How many papers are there in this subject, and what is each worth? Name the three topics where candidates lose the most marks. What will you do differently in the last six weeks? Will you mark a recent mock before we meet?

A specialist answers the first four in specifics and says yes to the fifth immediately, because the annotated script makes their case better than conversation can. A generalist answers with reassurance about building confidence - which is pleasant, is sometimes exactly what a younger child needs, and is not what a Year 11 candidate is losing marks for.

sections.heading: Identifying the board before anything else
paragraphs: In Ajman this step matters more than in most places, because several schools run Indian or mixed curricula and enter particular cohorts or subjects for Cambridge or Pearson papers. Families frequently do not know which board applies, and every later decision depends on it.

The codes resolve it. Cambridge uses four digits: 0580 mathematics, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English, 0510 English as a second language. Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a 4: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. Both appear on the statement of entry and in the exam information the school circulates, and the exams officer can confirm board, code and tier in one reply.

Why it matters so much: paper structures differ, question phrasing differs, and preparation differs accordingly. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended and its sciences include an alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson's maths sets two equally weighted papers. A student practising the wrong board's past papers for a term is building partly wrong habits, and usually discovers it in a mock rather than from the tutor.

While you are emailing, ask for two more things: the internal deadline for entry changes, which is earlier than the board's and is the one that constrains a tier change, and the mock window. With board, code, tier, deadline and mock dates in hand, you can brief any tutor in a single sentence - and the quality of replies you receive changes immediately.

Keep the reply. In a household that may deal with two schools in two emirates, the email confirming board, code and tier is the document everybody wishes they could find in February, and it takes no effort to file in the first week of term.

sections.heading: What to do when nobody local fits
paragraphs: Suppose you have done the verification and concluded, correctly, that nobody within reach has taught your child's course. There are four realistic options and they are not equivalent.

The first is self-study with strict marking, which is free. Papers and mark schemes exist through the school, and a disciplined candidate who completes a paper under timing and marks it honestly learns most of what a tutor teaches about technique. The failure modes are generous self-marking and avoiding the hardest papers, and a parent can partly police both.

The second is local general help for presence and routine, which is cheap and genuinely useful for the job it does. The third is paying a travel premium to bring a generalist out to the development - the least efficient purchase on this list, because it is the most expensive way to buy the cheapest kind of help.

The fourth is matching a specialist nationally and teaching over live video, which is what we do. For most Year 10 and 11 candidates the strongest combination is the first and the fourth: self-study for volume, plus a small number of specialist hours for direction and triage. That costs less than a term of weekly local sessions and reliably achieves more, because the hours are spent on diagnosis rather than on company.

A practical way to decide between the four: write down what you expect to be different in six weeks. If the answer is that homework gets done and the house is calmer, buy presence locally. If it is that the Paper 4 mark improves, buy diagnosis - and accept that the person who can provide it does not live nearby and does not need to.

sections.heading: The school run from a development with no school
paragraphs: Verification settles who should teach; the school run settles when. From Al Zorah every family commutes, and the journey is the number a tutoring plan has to be built on.

A child at a school in Ajman's older districts may be home between half past three and four. A child crossing into Sharjah is more likely home between four and half past, and one attending a Dubai school from this address could be later still. Those are the inputs. The published school finish time is not: dismissal, loading, a bus route serving several communities and afternoon traffic between them add up to more than most families expect.

The rule we apply is simple. Take the real arrival time, add thirty minutes for food and decompression, and place the session there. If that lands at six, the session is at six. If it lands too late to be useful, the honest conclusion is one shorter weekday session plus a longer weekend morning, rather than two weekday sessions that both underperform.

This is also where an in-home arrangement decays fastest. A tutor driving out to the coast is travelling in the same traffic, after their own working day, to a low-density address that is not on the way to anything. Start times drift, sessions get trimmed because another family is waiting, and the evenings when something goes wrong on the road are the evenings the lesson is cancelled. Online, a late bus moves the session by twenty minutes and nothing else changes.

sections.heading: What it costs, and the premium to avoid
paragraphs: Prices in this market are rarely published, so a family in a new development has very little to compare against. The bands below come from published UAE rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026. They are market figures rather than our price list.

Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, advertises from about AED 45 an hour. A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300. An in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed. An IGCSE or A Level specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 or more. Published packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The premium to avoid from this address is the travel one, and here it is larger than usual. A tutor driving from Ajman's older districts or from Sharjah to a low-density coastal development is pricing a journey that benefits nobody academically, and the destination is far enough that the quote sits high in the in-home band. The money buys fuel and time, not knowledge of a mark scheme.

The other premium to treat sceptically is the brand one. Examiner status is seldom evidenced, cannot be relied on to be current, and gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content - the mark scheme a good tutor works from is published. If a tutor at the middle of the qualified band can name the three things costing your child marks from one script, the additional several hundred dirhams an hour is buying something other than that diagnosis.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the questions nobody asks
paragraphs: Two administrative checks are worth making whoever you hire, and both are quick.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service handles applications in about two working days. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published - so ignore any figure quoted at you.

The conflict. Do not arrange paid tutoring with somebody who teaches and marks your child at school. Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules barring private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct pointing the same way. Beyond any rule, the person marking your child's work should not be on your payroll.

On regulators, for completeness: Ajman's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority - which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods - Dubai's by KHDA and Abu Dhabi's by ADEK. For clarity about us: IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from any of them, and has no office, centre or branch in this country.

sections.heading: What we will and will not do
paragraphs: A page that opens with an awkward answer should close with a precise one, so here is the scope of what we offer and what we decline.

We teach: one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, matched on board, syllabus code and tier, working from the syllabus document your school issues and that board's past papers, marked against the published mark scheme with errors logged by question type. We write down the next six sessions' targets and review on timed scores rather than attendance.

We do not send tutors to UAE addresses - home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India - and we have no premises here. We do not guarantee grades, because nobody can know what a particular candidate will score. We do not write, draft or edit assessed coursework, and we do not sell completed work: services that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice finding attaches to the student rather than the seller.

We also do not distribute boards' syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - the school is the proper route to current versions - and we claim no approval from any regulator or board. If what your family actually needs is an adult in the room with a younger child, a local arrangement is the better answer and we would rather say so than take the booking.

And where no specialist is free in your subject at a workable hour, we will offer another hour or a named date rather than a substitute. From an address with no local fallback, a generalist put into a dated block costs the whole window, so a clear no is the more useful answer.

faqs.question: Are there any IGCSE tutors actually living in Al Zorah?
faqs.answer: Very few, and almost certainly none who has taught your child's specific syllabus to grade standard. Tutoring markets form around schools and established residential density, and this development has no school inside it and a small, recently arrived population. The nearest supply is in Ajman's older districts and across the Sharjah boundary, and it is general rather than course-specific. That is a density fact rather than a judgement about anybody, and it is why we match nationally and teach over live video.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor really knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions and make one request. Which board and code is my child entered for, and how do you know? How many papers are there, and what is each worth? Name the three topics where candidates lose the most marks. What changes in the last six weeks? Then ask them to mark a recent mock before you meet. Specialists answer the questions in specifics and say yes to the request immediately, because the annotated script argues their case better than conversation does.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying extra for a tutor willing to drive out here?
faqs.answer: Only if presence is what you are buying - a younger child who needs an adult beside them to stay on task. For a Year 10 or 11 candidate the premium buys fuel and time rather than knowledge of a mark scheme, and from this address it sits at the top of the published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. We do not offer UAE home visits in any case, so for that need a local arrangement is better.

faqs.question: What does 'all subjects, all levels' on a listing actually mean?
faqs.answer: Willingness rather than experience. The phrase maximises enquiries, which is why it is used, and it tells you nothing about whether the person has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher. The same applies to years of experience, which may describe general tutoring, and to a degree in the subject, which proves subject knowledge rather than examination knowledge. Replace all of it with one question: which board and code have you taught, and how recently?

faqs.question: How do we find out which exam board our school uses?
faqs.answer: Look for the code on the statement of entry or in the exam information the school circulates. Cambridge uses four digits - 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500 - and Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a 4: 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1. The exams officer can confirm board, code and tier in one reply. This matters particularly in Ajman, where several schools run Indian or mixed curricula and enter particular cohorts for British-board papers in specific subjects.

faqs.question: Can a disciplined student here prepare largely without a tutor?
faqs.answer: A long way, yes. Past papers and mark schemes are available through the school, and a candidate who completes a paper under timing and marks it strictly against the scheme learns most of what a tutor teaches about technique. The two failure modes are generous self-marking and avoiding the papers that feel hardest. For most Year 11 candidates the strongest combination is self-study for volume plus a small number of specialist hours for diagnosis and triage.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start from this development?
faqs.answer: Take your child's actual arrival time and add thirty minutes. From a school in Ajman's older districts, home between half past three and four is typical, so half past four works. Crossing into Sharjah, home between four and half past makes five realistic. The published school finish time is not a useful input - dismissal, loading, a bus route serving several communities and afternoon traffic add up. One week of noting when your child walks in gives you the number.

faqs.question: Who supervises private schools in Ajman?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, along with Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods; Dubai's fall under KHDA and Abu Dhabi's under ADEK. If your children attend school in two emirates you are reading two sets of published information. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of these bodies.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit, and can I ask about it?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own licensing service handles applications in about two working days. Since holding it costs nothing, a working tutor has no practical reason to be without one.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit, and is a resit possible?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs June and November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and results from a November series reach students in January - the November 2025 cohort received theirs on 22 January 2026. A resit is a real option provided the receiving institution accepts a January result and the entry route is confirmed with the school or a registered centre first.

faqs.question: Should we worry that our child is at an Indian-curriculum school sitting IGCSE papers?
faqs.answer: Not worry, but do plan for it. The subject overlap is substantial; what differs is examination behaviour - question phrasing, the expectation that method is shown, and command terms treated as precise instructions rather than general invitations to write. A capable student can lose marks for reasons unrelated to knowledge. Two to four board-specific sessions working through the correct board's past papers, marked against the published scheme, usually close that gap faster than more content teaching.

faqs.question: Are the rates on this page what you charge?
faqs.answer: No. They are market bands from published UAE rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026, published so you can judge any quote - including ours - against something checkable. Three of the six best-ranked pages in our competitor research publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, which UAE families do not transact in. Ask us directly for our figure, and begin with the free trial lesson, which costs nothing.

faqs.question: Where a subject carries coursework, how far can a tutor go?
faqs.answer: With the teaching and the feedback, yes; with the writing, no. A tutor may explain what the task requires, question a plan, teach the skill involved and explain why a paragraph does not answer the question asked. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work, and IB Gram does not supply completed coursework. Services selling finished assessments appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody has taught our exact course at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we offer a different hour with the right specialist or a named date when one frees up. Narrow requests - Additional Mathematics, computer science 0478, a specific board's business paper in the weeks before a series - sometimes have nobody available. What we will not do is put a generalist into the slot and leave you to discover the mismatch over six weeks, because from an address with no local fallback that substitution costs the whole term.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.tutorsIntro: These are the subject specialists most often requested by families around Emirates City and the wider Ajman residential belt. Each one teaches a named IGCSE syllabus rather than a vague subject, and every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: Why proximity is the wrong thing to shop for
paragraphs: Emirates City is a dense cluster of residential towers on the Ajman side of Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, close to the Ajman-Sharjah boundary. Most households here have at least one parent commuting to Sharjah or Dubai, and children are spread across British, Indian and American curriculum schools in three emirates. That spread is the reason a search for an IGCSE home tutor in Emirates City rarely ends well. A tutor who lives ten minutes away may be excellent at Year 9 maths and have never opened a Cambridge 0580 Extended paper.

The syllabus code is the thing that decides whether a tutor is useful. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 cover overlapping content and assess it differently. Cambridge Extended candidates sit a paper without a calculator; Edexcel allows a calculator in both papers of 4MA1. A student drilled for the wrong one walks into the hall with the wrong habits. The same applies across the sciences, where Cambridge Physics 0625 splits theory and practical across three paper slots and Pearson 4PH1 does not.

So the question worth asking is not who is nearby. It is who has marked, taught or examined the exact specification printed on your child's exam timetable, and whether that person is free at the hour your child can concentrate. Once you ask it that way, geography stops being an advantage and starts being a constraint. A family in Emirates City choosing from tutors within a twenty-minute drive is choosing from a handful of people. A family choosing online is choosing from specialists across the UAE and beyond.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, not a tuition centre. There is no office in Ajman, no branch in Sharjah, and no tutor who will arrive at a tower lobby in Emirates City. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. For UAE families, every lesson is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own past papers on screen, and a recording the student can replay before a test.

This page answers the proximity question properly, then gives you the things the search results around it usually skip: what IGCSE tuition actually costs across the Ajman and Sharjah market in AED, which exam series a candidate registered in the UAE sits, what the Ministry of Education counts for an equivalency file, whether a private tutor needs a permit, and where the line sits between help and malpractice on assessed coursework.

Read it with your child's timetable next to you. If the subject codes on that timetable do not match the ones a prospective tutor talks about, you have learned something more useful than a driving distance.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.programmesIntro: Families around Emirates City send children to schools running several British-track routes. These are the ones that matter for an IGCSE search, with what each one means for a student living on this side of Ajman.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year course most British-curriculum schools in Ajman and Sharjah run to the end of Year 11. Subjects are graded 9-1 or A*-G depending on the syllabus, and most carry a Core and an Extended tier. Core caps the available grade at C, which is the single most consequential decision a Year 10 parent makes, because a capped tier closes off an A Level route in that subject.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A family in Emirates City with children at two schools in two emirates may be looking at two different zone timetables.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track option in this part of the UAE, with codes that start with a numeral: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Papers are linear in most subjects, and the calculator rules and formula sheets differ from Cambridge in ways that change how a student should revise.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always open the live timetable on the Pearson site rather than trusting a date repeated on a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, where the Core-or-Extended decision is quietly made. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and give a school a benchmark rather than a certificate. Families who start support in Year 9 rather than Year 11 are usually the ones who keep the Extended tier open in maths and the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: In Ajman the practical reason to start early is scheduling. Many households here have a parent driving to Dubai or Sharjah daily, so weekday evenings fill quickly once a child reaches Year 11 and school commitments stack up. A Year 8 or Year 9 slot is easier to protect and costs less per year of progress than a crisis block of lessons in the spring term.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, the next step
programmes.description: Where IGCSE grades stop being a report-card line and start being an entry requirement. Most schools set a grade threshold for A Level entry in a subject, usually a 6 or 7 at IGCSE for maths and the sciences, and that threshold is why a Core tier decision in Year 10 matters two years later.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education equivalency rule for British-curriculum students names one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of Ajman cluster around maths, the separate sciences and English, with Business and Economics rising in Year 11. Each entry names the syllabus and where marks are commonly lost.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended candidates face a paper with no calculator, which exposes weak number sense that a calculator has been hiding since Year 8. Marks go missing on bounds, on vectors, and on multi-step probability where the method mark is available but the working is not shown.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: A calculator is permitted in both papers, so the examiner tests structure instead of arithmetic. The recurring loss is in trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and in questions that ask for an exact answer where a rounded decimal scores nothing.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Maths, usually alongside 0580. It introduces calculus and permutations early, and the common failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than a different course with its own notation demands.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Theory carries the bulk of the grade and the practical component is assessed either by a timed practical test or by the alternative-to-practical paper. Students lose marks on graph work, on describing a method precisely enough to repeat, and on units in compound quantities.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and mole calculations account for most of the gap between a 6 and an 8. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards students who have thought about apparatus choice and sources of error, which is exactly what a crowded school lab rarely has time to teach.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where the examiner pays for precision, not volume. Answers that say a plant grows faster rather than naming the limiting factor earn nothing, and the data-response questions are where strong students quietly drop grades.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, one reading and one directed writing and composition, with a coursework route available at some schools. Reading marks are lost on the summary question, where students copy phrasing instead of compressing it in their own words.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The common entry for students whose home language is not English. The syllabus choice decides whether speaking is endorsed separately or counted in the overall grade, which changes how much oral practice is worth in the final term.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study questions carry the grade and the examiner rewards application to the stimulus business, not textbook definitions. Evaluation marks are the ones most Ajman students leave on the table, because a judgement without a justification scores half.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams are marks. A labelled, correctly shifted curve earns credit before a word of analysis is written, and the frequent loss is in questions asking for the effect on a specific group rather than on the economy in general.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions matter more than students expect, and the practical programming section rewards a candidate who can trace a loop by hand. Binary, hexadecimal and data-representation questions are reliable marks that get neglected until the final weeks.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Taken by non-Arabic-speaking students in UAE schools where Arabic is a mandated subject alongside the licensed curriculum. Progress depends on consistent short sessions rather than long ones, and on reading unseen passages aloud with a tutor who corrects pronunciation.

regions.note: Tower living close to Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, with a high share of commuting parents. Sessions here work best after 6pm once the Sharjah and Dubai traffic has cleared and the household has settled.

regions.name: Al Yasmeen

sections.heading: What a parent in Emirates City is actually asking
paragraphs: The literal question behind this search is whether somebody qualified lives close enough to come to the flat. The useful answer has two halves. First: the number of Cambridge and Edexcel subject specialists resident in Ajman is small, and almost none of them are free at 5pm on a weekday. Second: proximity was never the thing that made a tutor effective. Syllabus fluency was.

Consider what a parent really wants from the hour. They want somebody who recognises the difference between a 0580 Extended non-calculator paper and a 4MA1 Higher paper where a calculator is allowed throughout. They want somebody who knows that the Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper tests apparatus reasoning rather than lab technique. They want the tutor to have seen fifty students make the same mistake on bounds and to know which three sentences fix it. None of that correlates with a driving distance from Emirates City.

What proximity does buy is a specific, limited thing: a physical presence in the room for a child who will not otherwise sit down. That is a real benefit and worth naming honestly. It is also the only one, and it is purchased at a travel premium. For most families around here the better trade is a specialist on screen at a fixed hour, with the parent in the next room for the first fortnight until the routine holds.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to any address in the UAE. Home visits are offered only in India. For a family in Emirates City, the service is one-to-one tuition over live video, run on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the specification rather than the neighbourhood.

sections.heading: Proximity, travel time and what the premium buys
paragraphs: Put the three realistic options side by side and the picture clears quickly. An in-home visit in the northern emirates carries a travel cost whether or not it appears as a line on the invoice. A tutor crossing from Sharjah to Emirates City in the evening peak is giving up forty minutes each way, and that time is priced into the hourly rate. The student gets the same sixty minutes of teaching either way.

Group tuition at a centre is cheaper per hour and works for a confident student who needs pace rather than diagnosis. It fails the student who is two topics behind, because a centre class cannot stop for one child. Online one-to-one sits between them on price and above both on specificity, and it removes the failure mode that catches most families: a cancelled session because the tutor is stuck on the Emirates Road.

The table below compares the three on the things that actually differ. The rate ranges are market figures gathered from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, not IB Gram prices. They are included because almost no competing page in this market publishes an AED figure at all, which leaves parents guessing.

Read the last column carefully. The question of what happens when a session cannot run is the one that separates a service from an arrangement, and it is worth asking any prospective tutor before the first payment. A missed hour in October is an inconvenience; a missed hour in the fortnight before a mock is a topic that never gets covered, and the family discovers it from a results slip rather than from the tutor.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: find the code before you book
paragraphs: Schools around Ajman and Sharjah run both British-track boards, and some run them in parallel across different subjects. A child can sit Cambridge 0580 for maths and Pearson 4PH1 for physics in the same year. Parents frequently do not know which, because the school refers to subjects by name and the certificate arrives two years later.

Finding out takes one message to the subject teacher or one look at the statement of entry. It is worth the five minutes, because the boards differ in ways that change revision. Cambridge Extended maths includes a paper where no calculator is permitted; Pearson allows one in both papers of Mathematics A. Cambridge science splits the practical assessment into a timed practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson handles practical skills inside the theory papers. The command words differ, the formula provision differs, and the mark schemes reward different phrasing.

Tiering is the other divergence. Cambridge offers Core and Extended in most subjects, and Core caps the grade available at C. Pearson offers Foundation and Higher in maths. A Year 10 tier decision made for comfort can quietly close an A Level door, and it is reversible only inside the school's own entry deadlines, which sit months before the exam.

Once you have the codes, matching becomes concrete. A request for a maths tutor is vague. A request for a tutor who has taught 0580 Extended to a student aiming to move from a 5 to a 7 in nine months is a brief somebody can answer.

sections.heading: Five questions that test whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Credentials on a profile tell you little. A degree in physics does not mean somebody has taught 0625, and a teaching licence from another country does not mean they know how a Cambridge examiner words a six-mark question. The fastest filter is a short conversation with questions whose answers cannot be improvised.

Ask which paper carries the practical assessment in the subject your child takes, and what the alternative route is. Ask what the grade ceiling is on the Core tier. Ask which topic in the specification their students most often lose marks on, and then ask what they do about it in the first three sessions. Ask how they would use a past paper that the school has already set as a mock. Ask what they will not do with an assessed piece of coursework.

The answers you want are specific and slightly boring. Somebody who says they focus on building confidence has not answered. Somebody who says that Core candidates cannot score above a C, that bounds and compound-interest questions eat marks in 0580, and that they start by marking one paper against the published scheme to see where the method marks are being lost, has.

A free trial lesson does the same job faster. Watch the first ten minutes. A tutor who opens by asking which board the school entered the student for is already ahead of most of the market, and a tutor who asks to see a marked paper before talking about a plan is ahead again. The reverse signal is just as clear: somebody who spends the trial describing their own background rather than diagnosing your child's work will spend the paid sessions the same way.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs across the Ajman and Sharjah market
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is the number a household budget actually feels. One hour a week for a month is four sessions. At the lower end of the qualified-tutor band that is roughly AED 600 a month; at the specialist end it is closer to AED 1,200. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240-600 for budget tutors, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Rates in the northern emirates sit at or slightly below the Dubai bands.

Hourly figures from published provider pages fill in the detail. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour at the budget end and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for a premium named tutor. In-home visits in the UAE are quoted between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour once travel is accounted for, and monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions or AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What a parent can verify is more useful than any single figure. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, whether a 45-minute session is billed as an hour, whether the quoted price includes any VAT the provider charges, and what happens to a prepaid block if the match does not work. Those four answers explain most of the gap between two quotes that look identical.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly price on these pages, because the rate depends on subject, level and how close the exam series is. The free trial lesson and the consultation that follows are where the number for your child's case gets quoted, and no payment is taken before it.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation: the service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit for private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

u.ae also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. The relevant point for a parent is simpler: ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, and treat a vague answer as an answer.

There is a second layer that parents rarely hear about. In Abu Dhabi, professional-ethics rules reported in the press bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The ethical position is the same everywhere in the country: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay privately, however convenient it looks.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, and that permit is issued to an institute with a physical centre. IB Gram holds no such permit, claims no regulator approval or accreditation, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Anyone advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something that does not exist in that form.

sections.heading: The equivalency file: five subjects, grade E, and what does not count
paragraphs: Families in Ajman who plan to keep a child in the UAE for university eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process. It converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE institution can act on, and the British-track requirement is specific enough to plan around from Year 10.

For the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That exclusion matters in practice: a student taking Arabic as a mandated school subject still needs five other passes to reach the count.

The American track works differently, and families with children in both systems should know both. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule.

No IB points threshold is published in the source above, so no figure for the IB route appears on this page. A family on the Diploma route should confirm the requirement directly with the Ministry of Education or the attestation authority in their emirate. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of the equivalency or attestation process, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Where help ends and malpractice begins
paragraphs: This market contains providers who sell completed coursework. One page examined during research offers finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying one is not a shortcut; it is a malpractice case that can cost a student their qualification, and it is the clearest line in the whole tutoring business.

The honest version of coursework support is narrower and more useful than parents expect. A tutor can teach the skill the task assesses. They can explain the assessment criteria and what each band actually describes. They can look at a draft the student has written and say which paragraph does not do what the criterion asks. They can ask the questions that make a student notice their own gap in reasoning. They can set a timetable so the work does not land in one weekend.

A tutor cannot write a sentence of it, cannot edit it to completion, cannot supply a model answer for the student to reshape, and cannot hand over a finished piece. On the IGCSE side the same applies to any coursework component and to the controlled-assessment routes some subjects offer. Schools know what a Year 11 student writes like, and the gap between a student's classwork and a purchased draft is visible from across a staffroom.

IB Gram also does not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to the boards. A tutor can reference them, work from a paper the school has already issued, and point a parent to the official site. That is both the legal position and, in practice, the more useful one, because the official version is the current one.
