faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE home tutor in Emirates City who knows my child's exact syllabus?
faqs.answer: Probably not within a short drive, and that is the honest answer. Emirates City is a residential tower cluster, not a tutoring hub, and the number of Cambridge or Pearson subject specialists living nearby and free at 5pm is very small. IB Gram solves it the other way round: the tutor is chosen for the syllabus code on your child's statement of entry, then taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. No tutor comes to an address in Ajman, because home visits are an India-only service. What you gain is a specialist in 0580 Extended or 4PH1 rather than the nearest available graduate.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a tutor has really taught Cambridge 0580 before?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions a non-specialist cannot answer. What is the highest grade a Core candidate can be awarded? Which paper in the Extended route forbids a calculator? Which two topics do their students most often lose method marks on? A tutor who has taught 0580 will say C for the Core ceiling without hesitating, will name the non-calculator paper, and will reach for bounds, vectors or compound growth rather than offering general comments about confidence. Then take the free trial lesson and listen to the first ten minutes. If the tutor opens by asking which board the school entered your child for, that is a good sign.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 10 at a school in Ajman. Does online tuition suit that age?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the age it suits best. A fourteen or fifteen year old can hold a screen session for an hour, already works on a laptop at school, and benefits from the recording afterwards. Two practical conditions make the difference. The student needs a fixed study spot with headphones rather than a sofa, and the slot needs to be the same evening every week so it survives a busy term. Sit in the next room for the first fortnight. Once the routine holds, most parents step back and read the written note that follows each session instead.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for a family living in Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction is the first thing we check. Schools around Ajman and Sharjah use both boards, sometimes in different subjects for the same student. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit numeric codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson International GCSE codes start with a numeral, such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. Past papers are not interchangeable between them, calculator rules differ, and the mark schemes reward different phrasing. One message to the subject teacher, or a look at the statement of entry, settles which one applies.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition cost for families living around Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Think in months rather than hours. One session a week is four a month, which at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 an hour works out near AED 600 to 1,200. Bestimate's Dubai cost table puts monthly estimates at AED 240 to 600 for budget tutors and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and the northern emirates sit at or just below Dubai levels. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced in. Those are market figures from published pages, not IB Gram prices; ours are quoted after the free trial.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my child online still need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: A person providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. u.ae also states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals handled if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The practical assessment stays with the school; the tutor prepares the student for the paper that carries it. Cambridge assesses practical skills either through a timed practical test or through the alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on how the centre enters candidates. That written route is largely about apparatus choice, measurement precision, sources of error and graph work, all of which are taught well on a shared screen with a past paper open. Pearson handles practical skills inside the theory papers instead. The first thing a tutor should establish is which route your child's centre uses, because the preparation differs substantially.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE subjects does the Ministry of Education count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published rule for the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. There is no prescribed list of which five, so the practical advice is to protect five solid passes outside those two subjects from Year 10 onwards. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry of Education before you rely on it; IB Gram does not submit or guarantee any part of the process.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams run for a candidate registered in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate plans around June with November as the resit route. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Open the live timetable on the board's own site rather than trusting a date on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Arabic subject my child takes alongside the British curriculum?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits worth understanding. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and in Dubai the KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For mandated UAE subjects, schools may not use different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, so a tutor works with the school's own material and the published syllabus. Short, frequent sessions with reading aloud and correction do more for Arabic than long weekly blocks.

faqs.question: How quickly can lessons start for a student in Emirates City?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for mainstream subjects, because the slot rather than the tutor is the constraint. Maths, the separate sciences, English and Business are well covered, and the realistic delay is finding a weekday hour that works for both sides. Narrow or unusual combinations take longer, and the honest version of that answer matters: if nobody who has taught your child's specification is free at the hour you want, we say so and offer the nearest workable alternative instead of filling the gap. Evening slots after 6pm are the first to go in this part of Ajman.

faqs.question: Will the tutor work from my child's school worksheets or their own material?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order. The first two sessions usually work from what the school has already set, because a marked paper or a returned test tells a tutor more than any diagnostic they could design. From there the tutor builds a short plan around the pattern of loss, using past questions on the specification your child is entered for. What a tutor will not do is supply board-owned documents such as syllabus PDFs, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to Cambridge, Pearson or the IB and are referenced and linked, never reproduced.

faqs.question: My daughter is predicted a 4 in maths. Is the Extended tier still the right entry?
faqs.answer: It depends on what she needs the grade for, and the decision has a deadline. Cambridge Core caps the available grade at C, so a Core entry closes the door on an A Level maths route and on some university prerequisites, whatever happens in the exam. If the target is a 6 or better and there are two terms left, Extended with focused support is usually the better bet. If the entry has already been made, the school's own deadline governs any change. Ask the head of maths what the centre's deadline is before assuming either option is still open.

faqs.question: What happens in the first lesson, and what if the match turns out to be wrong?
faqs.answer: The trial session is free and no card details are taken beforehand. The tutor spends most of it on your child's own work, usually a marked paper, and finishes by naming two or three specific errors and what the first month would address. You get a short written note afterwards. If the match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is proposed; changing early costs a fortnight, while leaving a poor match until the spring costs a grade. Review again at six weeks, using marked work rather than impressions as the evidence.

ajman/igcse-home-tutor-in-emirates-city.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the five minutes it takes to find out which specification your child is entered for. With a code in hand, the search for an IGCSE home tutor in Emirates City stops being a question about driving distance and becomes a question somebody can answer precisely. Send the subject, the year group and the code, take the free trial lesson, and judge the tutor on whether they talk about your child's actual errors. intro.heading: Why a saved record is the real argument for teaching IGCSE over video
paragraphs: The debate about online tutoring is usually conducted at the wrong level. People argue about presence and rapport, which are genuine but unmeasurable, and ignore the thing that is measurable: what exists after the hour ends. A video session with a shared screen and a digital annotation tool produces a document. A session at a kitchen table in Al Rawda produces a used notebook and a verbal summary at the door. Six months later, one of those is still readable and one of them is not.

For an IGCSE student that difference compounds. The whole discipline of examination technique is pattern recognition across repeated attempts: the same unit dropped, the same compare question answered as two unrelated paragraphs, the same calculation finished without its final accuracy mark. Nobody can see a pattern across fourteen sessions from memory. You can see it immediately in a log that tallies error types, and the student can see it too, which is the part that actually changes behaviour in a fifteen-year-old.

There is a second structural advantage in Ajman specifically, and it is about who is available rather than how the lesson runs. A student in Al Zorah or Masfout who needs Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 is unlikely to find that specialist within a drivable evening radius. Over video, distance stops being the filter. The constraint becomes whether the tutor has marked the component, which is the right constraint, and the one that a family can actually check.

The honest counterweight needs stating early. A screen is worse for a younger child who needs an adult in the room to stay on task at all. It needs a quiet space and a connection that holds through the evening, which is harder in a shared Corniche apartment than in a villa. It needs a way for the tutor to see handwritten working, because maths and physics cannot be taught by talking. Where those conditions cannot be met, in-home tuition from a local provider is the better purchase, and we would rather say that than sell around it. Those four conditions are worth checking before the first session rather than after the third, because every one of them is cheap to fix in advance and expensive to discover in week three, when a month has gone and nothing has been produced.

What IB Gram offers in the UAE is one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; those exist only in India. Nothing here involves a promised grade either. What is committed to is the record, the review dates and an honest recommendation at week six, including a recommendation to stop if the evidence says the problem is not one a tutor can fix.

sections.heading: What an online IGCSE session produces that a kitchen-table one does not
paragraphs: Start with the artefacts rather than the atmosphere. A video session with a shared screen, a shared document and a digital annotation layer generates a set of files as a by-product of how it works. The annotated script exists because the marking happened on screen. The error tally exists because the annotations are categorised. The raw-mark log exists because the marks were entered as they were awarded. None of that requires extra admin from the tutor, which is why it actually happens.

A session at a table produces the same teaching and almost none of the record. The marking lives in a notebook that goes back in a bag. The diagnosis lives in a two-minute conversation at the door, usually with whichever parent is home. The pattern across fourteen sessions lives nowhere at all. That is not a criticism of in-home tutors as teachers; it is an observation about what the format leaves behind, and it is the thing that matters most in March when somebody has to decide which topics get the last four weeks.

For a parent in Ajman who is driving back from Dubai during most sessions, the saved record is also the only way to be present. You cannot hover in a doorway at 7.30pm if you are on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. You can read four annotated scripts at eleven o'clock, and you can see in thirty seconds whether the same error type is still being made. That is a better form of oversight than standing in a kitchen pretending to understand a chemistry mark scheme.

sections.heading: Science practicals when the lesson is on a screen: how experimental skill is actually examined
paragraphs: This is the objection every online provider gets and almost none of them answer with specifics. The specifics are reassuring. At IGCSE, experimental skill is examined on paper, not at a bench, on the routes most UAE schools use. On the Cambridge science syllabuses there is a written component that presents the experiment in text and asks the candidate to tabulate, plot, interpret and evaluate. On the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, practical understanding is examined inside the main written papers through questions that describe a method and ask the candidate to improve or critique it.

Read that again, because it determines what tutoring can and cannot do. Nothing in either model requires the candidate to perform an experiment in front of an examiner. What is being tested is the ability to read a method precisely, record data to a consistent number of decimal places, plot a line of best fit with a sensible scale, identify the dominant source of error rather than list every possible one, and write an observation in the language the mark scheme credits. All of those are text and data skills, and all of them are better taught with the data table on a shared screen than on a photocopy.

The school laboratory still matters enormously, and this page is not arguing otherwise. Handling apparatus is how a student builds the physical intuition that makes the written questions make sense, and that belongs in the school's own lessons where the equipment and the supervision are. What a tutor adds is the examination layer on top: which of the student's observations would have earned the mark and which would not. That layer is almost never taught explicitly, which is why it is where the recoverable marks sit.
The table sets out the two assessment models side by side with the specific question of what a screen can and cannot deliver for each. The honest column is the last one.

sections.heading: The setup that makes or breaks a session in an Ajman apartment
paragraphs: Most of what goes wrong with online tutoring is logistics rather than pedagogy, and almost all of it is fixable in one conversation before the first session. The non-negotiable item is a way for the tutor to see the student's handwritten working in mathematics and physics. A webcam pointed at a face is useless for this. A stylus tablet is ideal, a document camera is excellent, and an old phone propped on a stack of books pointing down at an A4 pad works perfectly well and costs nothing.

The second item is a room where the door closes. This is harder in Al Nuaimiya or on the Corniche than in Al Zorah, and it is worth solving rather than tolerating. A student doing algebra in a living room with a television on is losing half of every session, and no tutor can compete with a television. Where no quiet room exists, the better answer is to move the session to a weekend morning rather than to persist with an evening slot that was never going to work.

The third is connection planning rather than connection quality. Evening bandwidth in dense Ajman blocks is shared and it dips. The design response is to make the session survivable rather than to demand perfection: the work lives in a shared document that both sides can see, so a dropped call means thirty seconds of reconnection rather than a lost thread. A phone hotspot should be set up in advance as the routine fallback, not discovered as an emergency in week three.

The fourth is less obvious. Agree who is in the room. A parent sitting in on the first session is useful. A parent sitting in on every session usually produces a student who performs for the parent rather than works, and the error tally stops being honest. The arrangement that works is parental access without parental presence: you can join any session unannounced, and the normal pattern is that you read the record instead.

sections.heading: Verifying the person on the screen
paragraphs: Distance delivery removes geography as a constraint and puts the burden on verification instead, which is a fair trade as long as the verification is real. There are four things a family in Ajman can check, and all four are reasonable to ask for before a paid session.

First, the permit position. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page for private tutor licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. A provider should be able to tell you plainly how the permit position applies to the person teaching your child.

Second, the component. Ask which syllabus code and which paper the tutor has marked, and ask for a redacted sample of that marking. This filter removes more unsuitable tutors than any qualification check, because teaching a subject and marking a specific component are different competencies and only the second one predicts whether your child's technique improves. Third, the limits on assessed work: a tutor explains criteria and marks the student's own draft, and nothing is supplied for submission. Fourth, examiner claims. If somebody is presented as an examiner, ask for evidence of current status, and treat any suggestion that examiner status brings access to boundaries or paper content as a reason to walk away.

One more thing worth knowing. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That rule is press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it directly if it is material to you, but the principle is sound everywhere: your child's own classroom teacher, privately, is not the arrangement to seek.

sections.heading: The things a screen does worse, said plainly
paragraphs: A page that lists only advantages is advertising. There are four real weaknesses in video delivery and a family deciding between formats deserves them stated as clearly as the benefits.

The first is age. A nine or ten-year-old frequently needs an adult physically present to stay on task, and a screen cannot supply that. The second is specific learning differences and attentional difficulty: some students work substantially better with a person beside them, and that is not a motivation problem to be solved with a better platform. The third is physical practical work, which belongs in the school laboratory and cannot be replicated at a desk. The fourth is the household itself: a student with no quiet space and an unstable evening connection will have a worse experience over video than at a table with a tutor, regardless of who the tutor is.

Where any of those apply, the better purchase is in-home tuition from a local Ajman or Sharjah provider, and we would rather tell you that at the enquiry stage than take a month's fees first. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so there is no version of our service that solves those four problems, and pretending otherwise would waste your time and your money.

What video does well is narrow and valuable: it reaches specialists regardless of distance, it generates a record as a by-product, it absorbs a late arrival from Dubai without renegotiating anything, and it is well matched to the way IGCSE actually examines experimental skill. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student with a quiet room, a writing surface and a specific component problem, that combination is hard to beat in the northern emirates. For a Year 5 child who will not sit still, it is the wrong product.

sections.heading: Where an online-taught candidate actually sits the examination
paragraphs: Tutoring format and examination arrangements are separate questions, and families reasonably confuse them. Being taught over video changes nothing about where or how the papers are sat. A student enrolled at a school in Ajman, Sharjah or Dubai sits the papers at the school as an internal candidate, entered by the school's exams officer, on the school's timetable, exactly as they would if they had no tutor at all.

The position differs for a private candidate: someone resitting a single subject, someone being educated at home, or someone adding a subject their school does not offer. A private candidate must be entered through an approved examination centre, and centres set their own administrative charges in addition to the board's entry fee. Those arrangements have to be made well in advance, because entries close months before the papers rather than weeks.

One overseas-specific detail is worth repeating whichever route applies. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, so the live PDF on the board's own site is the only safe source for a date. Any revision plan counted backwards from the wrong set of dates is wrong by the same margin.

A tutor's role in all of this is limited and should be stated as such. We can tell you what questions to ask the exams officer and what the published board guidance says. We cannot enter a candidate, cannot act as a centre, and do not perform or guarantee any part of an entry or equivalency process. Anybody suggesting otherwise is overstating what a tutoring service is.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside an IGCSE programme
paragraphs: This is the gap in the whole UAE tutoring search. No competitor page in the researched set treats the mandatory UAE subjects as anything more than a chip in a subject list, and yet they occupy real timetable hours in every private school in the country and appear on real reports. For an Ajman family planning tuition around a child's week, that matters practically.

The federal position is the starting point: private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the Ministry of Education's supervision, so that federal baseline is the frame your child's school works within. Dubai schools sit under KHDA, and a child commuting from Ajman into a Dubai school will be subject to KHDA's own detailed requirements rather than to anything set in Ajman.

Those KHDA requirements are worth knowing for the cross-border families, because they are specific and they are published. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. KHDA also requires that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited.

The practical consequence for a tutoring plan is twofold. First, those lessons consume hours, so a realistic weekly plan has fewer slots in it than a parent assumes. Second, the content rule means any support in these subjects has to work from the school's own prescribed material rather than from an invented scheme of work. And note the separate point for equivalency: on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required GCSE or IGCSE subjects.

sections.heading: Six weeks of online tutoring: what should exist at the end of it
paragraphs: Six weeks is the right review point because it is long enough to produce comparable data and short enough that a wrong decision has not cost much. By then the shared folder should contain roughly six annotated question sets, two timed attempts marked against the published scheme, an error tally with category counts, and a written review that takes a position.

The test to apply is simple and unsentimental. Compare the error tally in week one with the tally in week six. If the same categories dominate at the same frequency, the sessions have been delivering content rather than correcting technique, and the plan is wrong regardless of how pleasant the sessions have been. If the categories have shifted, the plan is working and the next question is only about rate: how many sessions for the remaining items, and on what basis is that estimate made.

There is a third possible outcome and it should be named out loud. Sometimes six weeks of evidence shows that the barrier is not academic at all. A student arriving at a session exhausted at 7pm after a Sharjah school day and a long drive home is not short of teaching; a student who has not done a single between-session task in six weeks is telling you something about engagement rather than ability. In both cases the right recommendation is to change the schedule or the conversation at home, not to buy more hours.

A provider that cannot describe the circumstances under which you should stop paying is not describing a service. The review at week six exists to make continuing an active decision rather than a default, and for an online arrangement with no travel sunk into it, stopping is genuinely costless on both sides. That is worth something in a market where several providers sell prepaid terms.

process.title: Send the codes and the last script
process.description: Give us the syllabus codes and components from the school's entry statement, plus a photograph of the most recent marked paper or mock script. That script is the most useful document a family owns, and it means the first session starts on your child's actual errors rather than on a general diagnostic.

process.title: Sort the setup in five minutes
process.description: Before the first session, confirm how the tutor will see handwritten working, which room has a door, and what the hotspot fallback is. Five minutes here prevents most of the problems that get blamed on online tutoring, and it costs nothing to arrange.

process.title: Take the free first session
process.description: A full lesson at no cost, spent marking a question set on a shared screen. It produces the first annotated file and the first entries in the error tally. If you go no further, you keep both, and you will know more about the problem than the last report told you.

process.title: Run six weeks with two timed attempts
process.description: Weekly sessions plus two full papers sat alone under timing. The unsupervised attempts are the point: they measure what happens in the hall rather than what happens with an adult nearby, and they are the only comparison worth making.

process.title: Read the review and decide
process.description: At week six, compare the error tally with week one and read the written recommendation. Continue, change the subject focus, fix the schedule, or stop. With no travel sunk into the arrangement, stopping is costless for everyone, which is how it should be.

whyPoints.title: Everything is saved
whyPoints.description: Annotated scripts, the error tally, the raw-mark log and the between-session tasks live in a shared folder you can open at any hour. A parent driving back from Dubai during most sessions can still inspect every one of them afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Marking happens in front of the student
whyPoints.description: Marks are awarded and refused on a shared screen while the student watches, rather than reported afterwards. Watching a mark be withheld for a missing unit teaches more than being told about it later, and it is a thing video does better than paper.

whyPoints.title: The written practical paper is taught properly
whyPoints.description: Experimental-skills components are examined on paper, and we teach them from past papers and data tables. Most students have never had that component taught as a separate skill, which is exactly why marks are sitting there.

whyPoints.title: Distance is not a filter on specialists
whyPoints.description: A student in Masfout, Al Zorah or Emirates City reaches the same Cambridge 0606 or 0478 specialist as one in central Dubai. The constraint becomes whether the tutor has marked the component, which is the right constraint.

whyPoints.title: The weaknesses are stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: Video is worse for younger children, for some attentional profiles, and for any household without a quiet room and a stable line. Where that applies we say so at the enquiry stage and point you to a local in-home provider instead.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Criteria are explained and the student's own drafts are marked against them. No text is supplied for submission and no model answer is handed over to be adapted, which is the boundary IB academic-honesty rules draw and some providers in this market ignore.

faqs.question: Is an online IGCSE tutor as effective as someone sitting next to my child?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on the student rather than on the format. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student with a quiet room and a way for the tutor to see their handwritten working, video is at least as effective and has one clear advantage: the marking is saved, so a pattern across a term is visible rather than remembered. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, or a household with no quiet space and an unstable evening connection, in-home tuition from a local provider is genuinely the better purchase and we will say so.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals taught if the lesson is on a screen?
faqs.answer: On the routes most UAE schools use, experimental skill is examined on paper rather than at a bench. Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 assess it through a written component that presents the experiment in text; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences examine practical understanding inside the main written papers. So what is being tested is tabulating data, plotting a line of best fit, identifying the dominant source of error and writing observations in mark-scheme language. All of that is taught from past papers, with no apparatus on either side. School laboratory work still matters and belongs at school.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child need for an online IGCSE session in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. A laptop or tablet with a working microphone, a room where the door closes, and a way for the tutor to see handwritten working. That last item is the only one people get wrong: a webcam pointed at a face is useless for maths. A stylus tablet is ideal, a document camera is excellent, and an old phone propped on a stack of books pointing down at an A4 pad works perfectly well and costs nothing. A phone hotspot set up in advance covers the evening bandwidth dips common in dense Ajman blocks.

faqs.question: Can I watch an online IGCSE lesson or see a recording of it afterwards?
faqs.answer: You can join any session unannounced, and that access is the point rather than a concession. What we suggest instead, after the first session, is reading the record: the annotated script, the error tally and the between-session task sit in a shared folder you can open at eleven at night. Routine parental presence tends to produce a student who performs for the parent rather than works, which makes the error tally less honest. Access without presence is the arrangement that keeps the evidence usable, and it suits parents who are driving back from Dubai at session time.

faqs.question: How do I verify that an online tutor is permitted to teach in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly how the MoHRE private tuition work permit applies to the person teaching your child. Private tutoring is regulated through a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Then verify the thing that predicts teaching quality: which syllabus code and component the tutor has marked, with a redacted sample.

faqs.question: Our internet in Ajman drops in the evening. Does that ruin a session?
faqs.answer: Not if the session is designed for it. Evening bandwidth in dense blocks in Al Nuaimiya or on the Corniche is shared and it dips, so the work is held in a shared document that both sides can see rather than only in the video call. A dropped connection then costs about thirty seconds of reconnection instead of the thread of the lesson. Set up a phone hotspot as the routine fallback before the first session rather than discovering you need one in week three. If drops are constant rather than occasional, move the slot to a weekend morning.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's handwritten working over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for mathematics and physics it is the whole requirement. With a stylus tablet the student writes directly into a shared canvas the tutor annotates. With a document camera or a phone on a stand over paper, the tutor sees each line as it is written and can stop a wrong method at the second step rather than after five minutes of commitment to it. The script is then saved as a file and sent. That is better than paper in one specific respect: the annotated version still exists in April.

faqs.question: Where does an online-taught IGCSE student actually sit the exams?
faqs.answer: Exactly where they would have anyway. A student enrolled at a school in Ajman, Sharjah or Dubai sits the papers at the school as an internal candidate, entered by the exams officer on the school's timetable. Tutoring format changes nothing about it. A private candidate, meaning a resit, a home-educated student or someone adding a subject the school does not offer, must be entered through an approved examination centre, and centres set their own administrative charge on top of the board's entry fee. Those arrangements are made months ahead, because entries close long before the papers.

faqs.question: Does my child still need Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, in some form. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Ajman, private schools sit under Ministry of Education supervision; a child commuting into a Dubai school falls under KHDA's own detailed requirements, which mandate Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Those lessons consume weekly hours, so a tutoring timetable has fewer free slots than parents assume. Note that Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track equivalency.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a poor fit for a child who is easily distracted?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be tested rather than assumed. A screen gives a distractible student other tabs, and no tutor can compete with a phone face-up on the desk. The practical mitigations are real: a shorter session, a shared document that shows whether anything is being written, and a rule that the phone is in another room. What does not work is persisting with an evening slot in a room with a television on. If six weeks of evidence shows nothing is being produced between sessions, the honest recommendation is to change the format rather than buy more hours.

faqs.question: How long should an online IGCSE session be for a Year 10 student?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for technique drills, ninety where a full structured paper is being worked through, because an attempt and its marking cannot both fit into an hour. Beyond ninety minutes attention degrades for most fifteen-year-olds on a screen, and two shorter sessions in a week usually beat one long one for retention. In Ajman the practical limit is often the clock rather than the attention span: a session that cannot start until 8.30pm because the Dubai commute ran late should be sixty minutes, not ninety.

faqs.question: Can one online tutor cover both Cambridge and Edexcel science papers?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked explicitly rather than assumed. The science content overlaps heavily, but the assessment models differ in a way that changes teaching. Cambridge examines experimental skill through a written component on the alternative route; Edexcel embeds practical understanding inside the main written papers. A tutor who has marked only one model will prepare your child for a paper that will not be set. Ask which codes they have marked, 0620 and 0625 or 4CH1 and 4PH1, and ask for a redacted marked sample from each one they claim.

faqs.question: What should six weeks of online IGCSE tutoring have produced?
faqs.answer: A shared folder containing roughly six annotated question sets, two full papers sat alone under exam timing and marked against the published scheme, an error tally with category counts, and a written review that takes a position. The test is to compare the tally at week six with week one. If the same categories dominate at the same frequency, the sessions delivered content rather than corrected technique and the plan needs changing. If they have shifted, the only remaining question is the rate of progress and the estimate for what is left.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor need to know which Ajman school my child attends?
faqs.answer: Yes, for three specific reasons rather than as small talk. The school determines the exam board and the components entered, which decides what is practised. It determines the internal deadline calendar for any coursework, which decides the order work is done in. And it determines the school day, which decides what time a session can realistically start: a child at a school in Sharjah or Dubai gets home materially later than one at a school in Al Nuaimiya. None of that requires any contact with the school, and no relationship with any school is implied.

faqs.question: Can online sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they normally should. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the useful part of a student's evening shifts late, so holding a 6.30pm slot through the month tends to produce sessions nobody gets anything from. The usual arrangement is to move to a post-Iftar slot for the month, or to shift to a daytime weekend session instead. Because delivery is over live video with no travel involved, moving a session costs nothing to anyone and needs no notice beyond the courtesy of asking. Revision planning around the month is agreed in advance rather than improvised.

ajman/igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Send a mock script and see what the first session finds
ajman/igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing you can send is a photograph of your child's most recent marked paper, along with the syllabus codes from the school's entry statement. The first session is free, runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and is spent marking a question set on a shared screen rather than on introductions. You keep the annotated file and the first error tally whatever you decide afterwards. At week six you compare the tally with week one and take a decision, and because there is no travel sunk into the arrangement, stopping costs nothing.

ajman/igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the IGCSE subjects Ajman families ask about most: the two maths routes, the three separate sciences, and first-language English. Each card names the boards and the papers that tutor marks. Ask to see a marked sample from a previous student before you book any paid block of lessons.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Ajman is actually being hired to fix
paragraphs: Most families in Al Nuaimiya or Al Mowaihat start looking after a Year 10 report where the predicted grade slipped a band and nobody explained why. The usual cause is not that the child stopped working. It is that answers are being written in the wrong register for the mark scheme: a four-mark explain question answered as a two-mark state, a correct calculation handed in without its unit, a six-mark extended response in biology that lists true facts and never links them in the order the examiner credits. That is a diagnosable fault with a name, and faults with names get fixed in weeks rather than years.

So this page is built around what a session leaves behind rather than what it promises. A lesson that produces no artefact cannot be checked by you, by the school, or by the student in April when the revision actually matters. After a session here there is a scanned question with ticks and crosses on it, a line in the log that says what the raw mark was, and one sentence on what to practise before the next one. Three weeks of that is enough for a parent to decide whether to continue, and it is the only honest basis for that decision.

Ajman geography shapes the timetable more than anything else on this page. A large share of parents in Al Rashidiya, Al Jurf and Emirates City work in Dubai or Sharjah, and the drive back along Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road does not reliably finish before seven in the evening. A 4pm slot that works for an Abu Dhabi villa is unusable here. Sessions for Ajman students are normally set between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays, with Saturday and Sunday mornings held for paper practice under timed conditions, because a timed paper needs a quiet house.

The board mix matters too. Ajman schools run both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a number of Ajman children sit in Sharjah or Dubai classrooms, which widens the mix again. The papers are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers its candidates into Core and Extended with different paper pairs; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 tiers as Foundation and Higher. A tutor who does not ask for the syllabus code on the front of your child's exam entry is guessing, and guessing shows up as practice on questions that will never be set.

One thing to settle before you read further. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Ajman, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Nothing on this page promises a grade either. A tutor can teach technique, mark work honestly and keep a record, and no tutor can commit to a number on a results slip. If a provider quotes you one, that is the moment to close the tab.

ajman/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four routes cover almost every Ajman student who arrives here. Which one applies is decided by the school's entry policy and by the tier your child was placed in at the start of Year 10, not by preference.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: The Core tier covers a reduced subject content and caps the attainable grade at C in most syllabuses. In Mathematics 0580 that means Papers 1 and 3; in the sciences it narrows the supplement content out of the specification. Students placed in Core who are tracking a B or above need a tier review with the school early in Year 10, because a late move is an entry change rather than a teaching change.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman schools place Core candidates for different reasons: some to protect a predicted grade, some because the cohort is large and the set structure is fixed. If your child needs Extended for a sixth-form entry requirement in Sharjah or Dubai, raise it in the autumn term. By the November final-entry window the decision has effectively been made for you.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended carries the supplement content and the full grade range to A*. In Mathematics 0580 the papers are 2 and 4, with Paper 4 the longer structured paper where the multi-step questions sit. In the sciences the Extended papers reward chains of reasoning rather than recall, which is exactly where a strong Core student stalls when moved up without retraining.
programmes.countryNote: Extended is the tier most Ajman families eventually want, because the A-Level and IB Diploma entry criteria used by schools in Sharjah and Dubai are written in grades the Core tier cannot reach. The honest timeline is two terms of retraining, not two weeks, and the first evidence of it is a raw-mark rise on structured questions rather than on multiple choice.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Edexcel's International GCSE suite uses 4-prefixed codes: Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Tiering is Foundation and Higher. Assessment is written throughout, with practical skills examined on paper rather than in a laboratory, and the question style leans harder on structured calculation than its Cambridge equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year, and releases provisional timetables ahead of each series. For an Ajman family that matters in one specific way: a November entry gives a Year 11 student a genuine second attempt without losing a year, and the entry window for it closes long before the revision panic starts.

programmes.name: IGCSE to Diploma or A-Level bridging
programmes.description: The gap between a strong IGCSE grade and a comfortable first term of DP or A-Level is mostly about independence: reading a syllabus, planning a written response without a scaffold, and handling content that is introduced once rather than revisited. Bridging work in July and August is short, specific and far cheaper than repair work in November.
programmes.countryNote: Ajman students moving into sixth form often change school and emirate at the same time, which adds a commute and a new set of deadlines to an already steep term. Starting the bridge in the summer, while the family is still on an Ajman schedule, removes one variable from a transition that already has too many.

ajman/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Ajman parents ask about by name, with the syllabus code and the place marks are most often lost. A tutor should be able to tell you the second part before you book.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Paper 4 and the Higher papers punish method gaps rather than arithmetic. Marks go on unrounded intermediate values, missing units, and ignoring the instruction to show working on a question worth four or more marks. Practice is scored against the mark scheme, so the student sees exactly which line earned nothing.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by Ajman students heading for Maths AA HL or A-Level Mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities carry most of the difficulty, and the common loss is treating a proof as a calculation. Working is the answer here; a correct final value with no derivation attracts very little credit.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest spread of marks in any Ajman cohort. Students lose marks by describing a circuit instead of explaining it, and by writing formulae without defining the symbols. Paper 6 on the Cambridge route tests experimental skills in writing, which is a separate technique from the physics itself.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways are where the grade is decided. The recurring fault is answering a why question with a what answer. On the Cambridge route the alternative-to-practical paper rewards precise observation language, which students never practise unless someone makes them.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content feels manageable and the marks are hard. Extended response questions want linked reasoning in sequence, and lists of true statements score badly. Data questions need the figure quoted from the graph, not a paraphrase of the trend, and that single habit moves several marks per paper.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the comparative reading tasks reward structure over vocabulary. Marks are lost on audience and register, and on summaries that retell rather than compress. Sessions are built on timed writing with the mark scheme bands read aloud, so the student learns what a band boundary actually sounds like.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A large share of Ajman candidates sit this rather than 0500, and the two are marked on different criteria. The reading tasks reward exact lifting where the question allows it, and the writing tasks reward task fulfilment ahead of complexity. Over-ambitious sentences that collapse mid-clause cost more than simple ones that land.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application to the case study is the whole examination. Generic answers about motivation or cash flow score in the lowest band however accurate they are. The technique is to quote the stimulus, apply one concept, and evaluate with a reasoned judgement, in that order, every time.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that students leave on the table: axes unlabelled, no title, shifts drawn without an arrow or a reason. The evaluation marks on the longer questions need a stated condition, and answers that argue one side only cap well below the top band.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory on data representation and networks is learnable quickly; Paper 2 algorithm design is not. Pseudocode loses marks for undeclared variables and untraceable loops. Trace tables are practised until they are boring, because they are the single most reliable source of marks on that paper.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity decides the grade. Named places, figures and dates earn credit; a general description of coastal erosion does not. Skills questions on maps and graphs are the cheapest marks on the paper and the most commonly dropped through rushing.

subjects.name: Accounting (Cambridge 0452)
subjects.description: Format discipline is most of it. Marks follow correct headings, dates and the right side of the ledger, and a single misposting can cascade through a whole question. Practice is done under time, because speed is the constraint that actually decides this paper.

ajman/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Ajman is compact, and the difference between one community and the next is mostly about which school run the family does and how far into the evening the working parent gets home. Both change what time a session can realistically start.

regions.note: Mixed low-rise and apartment blocks near the Ajman city core. Families here often have two children on different curricula in different schools, so sibling sessions are staggered rather than stacked back to back.

regions.name: Al Mowaihat
regions.note: Villa communities spread across Mowaihat 1, 2 and 3, with Dubai and Sharjah commutes for a large share of households. Weekend morning paper practice works better here than a rushed weekday slot.

regions.name: Al Zahya and Al Tallah
regions.note: Newer developments along the Emirates Road corridor, which puts several Sharjah and Dubai schools within reach. These households are the most likely to be running a Cambridge and an Edexcel child at the same time.

regions.name: Al Helio and Al Rawda
regions.note: Established residential areas with a strong local school cluster. Short journeys make a second weekly session practical, which matters most in the term before a November entry.

regions.note: Apartment living near the seafront, often with shared study space and noise through the evening. Timed paper practice is scheduled for weekend mornings here as a matter of course.

modes.title: Timed paper clinic
modes.description: A weekend block in which the student sits a past paper under exam timing with no help, and the session that follows is spent only on the marking. No teaching happens during the attempt. This separates two things families usually blur together: whether the content is known, and whether it can be produced in the time allowed. Most grade losses in an Ajman mock season turn out to be the second problem.
bullets: Full paper under official timing, usually Saturday or Sunday morning
Marked against the published mark scheme, question by question
Error log categorised as content, technique, timing or reading the question
Repeat attempt on a parallel paper three to four weeks later for comparison

modes.title: Pre-entry sprint
modes.description: A short, dated block in the weeks before a November or June series, aimed at a specific paper rather than a subject. It assumes the content is broadly in place and that the problem is execution under pressure. It is the only format with a fixed end point, which is deliberate: a sprint that drifts into a permanent arrangement has stopped being a sprint and the family should be told so.
bullets: Fixed number of sessions with a stated finish date before the paper
Topic selection driven by the error log, not by the syllabus order
Command-word drills on the question types that paper repeats
Closing report listing what was fixed and what was left unaddressed

sections.heading: The marking record: what a tutoring session should leave behind
paragraphs: A session in Ajman should produce a paper trail you can read in five minutes. That means a specific list: the question attempted with its paper and year, the mark awarded out of the mark available, the mark-scheme point that was missed, and one named task to do before the next session. Nothing about that is unusual in a school department. It is unusual in private tutoring, where the normal output is a verbal reassurance at the end of an hour and an invoice at the end of the month.

The reason to insist on it is not bureaucracy. It is that grades move through accumulated small corrections, and small corrections are invisible unless they are written down. A student who stops dropping unit marks in Physics 0625 has gained perhaps three marks a paper. Nobody notices three marks in a conversation. Everybody notices it in a log that shows the same error type falling from six instances to one across four papers, and that log is also what persuades a sceptical fifteen-year-old that the hour is worth attending.

It also protects you as the person paying. With a record, the week-six decision is a reading exercise. Without one, it is a judgement about whether you like the tutor. Those are different questions and only the first one has an answer. If a provider in the UAE market cannot show you a redacted sample of this record from a previous student before you pay, that tells you what their sessions produce, and the answer is nothing you can audit.
The table below is the full artefact list. A parent should be able to ask for any row and receive it the same evening.
bullets: Ask for a redacted sample record from a previous student before the first paid session
Expect the paper, year and question number, not just a topic name
A raw mark out of the available mark, every time, not a percentage
One named task between sessions, with the paper reference attached

rows: Which mark-scheme points were earned and which were missed
Tutor, during the session on a shared screen

sections.heading: Command words in a Cambridge IGCSE paper, and the marks attached to each
paragraphs: Every Cambridge IGCSE question opens with an instruction, and that instruction is a contract about what will be credited. Students who read the instruction as a general invitation to write about the topic lose marks they already know the content for. This is the cheapest fault to fix in the whole examination and the one least often addressed in a normal school lesson, because a class of twenty-eight cannot be marked line by line every week.

The pattern repeats across subjects. State wants a fact and nothing else, and a student who explains it has spent three minutes earning one mark. Explain wants a reason with a mechanism, and a student who states it has written a true sentence that scores nothing. Describe wants the what; account for and justify want the why with a stated criterion. Compare wants both sides and an explicit linking word, and a paragraph on one side followed by a paragraph on the other does not count as a comparison in several mark schemes.

Drilling this is dull and effective. The method is to take six questions from past papers with different command words, cover the body of each, and have the student say what the examiner will credit before writing a word. Ten minutes a week for a term, and the habit sticks. The table sets out the command words that appear most often in Ajman students' papers across Mathematics, the sciences and the humanities, with the shape of the answer that loses the mark.

One caution on sources. Mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to the board and should be read on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a photocopy circulating on a parents group. Boards revise wording between series, and a two-year-old handout is a reliable way to practise the wrong thing.

table.caption: COMMAND WORDS AND THE ANSWER THAT LOSES THE MARK
rows: A single correct fact, no reasoning required
A paragraph of explanation around a fact that was never stated plainly
Observable features or a sequence of what happens
Reasons why it happens, with the description assumed
A reason with a mechanism or causal link
A restatement of the observation in different words
Method shown, then the value with its unit

Both subjects addressed with an explicit linking word
A paragraph on one, then a paragraph on the other, never joined
A plausible answer applied to the unfamiliar context given
A textbook answer that ignores the stimulus entirely
A judgement supported by a stated criterion
A one-sided argument with no criterion and no conclusion

sections.heading: Raw marks, not percentages: how an IGCSE grade actually moves
paragraphs: Parents are given percentages by schools and grades by boards, and neither tells you where the next improvement comes from. Raw marks do. A structured paper worth 130 marks does not reward effort evenly: some question types return a mark per thirty seconds of work and others return nothing for five minutes of writing. Knowing which is which is most of what a good revision plan is.

Work the arithmetic through with the student and the conversation changes. If the Extended maths paper carries around a third of its marks on multi-step structured questions, and the student is routinely losing the final accuracy mark on those, that is a recoverable block of marks sitting in a habit rather than in missing knowledge. Fixing it takes a fortnight of marked practice. Learning a new topic takes a term. Any revision plan that does not sort the student's losses into those two buckets first is spending the expensive weeks on the cheap problems.

Grade boundaries themselves move between series and are published by the board after marking, so nobody can tell you in advance how many marks a grade will cost. That is a reason to work in raw marks rather than predictions, not a reason to avoid the question. The useful framing for an Ajman family is simple: here is the paper, here is where your marks went last time, here is the cheapest block of marks to recover, and here is how many sessions that block realistically takes.

The log makes this visible without anybody needing to believe a claim. Four marked attempts at comparable questions, with the error types tallied, will show whether the cheap block is actually closing. If it is not, the plan was wrong and should change at week six rather than in March.
bullets: Sort losses into content gaps and technique gaps before planning any revision
Technique gaps usually close in two to three weeks of marked practice
Content gaps take a term, so they are started first and reviewed last
Never plan against a predicted boundary; plan against marks on the page

sections.heading: Six weeks, twelve weeks, a full year: what progress looks like on paper
paragraphs: Families ask how long this takes, and the honest answer depends entirely on which of the two problems the student has. Technique faults respond quickly and visibly. Missing content from Year 9 and the first half of Year 10 does not, and anyone who says otherwise is selling. What can be promised is a reporting rhythm, so that by a known date you have enough information to make a decision rather than a guess.

The first block is diagnostic. Three to six sessions, each producing a marked artefact, is usually enough to say what kind of problem this is and roughly how big it is. At the end of it there is a written review that takes a position: continue on this subject, switch the focus to a different paper, add a second subject, or stop because the issue is organisational rather than academic and a tutor is the wrong purchase.

The second block is where marks move. Twelve weeks of weekly sessions with a timed paper every three to four weeks produces four comparable data points, which is the minimum needed to distinguish a trend from a good day. Over a full academic year the pattern changes shape: content coverage through the autumn, technique through the spring, and a dated sprint on specific papers in the final weeks before the series the student is entered for.

The table below sets out what each block produces and what you can fairly judge at the end of it. The last column is the point of the whole exercise, because a block that does not support a decision is just an expense with a timetable.
