sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: finding out which paper your child will actually sit
paragraphs: This sounds like administration and it decides whether the practice is useful. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both operate widely in the northern emirates, and an Ajman student can easily be sitting Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and Edexcel Physics 4PH1 in the same series if the school has mixed its entries by department. Practising Cambridge Paper 6 experimental technique for an Edexcel candidate is wasted time that felt productive.

The document that settles it is the exam entry statement the school issues, which lists the syllabus code and the components. Ask the exams officer for it rather than relying on what the textbook cover says, because schools change boards and old books stay on shelves. The code is the thing to write down: 0580, 0620, 0625, 0610, 0500 on the Cambridge side; 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1, 4EA1 on the Edexcel side.

The differences are concrete enough to change a revision plan. Cambridge tiers Core and Extended with separate paper pairs and assesses experimental skills through a written alternative-to-practical component on several science syllabuses. Edexcel tiers Foundation and Higher and examines practical understanding inside the main written papers. Question styles differ too: Edexcel structured calculations tend to be longer with more steps carried forward, so an arithmetic slip early costs more.

Once the code is known, everything else on this page becomes specific. The command-word drills come from that board's papers, the timed clinics use that board's timing, and the error log is kept against that board's mark scheme wording. A tutor who never asks for the code is marking against the wrong rubric, and the student is the one who finds out in June.
bullets: Ask the school exams officer for the entry statement, not the textbook cover
Write down the syllabus code for every subject, including the component numbers
Check whether the science route uses a written practical paper or embeds it
Confirm the tier in writing before the final entry window closes

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, timetable zones and the dates that are genuinely fixed
paragraphs: The single most useful administrative fact for a UAE family is that entries close months before the exams. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 series shows the shape clearly, and it is a series an Ajman student can actually sit: the written papers run from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in the January that follows, the way November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026. Count backwards from a late-October first paper and the entry window, the centre fees and the decision to add a subject or move tier all fall in the summer before it, not in the term the exam sits in. Cambridge's UAE sessions carry the same lag. Entries for the June series close in the spring, several months ahead of the first paper, and the exact date for your centre is printed on the statement of entry the school issues rather than being something to guess at from a search result. The practical rule for a family here is to treat the entry deadline, not the exam, as the date that ends the planning window.

Cambridge runs its main IGCSE and O Level examining in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

There is a trap specific to overseas centres that is worth knowing. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Cambridge also says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For an Ajman family that means one thing: get the zone from the school, and read the dates off the timetable for that zone rather than off a page found by searching.

IB Diploma dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date here is confirmed from the IB, and publishing an unverified date on a page parents plan around would be worse than publishing nothing. For any Diploma date, ask the school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly.
bullets: Final entries close months ahead of the papers, so tier changes are an autumn decision
Confirm your centre's Cambridge administrative zone and use that timetable version
Pearson publishes provisional timetables before each series; read the live PDF
Treat any IB date not confirmed by the school coordinator as unverified

sections.heading: Coursework, practical papers and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry assessed work produced outside an examination hall, and the rules around it are not negotiable. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, and give feedback on the student's own finished draft. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a piece so that the authorship changes, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The student is the author of every word submitted, and the signature on the authentication form says so.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the UAE market contains providers that sell finished assessed work outright. One of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying that puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding that can cost the whole qualification, and it puts the family in the position of having paid for the risk. There is no version of this that is a shortcut; it is a different and worse outcome bought at a premium.

The practical components are a related question and a cleaner one. On the Cambridge science route, experimental skills on several syllabuses are assessed through a written paper rather than in a laboratory, which means the technique being tested is reading an experimental description, handling data and writing precise observations. That is teachable over video without any apparatus at all, and it is one of the places where online delivery is simply not at a disadvantage.

What a tutor can legitimately do with assessed work is still substantial: unpick the criteria in the student's own words, mark a draft the student wrote against those criteria, ask the questions that expose a weak argument, and hold the student to a timetable. That is the whole job, and done properly it is more useful than the alternative on offer.
bullets: Criteria explained, drafts marked, feedback given on the student's own writing
No model answers supplied for adaptation, and no text written for submission
Written practical papers are taught from past papers and data, not apparatus
Board documents are read on the official site rather than redistributed

sections.heading: The week-six review: four questions to ask, and when to stop
paragraphs: The decision point is week six, and it belongs to the parent rather than the tutor. By then there should be two timed attempts, a handful of marked question sets and an error tally. That is enough to answer four questions, and if any of them cannot be answered from the record, the record is the problem.

First: which error types have fallen, and by how much? A tally that looks the same at week six as week one means the sessions are delivering content rather than correcting habits. Second: what is left on the list, and is it content or technique? Third: how many sessions does the tutor estimate for the remaining items, and what is that estimate based on? Fourth, and least comfortable: is a tutor the right purchase at all? Some students at this stage need a study timetable, a sleep schedule or a conversation with the school, and an hour of paid teaching a week will not touch any of those.

Stopping is a legitimate outcome and should be said out loud. A tutor who cannot describe the circumstances in which a family should stop paying is not describing a service, and a provider whose only answer to a plateau is more sessions has an incentive problem. The pre-entry sprint format exists partly for this reason: it has a stated finish date, so continuing is an active decision rather than a default.

For Ajman families there is one practical addition. If the barrier turns out to be scheduling rather than teaching, say so and fix the schedule first. A student who arrives at a 6.30pm session having left Sharjah at 5.45pm is not going to absorb anything, and moving the slot to 8pm is free. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a change of time costs nothing in travel to anyone.
bullets: Which error types fell, and by how much, measured on the tally
What remains, split into content gaps and technique gaps
How many sessions the tutor estimates for the remainder, and on what basis
Whether the real barrier is scheduling, sleep or school communication

process.title: Tell us the codes
process.description: Send the subject list with syllabus codes and components from the school's entry statement, the tier your child is placed in, and the series they are entered for. Two minutes of accurate information here removes the most common cause of wasted sessions, which is practising the wrong board's question style.

process.title: Free first lesson
process.description: A full session at no cost, spent on a past-paper question set rather than on introductions. It produces the first marked artefact and the first entry in the error tally, so even if you go no further you leave with a diagnosis you did not have before.

process.title: Agree the reporting
process.description: Before any paid session, agree in writing what you will receive and when: the marked script within a day, the running raw-mark log, the error tally reviewed every fourth session, and a written review at week six. Reporting that is not agreed up front tends not to happen.

process.title: Run the first block
process.description: Three to six weekly sessions with one timed paper, set at a time that survives the Ajman evening commute. Reschedules inside the block are handled without a charge, because traffic on Emirates Road is not something a family controls.

process.title: Decide at week six
process.description: Read the review and take a position: continue, change the subject focus, add a second subject, or stop. The tutor states a recommendation with reasons, and the recommendation is sometimes to stop. That is the review working rather than failing.

whyPoints.title: The record exists before you pay
whyPoints.description: You can ask for a redacted sample of a previous student's marked script and raw-mark log before committing to any paid block. A provider that cannot produce one is telling you what its sessions generate, and the answer is nothing you can inspect afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Codes before content
whyPoints.description: Every subject is confirmed by syllabus code and component before teaching starts, taken from the school's entry statement rather than assumed. Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 are both chemistry and they are not the same examination.

whyPoints.title: Specialists rather than proximity
whyPoints.description: A student in Masfout or Al Zorah gets the tutor who marks that paper, not the one who lives nearest. Online delivery over live video is what makes that possible, and for the Ajman exclaves it is the only realistic route to a subject specialist.

whyPoints.title: An evening timetable that matches Ajman
whyPoints.description: Slots are set between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays and on weekend mornings for timed papers, because a large share of Ajman parents are driving back from Dubai or Sharjah until well into the evening and a tired student learns nothing.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, in writing
whyPoints.description: No session, block or sprint carries a promised grade, score or improvement figure. What is committed to is the artefact list, the reporting dates and an honest recommendation at week six, including the recommendation to stop.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Criteria are explained and the student's own drafts are marked. No text is supplied for submission and no model answer is handed over for adaptation, which is the line that separates teaching from the malpractice risk sold elsewhere in this market.

faqs.question: How will I know an IGCSE tutor in Ajman is actually making a difference?
faqs.answer: By reading the record rather than asking the tutor. After each session you should receive the marked question script with the mark-scheme points identified, the raw mark out of the mark available, and one named practice task. Every fourth session, the error tally is reviewed, so you can see whether unit losses in Physics or missing working in Mathematics are falling. At week six there is a written review. If error types look the same at week six as at week one, the sessions are delivering content and not correcting habits, and that is a reason to change the plan.

faqs.question: What should a marked past paper from a tutoring session actually look like?
faqs.answer: It should name the paper, the series and the question number, carry ticks against the mark-scheme points earned and crosses against those missed, and show the mark as a raw figure out of the available mark. Alongside it there should be a short note naming the fault in words a fifteen-year-old can act on, such as unit omitted or compare answered as two separate descriptions. A colour-coded sheet with no reference to the mark scheme is decoration. The point of marking is to tell the student which specific line earned nothing.

faqs.question: My son's school in Al Nuaimiya predicts a 5 in Maths. Can that move?
faqs.answer: It can move, and how far depends on which of two problems he has. If the losses are technique, such as unrounded intermediate values, missing units or no working shown on four-mark questions, those usually close within two or three weeks of marked practice. If whole topics from Year 9 and early Year 10 are missing, that is a term of work and it should be started first. Nobody can promise a number on a results slip. What the first three sessions will tell you is which of the two problems this is and roughly how large it is.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE syllabus code should I check before booking anything?
faqs.answer: All of them, taken from the exam entry statement the school issues rather than from a textbook cover. The codes that come up most in Ajman are Mathematics 0580, Additional Mathematics 0606, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, English as a First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511. The code fixes the tier, the papers and the mark scheme a tutor marks against. Without it, practice can be aimed at a component your child is not entered for, which feels productive and achieves nothing.

faqs.question: Is my child's private school in Ajman inspected by KHDA or by somebody else?
faqs.answer: Not by KHDA, which is Dubai's authority. The Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, while Dubai sits under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge. If your child commutes to a school in Sharjah or Dubai, the regulator is the one for the emirate where the school sits, not where you live. That matters when you are looking for a published inspection report.

faqs.question: Do Ajman students sit the November Cambridge series or only the June one?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examining in both a June series and a November series, so November is available where the school enters candidates for it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are likewise available in May or June and in November. Whether your child can use the November window is a school decision about entries, not a board restriction, and it has to be raised early because final entries close months before the papers. For a Year 11 student, a November entry can mean a genuine second attempt without repeating a year.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor keep asking which exam timetable zone our school is in?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. A revision plan counts backwards from real paper dates, so using the wrong zone's dates shifts the whole plan. Get the zone from the school's exams officer and read the dates from the timetable for that zone.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor stop on an IGCSE coursework piece?
faqs.answer: At the point where authorship would change. A tutor can explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, teach the skills the task needs, mark a draft the student wrote and ask the questions that expose a weak argument. A tutor cannot supply sentences for submission, restructure a piece so that the authorship changes, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. The student authors every word submitted and signs an authentication statement to that effect. Providers in this market that sell finished assessed work are selling a malpractice risk at a premium.

faqs.question: We live in Al Mowaihat and both parents work in Dubai. When can lessons run?
faqs.answer: Later than most providers assume. Sessions for Ajman families are normally set between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays, because the drive back along Emirates Road or Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road rarely finishes before seven. Weekend mornings are kept for timed paper practice, which needs a quiet house and a full uninterrupted slot. If a 6.30pm start means your child arrives having left Dubai at 5.45pm, move it to 8pm. Lessons run over live video, so changing the time costs nobody any travel.

faqs.question: Does somebody tutoring privately in Ajman need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE regulates private tutoring through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: For UAE equivalency, how many IGCSE passes does the British track need?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channels before planning around it, and note that tutoring is not a requirement of the process.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE tutoring in Year 11 after the mock results come back?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with the focus narrowed. Mock scripts are the best diagnostic document a family ever gets, because they show performance under timing rather than with help available. In Year 11 the sensible purchase is a dated block aimed at specific papers, built from the mock error log rather than from the syllabus order. Expect technique gains to show first and content gaps to need longer. What you should not buy at this stage is an open-ended arrangement with no finish date, because the calendar has already decided when the work stops.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the free first IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: It is spent on a past-paper question set rather than on introductions. The tutor works through questions on the subject you have flagged, marking against the published mark scheme as the session goes, on a shared screen so the student sees the marking happen. It produces the first marked artefact and the first entries in the error tally. At the end you receive the script, the raw mark and a short written view of what kind of problem this is. If you stop there, you still keep the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can one Ajman IGCSE tutor cover both of my children if they sit different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. A tutor who marks both Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 can reasonably take two maths students, because the subject knowledge transfers even though the papers and mark schemes differ. Across the sciences it is less often sensible, since the written practical components are examined differently on the two routes. Sessions are staggered rather than stacked, because two separate marked records have to come out of them. Tell us both sets of codes at the start and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for the subject and paper we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a date. Some combinations are genuinely thin in this market, particularly Additional Mathematics 0606 and the Edexcel written practical components in a specific term. The options are a wait with an estimated date, a different but related specialist with the limitation stated plainly, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. What does not happen is a general tutor being presented as a specialist for the paper. You would discover that in the marking, and by then a term would have gone.

ajman/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper and decide from there
ajman/igcse-tutor.closingBody: The first lesson is free and it produces something: a marked past-paper question set, a raw mark, and a written view of whether this is a content problem or a technique problem. Send the subject list with syllabus codes from your school's entry statement, say which series your child is entered for, and tell us what time works once the Dubai or Sharjah commute is done. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. At week six you read a written review and decide whether to continue, change the focus, or stop.

intro.heading: Proximity is a filter, and in Ajman it is an expensive one
paragraphs: A near-me search is a request for a shortlist within driving distance. It is a reasonable request and it has a cost that nobody itemises. Every kilometre you add to the requirement removes people from the shortlist, and every person removed raises the price of whoever is left. In a city the size of Ajman, with a specialist pool concentrated towards Sharjah and Dubai, a twenty-minute weekday-evening radius can reduce the field for a specific IGCSE component from a reasonable number of qualified markers to one or none.

The published numbers show the shape of it. An in-home one-to-one visit in the UAE is advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and home-tutor listings at AED 200 to 500. The same calibre of teaching delivered online is published at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. The gap is the drive. In Ajman that gap widens, because the drive is longer than it would be for an equivalent family in Jumeirah.

The second cost is less visible and matters more. Narrowing by distance does not narrow randomly; it narrows against scarcity. The subjects where the local pool is thinnest are precisely the ones where specialist marking matters most: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and the written practical science components. A parent in Al Zahya searching for a nearby 0606 tutor is likely to find either nobody or somebody whose only qualification for the job is being nearby, and the second outcome is worse than the first because it is harder to detect.

There is a third thing worth naming, because it is where the near-me search is actually right. Parents do not usually mean the same street. They mean someone who understands the school system their child is in, who is awake on Gulf Standard Time, who can run a session on a weekday evening in Ajman rather than at a European afternoon, and who knows what a school report from an Ajman private school actually means. All four of those are genuinely important and none of them requires a car. Three of the four are about timezone and context rather than geography.

IB Gram answers this search with one-to-one tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That means we are not the nearby option and do not claim to be. What we are is the option where distance stops filtering the shortlist, so the person teaching your child is chosen on whether they have marked the component rather than on where they parked.

sections.heading: What a twenty-minute radius actually contains in Ajman
paragraphs: Start with the geography, because the geography is the argument. Ajman is compact, but the people who have marked IGCSE papers are not distributed in proportion to where families live. The specialist pool across the northern emirates concentrates towards Sharjah and Dubai, where the schools and the teaching jobs are. So a near-me search run from an Ajman address is, in practice, a search for whoever is willing to drive out from there on a weekday evening.

Drive time rather than distance is what matters, and weekday-evening drive time is a different number from the one a mapping app shows at eleven in the morning. The run between Sharjah and the Ajman communities along Emirates Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road does not reliably clear before seven. A tutor committing to a 7pm session in Al Mowaihat is committing to leaving at six and getting home around nine. That is a three-hour evening for one hour of paid teaching, and only a particular kind of rate makes it rational.

The consequence is a shortlist that is short in a specific direction. It contains people for whom the drive is short, which correlates with living nearby, which does not correlate at all with having marked Cambridge 0606 or Edexcel 4CH1. Parents experience this as a thin market and interpret it as a quality problem. It is a geometry problem: the filter being applied selects on the wrong variable, and the thing being optimised is not the thing that moves marks.

sections.heading: The scarcity premium, subject by subject
paragraphs: Once you accept that a radius filters on drive time, the next question is which subjects that filter damages. The answer is counter-intuitive: it damages the scarce components, not the hard ones. Mathematics 0580 has a deep pool, so a tight radius costs you choice rather than capability. Additional Mathematics 0606 has a shallow pool concentrated towards Dubai, so a tight radius can remove every qualified marker from the list and leave you selecting between people who have not taught the syllabus.

This produces a specific and expensive failure mode. A nearby tutor is engaged for a scarce component at an ordinary rate, teaches the content competently for a term, and never addresses the examination technique the paper is actually testing. Nobody notices until the mock, because content teaching feels like progress and a parent has no way to distinguish it from technique teaching without marked evidence. The money was not wasted exactly; it bought the wrong thing at a fair price.

The filter that fixes this is not geography and not price. It is a redacted marked sample from the specific component, which takes one message to request and about thirty seconds to assess. Either the sample shows mark-scheme points identified against a real paper, or it does not. Applied honestly, that question removes more unsuitable tutors than any other check available to a parent, and it works identically on a nearby tutor and a distant one.

sections.heading: Price per teaching minute, and why the short session only works online
paragraphs: Hourly rates hide something useful. What a family actually buys is teaching minutes, and the proportion of a booking that is teaching varies enormously by format. An in-home visit carries arrival, settling, finding the right notebook and a courteous departure, which can take fifteen minutes out of a sixty-minute booking. A video session starts within thirty seconds of the agreed time because nobody is parking.

That changes which session lengths are viable. A forty-five minute in-home visit is uneconomic for everyone: the tutor cannot justify the drive and the family is paying a large travel share across a small amount of teaching. So the local market sells sixty, ninety and one hundred and twenty minute blocks, and a student whose problem is one recurring error gets sold an hour of general revision because that is the smallest unit on offer.

Online, the short format becomes available, and for narrow technique faults it is often the better buy. Three forty-five minute slots across a fortnight, each with one stated objective, will close a recurring unit-omission or a misread command word faster and at lower total cost than one long weekly session that tries to cover everything. Conversely, the ninety-minute slot is the cheapest per teaching minute and is the right purchase once full papers need to be attempted and marked in the same sitting.

sections.heading: The four things parents mean by near me, and which ones need a car
paragraphs: It is worth unpicking the search term, because most of what it asks for is available without proximity and one part of it genuinely is not. Four things sit inside it.

The first is the timezone and the evening. A tutor who is awake, available and sharp at 7.30pm Gulf Standard Time, after an Ajman school day and a commute, rather than at the end of a European working day. This is real, it matters, and it needs no car; it needs a tutor whose working hours are built around this timezone rather than around another one. The second is school context: someone who knows what an Ajman private school report means, which boards local schools enter, and that a child commuting to Sharjah gets home later. Also real, also available at distance.

The third is responsiveness: being able to reach a person quickly, reschedule without a negotiation, and get an honest answer the same day. Again no car required, and in practice an arrangement with no travel sunk into it reschedules more easily than one where somebody has already left the house. The fourth is the genuine exception: physical presence. A younger child who needs an adult in the room, a student with an attentional profile that works materially better in person, a household with no quiet space or stable connection. For those, nearby is not a proxy for anything. It is the requirement.

So the honest answer to a near-me search is a question back: which of those four do you need? If it is the fourth, a local in-home provider in Ajman or Sharjah is the right purchase and we are not it, because IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. If it is any of the first three, the radius is costing you access to the people who have marked your child's paper, and it is costing you money as well.

sections.heading: Tuition centres: the other thing a near-me search returns
paragraphs: Alongside individual tutors, a local search surfaces tuition centres with premises and a timetable. They are a legitimate and often sensible purchase, and they are a different product from one-to-one in ways worth being explicit about before comparing prices.

A centre sells a paced scheme of work to a small group. That is well matched to a student who is broadly behind across a whole subject and needs the content covered again in order, with the discipline of a fixed weekly slot and other students in the room. It is poorly matched to a student whose content is largely in place and who is losing marks on one component, because a group of eight cannot be redirected to one child's error log however good the teacher is. Paying group rates for an individual problem is as inefficient as paying specialist rates for a fluency gap.

There is a regulatory difference too, and it is useful to know as a consumer. An operation with premises and staff is treated differently from an individual tutor. In Dubai a training institute requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, obtained through initial approval followed by a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Those are two different instruments for two different things, and a provider should be able to say which one applies to them.

To be plain about our own position: IB Gram operates no premises, centre, branch or office in the UAE, holds no regulator or examination-board permit of any kind, and makes no claim to any. Tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video. Any provider in this market implying a regulator endorses them should be asked to produce the permit number, because the permit is a specific document issued for a specific activity.

sections.heading: What a genuinely local tutor gives you that distance cannot
paragraphs: This page has argued hard in one direction, so it should concede properly in the other. There are things a nearby tutor provides that no amount of bandwidth replicates, and a family for whom those things matter should buy locally without apology.

Physical presence is the main one and it is not sentimental. A ten-year-old who will not stay at a desk without an adult beside them is not going to be fixed by a better platform. A student who is genuinely dysregulated by screens, or who has a processing profile that works much better with a person in the room, is in the same position. A tutor who can take a pen out of a child's hand, turn the page, and sit in a short silence while something lands is doing something a camera cannot do, and anyone claiming otherwise is selling.

There are smaller advantages that add up. A local tutor can see the bedroom the homework is attempted in, which is diagnostic in a way a video call is not. They can be handed the actual exercise book rather than a photograph of it. They absorb household context without anybody having to explain it. For a family where the problem is as much organisational as academic, that observational access is worth real money.

The reason this page still argues for video in Ajman is narrower than a general claim about formats. It is that the specific subjects where IGCSE marks are most often recoverable, the scarce components, are the subjects where the local field is emptiest. For Mathematics 0580 with a nearby, well-reviewed tutor who has marked Paper 4, book them. For 0478 Paper 2 from an address in Al Zorah, the nearby option is unlikely to exist, and the honest alternative is a specialist on a screen.

sections.heading: When nothing nearby covers the subject: the fallback, disclosed
paragraphs: No competitor page in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-local delivery behind an overseas phone number. Here is ours, stated before you enquire rather than after.

Some subject and component combinations are genuinely thin even without a distance filter. Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 Paper 2, and the written practical science components at specific times of year are the recurring ones. When no tutor who has marked that component is free, there are exactly three honest responses and we will give you one of them with a date attached.

The first is a wait: a named estimate of when a specialist becomes available, usually at the start of a new teaching block. The second is a related specialist with the limitation stated plainly: a 0580 Extended specialist taking a 0606 student can do real work on calculus technique while being clear about what they have not marked, and you decide whether that trade is worth making. The third is a recommendation to look elsewhere, including at a local Ajman or Sharjah provider or at a tuition centre, which is sometimes simply the right answer.

What does not happen is a general tutor being presented as a specialist. You would find out in the marking, and by then a term would have gone and the window before the series would have closed. The whole value of being told a limit is that it arrives while you still have time to act on it, which is why availability is confirmed before any payment rather than after the first invoice.

sections.heading: Starting this week: what actually has to happen
paragraphs: A near-me search is usually urgent. Something has gone wrong in a report or a mock and the parent wants someone on it now. So here is the realistic timeline rather than a marketing one.

Confirming what is needed takes one message: the subject, the syllabus code and component from the school's entry statement, the tier, and a photograph of the most recent marked script. With that, matching to a tutor who has marked the component is usually a matter of a day or two for mainstream subjects. For the thin combinations above, it can be longer, and you will be told a date rather than kept waiting hopefully.

The first session is free and is spent marking a question set rather than on introductions, so the diagnosis exists at the end of the first hour rather than the third. After that it is billed monthly with no joining fee and nothing prepaid, which matters when the decision is being made quickly: a fast start should not create a long commitment. Sessions sit between 6.30pm and 9.30pm on weekdays, with weekend mornings for timed papers.

What cannot be compressed is the work itself. A technique fault takes two to three weeks of marked practice to close, and a content gap takes a term, and no start date changes those durations. The honest version of urgency is to start the diagnosis immediately so that the fortnight before the mock is spent on the right thing, rather than to promise a speed the examination does not permit.

whyPoints.description: The person teaching your child is chosen on whether they have marked the component rather than on how far they live from Al Jurf. For Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478 that is frequently the difference between a qualified marker and nobody.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 online. The gap is a drive, not a standard of teaching, and in Ajman the drive is longer than it would be in central Dubai.

whyPoints.title: Short sessions become viable
whyPoints.description: A forty-five minute slot is uneconomic for anyone who has to travel, so the local market does not sell it. Without travel it becomes the cheapest way to close a single recurring fault, which is what many students actually need.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist for your component is free, you get a date, a related specialist with the limitation stated plainly, or a referral elsewhere. No competitor in the researched set publishes a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: No premises, no permit claims
whyPoints.description: IB Gram operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE and holds no regulator or examination-board permit of any kind. Centres with premises in Dubai require a KHDA Educational Services Permit; individual tutors require the MoHRE permit. We claim neither.

whyPoints.title: Local is sometimes the right answer
whyPoints.description: For a younger child who needs an adult in the room, or a household with no quiet space or stable connection, in-home tuition from an Ajman or Sharjah provider is better than anything delivered on a screen, and we will say so at the enquiry stage.

faqs.question: What am I really looking for when I search for an IGCSE tutor near me?
faqs.answer: Usually four things bundled together. Somebody awake and sharp on Gulf Standard Time at 7.30pm, somebody who understands what an Ajman school report means and which boards local schools enter, somebody responsive who reschedules without a negotiation, and in some cases somebody physically in the room. The first three need no proximity at all. Only the fourth does, and it matters most for younger children and for students who work materially better with a person beside them. Working out which of the four you actually need is the most useful five minutes you can spend.

faqs.question: How far will a tutor realistically travel inside Ajman on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Less far than the map suggests, because the relevant number is evening drive time rather than distance. A tutor based in Sharjah faces roughly 15 to 25 minutes to Al Nuaimiya, 30 to 45 to Al Mowaihat or Al Zahya, and 35 to 50 to Emirates City in ordinary evening traffic. For one hour of teaching in Al Mowaihat that is about a three-hour evening commitment. Masfout and Manama are an hour or more each way, which means no weekly in-home arrangement there is rational at any rate anybody would pay.

faqs.question: Is there likely to be an IGCSE tutor within walking distance of Al Rawda?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream subject, possibly. Al Rawda and Al Helio have short internal journeys and an established local pool, so Mathematics 0580 or English 0510 may well be covered within a very short radius. For Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 Paper 2 or the written practical science components, almost certainly not: that pool is small across the whole northern emirates and concentrated towards Dubai. The honest check is to ask any walking-distance candidate for a redacted marked sample from the exact component.

faqs.question: Does a nearby tutor cost less than one based further away?
faqs.answer: For an in-home arrangement, yes, because you are paying for less driving. Published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour include travel, and the travel share is larger for Al Mowaihat than for Al Nuaimiya. For online delivery the question disappears entirely, since the published AED 150 to 300 band carries no travel component and the tutor's location is irrelevant to the rate. The place a nearby tutor costs you more is choice: a tight radius removes qualified markers from the list and leaves whoever is near.

faqs.question: Are tuition centres in Ajman cheaper than one-to-one tutoring?
faqs.answer: Per hour, almost always, because the cost is shared across a group. Whether they are cheaper per recovered mark depends entirely on the problem. A centre sells a paced scheme of work, which suits a student broadly behind across a whole subject and benefits from a fixed slot and other students in the room. It suits badly a student whose content is in place and who is losing marks on one component, because a group of eight cannot be redirected to one child's error log however good the teacher.

faqs.question: Do tuition centres in Ajman need a licence to operate?
faqs.answer: An operation with premises and staff is regulated differently from an individual tutor, and the instrument depends on the emirate. In Dubai, a training institute requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, obtained through initial approval followed by a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, with annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. An individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Ask any provider which one applies to them.

faqs.question: Why is there no local tutor for Additional Mathematics 0606 in Ajman?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is small nationally and concentrated where the teaching jobs are, which is Dubai and to a lesser extent Sharjah. 0606 is taken by a minority of candidates, so far fewer teachers have ever marked it than have marked 0580, and those who have tend to be attached to schools that offer it. A twenty-minute evening radius around an Ajman address usually contains none of them. A nearby option offered at a routine rate for 0606 is more likely to be someone who has read the syllabus than someone who has marked the papers.

faqs.question: Is a 45-minute IGCSE session worth booking or too short to be useful?
faqs.answer: It is often the best buy for a narrow problem, and it is almost never available locally. An in-home visit carries arrival, settling and departure overheads that make a short booking uneconomic for the tutor and poor value for the family, so the local market sells sixty minutes and upwards. Without travel, a forty-five minute slot with one stated objective becomes viable, and three of them across a fortnight will usually close a recurring unit omission or a misread command word faster and cheaper than one long weekly session covering everything.

faqs.question: Is a tutor from my child's own school an advantage or a conflict?
faqs.answer: No, and in some emirates it is specifically prohibited. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition permit also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than read from the current policy text, so verify it if it is material, but the principle holds everywhere. It is a conflict of interest for assessment and predicted grades, and it is not an arrangement to seek out.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest way to get IGCSE help in Ajman this term?
faqs.answer: In order of headline cost: a tuition centre group class, then a budget online tutor at the published AED 45 to 150 band, then a shared session split with another child in the same community, then one-to-one online at AED 150 to 300, then an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500. Cheapest per hour and cheapest per recovered mark are different questions though. For a Year 9 fluency gap the budget band is genuinely right. For a Year 11 component fault it buys somebody who has not marked the paper, which costs more in the end.

faqs.question: Does a nearby tutor understand the Ajman school system any better?
faqs.answer: Not inherently. What matters is whether they know which boards local schools enter, what an Ajman private school report contains, that private schools here sit under Ministry of Education supervision rather than KHDA or SPEA, and that a child enrolled in Sharjah or Dubai gets home materially later. All of that is knowledge rather than proximity. A tutor living three streets away who has never asked for a syllabus code knows less about your child's examination than one in another emirate who asked for it first.

faqs.question: Can I share a local tutor with a neighbour's child to split the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, and check three things before you do. Both children should be on the same board, the same subject and a similar level, or the session becomes two half-sessions at a discount. The commonest failure in Ajman villa communities is one child entered for Cambridge 0580 and the other for Edexcel 4MA1, where the papers and mark schemes differ enough that neither gets a full hour. Also agree who receives the marked work, because two children need two separate records and shared arrangements tend to produce one vague summary.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor near Ajman teaches the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You should be told, with a date, before any money changes hands. Thin combinations recur: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 Paper 2, and the written practical science papers at certain points in the year. The three honest responses are a wait with a named estimate, a related specialist with the limitation stated plainly so you can decide whether the trade is worth it, or a referral elsewhere including to a local provider or a centre. What should not happen is a general tutor presented as a specialist for a component they have never marked.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying more for a Dubai-based tutor than an Ajman one?
faqs.answer: Only if the Dubai tutor has marked the component and the Ajman one has not, and for scarce subjects that is frequently the case. Location itself is worth nothing. Marking experience on the exact paper is worth a great deal, because teaching a subject and training examination technique are different competencies and only the second moves marks on a structured paper. If delivery is over video the question collapses anyway: there is no travel in the rate, so a Dubai-based tutor costs the same as one next door and the choice is made purely on the component.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start if we decide tonight?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects, usually within a day or two once we have the syllabus code, the component, the tier and a photograph of the most recent marked script. For the thin combinations it takes longer and you get a date rather than a hopeful wait. The first session is free and is spent marking a question set, so the diagnosis exists after the first hour. What cannot be accelerated is the work: a technique fault needs two to three weeks of marked practice and a content gap needs a term, whatever date you start.

ajman/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Say which kind of near you actually need
ajman/igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If the requirement is an adult physically in the room, a local Ajman or Sharjah in-home provider is the right purchase and we will tell you so, because IB Gram delivers only over live video in the UAE. If the requirement is the same timezone, real school context, a weekday evening slot and a tutor who has marked your child's component, then the radius is costing you both choice and money. Send the syllabus codes and the most recent marked script, take the free first session, and decide from the evidence it produces.

al-ain.tutorsIntro: These are the subject specialists Al Ain families ask for most: Diploma Programme sciences at Higher Level, Mathematics AA and AI, and Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE sciences. Each one teaches a named syllabus and has marked or taught the exact paper your child will sit, not a general version of the subject.

intro.heading: Start with the inspection report, not the search results
paragraphs: Al Ain is the second city of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, 130 kilometres inland from the capital and a short drive from the Omani border at Buraimi. That geography decides more about tuition here than most parents expect. The private-school set is far smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so a Diploma Programme subject is often taught to a single class by a single teacher. If that teacher is strong, your child is fine. If the subject is one the school added recently, there is no second set and no second opinion inside the building.

Because Al Ain falls under the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, its private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, not by KHDA, which covers Dubai, and not by SPEA, which covers Sharjah. This matters practically. ADEK publishes an inspection outcome for each private school it inspects, and the report behind that outcome is written standard by standard: what students achieve, how they are taught and assessed, what the curriculum offers, how they are cared for, and how the school is led. A parent who reads it properly learns which subjects a school is thin in before the mock results arrive.

That is the honest starting point for choosing tuition. An ADEK inspection rating is not a verdict on your child. It is a map of where the school's own capacity sits, and where an outside specialist adds something the school cannot. A school judged strong overall can still have a Physics department that lost two teachers in a year. A school in a lower band can have a Mathematics team that holds its grades. Averages hide subjects, and you are buying support for a subject, not for a school.

IB Gram works the way a good head of year would. You send the last school report and, if you have it, the page of the ADEK report that covers teaching in your child's subject group. We work out whether the gap is content, exam technique, coursework, or the particular habit of answering a command term loosely. Then a tutor who teaches that syllabus takes the student for live one-to-one lessons online. Nothing about that model depends on who happens to live within twenty minutes of Al Mutaredh.

Lessons are delivered online over live video, one tutor to one student, with a shared whiteboard and the student's own past papers on screen. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India. In Al Ain the online format is the better buy and not a compromise: a Chemistry HL tutor who has taught the current guide is worth more than a generalist who can be in Falaj Hazzaa at six. We would rather say that plainly than sell a drive time.

al-ain.programmesIntro: Al Ain families run four routes in practice: the IB continuum through the Primary Years and Middle Years into the Diploma, and the Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel route through IGCSE. Each one is assessed differently, and each one fails differently. Here is what we actually tutor at each stage, and what the Al Ain version of it looks like.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external exams, which is exactly why gaps go unnoticed until Year 7. Learning is organised around transdisciplinary units and reported against learner-profile attributes rather than percentages, so a child can look settled while number fluency or extended writing quietly falls behind. Tutoring at this stage is diagnostic and short: arithmetic automaticity, reading stamina, and the habit of writing a paragraph that answers the question asked. Thirty focused minutes twice a week does more here than a long session.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain, PYP children often move schools when a parent's posting shifts between the city and Abu Dhabi island or Dubai. A move mid-primary usually means a change of curriculum model as well as campus, and the PYP-to-national-curriculum jump exposes gaps in formal grammar and written arithmetic. We start with a short written baseline rather than a conversation, because a Year 5 report that says 'developing' tells a parent almost nothing measurable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks everything against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale, then converts to a 1-7 grade. Students who have never been taught what criterion wording expects tend to plateau at 5 and 6 regardless of ability. Our MYP work is criterion-literal: the student marks their own piece against the published descriptors, sees where the band boundary sits, then redrafts once. eAssessment candidates in Year 11 also need timed practice, which most schools cannot fit inside a lesson.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's MYP cohorts are small, and the MYP-to-Diploma step is where the city's limited subject choice bites. A student who wants Physics HL but sat MYP Sciences as an integrated course arrives in DP1 without the algebra load the course assumes. We bridge that in the summer term of Year 11 rather than in October of DP1, when the Internal Assessment clock has already started running.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Diploma is scored out of 45, with up to three points from the TOK and EE combination. Most of the pressure is not the final papers; it is the overlap of five Internal Assessments, an Extended Essay and a TOK essay inside the same twelve weeks. Tutoring that ignores that calendar is tutoring for the wrong problem. An IB Diploma tutor in Al Ain should be able to say what is due in week six.
programmes.countryNote: Because few Al Ain schools run every Higher Level science, families here are the most likely in the emirate to need a subject their campus teaches to a handful of students, or does not teach at all. That is the single clearest case for an online specialist: the student gets the Chemistry HL tutor who has taught the current guide, from wherever that tutor is, rather than the nearest adult who did Chemistry at university a decade ago.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is code-specific, and the code changes what you revise. Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Mathematics tiers into Core and Extended, with Extended targeting the upper grades; 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology carry an alternative-to-practical or practical paper depending on the school's entry. Pearson Edexcel runs 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the sciences, with its own January series. We teach to the code on the student's statement of entry, not to a generic IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE tuition in Al Ain is complicated by mixed entries: it is common for one family's two children to sit Cambridge at one school and Edexcel at another, and for a single student to carry both boards across subjects. Before the first session we ask for the statement of entry and check the tier, the board and the practical arrangement. Half the wasted revision we see in this city is a student working through the wrong board's past papers.

al-ain.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme subjects Al Ain families request most, with what each one is actually assessed on. Where a subject is taught to one small class in the city, an online specialist is usually the only way to get someone who has taught the current guide rather than the previous one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Under the current guide both levels are assessed on Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Marks go missing in the data-based section of Paper 1B and in extended reasoning about energetics and equilibrium. A Chemistry HL tutor works from the student's own marked Paper 2 rather than from a textbook chapter.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The same 36/44/20 split applies. The HL-only material in fields, induction and quantum physics tends to arrive late in DP2, which is why Al Ain students often meet it for the first time three weeks before a mock. Sessions focus on unit discipline, graph linearisation and the difference between a derivation and an explanation in a six-mark answer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology rewards precision of language more than any other DP science: a correct idea in loose wording scores nothing. We drill command terms against the published markscheme, then work on the long-answer questions in Paper 2 where students lose marks for describing a process when the question asked them to explain or to compare.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: SL is Paper 1 at 40 per cent, Paper 2 at 40 per cent and the exploration at 20 per cent. HL adds Paper 3, worth 20 per cent, with two extended investigative questions that reward stamina and structure. Non-calculator fluency on Paper 1 is the usual weak point for students who learned maths on a graphical display calculator.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is not the easy route; it is the modelling and statistics route, with heavy technology use and a different Paper 3 at Higher Level. Students who chose AI for the wrong reason struggle with the volume of interpretation writing. We also check the route against degree plans, because some engineering and physics programmes still expect Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: SL splits 40/40/20 across Paper 1, Paper 2 and the portfolio of three commentaries. HL moves to 20/30/30/20 and adds the quantitative Paper 3, which is where HL grades are won and lost. Diagram accuracy and the explicit use of the nine key concepts carry marks that students regularly leave on the table.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The business research project at HL and the written commentary at SL are coursework pieces that need a real organisation and a real question, which is harder in a smaller city. Exam marks are lost on tool-dropping: naming SWOT or Ansoff without applying it to the stimulus. We work from the published assessment criteria outwards.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: SL is Paper 1 at 35 per cent, Paper 2 at 35 per cent and the individual oral at 30 per cent. HL replaces part of that with the HL essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words and reweights the oral. The guided analysis in Paper 1 is a timed close-reading skill, and it is teachable in a way that reading more books is not.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic runs two different ways in Al Ain: as a first language and literature course, and as a second language at B or ab initio level. Both are assessed on productive skills, and both reward structured writing practice far more than vocabulary lists. This is one of the subjects a smaller school set struggles to staff at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a working solution with documented development, and students regularly build something impressive that documents poorly. We split the work: design and testing evidence first, code second. Paper questions on data structures and object-oriented design need pencil-and-paper tracing practice, not more time in an IDE.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The TOK essay answers one of six prescribed titles in 1,600 words and is marked out of 10 on a single global impression; the exhibition adds three objects and 950 words. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words, marked out of 34. Together they carry up to three Diploma points. Tutors coach structure, argument and source handling only.

al-ain.igcseSubjectsIntro: On the IGCSE side the board and the syllabus code decide the revision plan. These are the subjects Al Ain parents ask about most often, with the codes you will find on the statement of entry.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 tiers, and a student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well they revise, so the tier decision matters more than any single topic. Edexcel 4MA1 is untiered at Higher and sets longer multi-step questions. Both reward method marks, which students lose by not writing the working down.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and the equations around it account for a large share of lost marks every series. Circuit reasoning, not formula recall, is the skill. Where a school enters students for the alternative-to-practical paper, we drill apparatus description, anomalous-result spotting and table-and-graph conventions on screen using past practical papers.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways are the two reliable separators at grade 7 and above. We also work on qualitative analysis questions, which read as recall but are really a sequence: observation, deduction, ionic equation. Students who skip the middle step lose both marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: The content is large and the examiner's vocabulary is narrow. Sessions pair a topic sweep with markscheme language drills on transport, homeostasis and inheritance. Genetic-cross questions are worth practising until the Punnett square layout is automatic, because presentation itself carries marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Both subjects are marked on application to the case material, not on definitions. The common failure is a correct textbook answer that never touches the business in the extract. We teach the two-mark, four-mark and extended-response shapes separately, because they are different writing tasks.

igcseSubjects.name: English
igcseSubjects.description: First Language English and English as a Second Language are different examinations with different reading demands, and students are occasionally entered for the one that suits the school rather than the student. Directed writing and summary tasks are the most coachable components in the whole IGCSE set.

al-ain.regionsTitle: Al Ain districts we schedule around
al-ain.regionsIntro: Al Ain is low-rise and spread out, and the school run shapes the timetable more than traffic does. These are the districts families book from most, with the scheduling detail that matters when you are fixing a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: The district next to the United Arab Emirates University campus, so households here often include a parent or sibling on the UAEU timetable. Study-space competition at home is real; we book sessions when the room is quiet, often after 7pm, rather than straight after school.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Dense, central and close to Al Jimi Mall, with several of the city's long-established private schools within a few minutes' drive. Pick-up is quick here, so a 4.30pm or 5pm start is realistic even in exam term, which makes Al Jimi families the easiest to give a consistent weekday slot.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Villa district close to the oasis and the central hospital, with a high share of medical and university households. DP sciences and maths dominate requests from here. Evening sessions work well because parents on shift patterns prefer a fixed slot the student can keep without a lift.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: West of the centre, near the Al Ain Palace Museum side of town, and a longer run back from the newer campuses on the city's edge. A 5.30pm start is safer than a 4.30pm one here; we build the first session late and bring it forward once the family sees the real arrival time.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Established residential area with a mix of British and Indian curriculum families, which means one household often runs IGCSE and CBSE timetables side by side. Siblings are better scheduled back to back on the same evening so one quiet room covers both lessons.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: On the southern edge towards Jebel Hafeet, with the longest school commute in the city for families whose children attend central campuses. Weekday sessions realistically start at 6pm. Many Zakher families move their heavier work to Friday or Saturday mornings instead.

regions.name: Falaj Hazzaa
regions.note: Large villa neighbourhood with a strong Emirati household share, so Arabic as a first language and Islamic Education sit alongside IB or IGCSE subjects in the same week. We coordinate so tuition does not collide with the school's own Arabic support sessions.

regions.name: Hili and Al Foah
regions.note: Northern districts out towards the Omani border crossing, where the archaeological parks are. Families here drive further for school than anyone else in Al Ain, and the online format removes the second journey entirely. Winter sunset timings change what counts as a late slot.

al-ain.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every Al Ain request. All of them are live one-to-one video lessons with a shared whiteboard, and all of them are timed in Gulf Standard Time. The choice is about rhythm, not about delivery.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: One or two fixed sessions a week against the school's own scheme of work, which is the format that actually changes a grade over a year. The tutor sees the marked class assessments, so the session targets the question the student got wrong last week rather than the next topic in the book. Most Al Ain families start here with a single subject and add a second only if the first is holding.

modes.title: Coursework clinics for the IA, EE and TOK essay
modes.description: Short, scheduled blocks aimed at one assessed piece, pinned to the school's internal deadline rather than the final submission date. The tutor reads the draft against the published criteria, marks it in the student's presence, and names the criterion losing the marks. The student does the rewriting. This is IA coaching, not drafting, and the boundary is explained to the student in the first session.

sections.heading: What an ADEK rating actually says about your child's subject
paragraphs: ADEK licenses and inspects the private schools of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain and Al Dhafra, and publishes an overall outcome for each school it inspects on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Those words are the part parents remember. They are also the part that tells you least, because an overall band is a weighted summary of an entire school across every phase and subject group it offers.

The useful information sits one level down. An inspection judgement is built from performance standards covering what students achieve, their personal development, teaching and assessment, the curriculum, the care and support around them, and leadership. Achievement itself is reported by phase and by subject group, which is where a parent of a DP2 Chemistry student should be reading. A school can hold a strong overall band while the judgement on attainment in secondary science sits a band lower, and that gap is the one tuition is for.

So use the band for what it is good at. It tells you the direction the school is moving and how much slack the leadership has. A school that has just moved up a band is usually investing in teaching and may fix your problem by itself within a term. A school holding a lower band for several cycles is unlikely to solve a single subject's staffing in the twelve weeks before your child's mocks, and that is a decision point rather than a complaint.

The table below is how we read each band when a family in Al Ain asks what it means for them. It is a working interpretation, not an official definition, and the current report for any named school should be checked on ADEK's own site before you act on it.

sections.heading: The six things an inspector looked at, and which of them you can fix privately
paragraphs: An inspection report is not a review. It is a structured judgement against standards, and each standard has a different relationship to private tuition. Two of them a tutor can genuinely compensate for. Two a tutor can partly offset. Two are entirely the school's, and no amount of tuition will touch them. Knowing which is which stops families spending money on the wrong problem.

Students' achievement, meaning attainment and progress against curriculum standards, is the standard tuition addresses directly. Teaching and assessment is the second: where a report says feedback is not used well to move learning on, an outside tutor marking the student's own work to the published markscheme is a direct substitute for the missing feedback loop. Those two are the reason most Al Ain families start.

Curriculum, and the care, guidance and support standard, are partly addressable. If the report notes that the curriculum is not adapted for higher attainers, a tutor can extend a student beyond the class pace. If it notes weak transition support between MYP and DP, a bridging block in the summer term covers much of it. What a tutor cannot replace is subject choice: if the school does not run Physics HL, tuition does not create a class, although it does make a private or transferred entry survivable.

Personal and social development, and leadership and management, are the school's own. A tutor has no standing there, and any provider implying otherwise is selling something it does not have. We say this openly because it narrows the question usefully. Read the achievement and teaching judgements for your child's phase, decide whether the gap is content or technique or feedback, and buy exactly that.
bullets: Directly fixable by tuition: attainment, progress, exam technique, marked feedback

Not fixable from outside: subject availability, pastoral provision, school leadership
Always read the achievement judgement for your child's phase, not the overall band

sections.heading: What tuition costs in Al Ain, and who publishes those numbers
paragraphs: Published pricing in this market is scarce, and that is deliberate on most sites. Three of the larger agencies competing for UAE search traffic publish no hourly figure at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, a currency no family here transacts in. Two more publish a rate in their structured data that contradicts the rate on the visible page. So before anything else: the figures below are market rates other providers publish, not IB Gram's price list.

The pattern across the market is consistent once you convert everything into dirhams per hour. Budget online tuition, usually delivered by university students, starts in the AED 45 to 150 band. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300. Visiting in-home tuition carries its travel cost inside the hourly rate and runs higher, commonly quoted between AED 180 and AED 500. Named IB and IGCSE specialists sit from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and examiner-level or heavily branded tutors are quoted at AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond.

Monthly packaging is where comparison gets slippery. Advertised bundles in the UAE include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are not comparable products: one buys eight contact hours, the other eight hours with travel folded in and half the frequency. Work in cost per contact hour and the picture clears up immediately.

Al Ain sits at the softer end of in-home pricing compared with Dubai, simply because the driving is easier and the rent lower, but the tutor pool is correspondingly smaller. That is the real trade-off for home tuition rates in Al Ain: you may pay less per hour than a Dubai Marina family and still have a much shorter list of people who have taught your child's actual syllabus.

sections.heading: In-home tuition in Al Ain against live online one-to-one
paragraphs: Parents searching for a home tutor in this city are asking a reasonable question, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home tuition does real things that online does not. A tutor in the room can see a child's body language, put a hand near the page, and keep a distractible twelve-year-old on task without a single reminder. For younger children and for students with certain additional needs, that presence is worth paying for, and families should weigh it honestly.

What it costs is the other half of the answer. An in-home session in Al Ain pays for the tutor's road time, and because the city is spread out from Zakher in the south to Hili in the north, one visit can absorb forty minutes of driving at each end. That time is in the rate, and it also caps the tutor's availability: whoever teaches your child on Tuesday at five must be physically within reach of your district on Tuesday at five. In a city with a small specialist pool, that constraint, not the money, is what usually decides the match.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as live one-to-one lessons online, over video, with a shared whiteboard and screen sharing. Home visits are part of our India service only. We are not pretending that online is identical to a tutor in the room; we are saying that for Diploma and IGCSE students the specialist you reach matters more than the metre of distance, and that the saved travel converts into frequency and continuity. A student who keeps the same tutor through a house move, a posting to Abu Dhabi island, or a summer abroad does not lose a term to re-matching.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the first paper
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market names an exam session at all, which is strange, because the session date is the only fixed point in the whole year. Everything else, including how much tuition is worth buying, follows from it. The Diploma runs two sessions: May, which is what nearly all Al Ain schools enter, and November. Cambridge IGCSE runs a May or June series and an October or November series. Pearson Edexcel adds a January series for many International GCSE subjects, which is why a January entry quietly exists in this city for resitting students.

Work backwards and the year has a shape. A year out, the decisions are structural: subject and level combinations, Mathematics AA and AI route choice, and whether a Higher Level science the school cannot staff should be carried. Nine months out, Internal Assessment topics are chosen and approved, and this is where most of the damage is done, because an unworkable research question costs the student weeks they never get back. Six months out, candidate registration has closed and the statement of entry exists; check the board, the tier and the paper options on it rather than assuming.

Three months out, coursework should be finished, and the student should be sitting whole timed papers rather than revising topics. Six weeks out is the point at which new content stops being worth teaching and markscheme behaviour starts paying. In the final fortnight the only useful work is timed questions, marked, with the errors logged by type rather than by topic. Results land in early July for the May Diploma session and in early January for the November session, with Cambridge and Edexcel publishing in August and January; confirm your own dates with the school's exams officer, because entry deadlines vary by centre.

Ramadan moves the middle of this plan. School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and the productive hours for a teenager shift late. We plan around it rather than through it: lighter content weeks, then post-Iftar sessions for the heavier work.
