al-ain/al-yahar.programmesIntro: Al Yahar households are spread across the British route, the IB continuum and the national and Indian boards. Each programme below is described by what it assumes about a student's week, because that assumption is where distance bites.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed by terminal papers, tiered in several subjects, with the entry made by the school months before the examination. Cambridge uses codes such as 0580 and 0620; Pearson uses forms like 4MA1 and 4CH1. Both assume consistent homework and question practice across two years rather than a concentrated final push.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series and allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that the correct zone timetable must be used. For families out here the practical point is that entries are made through a centre, never by the family directly, and the centre's entry deadline for the June series falls in the spring, months before the first paper. Ask the exams officer for that date and for the zone timetable in the same email.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at two levels plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, with internal assessment generally carrying twenty to thirty per cent of a subject grade. The programme assumes a substantial independent working week, which is the resource a long commute takes first.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student travelling in from Al Yahar loses more of the week to the road than almost any other student in the emirate. That makes weekend blocks and term-break intensives more valuable here than anywhere, and it makes a realistic hours budget essential rather than optional.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, closing with the Personal Project. Criteria assess skills, so a weak score points at a process rather than a missing chapter.
programmes.countryNote: Middle-years students out here often have the least supervised study time of anyone in the city, because the journey eats the window in which a parent might otherwise sit with them. Short, specific work at the weekend tends to achieve more than an ambitious weekday plan nobody can keep.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth with the weight in the final papers, modular with Pearson and stageable with Cambridge. Fewer subjects means fewer deadlines, which is genuinely easier to manage around a long commute than the Diploma's broader load.
programmes.countryNote: For a household on the city's outer edge, the lighter coursework load of an A Level route is a practical factor as well as an academic one. It is worth weighing honestly during the decision at sixteen rather than treating the choice as purely about breadth against depth.

al-ain/al-yahar.subjectsIntro: Requests from Al Yahar concentrate on the mainstream Diploma and IGCSE subjects, with occasional requests for a specialism that has no local provider at all. Each entry names the subject and the realistic availability position.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Well covered online and the most commonly requested subject from this district. The tier decision sets the ceiling, so establishing which paper the school has entered a student for comes before any revision planning.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and qualitative analysis carry the marks. Covered reliably online; harder to source in person out here, because the subject specialists in the city already carry full school timetables.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical component take most lost marks. The alternative-to-practical paper is coachable entirely on screen, which removes one of the usual objections to remote science support.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty, with command terms deciding the paper. Responsive to marked question practice, which is work that does not need anybody in the room.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level is well covered; Higher Level is tighter everywhere and tighter still for in-person delivery in this part of the emirate. Algebraic fluency under time is the gate, and it is trainable remotely.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator technique. The exploration needs a real dataset, which is one area where a household's internet access matters for the work itself rather than just for the lesson.

subjects.name: Chemistry at Diploma level
subjects.description: Higher Level availability is limited across Al Ain and effectively unavailable in person out here. Online matching is the realistic route, and where no UAE-based specialist is free that is disclosed before a booking.

subjects.name: Physics at Diploma level
subjects.description: The same position as chemistry, with the added factor that Higher Level demands algebraic confidence that is best diagnosed before the level is chosen rather than in the second term.

subjects.name: Biology at Diploma level
subjects.description: Better covered than the other two sciences, and the internal assessment is usually the request rather than the content. Design and statistical treatment are both screen work.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and application to supplied case material decide the grades. Both are well covered online and both have thin in-person provision anywhere outside the main cities.

subjects.name: English First Language and English A
subjects.description: Extended writing at a register most students have not been asked for. Six to eight weeks of marked writing typically moves it, and the marking is the part that needs another person rather than another room.

subjects.name: Less common Diploma languages, Music and Design Technology
subjects.description: Genuinely thin everywhere, including online. For these the first conversation gives either a named match time or a clear no, because a holding answer that never resolves costs a family more than a refusal.

al-ain/al-yahar.modesIntro: Three patterns work from a district this far out, and they are chosen by how much of the week the road has already taken. All three are one-to-one over live video, which is what makes them available here at the same rate as in the city.

modes.title: A weekend-led plan
modes.description: The main pattern out here. One substantial weekend block where the student is rested and nothing is competing for the hour, plus at most one short weekday session for consolidation. It inverts the usual advice because the usual advice assumes a thirty-minute school run, and this household does not have one.
bullets: Ninety minutes or more on a weekend morning, with no hard stop

modes.title: Term-break intensives
modes.description: Blocks of three to five consecutive sessions inside the winter and spring breaks, aimed at one weak topic or one assessed component. For a long-commute household these are worth more than the equivalent hours spread across a term, because nothing interrupts and nobody is tired from the road.

sections.heading: What living outside the catchment costs, counted in hours
paragraphs: Begin with the number nobody writes down. Ask your child how long they were on the bus this morning and this afternoon, and add the two figures. For a household out along the Abu Dhabi road attending a central campus, the honest total is frequently well over an hour and sometimes closer to two, because a bus serving a low-density area has to cover a great deal of ground before its seats are full.

Now compound it. An extra forty minutes a day against a child in Al Jimi is more than three hours a week, around thirteen hours a month and, across an academic year, somewhere in the region of a working fortnight. That is not an argument against living here. It is simply the resource constraint inside which every study plan has to fit, and a plan that ignores it will be abandoned in November and blamed on the child.

The practical consequence is that the standard advice is wrong for this district. Conventional guidance puts tutoring in a weekday evening and keeps the weekend clear. Out here the weekday evening is the part the road has already taken, and the weekend is the part that is genuinely available. Inverting the plan, so that demanding new material goes into a weekend block and weekdays carry only short consolidation, is the single most useful change a family here can make.

The table puts the arithmetic in one place. The figures are illustrative rather than measured for your route, and the point is the direction and the magnitude rather than the precise number. Collect your own two figures for a week and the rest of the table recalculates itself, which is a twenty-minute exercise that changes how a year is planned.

sections.heading: Why a travel-inclusive rate is mostly a travel rate
paragraphs: Published market rates for in-home one-to-one tutoring in the UAE run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel priced into the figure, according to the Bestimate rate survey and the home-tutor listings in this market. That is a reasonable price for a person's time. The question worth asking from a district like this one is how much of that time is teaching.

Work it through. A tutor living in the central Al Ain belt who drives out here for a one-hour lesson at five in the afternoon is committing roughly two hours of driving plus the hour of teaching: three hours of their working day for one billable hour. No rational person prices that as a single hour, which is why in-home rates in outlying districts sit at the upper end of the band or get declined altogether. The family is not being overcharged; the economics simply do not work.

This is also why the in-home pool shrinks so sharply with distance. The specialists in Al Ain already have full school timetables, and the ones who tutor privately in the evenings will reasonably choose a student fifteen minutes away over a student forty-five minutes away at the same rate. A family out here is competing for a scarce resource from the back of the queue, and no amount of searching changes the queue.

Online delivery removes the entire line. There is no round trip, so the hour that is paid for is an hour of teaching, and the rate sits in the published AED 150 to 300 band for a qualified subject tutor rather than at the top of the in-home range. The money saved is not the main benefit, though. The main benefit is that the choice of tutor is no longer a function of who is willing to drive to the E22 corridor on a Tuesday.

sections.heading: Making a lesson reliable from a district on the edge of the network
paragraphs: If the whole plan depends on a video connection, the connection deserves ten minutes of attention before the first lesson rather than a crisis in the third one. Out in the farm and small-holding belt this is a genuine consideration, and it is also entirely solvable. The common failure is not a lack of bandwidth; it is an untested setup discovered mid-session.

Three checks cover most of it. First, run a speed test from the room the lesson will happen in, at the time of day the lesson will happen, not from the room with the router in it at ten in the morning. Second, establish a fallback: a mobile connection on a different network, tested once, so that a dropped line costs three minutes rather than a session. Third, use a wired connection where the room allows it, because a cable removes the most common source of instability entirely.

Then the practical equipment, none of it expensive. Headphones with a microphone, which solve echo and let a household run two sessions in different rooms. A second device or a phone camera pointed at the page, so the tutor can see handwritten working as it happens, which matters enormously in mathematics and the sciences. And a table facing a wall rather than a room, because a student facing a doorway will watch the doorway.

It is worth saying what the format does not require. It does not need a laboratory, because practical work happens at school where it belongs. It does not need expensive software. And it does not need a parent in the room beyond the first few sessions for a student in Year 10 or above, which matters in a household where the adults may still be travelling home themselves when the lesson starts.
bullets: Test the connection in the actual room at the actual time
Set up a mobile fallback on a different network, once

sections.heading: Coverage and fallback, stated before you ask
paragraphs: No platform covers every subject at every level in every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise produce the disappointment they were trying to avoid. The honest position is that availability tracks cohort size: the smaller the number of students taking a subject anywhere, the thinner the supply of people who can teach it well. That is why Higher Level sciences, uncommon Diploma languages, Music, Design Technology and Further Mathematics are the hard cases everywhere, not just here.

Where a UAE-based specialist is available, that is the match. Where none is free, the fallback is a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same syllabus over the same live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and the position is stated before any booking rather than discovered in the first lesson. Several providers in this market route families to non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking contact route without disclosing it, which is a trust failure rather than a logistical one.

Match times should be given as numbers rather than adjectives. A common subject at a common level moves within days. A rare combination at Higher Level in the middle of an examination term may take longer or may not be possible at all that term. A clear no is more useful to a family out here than anywhere else, because the alternative plan takes time to arrange and the sooner it starts the better it works.

There is one more disclosure worth making on a page for this district. A tutor whose profile lists six subjects across four year groups is a generalist, and out here generalists are offered more often because the specialist list is short. A generalist is genuinely useful for consolidating content a student nearly understands. They will not move a Higher Level Paper 3 mark, and a family paying specialist rates should know which they have been matched with.

sections.heading: Choosing a school when distance is a real variable
paragraphs: Families in the outer districts face a trade that families in the city do not: the campus with the subject offer they want may be forty minutes further away than the campus with a narrower one. That is a legitimate decision in either direction, and the mistake is not choosing wrongly but choosing without stating the trade out loud. An extra forty minutes each way is roughly a working fortnight a year of a child's time, and a narrower subject offer may close a sixth-form route.

The question that resolves it is usually about the specific subject combination a student is likely to want at sixteen. If a child is heading towards sciences at Higher Level, a campus that runs those sets properly is worth the journey, because the alternative is a combination that does not exist locally and a move at the worst possible moment. If a child's direction is broader or still unclear, the shorter run and the hours it returns are worth a great deal.

It is worth asking any prospective campus three specific things in writing: which boards they enter candidates for, which Higher Level or A Level sets actually ran last year and how large they were, and what the transport arrangement is for this district including the position in the route order. The third question is the one nobody asks and the one that determines the shape of every evening for the next five years.

Inspection reports are the other free resource, and the useful part is not the overall band. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and accredited by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which publishes inspection outcomes. Read what the report says about teaching and assessment in the phase your child is entering and about the subject group they are likely to depend on, rather than the summary on the front page.

sections.heading: The private-candidate route when a campus is impractical
paragraphs: A small number of households out here end up entering a student for examinations through an approved centre rather than through a school they attend daily: families whose work keeps them mobile, students who need a subject no reachable campus offers, and home-educated students. It is a legitimate route and it is more common in outlying districts than in the city, where a campus is usually within reach.

The mechanics are worth understanding before committing. Entries are made through a centre, and the centre's administrative arrangements govern the candidate: Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six zones, and the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss a paper after using the wrong one. Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers in both live series: a June entry is lodged in the spring and a November entry in the late summer, with the exact day set out on the centre's key-dates schedule. For a private candidate in Al Yahar that order matters more than the dates themselves, because a centre that has already closed its entries for a series cannot add a candidate to it afterwards.

Pearson's position is similar in shape. International GCSE examinations run in May or June and in November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official document is always the one to work from.

What this route demands of a family is organisation rather than money. Somebody has to own the entry deadlines, the practical or alternative-to-practical arrangements, and the evidence requirements where a subject has a coursework component. Tutoring can support the teaching entirely, and online delivery is well suited to it, but no tutoring platform enters a candidate or manages a centre relationship, and anyone implying otherwise is overstating what they do.
bullets: Entries are made through a centre, with deadlines months ahead
Cambridge zone timetables differ; use the centre's own version

sections.heading: Building a week that respects the road
paragraphs: The plan that works out here looks different from the plan that works in the centre, and it is worth describing concretely. One weekend block of ninety minutes or more carries the demanding work: a new topic, a full timed paper, a coursework design session. One short weekday slot, thirty to forty-five minutes, carries consolidation of something already taught. That is the whole shape, and its virtue is that it survives to March.

The reason the weekend block does the heavy lifting is state rather than duration. A child who has spent an hour on a bus after a full school day is not in a condition to meet an unfamiliar method, however willing they are and however good the tutor is. The same child on a Saturday morning is a different student. Putting new material into the wrong state is the commonest way a family concludes their child cannot do a subject.

Term breaks deserve deliberate use for the same reason. The UAE academic year carries a long winter break and a spring break, both close enough to the examination series to matter. Three to five consecutive sessions inside a break, on one topic that has been failing all term, achieves more than six weekly sessions across the term because nothing interrupts and nothing is forgotten between appointments.

Ramadan changes the shape again, and planning it in advance is what separates families who keep momentum from families who lose a month. School hours shorten, afternoons are for rest, and useful work happens late. Sessions typically move to post-Iftar timing and frequency drops rather than holding steady. Agreeing that before the month starts takes two minutes; improvising it week by week costs most of the month.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the hour actually contains
paragraphs: The published figures, attributed, because most pages in this market publish none. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour; Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase shows AED 270; the Bestimate rate survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist IB and IGCSE work at AED 200 to 450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly patterns seen include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits.

Those are market rates, not an IB Gram price list, and your own figure should come from a conversation. What is worth comparing is not the numbers but what each tier buys. At the budget end the hour is generally homework help and content re-explanation. In the middle band it is content plus topic question practice. At the specialist end it is timed questions marked against the published scheme with error categories named, plus coursework criteria work, and that is the tier that changes an examination outcome.

For a household out here one further comparison matters. The monthly in-home package figures assume a tutor who can reach the address, and in this district that assumption frequently fails before price is discussed. A package that cannot be staffed is not a cheaper option; it is an unavailable one. Online pricing, by contrast, does not change with the distance from the school belt, which is the single clearest financial consequence of the format.

Two questions to ask any provider. Is the figure per hour or per session, because a sixty-minute hour and a forty-five-minute session at the same price are different products. And is value added tax included, which is a question for the provider rather than for a web page: the tax treatment of tuition is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and should not be asserted by a tutoring company.

sections.heading: Delivery, honesty and what is not claimed
paragraphs: To state the delivery position once more without ambiguity, because on this page it is the substance rather than the small print: IB Gram sells no home visits anywhere in the UAE and nobody will be sent to an Al Yahar address. Home visiting is a service offered only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the student sharing their own work and keeping the annotated material afterwards.

On assessed work the boundary is fixed and applies regardless of distance or deadline pressure. A tutor may teach the skills a task needs, explain what each assessment criterion asks for, question a draft the student has written and point out a section that does not answer its own research question. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or edit to completion an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. The student signs the authenticity declaration and carries any finding.

On regulation, the correct position for a parent to hold is that private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the labour ministry's own service for private tutor licensing. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone saying the permit is optional or carries a fee is wrong on both counts.

On status, plainly: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the labour ministry, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, runs no UAE office or centre, and publishes no self-assessed rating, success percentage or student headcount. Awarding-body documents are cited and linked rather than reproduced. No IB examination dates appear anywhere on this site, because none has been verified from the IB itself.

process.title: Measure both journey legs for a week
process.description: Morning and afternoon, written down, from the day the route settles rather than the first week of term. Add them. That total, not the distance on a map, is the number every other decision on this page follows from, and most families out here have never put it on paper.

process.title: Name the subject, level, board and syllabus code
process.description: Not physics but Cambridge 0625 Extended, or Pearson 4PH1. Not maths but Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. With that specificity the coverage question can be answered honestly in one conversation, including when the answer is that nobody is free this term.

process.title: Get the coverage answer before anything else
process.description: For a thin subject, the first thing worth knowing is whether a specialist exists and when. You will be given a named match time, a disclosed non-UAE option on Gulf time, or a clear no. Out here that conversation should happen before any discussion of money, because the alternative plan takes time to build.

process.title: Test the connection in the real room at the real time
process.description: A speed test from the room the lesson will use, at the hour it will run, plus a mobile fallback on a different network tested once. Ten minutes in advance removes the most common cause of a lost session, and a wired connection removes it almost entirely.

process.title: Build the week backwards from the weekend
process.description: Put the demanding work in a long weekend block and keep weekdays for short consolidation. Add term-break intensives for the topic that has been failing all term, and agree Ramadan timing before the month begins. That shape survives to March, which is more than most ambitious plans manage.

whyPoints.title: Distance is treated as the main variable, because here it is
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring advice assumes a short school run and a free weekday evening. Out along the Abu Dhabi road neither assumption holds, so the plan is inverted: weekend blocks for demanding work, short weekday consolidation, and term breaks used deliberately rather than left empty.

whyPoints.title: The travel arithmetic is shown rather than hidden
whyPoints.description: A visiting tutor driving out here commits around three hours of their day for one billable hour, which is why in-home rates in outlying districts sit at the top of the published band or get declined. Setting that out explains the pricing honestly instead of implying anybody is being overcharged.

whyPoints.title: Coverage is disclosed before money is discussed
whyPoints.description: For Higher Level sciences and uncommon subjects the first conversation gives a named match time, a disclosed non-UAE option on Gulf Standard Time, or a clear no. Out here a refusal delivered early is worth more than a holding answer, because the alternative plan needs time to arrange.

whyPoints.title: Rates do not rise with distance from the school belt
whyPoints.description: Online delivery has no round trip to absorb, so the published qualified band of AED 150 to 300 applies to a household thirty kilometres out exactly as it does to one in Al Jimi. The saving is real; the larger benefit is that the tutor is chosen by subject rather than by willingness to drive.

whyPoints.title: The technical setup is treated as part of the service
whyPoints.description: A plan that depends on a connection deserves ten minutes of preparation: a speed test in the real room at the real hour, a mobile fallback on a second network, headphones and a camera pointed at the page. That is cheaper than losing a session and it is said in advance rather than after a failure.

whyPoints.title: The private-candidate route is explained, not sold
whyPoints.description: For households whose distance makes a campus impractical, entry through an approved centre is a genuine option with real deadlines and zone-specific timetables. Those are set out with the boards' own published dates, together with the clear statement that no tutoring platform enters a candidate on your behalf.

faqs.question: How much of our week does the school journey actually take?
faqs.answer: More than most families out here have ever put on paper. Add the morning and the afternoon leg together for one week: from this corridor into a central campus the honest total is frequently over an hour a day and sometimes closer to two, because a bus serving a low-density area covers a lot of ground before its seats are full. An extra forty minutes a day compared with a child in Al Jimi is over three hours a week and, across an academic year, approaching a working fortnight of your child's time.

faqs.question: Why is the standard advice about weekday evening tutoring wrong for us?
faqs.answer: Because it assumes a thirty-minute school run and a free evening, and this household has neither. The weekday evening is the part the road has already taken, and a child who has spent an hour on a bus after a full school day is not in a state to meet an unfamiliar method however good the tutor is. The weekend is the part of the week that is genuinely available. Inverting the plan, with demanding new material in a long weekend block and short consolidation on weekdays, is the single most useful change a family here can make.

faqs.question: Why would an in-home tutor charge more to come out to Al Yahar?
faqs.answer: Because they are committing around three hours of their working day for one billable hour: roughly two hours of driving plus the lesson. Published in-home rates in this market run from AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and in outlying districts the quotes sit at the upper end or the request is simply declined. That is not overcharging. The economics of a two-hour round trip for a single hour do not work at any reasonable rate, which is why the pool thins so sharply with distance.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring cost more because we live far out?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the clearest financial consequence of the format. There is no round trip to absorb, so the published band of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor applies here exactly as it does in the centre of the city. Monthly in-home package figures of AED 1,599 to 1,799 assume a tutor who can reach the address, which in this district frequently fails before price is even discussed. A package that cannot be staffed is not a cheaper option, it is an unavailable one.

faqs.question: Can we actually get a Higher Level science specialist out here?
faqs.answer: Online, usually yes; in person, often not at all. Al Ain has a much smaller private-school set than the capital, so there are fewer resident teachers of any subject, and the ones who tutor in the evenings will reasonably choose a student fifteen minutes away over one forty-five minutes away at the same rate. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics are limited across the whole emirate and tighter in an examination term. You will be given a named match time, a disclosed non-UAE option on Gulf time, or a clear no.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find anyone for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: You get told, at the first conversation, with either a named match time or a straight refusal. Availability tracks cohort size, so the hard cases are the same everywhere: Higher Level sciences, uncommon Diploma languages, Music, Design Technology and Further Mathematics. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the fallback is a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same syllabus on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before any booking. A clear no matters more out here than in the city, because your alternative plan takes longer to arrange.

faqs.question: Our internet is not perfect. Will the lessons work?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly, and the failure that actually occurs is an untested setup rather than insufficient bandwidth. Run a speed test from the room the lesson will use, at the hour it will run, rather than from beside the router at ten in the morning. Set up a mobile fallback on a different network and test it once, so a dropped line costs three minutes instead of a session. Where the room allows a cable, use one; it removes the commonest source of instability outright.

faqs.question: What equipment does my child actually need?
faqs.answer: Very little, and none of it expensive. Headphones with a microphone, which solve echo and let two children work in different rooms. A second device or a phone camera pointed at the page, so a tutor can watch handwritten working appear, which matters a great deal in mathematics and the sciences. And a table facing a wall rather than a doorway, because a student facing a door will watch the door. No laboratory is needed: practical work happens at school, where it belongs.

faqs.question: Should we choose a nearer school with fewer subjects, or a further one with more?
faqs.answer: Decide it on the subject combination your child is likely to want at sixteen, and say the trade out loud. Forty extra minutes each way is roughly a working fortnight a year of their time. If they are heading for sciences at Higher Level, a campus that genuinely runs those sets is worth the journey, because the alternative is a combination that does not exist locally and a move at the worst moment. If the direction is still open, the shorter run and the hours it returns are worth a great deal.

faqs.question: What should I ask a school before accepting a place from this district?
faqs.answer: Three things, in writing. Which boards do you enter candidates for, by syllabus code? Which Higher Level or A Level sets actually ran last year and how large were they? And what is the transport arrangement for our district, including our position in the route order in both directions? The third question is the one nobody asks and the one that shapes every evening for the next five years. Being collected early and dropped late is the worst combination and the most common.

faqs.question: Can my child sit exams without attending a school daily?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a private candidate entered through an approved centre, and it is more common in outlying districts than in the city. What it demands is organisation rather than money: somebody has to own the entry deadlines, the practical or alternative-to-practical arrangements and any coursework evidence requirements. Entry deadlines sit months ahead, and Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. No tutoring platform enters a candidate on your behalf, and any that implies otherwise is overstating what it does.

faqs.question: How far ahead do exam entries actually close?
faqs.answer: Months, and the series a UAE candidate is entering is either June or November. Cambridge sets the final entry deadline for each of those series well before its first paper and publishes it to centres rather than to families, so the figure you can rely on is the one on your centre's key-dates schedule and statement of entry; a tutoring page quoting a specific day for a series two years out is guessing. Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May or June and in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables first, so always work from the live official document rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Are term breaks worth using for intensive sessions?
faqs.answer: Out here, more than anywhere. Three to five consecutive sessions inside the winter or spring break, aimed at one topic that has been failing all term, achieves more than six weekly sessions spread across the term. Nothing interrupts, nothing is forgotten between appointments, and the student is not arriving off a bus. For a household whose weekday hours are already spent on the road, the breaks are the one period when the time available matches the time a difficult topic actually needs.

faqs.question: How should the plan change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, the afternoon becomes rest time and useful work moves late, so sessions typically shift to post-Iftar timing and frequency drops rather than holding steady. The families who keep momentum agree that shift in advance, in writing, before the month begins. The ones who try to keep a normal afternoon pattern and improvise week by week usually lose most of the month and then attempt to recover it in a fortnight that is already full. Two minutes of planning saves four weeks.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether I have been matched with a specialist or a generalist?
faqs.answer: Look at how many subjects and year groups the profile covers. A tutor listing six subjects across four year groups is a generalist, and out here generalists get offered more often precisely because the specialist list is short. A generalist is genuinely useful for consolidating content a student nearly understands. They will not move a Higher Level Paper 3 mark. If you are paying a specialist rate, ask directly which syllabus code they have taught and for how long.

faqs.question: Do tutors in the UAE need a permit, and does it apply to online lessons?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the labour ministry's own private tutor licensing service. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Asking a UAE-based tutor for their permit reference is reasonable. Anyone claiming it is optional, or that it carries a fee, is wrong on both counts.

al-ain/al-yahar.closingHeading: Give us the journey time and the syllabus code
al-ain/al-yahar.closingBody: Two numbers get an Al Yahar enquiry to a straight answer: the combined morning and afternoon journey time, and the exact subject, level and syllabus code your child sits. From those we can tell you whether the week should be weekend-led, whether a specialist exists for that subject and when, and whether the tutor would be UAE-based or elsewhere on Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is that nobody covers it this term, you will hear that at the first conversation rather than after a payment. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, no home visits are sold anywhere in the UAE, and IB Gram holds no regulator approval of any kind.

intro.heading: A superlative nobody can verify is not information
paragraphs: A parent in Al Ain searching for the best IB tutor is given, within three results, half a dozen providers each asserting that they are the finest available, several with a star rating they awarded themselves and one with two different review counts on the same page. None of it can be checked, which means none of it is information. The search is a reasonable one, and the honest response is not another claim to the title but a method for judging any tutor you are considered, including ones who have nothing to do with this platform.

That is what this page is. A rubric. Six checks a parent can perform without specialist knowledge, the question of legal permission to tutor in the UAE, a set of specific tests to run during a trial lesson, four student profiles that genuinely need different kinds of tutor, and a comparison of provider models rather than of brands. Where money appears, every figure is a published market rate attributed to whoever published it, because the relationship between price and quality in this market is weaker than families assume and worth examining directly.

A word on the Al Ain context, because it changes the answer. The city sits 130 kilometres inland from the capital, is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and therefore inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than KHDA, and has a private-school set much smaller than Abu Dhabi island's. Diploma cohorts here are small. For several Higher Level subjects and the less common languages, the number of qualified local specialists is very low and occasionally nought. A family that treats proximity as the first filter in Al Ain is filtering on the least informative variable available.

There is a related point about what the word best can even mean here. There is no single ranking of tutors, no register of quality, no examining body that certifies tutor competence, and no published dataset against which a provider's claim could be tested. What exists is a set of verifiable facts about a particular person: what they have taught, at what level, how recently, whether they are permitted to work, and how they behave in a lesson with your child. Those facts are knowable. The superlative is not.

Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service available only in India. That is stated at the top rather than buried, because a parent judging tutors deserves to know the delivery model before reading anyone's argument for it. The argument, in short, is that in a city with small cohorts the specialist who teaches your child's exact Higher Level option may not live within driving distance, and a screen removes that constraint.

al-ain/best-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Judging a tutor requires knowing which programme your child is actually on, because the skills that make someone good at one are not the skills that make them good at another. These are the three an Al Ain family is most likely to be choosing for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with internal assessment carrying roughly twenty to thirty per cent of most subject grades. A good Diploma tutor therefore needs two distinct competences: examination technique for the written papers, and the ability to give criterion-referenced feedback on coursework without ever writing any of it.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the relevant test of a Diploma tutor is whether they can name the components of your child's specific course and say which one is losing the marks. With small local cohorts and teachers often covering several courses, families here value a tutor who knows one Higher Level option deeply over one who claims the whole subject group.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment with four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight. A tutor who cannot name the criteria for the subject group in question is not an MYP tutor, whatever the profile says, because almost every MYP problem is a strand problem rather than a topic problem and topic revision will not touch it.
programmes.countryNote: This is the clearest single filter available to an Al Ain parent with a middle-school child. Ask a prospective tutor to name the four criteria for the relevant subject group. The answer takes ten seconds to give and is not available to anyone who has not actually taught the programme.

programmes.name: International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers under Cambridge or Pearson, with tiered entry in many subjects and four-digit or alphanumeric syllabus codes identifying the exact specification. The relevant competence is mark-scheme fluency: knowing what a four-mark question expects and where a command term changes the required answer.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain schools split between the two boards and sometimes run different boards for different subjects in one year group. A tutor who asks for the syllabus code before the first lesson is demonstrating the single most useful habit in this market; one who does not ask is working from the subject name alone.

programmes.name: International A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects with no compulsory core and longer, narrower papers. The judging question here is different again: whether the tutor teaches to the specific specification and assessment objectives, since the same subject under different awarding bodies rewards noticeably different answer structures.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain campuses run A Levels rather than the Diploma, so some families are choosing a tutor while still choosing a qualification. A tutor worth hiring will tell you honestly when the question in front of you is a curriculum decision rather than a tutoring one.

al-ain/best-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: The judging question changes by subject, because what separates a competent tutor from a strong one is subject-specific. Below is what to probe for in the courses Al Ain families most often ask about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask which course the student should be on. A tutor willing to say that Applications and Interpretation is the better fit, when it is, is telling you something about their incentives. Ask also how they teach the mathematical exploration, which carries twenty per cent and is routinely started too late.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask about technology use, because this course assumes it and many tutors trained on the analysis route under-teach it. A tutor who treats Applications as an easier version of Analysis rather than a different course with different demands has not taught it recently.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask what they do about sign conventions in energetics, and how they coach the scientific investigation without touching the writing. A tutor who answers the second question with a clear boundary rather than a vague reassurance understands the academic honesty rules they are working under.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask how they teach uncertainty propagation, which is where Diploma Physics separates from IGCSE Physics and where most internal assessment marks are lost. A tutor who begins with content topics rather than with uncertainties and graphing has not diagnosed many Physics candidates.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask how they drill command terms. Biology marks turn on the difference between outline, explain, discuss and evaluate more than on conceptual difficulty, and a tutor without an explicit method for teaching that distinction is teaching content into a leaking bucket.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what they do with a student who scored highly at IGCSE First Language and is now struggling. The right answer names the change in task type, from directed writing to unseen analysis of a writer's choices, rather than suggesting more reading.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask how they select articles for the internal assessment commentaries. Article choice decides the achievable mark more than the writing does, and a tutor who has a method for judging whether an article can carry the required analysis has supervised real commentaries.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask when they start on the Higher Level pre-released case study. Months early is the correct answer; the final term is not. This single question separates tutors who plan around the assessment calendar from those who respond to it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Ask what the commonest failure is. The answer should be writing about the subject matter rather than about how knowledge in that area is produced and justified. Few tutors offer Theory of Knowledge at all, which makes it one of the easier places to find genuine expertise or its absence.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Ask at what stage they prefer to be involved. A tutor who wants to see the research question before any drafting understands where the grade is decided. One who offers to review a finished draft is offering the least valuable version of the service.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Language B and ab initio, plus first language
subjects.description: Ask which stream they teach and how they handle a student placed in the wrong one, which is a recurring issue in Al Ain. First-language and acquisition routes are assessed against different criteria and a tutor should be clear about which they work in.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Ask about pseudocode conventions and the solution-development internal assessment. A tutor who teaches in Python without reference to the board's own pseudocode expectations will produce correct code that loses marks, which is a specific and common failure.

al-ain/best-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a household sits in Al Ain affects the local pool and the practical lesson time. These notes are about availability and timing rather than about which district is nicer.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central and school-dense, so the local tutor pool is at its deepest here for common subjects. Even so, for Higher Level sciences the number of nearby specialists is small, and short school runs make an earlier slot possible.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: Close to United Arab Emirates University, so some households have direct academic contacts and better access to informal recommendations. Those recommendations still need checking against what the person has actually taught.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza
regions.note: South-west, with campuses on different curricula within a short drive, so families here are often judging a tutor and a school at the same time. A tutor who distinguishes the two questions is worth more than one who does not.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: Southern villa belt with long runs into the centre, which historically pushed families towards whichever tutor would travel. That constraint is what makes proximity-based choosing most costly here.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Older central district by the Al Ain Oasis, with longstanding schools nearby and a correspondingly larger pool of former teachers offering private lessons. Recency of teaching is the check that matters most in that group.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Western and heavily Emirati, with high demand for Arabic alongside Diploma subjects. Stream placement is the recurring issue, and a tutor should be able to say which stream they teach without hedging.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Near the hospital campus, where shift rotas mean reliability matters more than convenience. A fixed online slot survives a rota change; an arrangement depending on anyone travelling usually does not.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: Northern Al Ain near the Buraimi crossing, with some households crossing the border daily. Here the practical question is which tutor can hold an earlier fixed slot rather than who is nearest.

schoolClusters.city: Al Ain campuses running the Diploma
schoolClusters.note: The city's IB campuses, where most of the demand behind this search originates. Ask each school how many candidates sat each Higher Level subject in the last session, because the answer tells you how much subject-specific depth exists inside the school and therefore what you are actually buying from outside it.

schoolClusters.city: Al Ain campuses on other curricula
schoolClusters.note: Schools running international GCSE and A Levels or an Indian-curriculum stream. Families here sometimes search for an IB tutor because they are considering a move to the Diploma, which is a curriculum decision first and a tutoring decision second.

The output is a written statement of which component or criterion is losing marks and what the work should be. sections.heading: What the word best can and cannot mean in this market
paragraphs: There is no register of tutor quality in the UAE, no examining body that certifies tutor competence, and no published dataset against which any provider's claim to be the finest could be tested. That is not a gap this page can fill, and a page claiming to fill it would be doing the same thing as everyone else. What exists instead is a set of facts about an individual person that a parent can establish in an afternoon, and a set of behaviours in a lesson that are observable in forty minutes.

The research behind this page examined around sixty competitor pages across the UAE tutoring market, and the pattern in the claims is consistent. Several publish a star rating they awarded themselves, one showing two different review counts on a single page. Three publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in. Several list long rosters of schools as clients with no evident relationship, and one names a school that appears not to exist. Two offer to supply completed Internal Assessments, which is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than a service. These are not reasons to pick a different brand; they are reasons to stop treating claims as evidence.

The replacement is less satisfying and more useful. For each tutor you are considering, you want: what they have taught, at what level, under which board or programme, and how recently; whether they hold the work permit the UAE requires; what they do in the first ten minutes of a lesson; what they send you afterwards; and what they say when asked what they cannot do. Every one of those is checkable. None of them is a superlative.
The table below sets the common claims beside what could actually substantiate them, which is the quickest way to see how little most of them carry.

sections.heading: Six checks a parent can make without specialist knowledge
paragraphs: None of the following requires any understanding of the subject. They are process checks, and they separate a serious arrangement from a casual one more reliably than any discussion of pedagogy. Run them on every tutor you consider, including the one this page would otherwise be selling you.

The first is specificity of experience. Ask which exact course and level the tutor has taught, under which programme or board, and in which years. The useful answer sounds like Higher Level Chemistry under the current guide, most recently last session. An unhelpful answer sounds like all sciences up to university level. The second is recency, which is a separate question and frequently the weaker one: a tutor who last taught the current Diploma guide four revisions ago is working from memory of a different course.

The third is the permit, covered in full in the next section. The fourth is the written record: ask what arrives after each lesson and ask to see a sample. A tutor who sends a short note naming what was covered, what was set and what the student found difficult is producing the only evidence a parent has, and the absence of that note is why families cannot tell in March whether five months of tuition achieved anything. The fifth is the review mechanism: ask what event triggers a review and what happens if the targeted component has not moved. The honest answer involves changing the approach or ending the arrangement.

The sixth is the one most parents skip. Ask what the tutor cannot do. A tutor who names limits credibly, including that they will not touch assessed coursework, that they cannot promise a grade, and that they would not be the right match for a particular profile, is demonstrating the judgement you are actually hiring. A tutor whose answer is that they can handle anything has told you that they do not distinguish between cases.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child permitted to do it?
paragraphs: This is the check almost no listing answers and almost no parent makes, and it is the only one with a legal dimension. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

The application route is published. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the Ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere official, so no amount is quoted on this page, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source.

Two points follow for an Al Ain family in particular. Because the permit is free and takes two working days, a tutor who does not hold one has no cost-based excuse for it. And because Al Ain sits in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, there is a further consideration: press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff are barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

The practical consequence is that the common Al Ain arrangement of quietly engaging a child's own subject teacher for private lessons is the one arrangement this page will not recommend, independently of how good that teacher is. It places the teacher in a position their employer and the permit's code of conduct both address, and it gives the family no recourse if it goes wrong.

sections.heading: The trial lesson, used as an assessment rather than an introduction
paragraphs: Most families treat a trial lesson as a chance for the student to meet the tutor and for everyone to be pleasant. Used properly it is the single most informative forty minutes in the whole process, because it reveals how the tutor thinks under conditions nobody can prepare for. The way to use it is to send the student in with a specific piece of marked work and to watch what the tutor does with it.

The first ten minutes carry most of the signal. A tutor who spends them asking what the student can already do, reading the marked script, and asking why a particular answer was written the way it was, is diagnosing. A tutor who spends them teaching a topic from the start is guessing, however well they teach it. A tutor who spends them describing their own qualifications is selling. Those three openings predict the next six months more accurately than any profile.

Three further things are worth watching. Does the tutor name a component, a criterion or a command term at any point? Diploma and MYP work both turn on that vocabulary, and its complete absence means the tutor is working from content alone. Does the tutor let the student speak? A session where the tutor talks for thirty-five of forty minutes is a lecture, and a student who is already lost will stay lost through it. And at the end, does the tutor say something specific about what they think is wrong, or something general about potential?

Afterwards, ask the student one question and nothing else: did you understand something today that you did not understand yesterday. Parents tend to ask whether the student liked the tutor, which is worth knowing but is a different variable, and a likeable tutor who changes nothing is the commonest way a year of tuition passes without result.

sections.heading: Best for whom? Four profiles that need different tutors
paragraphs: The question behind this search is usually not which tutor is strongest in the abstract, but which tutor fits the student in front of you. Four profiles cover most Al Ain enquiries, and the right tutor is materially different in each. Matching the profile is where most of the available gain sits, and it costs nothing to get right.

The first profile is the capable student losing marks on technique. Grades sit a band below what the classwork suggests, and the losses are in timing, command terms and unshown method. This student needs a tutor who marks to the official scheme and drills question types, not one who re-teaches content, and the engagement should be short and intense rather than year-long.

The second is the student with a genuine content gap, usually accumulated over more than a year and often starting with a topic missed during a move between schools or systems. This student needs patient sequential teaching and a tutor willing to go back further than feels comfortable. The third is the coursework-stalled student, whose papers are adequate and whose internal assessment or Extended Essay is late and unfocused. This one needs a supervisor rather than a teacher: someone who questions a research question and a method, and refuses to write anything.

The fourth is the student in the wrong course or at the wrong tier, which in Al Ain is more common than elsewhere because small cohorts mean fewer chances to correct it. This student does not primarily need tutoring at all; they need an honest external assessment of fit, which may conclude that a course change is the answer and that a year of tuition would be paying to postpone the real decision. A tutor willing to reach that conclusion is demonstrating exactly the judgement this page is about.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, without naming brands
paragraphs: Comparing brands is both unhelpful and unfair, because the variation within any model is larger than the variation between models. Comparing models is useful, because each has a structural tendency that affects what a parent gets. Five models cover the market an Al Ain family will meet, and knowing their tendencies tells you which questions matter for each.

An agency selects and manages tutors and charges a margin for that work, so the question to ask is how the selection is done and who replaces a tutor when the match fails. A marketplace lists tutors and lets parents choose, so the price is often lower and the selection burden falls entirely on the parent; the question is what verification the platform performs. An independent freelance tutor offers the most direct relationship and the least recourse, so the questions are about the permit, references and what happens during an absence.

A tuition centre with premises offers group classes at a lower price per student and operates under a different regulatory regime: an operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the emirate regulator for a training institute, which is a specific thing and not something any individual tutor holds. For a Diploma student a group class is rarely the right format, because the losses are individual. School-provided support is usually the cheapest and best-aligned option and is frequently underused; ask what the school already offers before buying anything, since the answer is sometimes sufficient.

sections.heading: Does a higher rate mean a better tutor?
paragraphs: Not reliably, and the published spread shows why. UAE tutoring rates range from roughly AED 33 an hour to AED 650, a factor of nearly twenty, across a market with no quality register and no standard credential. Budget online tutoring from university students is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one with travel runs roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting 180 to 350 and independent home tutors 200 to 500. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

Two things in that spread are not quality signals. The first is travel: a visiting rate includes the tutor's road time, so a large part of an in-home premium buys movement rather than teaching, and in a city as spread out as Al Ain that share is higher than in a dense coastal district. The second is positioning. A premium rate can reflect scarcity, a claimed credential or simply a decision about market position, and none of those three is the same as teaching quality for your particular child's problem.

What does correlate with usefulness is specificity. A tutor at AED 200 who has taught your child's exact Higher Level option under the current guide within the last two sessions is likely to be more useful than one at AED 450 who teaches the subject group broadly. The highest-return hours in the Diploma are coursework supervision hours, and they are not the most expensive ones. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support, which is the band most Al Ain Diploma families end up in for one subject.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, and the AED figures above are the market, attributed, rather than a price list. The next step is a trial lesson at no charge once a tutor has been matched to the named course and level: one introductory session, nothing charged, no card required to book it. Then a quote against the actual course rather than against a general subject.

sections.heading: What no tutor can promise, and what is not claimed here
paragraphs: No tutor can promise a grade, a point total or a university place, and anyone who does is making a commercial representation they cannot honour. Examination outcomes depend on the student's own work over two years, on components settled months before the papers, and on boundaries set after the marking. A tutor can change the odds and can remove specific identifiable losses. That is a real service, and it is a different sentence from a promise.

Nor can a tutor influence a forecast grade, obtain papers or boundaries in advance, or produce any part of assessed work. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own, and a finding of academic misconduct removes the Diploma award independently of any point total. Providers offering completed Internal Assessments exist in this market and one publishes a price for them; that is not a service a family should buy at any price, because the cost falls on the student's own result.

What IB Gram does not claim is worth stating plainly on a page about judging providers. There is no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. No star rating, review count or success statistic appears on this site, because a figure we award ourselves is not evidence. No named school is a client or a partner. No IB or board syllabus document, past paper or mark scheme is distributed; the official sites hold those.

Finally, coverage. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service available only in India. Where a UAE-based specialist covers the course, that is the first match offered. Where none is free at the level needed, which in Al Ain happens most often in Higher Level sciences, Higher Level Computer Science and the less common languages, the match comes from the wider tutor pool at Gulf Standard Time, and that is said before any lesson is booked rather than discovered afterwards.

process.title: Write down the problem before contacting anyone
process.description: One paragraph: the course and level, the component or criterion where marks are being lost, what the last marked assessment said, and the next date that matters. A specific problem attracts a specific match, and it also exposes any provider whose first response does not engage with it.

process.title: Run the six checks on every candidate
process.description: Specificity of course and level taught, recency, the private tuition work permit, the written record after each lesson, the review trigger, and the stated limits. Fifteen minutes per tutor, no subject knowledge required, and it eliminates most of the field before any money changes hands.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as an assessment
process.description: One introductory session at no charge, once a tutor is matched to the named course, with no card required to book it. Send the student in with a specific marked script and watch the first ten minutes. Diagnosing, teaching or selling: the opening predicts the next six months.

process.title: Agree the review trigger in advance
process.description: Name the assessment that will tell you whether this is working, and agree what happens if the targeted component has not moved. An arrangement with no agreed end condition tends to continue on habit, which is how families spend a year without being able to say what changed.

process.title: Reassess the match, not just the effort
process.description: If the component has not moved after a fair run, the first hypothesis should be that the diagnosis or the match was wrong rather than that the student needs more hours. Changing tutor is a normal event and should not require starting the whole process again.

whyPoints.title: A rubric instead of a claim
whyPoints.description: This page gives you checks you can apply to any tutor in Al Ain, including ones who have no connection to this platform. A method survives a change of provider; a superlative does not survive a single question.

whyPoints.title: No self-awarded numbers anywhere
whyPoints.description: There is no star rating, review count or success statistic on this site. Several providers in this market publish ratings they awarded themselves, one with two different review counts on the same page, and a figure like that tells you nothing about any individual tutor.

whyPoints.title: The permit question answered properly
whyPoints.description: The private tuition work permit, its legal basis, its two-year validity, the fact that it is free of charge and the official application route are all set out here. Almost no tutoring page in this market addresses it, and it is the only check with a legal dimension.

whyPoints.title: Profile matching over generic strength
whyPoints.description: A mark-scheme specialist and a patient sequential teacher are both excellent and suit opposite students. Most of the available gain in this decision comes from matching the profile, and it costs nothing to get right.
