faqs.question: What makes one IB tutor better than another for my child?
faqs.answer: Fit with the specific problem, far more than general strength. A student losing marks on timing and command terms needs a mark-scheme specialist who drills question types; a student with a two-year content gap needs a patient sequential teacher; a student with a stalled Internal Assessment needs a supervisor who questions method and writes nothing. Those are three different people and each would be the wrong choice for the other two cases. Identify which problem you have before judging anyone's credentials, because the credential only matters once the category is right.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective IB tutor in the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Six questions, none requiring subject knowledge. Which exact course and level have you taught, under which programme, and in which sessions? When did you last teach it? Do you hold the UAE private tuition work permit? What arrives after each lesson in writing, and may I see a sample? What event triggers a review of whether this is working? And what will you not do? The last one is the most informative, because a tutor who names limits credibly is showing the judgement you are hiring.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the private tuition work permit and how they obtained it. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is the Ministry's Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Because it is free and quick, there is no cost-based excuse for not holding one.

faqs.question: Is a former IB examiner worth paying more for?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only with two conditions. The status should be current or recent and evidenced for that specific individual rather than asserted about a roster, and the premium should buy something nameable. Useful answers include fluency in how mark schemes are applied and where candidates routinely lose marks on a particular component. Examiner status does not give access to unreleased papers, boundaries or marking in progress, and any suggestion that it does should end the conversation. For a content gap or a stalled Internal Assessment it is largely irrelevant.

faqs.question: How do I tell subject knowledge from teaching skill in a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Watch the first ten minutes and count who is talking. A tutor who reads the student's marked script, asks why a particular answer was written that way and establishes what the student can already do is teaching. A tutor who delivers an excellent explanation of a topic nobody asked about has demonstrated knowledge and nothing else. Then ask the student one question afterwards: did you understand something today that you did not understand yesterday. Whether the student liked the tutor is worth knowing, but it is a different variable.

faqs.question: Should I pick a tutor who already knows my child's Al Ain school?
faqs.answer: It helps at the margin and should not override course specificity. Knowing a school's internal deadlines, which teacher sets what and how the mocks are structured saves a little time and can be genuinely useful for coursework scheduling. It does not substitute for having taught the exact course at the exact level recently. In Al Ain, where Diploma cohorts are small and some Higher Level subjects have very few local candidates, insisting on school familiarity can mean choosing a non-specialist over a specialist, which is the wrong trade.

faqs.question: What are the warning signs in a tutoring advertisement?
faqs.answer: A star rating with no named, dated, countable reviews behind it, and especially two different review counts on one page. A promised grade outcome with no published refund terms. Claimed approval or accreditation from a regulator or examination board. Long lists of schools presented as clients. Any offer involving help with an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or coursework beyond feedback on the student's own writing. A non-UAE contact number as the only conversion path on a UAE page. Each of these is checkable in under a minute.

faqs.question: How many lessons before I can tell whether the match is working?
faqs.answer: Judge the diagnosis after one lesson and the result at the next marked assessment. After the first session you should know whether the tutor identified a specific component, criterion or habit, because that is a deliverable rather than a matter of time. The result takes longer and must be measured externally: the targeted component either moves on the next marked school assessment or it does not. Four to six weeks is usually a fair run. Judging by whether sessions feel productive is how families spend a year without evidence.

faqs.question: What should a tutor send me after each lesson?
faqs.answer: A short note, three or four sentences, naming what was covered, what was set, and what the student found difficult. That is the only record a parent has, and its absence is the main reason families cannot say in March whether five months of tuition achieved anything. Ask to see a sample before booking. A tutor who regards this as bureaucracy is telling you that your ability to evaluate the arrangement is not their concern, which is itself useful information about the arrangement.

faqs.question: Is a higher hourly rate in Al Ain evidence of a better tutor?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Published UAE rates run from roughly AED 33 to AED 650 an hour in a market with no quality register. Two large components of the spread are not quality: travel, since a visiting rate includes the tutor's road time and Al Ain is spread out, and positioning, which reflects a market decision rather than teaching quality. What does correlate with usefulness is specificity. A tutor at AED 200 who taught your child's exact Higher Level option last session is likely to beat one at AED 450 who covers the subject group broadly.

faqs.question: Can I change tutor without starting the whole process again?
faqs.answer: You should be able to, and the answer to this question before booking tells you a good deal about the arrangement. Ask who replaces a tutor if the match fails, how quickly, and whether the written record of what has been covered transfers to the next person. With a managed provider that replacement is part of what the margin pays for. With an independent tutor there is no recourse beyond ending the arrangement, which is not a reason to avoid independents but is a reason to keep your own record of what has been taught.

faqs.question: Should my child's own school teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: This page does not recommend it, independently of how good the teacher is. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain, are barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document. Beyond the rules, the arrangement leaves a family with no recourse if it goes wrong.

faqs.question: How do tutoring agencies, marketplaces and freelance tutors differ?
faqs.answer: In who selects the tutor and what recourse you have. An agency selects and manages, charging a margin for that work, so ask how selection is done and who replaces a failed match. A marketplace lists and lets you choose, which usually costs less and moves the selection burden to you, so ask what the platform verifies. A freelance tutor offers the most direct relationship and the least recourse, so the permit, references and absence cover are the questions. Variation within each model is larger than variation between them.

faqs.question: What can no IB tutor promise, however good?
faqs.answer: A grade, a point total or a university place. Outcomes depend on the student's own work across two years, on components settled months before the papers, and on boundaries set after marking. A tutor also cannot influence a forecast grade, obtain papers or boundaries in advance, or produce any part of assessed work. What a tutor can do is remove identifiable, specific losses and change the odds, which is a genuine service described honestly. Anyone offering a promise instead is making a representation they are not able to honour.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to be in Al Ain to teach my child well?
faqs.answer: No, and in Al Ain specifically the insistence often costs more than it gains. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so distance has no effect on the lesson itself. What distance affects is availability: with small local Diploma cohorts, the number of qualified specialists within driving distance for a particular Higher Level option can be very low or nil. Choosing locally for those subjects usually means choosing a non-specialist. For common subjects the local pool is deeper and the question matters much less.

Each works to the syllabus code your child's school has entered them for, marks timed scripts against the published criteria, and reports what changed rather than what was covered.

intro.heading: The word "best" is doing a lot of work in that search, so let us take it apart
paragraphs: There is no league table of IGCSE tutors in Al Ain. Nobody publishes one, no regulator ranks tutors, and any provider claiming the title is ranking itself. What does exist is a set of four genuinely different ways to buy IGCSE support in this city, each with a different price, a different output and a different failure mode. A parent who picks the right one of those four has done more for their child's grade than a parent who spends three weeks hunting for a mythical highest-placed individual on a list that was never compiled.

So this page is a comparison rather than a sales pitch. The four options are: a subject specialist working one-to-one; the after-school clinic or intervention group your child's school may already run at no extra cost; a holiday or weekend revision course at a tuition centre; and a marking-and-feedback arrangement where the student works alone and a teacher marks the output. A fifth sits alongside them for completeness, the in-home visiting tutor, which is what many parents picture when they start searching and which carries a travel cost nobody itemises.

Al Ain changes the arithmetic. The city sits 130 kilometres inland from Abu Dhabi island and is governed, like the rest of the emirate, by the Department of Education and Knowledge. Its private-school set is considerably smaller than the capital's, which means fewer schools, fewer option blocks per subject, and a local pool of qualified subject teachers that thins quickly once you ask for Physics, Chemistry, English Language criteria marking or Arabic as a first language. Proximity is cheap to advertise and expensive to deliver here.

The figures on this page are market figures. They come from rate tables published by other providers and from a 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey, each attributed where it is used, and they are quoted so that you can judge any quote you receive against the band it sits in. They are not an IB Gram price list. What IB Gram does publish is the model: one-to-one IGCSE tuition in Al Ain delivered over live video, a free trial lesson before anything is agreed, and a written note after each session saying what was marked and what moved. Treat every band below as a yardstick for the quote in front of you rather than as a figure to pay.

One more thing, said at the top because it changes what you should expect. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; sending a teacher to a residence is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for an Al Ain family happens over live video, one-to-one. That is a constraint and also the reason an Al Ain household can work with a Chemistry specialist who marks 0620 scripts weekly rather than with whoever is available within a twenty-minute drive of Falaj Hazza.

al-ain/best-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Al Ain families arrive at IGCSE from several directions, and leave it in two. These are the programmes the tutors on this page work across, with what each one means for a student in this city specifically.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The qualification most British-curriculum schools in Al Ain enter candidates for. Subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes - 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English - and several are tiered, with a Core paper set and an Extended paper set that lead to different grade ranges. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series each year for UAE centres, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the practical consequence is tier placement. A smaller cohort means a school may run a single teaching group for a subject and split the entry by tier late, so the paper your child will actually sit is often not settled when you start looking for a tutor. Ask the department, in writing, which code and which tier appears on the entry before you buy hours against the wrong syllabus.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board in common use, with its own codes — 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Content overlaps heavily with Cambridge, but paper structure, the number of papers, the tiering arrangements and the way practical skill is assessed differ enough that preparation material written for one board wastes time when used for the other.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain schools enter candidates for a mixture of boards across a student's subject set, which is why a parent can be told confidently by one teacher that the course is Cambridge and by another that it is Edexcel. Both can be true. Pearson publishes provisional and final timetables per series, so confirm the series, the board and the code for each subject individually rather than for the child as a whole.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, the two years before the IGCSE entry
programmes.description: The years in which the Core-or-Extended decision is quietly being made. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and many Al Ain schools use internal end-of-year results to stream students into the tier they will later be entered for. Support at this stage is cheaper than remedial work in Year 11 and targets something more durable: arithmetic fluency, writing at length, and the habit of answering the question that was asked.
programmes.countryNote: This is where an Al Ain family has the most leverage and usually spends the least. A student who reaches Year 10 secure in algebraic manipulation and able to write a structured paragraph has access to the Extended tier in every subject. One who does not may find the ceiling set for them by a streaming decision taken in Year 9 that nobody announced.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: Two routes, and the IGCSE grades decide which doors stay open. A Level programmes usually set subject-specific entry grades, often a 6 or 7 in the subject to be continued and sometimes a grade in Mathematics for the sciences. The IB Diploma asks for breadth across six groups plus the core, which rewards a balanced IGCSE profile rather than three strong subjects and three weak ones.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's post-16 provision is smaller than the capital's, so a student wanting a particular subject combination may be choosing between a school in the city, a daily commute towards Abu Dhabi, or a route the family had not considered. Work backwards from that decision when choosing which IGCSE subjects to support in Year 10, rather than treating all nine as equally important.

al-ain/best-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: The specialist premium is not the same in every subject. In some, a capable generalist with the mark scheme gets most of the way; in others, the marks sit in places only someone who has taught that paper repeatedly knows to look. These are the subjects Al Ain families most often ask about.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Wide content, stable from series to series, and marked largely objectively. The common loss is not knowledge but working: method marks dropped because a line of algebra was done in the head, and non-calculator fluency that has decayed. Tier placement matters more here than in any other subject, because the Core paper caps the achievable grade.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, and the paper that assesses practical skills, are where Al Ain candidates lose most. Circuit questions reward a method stated in order; descriptions of experiments reward naming the variable controlled and the measurement repeated. Both are trainable in a few sessions and both are routinely untrained.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Two different failure modes that need two different drills. Mole arithmetic fails on unit handling and on rounding too early. Organic chemistry fails on pathway recall, because students learn reactions as isolated facts rather than as routes between functional groups. A tutor who treats both as one problem fixes neither.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mostly recall, which makes it look easier than its grade distribution suggests. The extended-response marks turn on command words: a six-mark answer to "explain" that only describes will take two or three marks. Practising against the published mark scheme, rather than against a textbook, is what moves this subject.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Marked against criteria rather than against content, which is why well-written work still scores modestly. Directed writing needs the register and the audience the task specified; the reading summary is marked on selection and concision, not on elegance. Specialist marking has more effect here than extra reading does.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Essays are rewarded for argument and for close reference to the text, not for plot retelling. Al Ain candidates studying a set text alongside English as an additional language often know the book well and still underperform, because the essay structure and the quotation discipline were never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Evaluation marks sit in the last paragraph of a long answer and are the most commonly unwritten marks in the whole subject. Students explain thoroughly, then stop. A session spent entirely on how to close an eight-mark answer usually returns more than a session spent on content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Two halves that fail separately: theory, where answers need precise terminology, and programming, where students can produce working code and still lose marks for failing to explain it. Pseudocode conventions are examined, and Al Ain candidates often meet them for the first time in a paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and further topics
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Diploma Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. The content is a genuine step up, and it is the clearest early indicator of whether a student will cope with an HL maths course two years later.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Governed federally rather than by the exam board, and taught to a separate requirement that runs in parallel with the licensed curriculum. Al Ain families routinely tell us this is the hardest subject to find specialist support for locally, and the grade affects school reporting even where it sits outside the Ministry's five-subject equivalency count.

al-ain/best-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Al Ain families ask from, and what changes district by district
al-ain/best-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Al Ain is low-rise and spread out, and the practical difference between districts is the earliest hour a session can realistically start. These are the parts of the city families contact us from, with what each one tends to be asking about.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central, dense and close to several of the city's larger private schools, so school-run times are short and a 16:30 start is usually workable. Most enquiries here are single-subject: Mathematics or Physics, stuck a grade below target.

regions.name: Al Muwaiji
regions.note: Established residential district with a mix of villa households running three or four children through one evening. Enquiries tend to be about sequencing — which child gets the weekly hour this term — rather than about a single subject.

regions.name: Falaj Hazza
regions.note: Western Al Ain, with a longer run to the city's British-curriculum schools. Sessions here often start at 18:00 or later, which is one reason an online slot survives a traffic delay that a visiting tutor's appointment would not.

regions.name: Al Mutaredh
regions.note: Close to the centre and to Al Ain Oasis, with shorter commutes and families who tend to start earlier in Year 10 rather than in the final term. Questions here are more often about tier placement than about revision.

regions.name: Al Khabisi
regions.note: Residential and well served by school buses, which fixes arrival times and makes a standing weekly slot easy to hold. Common request: marking-only support for a disciplined Year 11 student who revises alone.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: Northern district near the Oman border crossing, where some households have a working parent commuting out of the city. Later sessions and weekend slots are the norm, and we are often asked whether a Friday morning hour is any use.

regions.name: Al Towayya
regions.note: Villa district with a short run to central schools. Enquiries skew towards sciences at Extended tier and towards the English Language criteria problem, which is the subject families are most surprised to need help with.

regions.name: Zakher
regions.note: Southern edge of the city, the longest drive to most private schools and the district where travel time most clearly favours a video lesson. Families here ask the most direct questions about whether anyone will actually turn up.

schoolClusters.city: Central and western Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: The city's longest-established private schools sit in this band, and between them they cover British, Indian and American curricula. Students we support attend schools across this group; the entry board and tier differ by department within a single school, so confirm both per subject.

schoolClusters.city: Newer developments and the city's outer ring
schoolClusters.note: Schools opened or expanded more recently, several running British curriculum through to post-16. Smaller cohorts here mean fewer option blocks, which is the single most common reason an Al Ain family looks outside the school for a subject specialist.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one or two subjects
modes.description: A standing slot in the same place every week, held for the academic year. The hour divides into reviewing the work set since the last session, teaching the next piece of content or technique, and setting a timed task to be marked before the next meeting. This is the shape that produces a visible record, because a parent can lay eight marked scripts side by side and see whether the same mark is still being lost.

modes.title: Marking and feedback only
modes.description: For the student who already revises without supervision. The tutor sets or agrees a paper, the student sits it to time, and the session is spent entirely on the marked script: where marks were lost, what the mark scheme actually rewarded, and what to repeat. It costs a fraction of weekly teaching because the teaching hours are the student's own, and it fails completely if the self-study habit is not already there.

modes.title: A short pre-series block
modes.description: Six to eight hours, concentrated in the weeks before a June or November series, aimed at technique rather than content. This is the right purchase when the content is broadly known and the marks are being lost in how answers are written: command words, working shown, evaluation unwritten, time mismanaged across a paper. It is the wrong purchase when a whole syllabus is missing, and we will say so at the trial.

sections.heading: Four ways to spend the same AED 1,500 on IGCSE support in Al Ain
paragraphs: Set a budget first and the question changes shape. Instead of asking who the best IGCSE tutor in Al Ain is, you are asking what AED 1,500 buys, and the answer varies by a factor of three depending on which of four products you buy. The table below prices each one at published market rates and states what each actually produces, which is the only comparison that helps.

The first option is a subject specialist working one-to-one. At the AED 200 to 270 band that Unitors publishes for IB tuition and TutorChase quotes for specialist work, AED 1,500 buys roughly six hours. Six hours is not a programme; it is enough to diagnose two or three recurring loss patterns and drill them. The second option costs nothing, because it is the intervention session your child's school may already run. Al Ain departments frequently offer these and parents frequently do not know, partly because they are announced once in a newsletter in September.

The third is a holiday or weekend course at a tuition centre, where EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 per hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both researched in October 2026. At those rates the same budget buys fifteen to twenty group hours, which covers a syllabus broadly and diagnoses nothing. The fourth is marking only: the student works alone and buys a teacher's judgement every fortnight. It is the cheapest per unit of movement and the most dependent on a habit that may not exist.

A fifth sits alongside for completeness. The visiting in-home tutor is what many parents picture first, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors charging AED 200 to 500 once travel is inside the number. In a city as spread out as Al Ain that travel element is real and is paid for by somebody. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the comparison here is honest rather than self-serving: it is in the table because you will be quoted for it elsewhere.

sections.heading: Marked work is the discriminator, and almost nobody asks about it
paragraphs: If you ask one question of a prospective IGCSE tutor in Al Ain, make it this: who marks the practice paper, and against what? The answers divide the field faster than any qualification does. A tutor who marks the script themselves, against the board's published assessment criteria, and can tell you which mark was lost and why, is doing the thing that moves grades. A tutor who sets a paper, takes it away, and returns a percentage has given you a number you already had from the school.

The reason this matters is arithmetic. IGCSE grades move in raw marks, not in percentages, and the raw marks cluster in predictable places. In Physics it is method marks on circuit and calculation questions, and the experimental-description marks on the practical paper. In English Language it is the directed-writing criteria for audience and register. In Economics it is evaluation. A tutor who marks weekly sees the same three marks going missing and builds the term around them. A tutor who teaches content for an hour a week may never see the student's written output at all.

There is a second-order benefit. Marked scripts are the only evidence a parent can read without specialist knowledge. You do not need to know the 0620 syllabus to see that in week one a student lost four method marks on moles and in week eight lost one. That is why the sessions described on this page always produce a marked artefact, and why the written note after each hour names the mark rather than the topic.

A caution that belongs here. Published mark schemes and past papers are the property of the awarding bodies, and reproducing or redistributing them is not something a tutor should be doing. Working from material the school has issued, or from resources the board itself makes available through the proper channel, is the correct route. If a provider offers you a library of downloadable papers and mark schemes as a selling point, that is a question about their judgement, not a feature.
bullets: Ask who marks, against what, and how quickly the script comes back
Expect the mark lost to be named, not the topic covered
Eight marked scripts across a term are readable evidence for a non-specialist

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects actually reward a specialist, and which do not
paragraphs: The phrase "specialist tutor" is used as though it meant the same thing in every subject. It does not. In some IGCSE subjects a capable graduate working carefully from the mark scheme gets a student most of the way. In others the marks sit in places that only repeated contact with that specific paper reveals, and a generalist will teach the content correctly and still leave the grade where it was.

Mathematics is the clearest case of the first kind. The content is wide, stable and objectively marked, and the usual problem is working shown rather than knowledge held. What matters far more in Mathematics is tier placement: a candidate entered for the Core paper set has a ceiling, and an enthusiastic tutor teaching Extended content to a Core-entered student is wasting the family's money in the most frustrating way available.

Physics, Chemistry and English Language sit at the other end. In Physics the practical-skills paper is marked on a specific vocabulary of control, repetition and measurement that students do not pick up by osmosis. In Chemistry the two major loss areas fail by different mechanisms and need different drills. In English Language the marking is criterion-based, which is why a well-written piece of work can score modestly and a parent reading it cannot see why. These are the subjects where asking how many of these papers the tutor has marked is a fair and useful question.

Arabic as a first language deserves separate mention. It runs alongside the licensed curriculum as a federal requirement rather than as an exam-board subject, the teaching requirements are set centrally, and Al Ain families tell us consistently that it is the hardest subject to resource locally. sections.heading: Cost per grade movement, rather than cost per hour
paragraphs: Hourly rate is the wrong unit, and it is the only one most providers publish. A tutor at AED 150 an hour who needs thirty hours to shift a grade costs more than one at AED 270 who needs twelve. Neither can be known in advance with confidence, but the shape of a plan can be priced, and comparing plans rather than rates is how a family avoids buying the cheapest hour repeatedly for a year.

Four plan shapes cover most of what Al Ain families actually buy. A short pre-series block of six hours, aimed at technique. A full academic year at one hour a week, aimed at content plus technique with enough time to re-test each repair. A two-year arrangement across Years 10 and 11 at two hours a week, which is the only shape that reliably changes working habit as well as grades. And marking only, which prices the teacher's judgement and nothing else.

The table prices each at the market bands already quoted, and states what a block of that size realistically repairs. Read the last column harder than the third. A six-hour block will not close a two-year content gap in Chemistry, and any provider who implies otherwise six weeks before a series is selling hope. Equally, a family who commits to thirty-six hours for a student whose only problem is that they never write to time has bought thirty hours they did not need.

What nobody can price is the outcome, and this page will not pretend otherwise. No tutor can promise a grade, and a provider who offers a promise of grade movement in writing is making a claim they cannot stand behind. What is honest to say is that the loss patterns above are diagnosable within one session, that most are trainable, and that the record of whether training worked is in the marked scripts rather than in anybody's testimonial.

sections.heading: Reading your school's inspection judgement before you hire anybody
paragraphs: Private schools in Al Ain are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. Inspection reports are published, use a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and are one of the few genuinely free sources of information a parent has before spending anything on tuition.

The headline band is the least useful part. A school judged Good overall can contain a Mathematics department that is a clear strength and a Physics department identified as needing improvement, and the detail that tells you which is in the body of the report rather than in the grade on the cover. A parent reading at subject level sometimes discovers that the gap they were about to pay a tutor to close is a gap the school has already named and already has a plan for.

Two further things to check. First, the date. An inspection judgement describes the school as it was on the inspection dates, and a department can be rebuilt in two years. Second, whether the report comments on the phase your child is actually in; strong primary provision tells you very little about how Year 11 candidates are prepared for an Extended-tier entry.

The table sets out what each band generally describes, what it does not tell you, and the question worth asking next. Use it as a filter on your own spending. If the report says the sciences are a strength and your child is three grades below target in Chemistry, the problem is more likely to be specific to your child than to the teaching, which changes what a tutor is for.

sections.heading: What a first hour should tell you about your child's paper
paragraphs: A trial lesson is an assessment, and the thing being assessed is the tutor. By the end of a first hour with a recent script in front of them, a competent IGCSE teacher should be able to tell you four things, in plain language, without hedging. Which board and code the work belongs to. Whether the entry looks like Core or Extended. Where the marks went, named by mark rather than by topic. And what the first three weeks would do about it.

The fourth is the one that separates people. "We will build confidence and cover the syllabus" is not a plan. "The first three weeks are mole calculations with units written on every line, then two timed six-mark questions a week marked against the criteria, then a full Paper 2 in week four" is a plan, and it is falsifiable, which is what makes it worth buying. You will know in a month whether it worked.

Ask also what the tutor will not do. The honest answer includes a refusal to be the author of any assessed work, a refusal to supply board materials they should not be distributing, and a refusal to promise a grade. For Al Ain families, add one more: ask what happens if your child's school turns out to have entered them for a different board than you were told. A tutor who says they would re-plan around the actual code is telling you something true about how they work.

IB Gram runs the first lesson free, with no payment taken before it, precisely so that this assessment is possible. If the diagnosis in that hour is that the problem is not a tutoring problem — a student who needs to be reading, or sleeping, or sitting fewer subjects — we will say so, and there is nothing to cancel.
bullets: Board, code and tier identified from the script, not from the parent
Marks named, not topics listed

sections.heading: The terms of the arrangement: cancellation, replacement, records and your child's data
paragraphs: This is the part of choosing a tutor that nobody enjoys and everybody wishes they had done. Four things are worth settling in writing before the second lesson, and all four are cheap to agree at the start and expensive to argue about in April.

Cancellation and rescheduling. Al Ain school calendars produce clashes — mock weeks, trips, the series itself — and a sensible arrangement lets a family move a slot with reasonable notice rather than forfeit it. Replacement. If the tutor becomes unavailable mid-block, you want to know in advance whether you are matched with somebody else at the same rate, and whether the marked-work record travels with the student. Records. Agree that the error log and marked scripts belong to the family and are handed over on request.

And data. Lead forms and tuition arrangements collect personal information about a minor: name, school, year group, grades, sometimes a timetable. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how that information is handled, and a provider should be able to tell you plainly what they collect, why, how long they keep it and how to have it deleted. Nobody needs a photograph of your child or a copy of their report card to arrange a first lesson.

A related point about recordings. Some providers record sessions by default. That can be genuinely useful for revision, and it is also a file containing a minor's voice and image sitting on somebody's server. Ask whether recording happens, who can access it, and how to switch it off. The answer should be immediate and specific.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for teaching your child in Al Ain
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit – Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, and states a two-working-day completion time.

Two consequences follow for an Al Ain family. The first is that asking about the permit is not an awkward question. It is free and takes two working days, so a tutor who has not obtained one has chosen not to, and that is information. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so anybody quoting you a figure is guessing.

The second concerns your child's own teachers. In Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain, professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. That is press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication before relying on it — but the direction is clear enough that "your child's own teacher, privately" is not an arrangement to go looking for.

A final distinction that matters. An individual tutor holding a permit is a different legal animal from a business with premises and staff, which needs an educational services permit of its own from the relevant authority. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none; what it does is match families with tutors and deliver lessons over video. Any provider telling you their tutors carry a regulator's seal of approval is describing something that does not exist in the form they are implying.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the line a tutor works inside
paragraphs: IGCSE subjects carry coursework and practical components in several cases, and every one of them must be the student's own work. The boundary is not subtle, and it is worth stating because two providers found in this market sell the other side of it. A tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, question a draft, point at a weak paragraph and ask what the student meant, and mark a timed task. A tutor may not be the author of any part of assessed work, and a parent should walk away from anyone who offers to be.

The practical test is simple: could your child explain every sentence in the submitted piece and defend the choices behind it to their teacher? If the honest answer is no, the work is not theirs, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the person who typed it. Awarding bodies treat authorship breaches as malpractice, and the outcome can affect an entire entry rather than a single component.

The same principle governs materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the awarding bodies. The right way to work with them is to reference them, cite the official page, and use what the school has legitimately issued. Offering a downloadable archive of them is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is worse than that.

Say the boundary out loud to your tutor in the first session. In our experience it changes the arrangement for the better: the student stops asking for sentences and starts asking for criteria, which is the skill the component was designed to assess in the first place.

sections.heading: How lessons actually run from Al Ain, and the home-tutor question answered straight
paragraphs: Every lesson for an Al Ain family runs over live video, one-to-one, at a time set in Gulf Standard Time. The student needs a device with a camera, a stable connection, paper and a pen, and the same desk each week. Written work is photographed or scanned and shared before the session so the tutor has marked it in advance, which is what makes the hour about the marks rather than about reading.

Many parents start by searching for someone to visit. It is worth saying plainly why this page does not offer that. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that is an India-only service — and pretending otherwise would waste your time. What the online format buys in a city like Al Ain is access: the pool of people who can mark 0625 practical papers weekly is not the pool of people who live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mutaredh, and in a smaller city those two sets barely overlap.

There are things a screen does worse, and they belong in this section rather than in a footnote. A tutor on video cannot supervise a reluctant fifteen-year-old into opening a book, cannot handle laboratory apparatus, and cannot read a room the way a person sitting at the same table can. Where supervision is the actual need, the market option in the comparison table is the honest recommendation, and we will say so at the trial rather than after it.

What the format does well is everything that depends on marked work arriving on time and a specialist being available at 19:00 on a Tuesday. For the majority of Al Ain enquiries we receive — one or two subjects, a grade below target, a series in June — that is the whole of the job.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the subject-count rule one ranking page gets wrong
paragraphs: IGCSE grades are not only a school matter in the UAE; they feed the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which is what converts a foreign school certificate into something a UAE institution can act on. The British-track requirements have been published clearly, and they are worth knowing before Year 10 subject choices are made rather than after results day.

For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last clause matters: one page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published requirement says.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry and the relevant attestation authority, not by any tutoring provider, and nobody should present it as something they perform or guarantee on your behalf. And there is no IB points threshold quoted anywhere on this page, because the figures circulating for it have not been read on the Ministry's own site; the British-track numbers above have a published source, the IB one does not.

The useful action for an Al Ain family is small and specific. Count the subjects on your child's entry that could land at grade E or 3 or above, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, and check that the number is comfortably above five rather than exactly five. If it is exactly five, one bad series becomes an administrative problem as well as an academic one, and that is a reason to support a subject you had written off.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we say when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You send the subject, the board and code if you know it, the year group, the target grade and the two or three windows in the week that genuinely work. We come back with a tutor and a time, or with an honest statement that we cannot cover that subject at that level this week. The first lesson is free and is a diagnostic, and nothing is taken before it.

The availability question deserves a straight answer, because no competitor in this market gives one. Core IGCSE subjects — Mathematics, the three sciences, English Language, Economics, Business Studies, Computer Science — are generally coverable within a few days at the levels Al Ain families ask for. Less common requests take longer: Arabic as a first language, a second modern language at first-language standard, and some of the arts subjects. When we cannot cover something, the useful thing we can still do is tell you where the gap is so you look in the right place rather than waiting.

If the series is six weeks away and the gap is two years wide, we will say that too. A short block can repair technique and it cannot install a syllabus, and a family who spends AED 1,600 believing otherwise has been sold something. The better conversation in that situation is about which subjects to protect, whether a November entry is the sensible route, and what the student can realistically carry.

What you should expect from the arrangement if it goes ahead: a standing weekly slot, a timed task between sessions, a marked script and a written note each week, and a review at week six where the three of us look at the evidence and decide whether to continue. That review is the point at which an honest provider is willing to tell you to stop.

process.title: Send the script, not just the subject
process.description: A photograph of a recent marked paper or school assessment tells us more in thirty seconds than a paragraph of description. It shows the board, usually the tier, the handwriting under time pressure, and where the marks went. Add the year group, the target grade and the two windows in the week that genuinely work.

process.title: We match on the paper, not on the postcode
process.description: Because lessons run over video, the question is who marks that specific paper well rather than who lives near Al Jimi. We come back with a named tutor, their subject and level coverage, and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time — or with a straight statement that we cannot cover it this week.

process.title: A free diagnostic first lesson
process.description: One hour, no payment taken beforehand, with the script in front of both of them. The output is a short written diagnosis: board and code, apparent tier, the two or three marks being lost repeatedly, and a three-week plan specific enough to be proved wrong by week four.

process.title: Weekly work, marked before the session
process.description: A timed task every week, sat to the real time limit, photographed and sent ahead. The tutor marks it against the published criteria before the hour starts, so the lesson is spent on the marks rather than on reading. A written note follows each session naming what moved.

process.title: The week-six review
process.description: Parent, student and tutor look at six marked scripts and the error log together and answer one question: is the same mark still going missing? If it is, the plan changes or the match does. If the evidence says tutoring is not the bottleneck, we say so and the arrangement ends there.

Video delivery means the subject decides the match. That is the single concrete advantage of the format, and it is the reason for it.

whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, a per-topic error log and a written note after each session. You do not need the syllabus to see whether the same four method marks are still being lost in week eight. Progress claims on this site are built from that record rather than from testimonials.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark and give feedback. They are never the author of assessed work, and they do not distribute board materials they should not be distributing. One operator in this market sells completed coursework; knowing where the line sits is a reason to choose carefully rather than quickly.

whyPoints.description: If the subject is not coverable this week, if six weeks is not enough for the gap, or if the diagnosis is that the problem is not a tutoring problem, you will be told at the trial rather than after a term of invoices. That is cheaper for you and sustainable for us.

faqs.question: How do I tell a strong IGCSE tutor in Al Ain from a confident one?
faqs.answer: Ask who marks the practice paper and against what. A strong tutor marks it themselves, against the board's published criteria, and tells you which mark was lost rather than which topic was weak. Then ask for a three-week plan specific enough to be wrong: "two timed six-mark questions a week, marked against the criteria, then a full paper in week four" is checkable, while "build confidence and cover the syllabus" is not. Finally ask what they refuse to do. An honest answer includes never being the author of assessed work and never promising a grade.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE tutor be able to tell me after one hour with my child's paper?
faqs.answer: Four things, without hedging. Which board and syllabus code the work belongs to. Whether the entry looks like Core or Extended. Where the marks actually went, named mark by mark rather than topic by topic. And what the first three weeks would do about it. If a tutor cannot identify the board from a script, or describes the problem only as a confidence issue, the diagnosis has not happened. The first lesson exists so that you can make this judgement before any money changes hands, which is why it is free and why no payment is taken before it.

faqs.question: Is a specialist worth the extra AED 100 an hour for IGCSE Physics?
faqs.answer: In Physics, usually yes. The practical-skills paper and the electricity topics are marked on a specific written method — naming the controlled variable, stating the repeat, setting out circuit reasoning in order — and students do not acquire that vocabulary by covering content again. Someone who has marked 0625 or 4PH1 papers repeatedly knows where those marks go. In Mathematics the premium is far smaller, because the marking is more objective and the common problem is working shown rather than knowledge held. The honest answer differs by subject, which is why this page prices the premium subject by subject rather than quoting one rate.

faqs.question: Which is better value in Al Ain, weekly one-to-one or a holiday revision course?
faqs.answer: They buy different things. At the AED 33 to 65 per-head group band published by Tutopiya and EdFlik in October 2026, a holiday course gives you fifteen to twenty hours of syllabus coverage and a cohort to pace against, which suits a student behind on content across a whole subject. Weekly one-to-one at the AED 200 to 270 specialist band buys diagnosis: six hours that identify and drill two or three specific loss patterns. If you do not know why the grade is stuck, buy the diagnosis first. Coverage without diagnosis often repeats what the student already knows.

faqs.question: Does my child's school in Al Ain already run the support I am about to pay for?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and parents frequently do not know. Departments in Al Ain schools often run after-school clinics, intervention groups or coursework surgeries, announced once in September and then assumed to be common knowledge. They cost nothing beyond fees already paid, they are run by the teachers who know which tier your child is entered for, and they use departmental mark schemes. Email the head of department and ask directly what is available and who attends. If the gap is content rather than individual technique, this is the first thing to use and the last thing most families check.

faqs.question: What does a published school inspection band actually tell me about my child's subject?
faqs.answer: Less than you would hope, and the detail that helps is inside the report rather than on its cover. A school judged Good overall can hold a Mathematics department that is a named strength and a science department identified as needing improvement. Read at subject level, check the phase the comments refer to, and check the date, because a department can be rebuilt in two years. Published reports from the Department of Education and Knowledge are free and are one of the few pieces of evidence a parent has before spending anything on tuition.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should we actually buy tutoring for at once?
faqs.answer: One or two, in almost every case. A student carrying nine subjects has roughly fifteen hours of homework and revision a week to distribute, and adding three weekly tutoring hours to that does not add three hours of capacity. Pick the subjects where the gap between current and target grade is widest and the loss pattern is clearly diagnosable, and protect the rest with the school's own support. Families who buy four subjects at once usually end up attending six sessions and completing the set work for two of them, which is the most expensive way to make no progress.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE tutor mark my child's past papers against the official mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Marking against the published criteria is exactly what a tutor should be doing, and it is the activity that moves grades most reliably. What a tutor should not be doing is supplying you with a library of downloadable papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because those documents belong to the awarding bodies. The correct route is to work with material the school has legitimately issued, or resources the board itself makes available through the proper channel, and to reference official pages rather than reproduce them. A provider advertising an archive of board materials as a feature is telling you something about their judgement.

faqs.question: What happens to our sessions if the tutor we are matched with becomes unavailable?
faqs.answer: Agree this before the second lesson rather than in April. The three things worth settling in writing are whether you are rematched at the same rate, how quickly, and whether the marked-work record and error log travel with the student to the new tutor. That record is the reason a replacement does not start from zero: a new tutor reading eight marked scripts and a per-topic error log knows more about your child's paper in twenty minutes than a diagnostic session would tell them. Ask for the same clarity on notice periods for moving a session.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start IGCSE tutoring in January for a June series?
faqs.answer: For technique, no. Five months at an hour a week is thirty-two to thirty-six hours, which is enough to diagnose and drill the recurring loss patterns, build a timed-paper habit and re-test each repair. For a two-year content gap in a subject like Chemistry, January is tight and the honest plan involves triage rather than coverage: protect the subjects that are nearly there, decide which one gets the hours, and consider whether a November entry is the sensible route for the weakest. Anyone promising a full syllabus rebuild in that window is selling hope.

faqs.question: Do you send an IGCSE tutor to our house in Al Ain, or is everything online?
faqs.answer: Everything for UAE families runs online, one-to-one, over live video at times set in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. The market option exists and is priced in the comparison table on this page at the AED 180 to 350 band Bestimate publishes for in-home visits, so you can weigh it fairly. What video delivery buys in a city of Al Ain's size is access: the specialist who marks your child's specific paper weekly rarely lives within driving distance.

faqs.question: What personal information do you need about my child before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Very little, and you should expect any provider to justify every field. The subject, the board and code if known, the year group, the target grade and the times that work are enough to arrange a diagnostic lesson. A photograph of a recent marked script helps the diagnosis. Nobody needs a copy of a full report card, a passport, a photograph of your child or their home address to book an hour. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs how personal data is handled, and a provider should state plainly what they collect, why, how long they keep it and how to have it deleted.

faqs.question: How do I check that an IGCSE tutor is legally allowed to charge us for lessons?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE's own service page states a two-working-day completion time, and the eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because it is free and quick, a tutor without one has chosen not to apply. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with scepticism.

faqs.question: Can we hire one of my child's own teachers from their Al Ain school privately?
faqs.answer: It is not an arrangement to go looking for. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi, which includes Al Ain, have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the private tuition permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Those reports are press accounts rather than readings of the current policy document, so verify against the authority's own publication before relying on the detail. The direction is clear enough that a provider marketing your child's own teacher privately is a reason for caution.

faqs.question: For an Al Ain leaver, how many IGCSE grades does the equivalency file actually need?
faqs.answer: Five. British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A further requirement applies at the next stage: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for UAE tutoring searches states six subjects, which is not what the published requirement says. Verify your own case on the Ministry's own pages, since no tutoring provider performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: What should we do if the tutoring is not working after six weeks?
faqs.answer: Look at the evidence rather than at how the sessions feel. Lay out the six marked scripts and the error log and ask one question: is the same mark still going missing? If it is, something specific is wrong — the wrong loss pattern was targeted, the set work is not being done, or the match is poor — and each has a different remedy. A tutor unwilling to hold that review, or who answers it with general reassurance, has told you what you needed to know. Sometimes the honest conclusion is that tutoring was not the bottleneck, and stopping is the right call.

al-ain/best-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a diagnosis, then decide what to buy
al-ain/best-igcse-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step is not choosing a tutor; it is finding out what is actually wrong. If the conclusion is that the school's own clinic, a group course or nothing at all is the better purchase, we will tell you that instead. Nothing is taken before the first lesson.

intro.heading: What a 0606 tutor in Al Ain is actually for
paragraphs: Additional Mathematics 0606 is the Cambridge IGCSE that families only discover once their child is already in it. A Year 11 student in an Al Ain private school sits 0580 Extended, does well, and is entered for 0606 alongside it because the maths department thinks they can carry both. Then the topic list arrives: radians instead of degrees, the factor theorem, laws of logarithms, nCr and nPr, differentiation and integration. None of it is an extension of what 0580 taught. It is new material, examined formally, in two timed papers with no coursework to cushion a bad morning.

That is the gap a Cambridge IGCSE Additional Maths 0606 tutor in Al Ain is hired to close, and it is a narrow, technical gap rather than a general confidence problem. A student who cannot differentiate a quotient is not lacking motivation. They have missed a rule, or they learned it in a crowded double period in week three of term and nobody has gone back over it since. One-to-one teaching is unusually efficient on material like this, because the diagnosis is specific and the fix is a method practised to the point of being automatic.

Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, so its private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge rather than by Dubai's KHDA. The practical consequence for your family is a smaller private-school set than Abu Dhabi island carries, and a correspondingly smaller pool of adults within driving distance who have taught 0606 to examination standard. Additional Mathematics is a minority entry in most schools. The teacher who covers it may be the only person on campus who does.

IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. On a subject this specialised that is the point rather than a compromise. An Al Ain family gets the person who has taught 0606 for years and marks to the scheme, instead of whoever happens to live twenty minutes away and is willing to try. Lessons are set in Gulf Standard Time and fitted around the school run, prayer times and the mock calendar your child's school actually uses.

The pages that rank for this query tend to stop at a subject list and a contact form. This one does the opposite. Below you will find the 0606 topic areas mapped to where marks go missing, a straight comparison with 0580 Extended, the Cambridge calendar counted backwards from a published set of key dates, and what the Al Ain market charges per hour with every figure attributed to whoever published it. If you read nothing else, read the calendar section: entry deadlines sit months before the paper, and that is the single most expensive thing for a family to learn late.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-.programmesIntro: Most families arriving on this page are inside Cambridge IGCSE, but the reason 0606 was chosen usually sits one stage further on. These are the programmes our Al Ain students are working within, and what Additional Mathematics does for each of them.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge IGCSE course, assessed entirely by terminal written papers in most subjects. Additional Mathematics 0606 sits alongside Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier rather than replacing it, and both grades appear separately on the statement of results. The entry decision is made by the school's maths department, usually in Year 10 or early Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the Cambridge entry is concentrated in a handful of British-curriculum and mixed-curriculum campuses, all licensed by ADEK. Because Additional Mathematics is a minority entry, two children in the same year group at the same school can be on different pathways, and a parent often finds out that 0606 is coming only when the first topic test comes home.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: AS and A Level Mathematics 9709 opens with Pure Mathematics 1: quadratics, functions, coordinate geometry, circular measure, trigonometry, series, differentiation and integration. A student who has genuinely absorbed 0606 meets most of that list for the second time rather than the first, which is why maths departments recommend it.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain sixth forms are fewer in number than the city's IGCSE provision, so some families look at Abu Dhabi campuses or an online sixth form for Year 12. Carrying 0606 into that transition matters more when the Year 12 school is new to your child, because the maths teacher will not know what was covered in Year 11 and will assume the 0580 baseline.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the IB route that overlaps with 0606. Calculus, functions, sequences and series and the binomial theorem all reappear, assessed across three papers plus an Internal Assessment exploration that the student researches and writes themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Several Al Ain families move from a Cambridge Year 11 into an IB Diploma Year 12, sometimes at a different campus in Al Ain and sometimes in Abu Dhabi. That jump is where 0606 earns its keep: students arriving at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level without any prior calculus spend the first term catching up on technique while also learning IB command terms and the exploration process.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses mathematics against four criteria rather than by a single examination grade, with extended and standard mathematics streams in the final two years. Students finishing MYP extended mathematics and moving into a Cambridge pathway often meet 0606 content with strong reasoning habits but thinner procedural fluency.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain has campuses running MYP as well as Cambridge, and families occasionally transfer between them mid-secondary. A student who moves from MYP into a Cambridge Year 11 that already has 0606 under way needs a short, targeted bridge rather than a general maths course, and that bridge is almost always indices, surds and algebraic fractions first.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-additional-maths-.subjectsIntro: 0606 is rarely the only thing on a Year 11 timetable that needs attention. These are the Cambridge subjects our Al Ain students most often pair with Additional Mathematics, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Two written papers, 80 marks and two hours each, both drawing on the whole syllabus. Functions, quadratics, indices and surds, polynomials, simultaneous equations, logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs, circular measure, trigonometry, counting, series, vectors and calculus. No part of the course can be dropped before the exam.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The main Cambridge IGCSE maths entry. Extended tier is the prerequisite in practice for 0606, because 0606 assumes fluent algebraic manipulation from the first lesson. Students who are still losing marks on algebraic fractions and indices in 0580 are better served by fixing that before adding Additional Mathematics work.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: The graphics-calculator variant of Cambridge IGCSE maths, with an investigation-style paper and a modelling paper. Schools that run 0607 rather than 0580 sometimes still enter strong candidates for 0606, which creates an odd mix of calculator-rich and calculator-light habits that is worth unpicking early.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The science most helped by 0606. Kinematics, graphs of motion, and rearranging formulae all become easier once a student differentiates comfortably and reads gradient and area questions as calculus rather than as geometry. Extended tier adds a practical paper, assessed either as Paper 5 or the alternative-to-practical Paper 6.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, titration arithmetic and rate-of-reaction graph work are where a strong 0606 student pulls ahead. Chemistry marks are usually lost on method and unit presentation rather than on recall, which is the same failure mode 0606 Paper 2 punishes in longer structured questions.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers data representation, networks, hardware and security; Paper 2 covers algorithms, programming and logic. Binary and hexadecimal conversion, truth tables and iteration all reward the same procedural precision that 0606 demands, and a student strong in one is usually fixable in the other.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Two papers, one multiple-choice and one structured with a data-response section. The calculation content is light compared with 0606, but the graph-reading discipline transfers directly: read the axes, state the units, and answer the command word rather than describing the diagram.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Paper 1 reading and Paper 2 directed writing and composition. Strong mathematicians often arrive here with the thinnest margin in their subject set, because the paper rewards structured argument under time pressure rather than correct answers, and nothing in the 0606 toolkit helps.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Mostly recall and application, with magnification calculations and graph interpretation as the quantitative content. Students carrying 0606 alongside three sciences are the ones most at risk of running out of revision time, so sequencing across subjects matters as much as teaching within one.

subjects.name: AS and A Level Mathematics (9709)
subjects.description: Pure Mathematics 1 revisits quadratics, functions, coordinate geometry, circular measure, trigonometry, series and introductory calculus. Al Ain students who move straight from 0606 into 9709 in Year 12 usually find the first term familiar; those who skipped 0606 spend it learning technique and content at the same time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one over live video
modes.description: A single fixed slot each week, one student and one tutor, on a shared whiteboard where both of you can write. This is the default for a Year 11 running 0606 alongside 0580 from the start of the year, because it tracks the school's teaching order rather than fighting it.

modes.title: Twice-weekly technique blocks
modes.description: Two shorter sessions in a week, used when a single topic area is the problem. Calculus is the usual reason: differentiation rules need to be practised across several days to become automatic, and one long weekly lesson leaves six days for the method to fade.

sections.heading: What the search for a 0606 tutor in Al Ain is really asking
paragraphs: A parent typing this query has almost always had the same conversation at home. The maths that used to be straightforward has stopped being straightforward, and the child cannot explain why. The answer is nearly always structural: Additional Mathematics 0606 is not a harder version of 0580, it is a different syllabus with new content, and the first weeks of it depend on algebra fluency that a comfortable 0580 Extended student may have been getting away with rather than owning.

So the useful question is not whether your child needs a maths tutor. It is which of the fourteen 0606 topic areas is actually broken, whether the cause is content never taught or technique never practised, and how many weeks remain before the series the school has entered them for. Those three answers produce completely different plans. A student eight months out needs a teaching sequence that runs alongside school. A student eight weeks out needs breadth-first revision and timed sections, and should stop trying to master every topic.

The second half of the query matters too. Al Ain is a smaller private-school market than Abu Dhabi island or Dubai, and Additional Mathematics is a minority entry inside it. The number of adults within a reasonable drive who have taught 0606 to examination standard is genuinely small. That is why we teach this subject one-to-one over live video rather than by sending anyone to a UAE address: the constraint on quality here is the size of the local pool, and online delivery removes that constraint entirely while keeping the lesson live, interactive and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: The 0606 syllabus, topic area by topic area
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics is assessed in two written papers of two hours and 80 marks each, and both papers can draw on any part of the syllabus. There is no coursework, no practical and no optional topic. That single design fact drives everything about how the course should be revised: nothing can be safely dropped, so a revision plan that goes deep on three topics and ignores the rest is a gamble rather than a strategy.

The content splits into four families. There is the algebra extension work, which builds on 0580 Extended: functions with formal domain and range, quadratics and the discriminant, indices and surds, the factor theorem for polynomials, simultaneous equations with one non-linear equation. There is the analytic work: logarithmic and exponential functions, straight-line graphs used to linearise relationships. There is the geometry and trigonometry block, taught in radians throughout, with arc length, sector area, identities and general solutions. And there is calculus, which is new to the student and carries the heaviest teaching load.

The table below maps each family to what it adds beyond 0580, when Al Ain schools typically first teach it, and the error that most often costs marks. The syllabus version your child's school is following matters, because Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle and the document for your series is the one that governs the paper. The current syllabus, the specimen papers and the calculator and formula-list rules are all published on cambridgeinternational.org, and the school's exams officer can confirm which version applies to your child's entry.

sections.heading: 0580 Extended against 0606: same student, different exam
paragraphs: Families often assume Additional Mathematics is the top end of the same course. It is not. Both qualifications appear separately on the statement of results, both are examined in their own papers, and a child can do well in one and badly in the other. Understanding where the two diverge is what stops a tutoring plan from being spent in the wrong place, which in practice means spending it on algebra that was already fine rather than on the calculus that was not.

The honest test of readiness is 0580 Extended algebra under time pressure. A student who can simplify algebraic fractions, manipulate indices, rearrange a formula with the subject appearing twice and solve a quadratic three different ways is ready for 0606 content. A student who can do those things slowly, with prompting, is not yet ready, and adding 0606 work on top will usually damage both grades. We say this at the trial lesson when it is what the diagnostic shows, because the alternative is a family paying for months of the wrong teaching.

The comparison below is the one we walk Al Ain parents through at the start. It also answers the question maths departments get asked every year: should a borderline candidate be entered for Additional Mathematics at all? The qualification is useful, particularly as preparation for AS Pure Mathematics 1 or for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, but a weak 0606 grade earned at the cost of a strong 0580 grade is a poor trade, and no tutor can promise a grade in either.

sections.heading: Calculus from a standing start, and the weeks it really takes
paragraphs: Calculus is where 0606 is won and lost, and it behaves differently from every other topic on the course. Algebra and trigonometry can be improved by revision, because the student has met the ideas before and is sharpening them. Differentiation is genuinely new. A student is being asked to accept a definition, learn three rules, recognise which rule a question needs, and then apply it inside a context such as a stationary point, a tangent, a rate of change or a kinematics problem. Each of those layers fails separately.

What that means in a teaching plan is sequence and spacing rather than volume. The rules have to be practised across several days until selecting the right one stops being a decision. Then the contexts are layered one at a time: tangents and normals, then increasing and decreasing functions, then stationary points and their nature, then connected rates, then kinematics where the language changes but the mathematics does not. Integration follows the same pattern, with the constant of integration and definite-integral limits as the two reliable sources of lost marks.

The realistic timescale is the thing families most want and least often get told straight. For a student meeting differentiation for the first time with a competent algebra base, the rules and the standard contexts take several weeks of regular work rather than a single intensive weekend, and integration adds more on top. A plan that starts in the autumn term can afford to teach this properly alongside school. A plan that starts six weeks before the papers cannot, and should instead secure the marks that are reliably available: the algebra families, radians, series and the standard differentiation questions that appear in almost every paper.
