sections.heading: Three ways to buy 0450 help around Al Ain, and what each gets you
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for this search publishes a price, which is odd given that price is the first thing a parent wants to know. The figures below are market rates taken from what providers advertise publicly, with the provider and the month named. They are not IB Gram's price list. What a 0450 block costs here depends on level and session count, and that figure comes from a consultation after the free trial lesson rather than from a rate card on a landing page.

Two things move the number in Al Ain specifically. The first is the specialist pool. Al Ain's Cambridge cohort is smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so a family hunting for someone experienced with 0450 Paper 2 inside the city is choosing from a short list, and short lists price upwards. The second is travel. Any in-home rate carries the drive, and Al Ain's low density means a tutor crossing from Zakher to Al Towayya is pricing forty minutes of road into a sixty-minute lesson.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and every UAE lesson runs live over video. That removes travel from the price and widens the pool from the adults available in Al Ain to the teachers available in Gulf Standard Time. A parent who wants to watch a lesson can join from the same room; the screen is shared and nothing about the session is hidden from the household.

Ask any provider three questions before paying: what is the hourly figure, is VAT included or excluded, and what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. Providers who answer all three in writing are the ones worth shortlisting.

sections.heading: Entry deadlines, timetable zones and sitting 0450 from Al Ain
paragraphs: The dates that matter in a Cambridge subject sit months before the examination, and the school sets them, not the family. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and those are the two an Al Ain centre enters candidates for; the series examined in February and March is an India entry route and should not appear on your calendar at all. Read as a decision rather than as a date list, it works like this: entries for June close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper; forecast grades go in before the exam period opens; the papers run through June on the zone timetable; and results reach the school through Direct in the summer. November then repeats the whole sequence on its own dates, which is why November is the resit route for a 0450 grade that came in under target rather than a different qualification.

That gap is the planning tool. Counting backwards from a series, the useful markers are entries closing roughly ten weeks before the first paper, school mock examinations somewhere between six and ten weeks out, and the last productive window for changing technique about eight weeks out. A family starting Paper 2 work four weeks before the examination is not too late to gain marks, but the work changes: it becomes timing and command words rather than content coverage.

One Cambridge detail catches UAE families every year. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A timetable downloaded from a forum is not necessarily the one your child's Al Ain centre is working to. Ask the examinations officer for the zone, in writing, at the start of the examination year.

Private candidates sit the same papers through a centre that accepts them rather than through their own school, and that centre sets its own internal deadline on top of Cambridge's. Al Ain families who have changed schools mid-course, or who want a subject the school does not teach, should open that conversation a full term before the entry deadline, since the nearest accepting centre may be in Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: What a 0450 tutor may do with your child's work, and what it may not
paragraphs: 0450 has no coursework, which removes the academic-honesty question that dominates IB subjects. There is nothing to submit and nothing to declare. What remains is school-set work: internal assessments, mock papers, projects and the homework a teacher grades and reports on. A tutor's boundary there is the same as in any subject, and it is worth stating plainly, because at least two providers in this market sell finished work rather than teaching.

A tutor teaches, models, questions and gives feedback on what the student has produced. It may mark a practice answer against a published scheme, show a better structure and ask for a rewrite. It does not supply sentences for a piece of work a teacher will grade as your child's own, and it does not sit beside a student during a timed school assessment. A provider offering to produce assessed work for a fee is a reason to walk away, whatever the subject and whatever the deadline.

There is a related rule specific to the Emirate of Abu Dhabi that Al Ain parents should know. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours is expected to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That has been press-reported rather than read from the policy document, so verify the current wording with the school before arranging anything. The practical point stands: your child's own teacher, privately, is not an arrangement to pursue here.

On permits generally, private tutoring in the UAE is regulated rather than informal. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted with scepticism.

A single marked paper tells a subject teacher more than a long conversation does, because it shows whether marks are going on content, on command words or on the clock.

process.description: Sessions are booked as a short block rather than open-ended, at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time that survives the Al Ain school run. The plan names the units to be covered, the papers to be practised and the number of marked questions due between sessions.

process.title: Marked work between every session
process.description: Two examination questions a week, returned marked with the scheme alongside them. The student keeps a running error list, and that list becomes the revision plan for the final weeks instead of a freshly rewritten set of notes nobody reads twice.

process.title: Review at week six, including the option to stop
process.description: A short written review of what has moved and what has not. If the marks are not responding, the honest answer is sometimes a different tutor, a different subject decision, or no tutoring at all. That conversation happens at week six rather than at the end of the year.

whyPoints.title: A 0450 specialist, not a general business tutor
whyPoints.description: 0450 is not AS Business and not IB Business Management. Its papers, tariffs and command words are its own. The tutor matched to an Al Ain student is one who has marked these two papers in quantity and can name the band an answer landed in and the clause that would have moved it.

whyPoints.title: The pool is not limited to who lives in Al Ain
whyPoints.description: Al Ain's Cambridge cohort is small and its pool of 0450 specialists smaller. Teaching live over video means the match is made on subject and examination experience rather than on driving distance from Al Jimi, Zakher or Al Muwaiji.

whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, the published scheme beside them, a dated error list and a short written note after each session. Progress in 0450 is visible in a script or it is not visible at all, and a parent should never have to take progress on trust.

whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, marks and gives feedback on your child's own answers. It does not produce work a school will grade as theirs. That line is published on the page because at least two providers in this market cross it and advertise the fact.

whyPoints.title: Regulators named, not borrowed
whyPoints.description: Al Ain's private schools sit under ADEK, and tutoring permits come through MoHRE. This page explains what each body does and points to the official route. IB Gram claims no licence, approval or partnership from either of them, or from Cambridge.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450 split into Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: No. 0450 is untiered, so every candidate sits the same two papers and the full grade range stays open to all of them. That differs from Mathematics 0580 and Physics 0625, where a Core entry caps the grade available before the examination begins. The practical consequence for an Al Ain family is that there is no tier decision to get wrong in Business Studies and no negotiation with the school about moving a child up or down a route. Everything is decided on the day, across two ninety-minute papers of 80 marks each.

faqs.question: Is the Paper 2 case study released to students before the examination?
faqs.answer: No. The case study material for 0450 appears in the examination itself, so candidates meet the business for the first time in the room. There is no pre-release booklet to study and nothing to prepare about that particular firm. What can be prepared is the method: reading the questions first, annotating the insert for figures and market detail, and carrying one named detail into every paragraph. Confirm the arrangements for your child's series with the school's examinations officer, since Cambridge publishes component details per syllabus version.

faqs.question: My daughter is taking 0450 and 0455 in the same year. Is that too much overlap?
faqs.answer: It is a common pairing and a workable one, provided she knows which examination is asking what. The content overlaps around demand, costs, competition and government influence, so revision is efficient. The examinations do not overlap. 0450 wants applied judgement about a named firm; 0455 wants modelled reasoning, often with a diagram. Students who revise them as one subject tend to write economics answers in the business paper and lose application marks. Keeping two separate answer-structure habits is the thing to practise, and one session on each paper's command words usually settles it.

faqs.question: How many marks does the biggest 0450 question usually carry?
faqs.answer: The highest-tariff questions on each paper are the evaluation ones, which ask for a judgement with justification and sit well above the explain questions in value. They deserve specific planning, because they are where the spread between a middle grade and a top grade opens up. A balanced discussion that never reaches a decision loses the justification marks however well written it is. Check the current specimen papers through your child's school for the exact structure of the series they will sit, since Cambridge revises question patterns on a published cycle.

faqs.question: What does justify actually require in a 0450 answer?
faqs.answer: A decision, plus a reason that could only apply to the business in front of you. A justified recommendation names the option chosen, says why it beats the alternative, and ties that to something in the insert: the firm's cash position, its market, its capacity, its workforce. Generic justification, such as saying it will increase profits, scores at the bottom of the band. The test a student can apply alone is whether the final paragraph would still make sense if the case study were about a different company. If it would, it is not justification yet.

faqs.question: Which 0450 unit do students most often arrive weak in?
faqs.answer: Financial information and decisions, by a wide margin, and not because the arithmetic is hard. Break-even, cash-flow forecasts and simple ratios are mechanically simple; the marks sit in interpretation. A student can calculate a break-even output correctly and then write nothing about what it means for the firm's pricing or its margin of safety. External influences is the second common gap, usually because it is taught late in Year 11 once revision has already started. Both respond quickly to question practice rather than to rereading the chapter.

faqs.question: Can my son use Al Ain or UAE businesses as examples in his answers?
faqs.answer: In Paper 2 the marks come from the insert, so outside examples add nothing and cost time. In Paper 1 a brief, accurate example can support an explanation, and a local one is as good as any other if it is correct and relevant to the point. Where UAE context genuinely helps is understanding: exchange rates, import costs, free-zone ownership rules and seasonal demand are easier to grasp from a business a student has walked past than from a textbook abstraction. Learn the idea locally, then answer the question in front of you.

faqs.question: What is a realistic hourly figure for 0450 support around Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Published market rates across the UAE run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for exam-year specialist support. In-home visits sit around AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in. Those are providers' own advertised figures as at October 2026, not IB Gram's rates. Al Ain pushes the specialist end upwards because the local Cambridge pool is small. Our own figure follows a consultation after the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is a group class at an Al Ain centre better value than one-to-one for 0450?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, often yes: a group spreads the hourly cost and suits a student who simply has not met Unit 5 yet. For paper technique, usually not. What moves 0450 marks is having a specific answer marked and rewritten, which is hard to deliver to eight students at once. A sensible pattern is group or school teaching for content, with a short one-to-one block on Paper 2 technique in the ten weeks before a series. Compare the monthly package price against the hours it actually contains first.

faqs.question: Does my child need a calculator in the 0450 examinations?
faqs.answer: Calculators are permitted in Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies, and the calculations involved, percentage change, simple ratios, break-even and cash-flow totals, are within reach of a basic scientific model. The marks lost on calculation questions are rarely arithmetic. They go on missing working, missing units and missing interpretation: a figure written without AED or a percentage sign, or a correct answer with nothing said about what it means for the firm. Confirm permitted equipment for your child's series with the examinations officer, because centre instructions are issued per series.

faqs.question: Our school enters candidates in June. When does the entry actually close?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, and the school submits it rather than the family. Cambridge gives UAE candidates a June series and a November series, so the real question is which of the two the entry names. For June, final entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper; forecast grades follow before the exam period opens; and results reach schools through Direct in the summer. The November series closes its own entries well ahead of its own papers, and that is the part worth understanding in advance: a disappointing June grade in 0450 is re-entered in November, but only if somebody files the entry before that window shuts. Ask the examinations officer for your centre's internal deadline, which is usually earlier again, and get it in writing.

faqs.question: Can my daughter sit 0450 as a private candidate from Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a centre that accepts private candidates, which is not the same as any school teaching Cambridge. The centre handles the entry, sets its own earlier deadline and charges its own fees, and the nearest accepting centre to Al Ain may be in Abu Dhabi. Start the conversation a full term before the entry deadline, because a late enquiry often means waiting for the next series. Tutoring can prepare a private candidate for both papers, but the entry is arranged between the family and the centre.

faqs.question: Does ADEK regulate who tutors my child in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included, so it regulates your child's school rather than your private tutoring arrangement. Individual tutors sit under a different rule: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. ADEK's ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. IB Gram holds no approval from either body.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write the answers my son hands in to his teacher?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to do that is selling something that can get a student into real trouble. A tutor's job is to teach, to mark your son's own answers against the published scheme, to show a better structure and to make him rewrite it himself. 0450 has no coursework component, so there is nothing to submit and nothing to declare, but school-set assessments still have to be his work. A useful test: after a session he should be able to explain the improvement in his own words.

faqs.question: Does 0450 help if she wants to study business at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: It is useful preparation and it is not a requirement. University entry for an IGCSE and A Level student runs through Ministry of Education equivalency, which on the British track asks for five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with grades no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Business Studies can be one of the five. Verify current requirements on the ministry's own channels; tutoring is not required for equivalency.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-business-studies-.closingBody: If you are weighing 0450 against 0455 or 0452, or watching Paper 2 marks stall in the fifties, the useful first step is small. Send the most recent marked script and the school's entry statement, take the free trial lesson with a tutor who teaches this syllabus, and read the written note that comes back. intro.heading: Where your child is now, where they have to be, and what the weeks between look like
paragraphs: Almost every 0620 enquiry from Al Ain arrives with the same three facts missing. A parent knows the last mark, roughly. They know the grade the school has predicted, roughly. They do not know how many weeks remain before the papers, which topics are actually unfinished, or what a week of work is supposed to produce. Without those, tutoring becomes an open-ended subscription, and the only signal available is whether the student seems happier. That is a poor instrument for a decision this expensive.

So this page is built around a timeline rather than around a sales argument. Week one establishes where the student genuinely is, on paper, measured against the mark scheme rather than against a feeling. Week two produces a written plan with topics against dates. From there each fortnight closes a named gap and the plan is updated, and by the time the series arrives there is a document showing what was fixed, what was not, and what was consciously dropped. A parent can audit that without knowing any chemistry.

Chemistry suits this treatment better than most subjects, because 0620 is unusually legible. Twelve topic areas, and a candidate sits three papers at either tier: a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper worth half the grade, and either the practical test or the alternative to practical worth a fifth. Nothing is hidden in coursework. That means every week of work maps onto a specific component, and a plan can be written in a way that is checkable. Confirm the component details for your child's series on cambridgeinternational.org, since Cambridge revises syllabuses on a published cycle.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-tu.programmesIntro: 0620 sits inside a Cambridge science sequence, and where your child is on it determines what a week of work is for. The same hour spent in Year 9, in the first term of Year 10 and in February of Year 11 should look completely different, and a tutor who runs all three the same way is working to a template rather than to a timeline.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Science
programmes.description: Science taught as one subject, with the chemistry strand covering particles, states, mixtures, separation techniques and simple reactions. The content is not demanding and the habits are: reading a measuring cylinder properly, recording to a sensible precision, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data. Students who leave Year 9 without those habits arrive in 0620 with a gap that looks like a chemistry problem and is actually a laboratory-practice problem.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain schools vary in how much practical work the lower secondary years get, because laboratory time is a timetabling and staffing question rather than a syllabus one. Ask how many practical sessions your child had in Year 9. That number predicts the alternative-to-practical paper two years later better than any end-of-year science grade does.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: The syllabus this page covers, in twelve topic areas: states of matter, atoms and elements, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, chemical energetics, chemical reactions, acids and bases, the Periodic Table, metals, chemistry of the environment, organic chemistry, and experimental techniques and chemical analysis. Tiered into Core and Extended. A candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper worth half the grade, and either the practical test or the alternative to practical worth a fifth.
programmes.countryNote: Two things an Al Ain family should establish in writing from the school: the tier your child is entered for, and whether the centre has entered the practical test or the alternative to practical. The second question is the one nobody asks, and it changes the last month of preparation completely because the two papers reward different skills.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics in two IGCSE grades rather than three separate ones. Schools run it where the option blocks will not carry three separate sciences, and the chemistry content inside it is a reduced version of 0620 rather than a different subject. Families frequently discover the difference only when a tutor asks for the syllabus code and the answer turns out not to be 0620 at all.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's smaller schools use Co-ordinated Sciences more often than Abu Dhabi's larger campuses do, simply because a cohort of sixty cannot staff three separate science sets. If your child is on 0654, past papers for 0620 will contain content they are not sitting, and a plan built from them wastes weeks. Check the code before anything else.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry
programmes.description: The continuation route, and the reason the Extended content matters beyond the Year 11 grade. AS Chemistry assumes fluency in moles, equations and bonding from the first week, treating them as tools rather than as topics. A candidate who got through 0620 by learning reaction facts and avoiding the calculations meets that assumption immediately, and the gap shows up in the first AS assessment rather than gradually over the year.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 science provision in Al Ain is narrower than in Abu Dhabi, and some families end up weighing a move or a commute. That decision is much easier to take with a secure Extended 0620 grade in hand, which is a better reason to fix stoichiometry in Year 11 than the IGCSE grade considered alone.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-tu.subjectsIntro: 0620 is published as twelve topic areas, and the list below is ordered the way a timeline has to treat them rather than the way the syllabus numbers them. Some of these are a week's work and some are a fortnight's, and knowing which is which is most of what makes a revision plan realistic.

subjects.name: Stoichiometry
subjects.description: Formulae, equations, the mole, molar mass, concentration, reacting masses, limiting reagents and percentage yield. The largest single block of work in the subject and the one that decides grades, because the calculations appear inside questions about every other topic rather than only in their own section.

subjects.name: Atoms, elements and compounds
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, electronic configuration, ionic and covalent bonding, giant structures and metallic bonding. Students lose marks explaining properties from structure: the question asks why graphite conducts, and an answer that describes graphite's structure without linking it to delocalised electrons scores part marks.

subjects.name: Acids, bases and salts
subjects.description: Acid and base properties, pH, neutralisation, salt preparation, titration and tests for ions and gases. Rich in marks and heavily examined on both the theory and the practical route, which makes it the highest-value fortnight in a twelve-week plan.

subjects.name: Chemical reactions
subjects.description: Rate of reaction, reversible reactions, equilibrium and the factors affecting each, plus redox. Rate questions reward explanation in terms of particle collisions and energy, and answers that restate the trend without a mechanism are the standard loss here.

subjects.name: Electrochemistry
subjects.description: Electrolysis of molten and aqueous compounds, electrode products, half equations at Extended, and electroplating. Mechanical once understood, and reliably dropped because it is taught late and feels unlike the rest of the course.

subjects.name: The Periodic Table
subjects.description: Group trends, Group I and VII properties, transition elements and noble gases. Learnable in a week and generous in the examination, provided the student can explain a trend rather than recite it, which is the distinction the mark scheme draws.

subjects.name: Metals
subjects.description: Reactivity series, extraction including the blast furnace, alloys, rusting and its prevention. Fact-heavy and therefore well suited to the weeks when a student is tired, which is a genuine planning consideration in February.

subjects.name: Chemical energetics
subjects.description: Exothermic and endothermic changes, energy level diagrams, bond breaking and making, and energy calculations at Extended. Short, and the energy-change calculation is a predictable question that students lose through sign errors rather than through misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry
subjects.description: Fuels, homologous series, alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, polymers and at Extended esters and structural formulae. Almost always taught last and almost always rushed, which is why it appears as a known gap in most Year 11 plans rather than as a surprise.

subjects.name: Experimental techniques and chemical analysis
subjects.description: Measurement, purity, separation and purification methods, chromatography and identification of ions and gases. This is the content the practical route examines directly, and it is the single most under-revised area in the subject.

subjects.name: States of matter
subjects.description: Solids, liquids and gases, kinetic particle theory, changes of state, diffusion and the effect of molecular mass. Taught first, assumed secure, and quietly responsible for lost marks whenever a later question asks for a particle-level explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry of the environment
subjects.description: Water treatment and tests, fertilisers, air quality, pollutants and their sources and effects, and the greenhouse gases. Short, applied, and a reliable source of marks for a student who can name a pollutant, its source and its specific effect in one sentence.

sections.heading: Week one: what a 0620 baseline actually measures
paragraphs: The first session should produce a number and a map, not a rapport. A baseline means a set of past-paper questions attempted cold under something close to exam conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, with the lost marks tallied against the twelve topic areas. That takes most of an hour and it is the most valuable hour in the whole arrangement, because every decision afterwards depends on it being honest.

What a baseline reveals is usually not what the family expected. Students self-report their weaknesses badly, and in chemistry they report the topics that felt hard in class rather than the ones costing marks. A student who says organic chemistry is the problem frequently turns out to be losing more marks on structure-and-properties explanations and on the mole calculations threaded through other questions. Those are invisible from the inside, because the student does not know what the mark scheme wanted.

A baseline also distinguishes between three failure modes that look identical in a percentage. Content the student has never been taught properly. Content they know but cannot apply to an unfamiliar context. And content they know and can apply but cannot produce at speed. Those call for three different responses: teaching, question practice and timed drilling respectively. A tutor who cannot tell you which one dominates is going to spend your weeks on the wrong activity.

Finally, the baseline should establish the administrative facts, because they are surprisingly often unknown. Which tier is the entry. Which syllabus code: 0620 as a separate science or 0654 as part of Co-ordinated Sciences. And whether the centre has entered the practical test or the alternative to practical. All three come from the examinations officer, all three change the plan, and a family that has them in writing can check every claim anybody makes afterwards.

sections.heading: The three papers your child sits, and which fifth of the grade nobody revises
paragraphs: 0620 candidates sit three components, which surprises parents expecting two. There is a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper that carries half the grade, and a practical component worth a fifth, offered either as a laboratory test or as a written alternative to practical. Core and Extended candidates sit different versions of the first two, and the same choice of practical route applies to both.

The theory paper is where attention naturally goes, and reasonably so at half the grade. The multiple-choice paper gets less, and loses marks in a specific and fixable way: students treat it as a recall exercise when a significant share of the questions require a short calculation or an elimination step. Practising it against the clock, with no blanks left, is worth more than re-reading notes, and it is the single easiest component to improve in the final month.

The practical fifth is the one almost nobody plans for. Whichever route the centre has entered, the content examined is experimental techniques and chemical analysis: measurement and precision, separation and purification, chromatography, and the tests for ions and gases. That is a defined body of material with predictable questions, and it is routinely left unrevised because it does not feel like chemistry in the way an equation does. A fifth of the grade is a grade boundary or two.

Ask the examinations officer which practical route the centre uses and get the answer in writing, because the two reward different preparation. The laboratory test rewards having actually done the manipulations; the written alternative rewards being able to read a described method, spot the control and the variable, criticise the procedure and improve it. Both are teachable over video, but they are not the same job, and a plan written without knowing which one applies is guessing with a fifth of the grade.

sections.heading: The twelve-week 0620 plan, week by week
paragraphs: A plan is not a list of topics. It is a list of topics with dates and with a stated product for each block, so that at the end of any fortnight you can ask whether the thing that was supposed to exist exists. Below is the shape of a twelve-week plan for an Extended candidate who has covered the syllabus once and is losing marks rather than missing content, which is the most common position after January mocks.

The ordering is by mark yield, not by syllabus number. Stoichiometry comes first and takes a fortnight because mole work appears inside questions about every other topic, so fixing it raises the ceiling everywhere at once. Acids, bases and salts comes second because it is heavily examined on both the theory paper and the practical route. Experimental techniques comes earlier than feels natural, because it is a fifth of the grade and the least revised part of the course.

Weeks seven to ten take the remaining content in descending order of yield, with the order adjusted by what the baseline showed rather than by a template. Energetics and the Periodic Table are quick. Metals and environmental chemistry are fact-heavy and suit a tired week. Organic chemistry sits late because it was taught late and because it is self-contained enough to be learned in a block. Electrochemistry is mechanical and goes where there is room.

The last two weeks are deliberately not content. They are full papers sat to time, marked, and a short list of the three things most likely to cost marks on the day. What a plan like this cannot do is promise a grade, and no tutor should offer one. What it can do is leave you holding a document that says which gaps closed, which did not, and which were dropped on purpose, which is a reasonable thing to expect for the money.

sections.heading: Stoichiometry: the fortnight that decides the grade
paragraphs: If a plan has to put one thing first, it is stoichiometry, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of taste. Mole calculations do not stay inside their own section of the paper. They appear inside electrolysis questions, inside titration questions, inside yield and purity questions, and inside almost anything about reacting masses. A student who is slow or uncertain with moles therefore loses marks in topic areas they otherwise know well, which is why their script looks randomly weak rather than weak in one place.

The specific failures are consistent across cohorts. Converting between mass, moles and molar mass without writing the relationship down, then losing the thread in a two-step question. Not balancing the equation before using the ratio. Concentration in mol/dm3 and g/dm3 treated as interchangeable. Limiting reagent questions where the student calculates both reactants and then picks the wrong one. And percentage yield and percentage purity confused, which costs the whole question rather than a method mark.

The fix is unglamorous: a worked structure applied every single time, even on questions the student could do in their head. Write what is given, write what is wanted, write the relationship, balance the equation, then substitute. Students resist this because it feels slow, and it is slow, right up to the point where it becomes automatic and they stop making the two-step errors that were costing them four marks a paper. A fortnight is about what this takes.

There is a second reason to front-load it. AS Chemistry assumes mole fluency from the first week, treating it as a tool rather than a topic. A candidate who reached a decent 0620 grade by learning reaction facts and avoiding calculations meets that assumption immediately in Year 12. For an Al Ain family weighing a narrower local post-16 offer, that matters: keeping 9701 genuinely viable is a better argument for this fortnight than the IGCSE grade on its own.

sections.heading: The practical route, and what a video lesson can honestly do
paragraphs: Here is the honest position, since this is where online tuition is most often oversold. If the centre has entered the laboratory practical test, a tutor working over video cannot replace time at a bench. Manipulation, reading a burette, judging an end point and managing apparatus under time pressure are physical skills, and they are learned in a laboratory. What a tutor can do is prepare everything around the manipulation, which is most of the marks.

That preparation is substantial. The recording of results to an appropriate precision, the table drawn before the experiment rather than during it, the graph with sensible axes and a line of best fit, the conclusion that refers to the actual data rather than to the expected result, and the evaluation that names a specific source of error and a specific improvement. Those are written skills, they are heavily marked, and students lose them routinely regardless of how competent they are with apparatus.

Where the centre has entered the alternative to practical, the position is different and online delivery is a genuinely good fit. That paper gives the student a described method to read critically: identify the variables, spot what is controlled and what is not, criticise the procedure, suggest an improvement, and interpret the results given. It is a reading and reasoning paper about experiments rather than an experiment, and working through methods line by line on a shared screen is close to the ideal way to practise it.

Both routes examine the same underlying content: measurement and precision, separation and purification techniques, chromatography, and the tests for ions and gases. That body of material is finite and the questions on it are predictable, which makes it the best value in the whole subject per hour spent. Learn the ion and gas tests to automatic recall. No tutor will supply Cambridge past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because those are Cambridge's to publish; work from what your centre provides and cite cambridgeinternational.org.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, and why it is always the rushed topic
paragraphs: Organic chemistry appears near the end of the 0620 syllabus and near the end of Year 11, and the two facts combine badly. By the time a department reaches it, the year has lost days to assessment weeks, school events, the winter break and whatever else the calendar did, and a topic scheduled for five weeks gets three. This is not a criticism of any particular school; it is a structural feature of how a two-year course meets a real calendar.

The result is a predictable shape in a baseline. Students can name the homologous series and often remember a reaction or two, and they cannot reliably draw a structural formula, distinguish addition from substitution, or explain what makes a polymer different from its monomer. At Extended the esters and the structural work are frequently blank rather than wrong, which is the signature of content taught too fast rather than content misunderstood.

The useful response is to treat it as a self-contained block rather than as revision spread thinly. Organic chemistry has little dependency on the rest of the syllabus beyond basic bonding, which means it can be learned properly in a concentrated fortnight late in a plan without anything else suffering. Drawing comes first: a student who can draw and name the first few members of each series has a scaffold for every reaction that follows. Reactions come second, as transformations between drawn structures rather than as facts in a list.

This is also the clearest example of why a plan should name the topics it is dropping. If organic chemistry has three weeks of content and the plan has one week left, something has to give, and the choice should be made deliberately and written down rather than discovered in the examination hall. Telling a family that polymers will be covered and esters will not is uncomfortable and considerably more useful than implying that everything will be fine.

sections.heading: What the weeks cost around Al Ain, starting from the cheapest option
paragraphs: Work upwards rather than downwards, because the interesting question is what each step up actually buys. At the bottom of this market are group classes and recorded courses, then budget online tutors advertising from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and from about AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. For a Core candidate working on recall and the multiple-choice paper, that band can genuinely be adequate, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling.

The first step up is to a qualified subject tutor, published at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. What the extra buys is marking: someone who knows what the theory paper's mark scheme rewards and can tell you whether a lost mark was knowledge, application or speed. On a timeline that distinction is the whole product, because it determines what the next eight weeks are spent on. This is the band most 0620 plans belong in.

The next step reaches specialist IGCSE and A-Level rates of about AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. What that buys is subject depth: stoichiometry taught as a single coherent method rather than as a set of question types, and the practical route handled properly. The step after that, named and examiner-background tutors at AED 500 to 650 and above with BartyED publishing AED 650, is rarely what a 0620 candidate needs. Paying for it is usually paying for reassurance.

The in-home band sits outside this ladder rather than on top of it, published at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. The premium is travel. In a city as spread out as Al Ain that premium is larger in practice than the figures suggest, and it buys presence rather than subject depth. All of these are other providers' published rates as at October 2026, quoted for reference, and none of them is an IB Gram price.

sections.heading: The Al Ain calendar the plan has to bend around
paragraphs: A twelve-week plan drawn on a blank calendar is a work of fiction. The real calendar has a winter break in it, a mock window, an assessment week, and in some years Ramadan sitting directly across the revision period. Al Ain's private schools operate inside the Abu Dhabi framework under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, so the term dates and inspection arrangements are Abu Dhabi's rather than Dubai's.

Begin with the fixed external dates, because they are not negotiable and they fall earlier than families expect. A UAE candidate has two Cambridge sittings available: the June series and the November series. A February sitting exists for India only, so any timetable you find with winter paper dates on it is the wrong document for Al Ain. Count backwards from June. Entries are submitted by the centre, not by the family, and the final entry deadline falls in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, with the exact date printed on the centre's statement of entry. Forecast grades are collected weeks before that paper sits, June results reach centres in August, and November is where a disappointing grade gets retaken rather than argued over. A plan that starts in January is therefore already inside the administrative window, not ahead of it.

Then the zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong one. Ask the examinations officer for the zone in writing before the final weeks of the plan are scheduled. A revision calendar built from a timetable found online is a genuine risk and a trivially avoidable one.

Finally, Ramadan. It moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, so in some years it covers the heaviest revision weeks and school days shorten. The plan that survives assumes that from the start: fewer and later sessions, often after Iftar, and the fortnight reallocated rather than crammed. Because lessons run over live video, shifting a slot two hours later costs nothing and nobody drives across the city to do it. Build that into the plan in week two, not in week eight when it is already happening.

sections.heading: What a 0620 tutor will and will not do with school work
paragraphs: Chemistry generates a steady stream of school-set work, and the boundary matters because at least one site ranking for UAE tutoring queries sells completed coursework outright. The position here is narrow and stated rather than implied. A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not write the assignment a student hands in, and will decline if asked, because the risk of that falls on the student rather than on anybody else.

In practice that distinction is easy to apply. On a practical write-up the tutor will read what the student has written, ask what the data actually shows, point at the conclusion that does not refer to the results and let the student rewrite it. On a question the student got wrong, the tutor will ask what the command word was asking for rather than supplying the model answer. The student leaves able to do the next one, which is the only outcome worth paying for.

There are two further things not on offer. Cambridge past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and syllabus documents are not supplied as downloads, because they are Cambridge's to publish; the correct move is to cite cambridgeinternational.org and work from what the centre provides. And no regulator or examination-board approval is claimed. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA or Cambridge status of any kind, operates no office or centre in the UAE, and is a matching platform delivering lessons over video.

The permit framework is worth knowing because it is checkable. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, treat any quoted amount as unverified. Separately, press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff in the emirate from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school; verify the current wording with the authority before relying on it.

process.title: Send the three administrative facts
process.description: The syllabus code, the tier, and whether the centre entered the practical test or the alternative to practical. All three come from the examinations officer in one email, and all three change the plan. A match made without them is a guess, and the practical route in particular is a fifth of the grade nobody usually asks about.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as the baseline
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, no card details taken, and the only condition is that it is a single lesson. Ask for it to be a cold attempt at past-paper questions, marked. That turns an introduction into the first piece of evidence and tells you within the hour whether this tutor marks to the scheme or to an impression.

process.title: Get the plan in writing by week two
process.description: A one-page document: topic areas against dates, what each block will produce, and which topics are being dropped if the timeline is short. You keep a copy. Everything afterwards is measured against it, and a tutor who will not write one is offering weekly lessons rather than a route to the series.

process.title: Audit at the halfway point
process.description: At week six, compare the plan with what exists. Did the stoichiometry assessment happen and did the marks move on the same question types that failed in week one? If the answer is no, the plan changes then rather than in the final fortnight, when there is nothing left to reallocate.

process.title: Finish on papers, not on content
process.description: The last two weeks should be full papers sat to time and marked, plus a short written list of the three habits most likely to cost marks on the day. Specific enough to act on: sign conventions, no blanks on the multiple choice, balance before using a ratio. Not a pep talk.

whyPoints.title: A dated plan, not an open subscription
whyPoints.description: The arrangement starts with a marked baseline and produces a written plan with topics against dates in week two. That makes the work auditable by a parent who has never balanced an equation, and it converts a question nobody can answer, is this working, into one anybody can: did the thing that was supposed to exist this fortnight exist?

whyPoints.title: The practical fifth taken seriously
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the 0620 grade sits on the practical route, and it is the least revised part of the subject because it does not feel like chemistry. The route the centre entered is established first, the ion and gas tests are drilled to automatic recall, and the written skills around any experiment are taught deliberately rather than assumed.

whyPoints.title: Stoichiometry first, for structural reasons
whyPoints.description: Mole work appears inside questions about almost every other topic, so a student slow with moles loses marks in areas they otherwise know. Front-loading it raises the ceiling across the paper at once, and it is also what makes AS Chemistry viable later, which matters where local post-16 options are narrow.

whyPoints.title: Topics dropped out loud
whyPoints.description: On a short timeline something has to give, and the choice should be made deliberately and written down rather than discovered in the examination hall. Saying that polymers will be covered and esters will not is uncomfortable and far more useful than implying that twelve topic areas fit into five sessions.

whyPoints.title: Boundaries stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor marks and teaches your child's own work and will decline to produce work for submission. No past papers or mark schemes as downloads, no regulator or board status claimed, no UAE office, and no promised grade. Several pages competing for this search fail at least one of those, and the exposure lands on the student.

faqs.question: Which three 0620 papers will my child actually sit?
faqs.answer: At either tier a 0620 candidate sits three components: a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper carrying half the grade, and a practical component worth a fifth, entered either as the laboratory practical test or as the written alternative to practical. Core and Extended candidates take different versions of the first two. Parents expecting two papers are often surprised by the third, and it is the one least likely to have been revised. Ask the examinations officer which practical route the centre has entered and get it in writing, then confirm the component details for your series on cambridgeinternational.org.

faqs.question: Is the practical test or the alternative to practical better for my daughter?
faqs.answer: The centre chooses, not the family, so the first job is finding out which one applies. They reward different preparation. The laboratory test rewards having actually performed the manipulations, judged an end point and handled apparatus under time pressure. The written alternative rewards reading a described method critically: identifying variables, spotting what is controlled, criticising the procedure and suggesting a specific improvement. Both examine the same underlying content, which is experimental techniques and chemical analysis including the ion and gas tests. The written route suits online preparation better; the laboratory route needs bench time the school provides.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the series should 0620 chemistry support start?
faqs.answer: Twenty weeks or more allows a complete plan: all twelve topic areas scheduled, a marked assessment closing each fortnight, and the practical route handled deliberately. Ten to fourteen weeks forces selection by mark yield, usually stoichiometry and acids, bases and salts first, with some topics consciously dropped. Under six weeks, teaching new content is generally the wrong call and the work becomes paper technique. None of those is useless, but they are different products, and the number of weeks remaining should decide the arrangement rather than being discovered partway through it.

faqs.question: What should a 0620 baseline assessment test in the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Past-paper questions attempted cold under something close to exam conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, with lost marks tallied against the twelve topic areas. It should also distinguish three failure modes that look identical in a percentage: content never properly taught, content known but not applicable to an unfamiliar context, and content known but not producible at speed. Those call for teaching, question practice and timed drilling respectively. Finally it should establish the administrative facts, which are the tier, the syllabus code and whether the centre entered the practical test or the alternative.

faqs.question: Why does stoichiometry cause so much trouble in IGCSE chemistry?
faqs.answer: Because mole calculations do not stay inside their own section of the paper. They appear inside electrolysis questions, titration questions, yield and purity questions and anything about reacting masses, so a student who is slow or uncertain with moles loses marks in topic areas they otherwise know well. That makes a script look randomly weak rather than weak in one place. The failures are consistent: not balancing before using a ratio, confusing concentration units, picking the wrong limiting reagent, and mixing up percentage yield with percentage purity. A written method applied every time fixes most of it inside a fortnight.

faqs.question: Can a tutor working over video prepare my son for the 0620 practical test?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the honest answer matters more than a reassuring one. Manipulation, reading a burette and judging an end point are physical skills learned at a bench, and the school provides that. What a tutor can prepare is everything around the manipulation, which carries most of the marks: recording to an appropriate precision, drawing the results table before the experiment, graphs with sensible axes, conclusions that refer to the actual data, and evaluations naming a specific error and a specific improvement. If the centre has entered the written alternative to practical instead, online preparation is a genuinely good fit.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0620 chemistry tiered into Core and Extended?
faqs.answer: Yes. Core and Extended candidates sit different versions of the multiple-choice and theory papers, with Extended covering additional content including half equations, yield calculations and extra organic material. The practical route is the same choice at either tier. The tier decision is made by the school and submitted with the entry, which closes months before the papers, so it is effectively settled during Year 10 or early Year 11. Ask which marked scripts the decision rests on, and confirm the current grade ranges available at each tier on cambridgeinternational.org before acting on anything.

faqs.question: My daughter's organic chemistry was taught in three weeks. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Common rather than ideal, and it is structural rather than anybody's fault. Organic chemistry sits near the end of the syllabus and therefore near the end of Year 11, by which point the calendar has absorbed assessment weeks, school events and the winter break, so a topic scheduled for five weeks gets three. The signature in a baseline is distinctive: students can name the homologous series but cannot reliably draw a structural formula or distinguish addition from substitution, and at Extended the esters are often blank rather than wrong. It responds well to one concentrated fortnight late in a plan.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest sensible way to get 0620 help in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: Start at the bottom and ask what each step up buys. Group classes and recorded courses are cheapest, then budget online tutors advertising from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at EdFlik and about AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. For a Core candidate working on recall and the multiple-choice paper, that can genuinely be adequate. The first step worth paying for is a qualified subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300, published by Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE, because that buys marking that tells you whether a lost mark was knowledge, application or speed.

faqs.question: How does the Al Ain school calendar change a chemistry revision plan?
faqs.answer: It removes weeks that a plan drawn on a blank calendar assumes it has. Al Ain's private schools work within the Abu Dhabi framework under ADEK, so the winter break around mid-December, the mock window in January or February and the assessment weeks are set there rather than on Dubai's calendar. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and in some years covers the heaviest revision period, shortening school days. A plan that assumes shortened days from the outset, with fewer and later sessions often after Iftar, survives. One written for normal hours is abandoned in week two.

faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 the same as separate 0620 chemistry?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the single most expensive mix-up available in UAE science tutoring. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering biology, chemistry and physics across two IGCSE grades, and the chemistry inside it is a reduced version of 0620 rather than the same syllabus. Schools with smaller year groups use it because a cohort of sixty cannot staff three separate science sets, which makes it more common in Al Ain than at larger Abu Dhabi campuses. A plan built from 0620 past papers for a 0654 candidate wastes weeks on content they will not sit.

faqs.question: How many 0620 past papers should my child have sat before the exams?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, and each one used properly rather than collected. Two or three full papers sat to time and marked question by question against the published scheme teaches more than eight skimmed without marking. The value is in the marking conversation: what the scheme awarded, what it refused, and why. A reasonable shape for a twelve-week plan is a marked assessment closing each fortnight, a timed multiple-choice paper around week ten, and two complete papers in the final fortnight. Work from the papers the centre provides and cite cambridgeinternational.org for anything else.

faqs.question: Does an ADEK inspection report tell me anything about chemistry teaching?
faqs.answer: Very little that is specific. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, Al Ain included, and an inspection band describes the school as a whole. A strong overall rating is not evidence that Extended chemistry is well taught, and a weaker one is not evidence that it is not, because a single department can sit well above or below its school's average. The more useful questions are local: how many taught hours chemistry gets, how many staff teach it, and whether practical sessions actually happen weekly.

faqs.question: Will a 0620 tutor help with the school's chemistry practical write-up?
faqs.answer: Yes, by teaching it rather than producing it. The tutor will read what your child has written, ask what the data actually shows, point at the conclusion that does not refer to the results, and let the student rewrite it. What will not happen is a tutor writing the write-up your child submits, and anyone offering that is creating an exposure your child carries rather than helping. The skills involved are heavily marked and genuinely teachable: precision in recording, a results table drawn in advance, a conclusion anchored in the data, and an evaluation naming one specific error and one specific improvement.

faqs.question: What does a realistic eight-week change in 0620 marks look like?
faqs.answer: Specific rather than dramatic, and stated in terms of errors rather than grades. No tutor can promise a grade, and a confident number attached to an outcome is the clearest reason to walk away. What can honestly be claimed after eight weeks is that named failures have stopped recurring across three marked scripts: the equation is balanced before the ratio is used, the limiting reagent is identified before the calculation proceeds, and nothing is left blank on the multiple-choice paper. Those are checkable on paper, which is why a plan reports against them rather than against a predicted grade.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-tu.closingHeading: Count the weeks before you count the money
al-ain/cambridge-igcse-chemistry-0620-tu.closingBody: The first question is not what a tutor costs. It is how many weeks remain, which syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, and whether the centre chose the practical test or the written alternative. One email to the examinations officer answers all three, and everything after that becomes a planning exercise rather than a guess. Take the free trial lesson as a marked baseline, insist on a one-page plan with topics against dates by week two, and audit it at week six rather than in the final fortnight. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which means the plan bends around Ramadan and the Al Ain school run instead of breaking on them.

Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, late enough that an Al Ain student is home, fed and at a desk rather than in a car.

intro.heading: Al Ain sits under ADEK, and that changes where you look for answers
paragraphs: Al Ain is part of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, which means its private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, not by the Dubai authority most tutoring websites write about. The u.ae government portal states plainly that ADEK 'supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate'. That single sentence settles a question Al Ain parents ask constantly and almost no tutoring page answers: who to approach, which inspection report applies, and whose rules govern the school your child attends. ADEK was named by none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, which tells you how little of what ranks was written with the Garden City in mind.

The second thing ADEK does not control is the syllabus. Cambridge International owns Computer Science 0478: the content, the two papers, the entry deadlines and the zone timetable your child's centre must use. The school chooses whether to offer 0478 at all, whether to run Information and Communication Technology 0417 instead, and which option block the subject sits in. Those three decisions are made inside the school and are usually fixed by the spring of Year 9. A parent who understands that split stops asking the wrong body for the wrong permission.

The third thing, and the one that drives most 0478 enquiries from Al Ain, is scarcity. Al Ain's private-school set is a fraction of the size of Abu Dhabi island's, and specialist computing teaching is thin wherever the cohort is small. A school with eleven Year 11 computer science candidates cannot justify a dedicated computing specialist, so the subject is frequently taught by a maths or physics teacher with a term's head start on the class. That is not a failure of effort. It is arithmetic, and it is the reason a family 130 kilometres inland ends up looking outside the city for subject-specific help.

What a 0478 tutor is for, then, is narrow and definable. Paper 2 rewards a particular habit of mind: reading a problem statement, choosing a structure, tracing values through it, and writing in pseudocode that an examiner can follow. Paper 1 rewards precise technical vocabulary across six content areas, where an answer that is broadly right and loosely worded scores nothing. Neither of those is learned by watching more videos. Both are learned by writing answers, having them marked against the scheme, and finding out which word was missing.

This page is built around the parts of the system that are checkable: who licenses the school, who sets the paper, when the deadlines fall, what the papers contain, what the Ministry of Education counts for equivalency, and who is legally permitted to charge you for private lessons in the UAE. Every claim below either carries the authority that published it or says openly that it needs confirming for your child's exam year. Tuition itself is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in Al Ain, because home visiting is a service it runs only in India.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-computer-science-.programmesIntro: Computing at 0478 is a stage in a longer route, and in Al Ain that route is often interrupted by a school move between the city, the capital and overseas. Each stage below is described for what it means to a family here rather than for what a prospectus says about it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by two written papers of 50% each. Paper 1 covers data representation, data transmission, hardware, software, the internet and its uses, and automated and emerging technologies. Paper 2 covers algorithm design and problem-solving, programming, databases and Boolean logic. There is no coursework, no tiered entry and no on-screen examination, so the whole grade is decided on two mornings. Confirm the current component structure for your child's exam year at cambridgeinternational.org.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Ain the limiting factor is rarely the syllabus and usually the staffing. Several campuses offer 0478 in a single option block alongside a second science or a language, which forces a choice in Year 9 that nobody explains at the time. If the block is full, the subject is gone for two years, and an Al Ain family that wanted computing has to decide between changing schools and taking it as a private candidate.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Information and Communication Technology 0417
programmes.description: The subject Al Ain parents most often confuse with 0478. ICT is about using software competently and includes practical assessment work at a computer; Computer Science is about how systems and algorithms work and is assessed entirely on paper. A student who enjoys spreadsheets and presentations is not necessarily a student who will enjoy tracing a bubble sort. The two subjects also lead to different A Level routes, which matters if the plan involves an engineering or computing degree.
programmes.countryNote: Smaller Al Ain campuses often run only one of the two, and which one depends on whether the department grew out of the IT suite or the maths corridor. Before booking any tuition, read the subject code off the statement of entry rather than the school report. A tutor preparing a child for 0478 when the school entered them for 0417 is an expensive mistake that takes about six weeks to notice.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level Computer Science 9618
programmes.description: Where a strong 0478 grade normally leads for students staying on a British pathway. The A Level assumes fluency in the algorithmic thinking 0478 introduces and moves quickly into data structures, assembly-level understanding and a substantial programming project. Students who reached grade B at 0478 by memorising Paper 1 definitions rather than by solving problems meet that gap in the first term, and it is a harder gap to close at sixteen than at fifteen.
programmes.countryNote: Al Ain's sixth-form provision is narrower than the capital's, so some families relocate a child to an Abu Dhabi campus for Years 12 and 13 or switch to the Diploma. Either move is easier from a genuine 0478 grade than from a padded one, which is the real argument for spending on Year 11 rather than on Year 12 catch-up.

al-ain/cambridge-igcse-computer-science-.subjectsIntro: The 0478 syllabus divides into ten content areas across the two papers. They do not cost the same number of hours, and they do not fail in the same way. The notes below say what each area actually demands and where marked scripts come apart.

subjects.name: Data representation
subjects.description: Binary, hexadecimal, two's complement, character sets, sound and image representation, and compression. The conversions are mechanical and students get them right. The marks disappear on the explanation questions, where a candidate says a larger sample rate gives better quality without saying that more samples per second capture the waveform more closely. Precision of wording, not arithmetic, is what is being tested.

subjects.name: Data transmission
subjects.description: Packet structure, serial and parallel, simplex and duplex, USB, and error-checking methods including parity, checksums, echo check and check digits. Al Ain candidates reliably lose the parity question because they describe the method without stating what the receiver does when the count disagrees. Error checking is short, examinable every series, and among the cheapest content in the syllabus to repair.

subjects.name: Hardware
subjects.description: The central processing unit, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, registers, embedded systems, input and output devices, and primary and secondary storage. The examinable core is the cycle and the role of each register, which has to be reproduced in sequence. Students who learned the components as a list, rather than as a loop with an order, lose the sequencing marks even when every component is named correctly.

subjects.name: Software
subjects.description: System and application software, operating systems, interrupts, high- and low-level languages, translators and integrated development environments. The distinction between a compiler and an interpreter appears constantly and is answered loosely just as constantly. The mark is for what each produces and when errors are reported, not for which is faster, and that is the sentence most candidates never write.

subjects.name: The internet and its uses
subjects.description: The difference between the internet and the world wide web, URLs, HTTP and HTTPS, browsers, cookies, digital certificates, encryption, and the common security threats. This is the area where general knowledge feels sufficient and is not. A question on a digital certificate wants the role of the certificate authority and the public key, and a plausible paragraph about trust earns nothing.

subjects.name: Automated and emerging technologies
subjects.description: Automated systems built from sensors, microprocessors and actuators, robotics, and the distinction between artificial intelligence, machine learning and expert systems. Candidates must trace a control loop: which sensor reads what, what the microprocessor compares it against, which actuator responds. Writing about the benefits of automation instead of the mechanism is the usual way this topic is lost.

subjects.name: Algorithm design and problem-solving
subjects.description: Decomposition, flowcharts, pseudocode, trace tables, validation and verification, test data, and searching and sorting algorithms. Trace tables carry real marks and are mechanical: every variable gets a column, every pass gets a row, and the final output is read off the bottom. Students who trace in their heads and write only the answer lose most of the question even when the answer is right.

subjects.name: Programming
subjects.description: Data types, variables and constants, sequence, selection, iteration, totalling and counting, string handling, arrays, procedures and functions, and file handling. The examined skill is writing readable, declared, commented code in pseudocode or a permitted high-level language. A fluent coder who never declares a variable or indents a loop scores below a careful student with half the ability.

subjects.name: Databases
subjects.description: Single-table databases, field types, primary keys, and structured query language using SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, SUM and COUNT. This area is short, scores well and is taught last, which is why it is often missing entirely from a January mock. Al Ain students who spend two sessions on SQL syntax usually recover more marks per hour here than anywhere else in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Boolean logic
subjects.description: Logic gates, logic circuits, truth tables and logic expressions. The common failure is a circuit drawn from a written statement where the student guesses the gate order instead of building the expression first and then drawing it. Truth tables are marked row by row, so a systematic student picks up partial credit that a student working intuitively does not.

These notes are about timing and school intake, because those decide whether a Tuesday slot survives to week ten.

regions.name: Asharej
regions.note: Close to the university district and to several of the city's established private campuses. Households here are often academic or public-sector, with a parent who finishes locally rather than commuting, so a 5pm computing session is realistic in a way it is not further out.

regions.name: Al Jimi
regions.note: Central Al Ain around the Jimi area, with short school runs and heavy late-afternoon traffic near the mall. A session set for the window straight after school tends to collide with that traffic, so families here usually settle on a slot after the evening meal instead.

regions.name: Al Khabisi
regions.note: Older residential Al Ain, close to the city centre and to the main hospital. Several households here run shift patterns, which makes a fixed weekly slot more valuable than a flexible one: a 0478 student needs the same hour each week to build the writing habit Paper 2 rewards.

regions.name: Al Maqam
regions.note: Towards the southern edge of the city near the Al Maqam district and the agricultural belt. Distances here are long and few subject specialists live within a reasonable drive, which is exactly the scarcity a video connection removes rather than works around.

regions.name: Hili
regions.note: Northern Al Ain near the Hili area and the Oman border crossing. Families here frequently have children in two different school systems at once, so checking the subject code on each statement of entry matters more than it does for a single-school household.

regions.note: Spread-out villa plots on the south-western side of the city. The school run is the defining constraint: a parent collecting from two campuses rarely has a child at a desk before 6.30pm, which is the single most common reason an early-evening computing slot gets abandoned.

regions.note: Out beyond the main built-up area, where the drive into the city centre is a genuine journey rather than a trip. Any model that depends on a tutor arriving at a particular hour fails here on the first wet evening; a scheduled video session does not.
