sections.heading: How online mentoring actually works for an Al Ain student
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers mentoring for UAE families one-to-one over live video. It does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For this component the format is close to ideal, because the Extended Essay is a document and a document is better worked on together on a shared screen, with the criterion open beside the paragraph being discussed, than read aloud across a table.

The sessions that matter most are short and specific, which also suits video. A design session is a conversation about a question, with somebody writing successive versions of it in a shared file until one survives scrutiny. A draft review is a criterion-by-criterion read with annotations the student keeps. A reflection session is a rehearsal of honest answers. None of those benefits from physical presence, and all of them benefit from the recording or the shared file that a video session leaves behind, because the parent paying for it can see exactly what was advised.

The real advantage in Al Ain is matching. The pool of people within driving distance of this city who have supervised an Extended Essay in Psychology, or in Mathematics, or in Arabic, is small enough that insisting on physical presence effectively means accepting whoever is available. Removing distance from the decision means the person reading the draft is someone who knows that registration subject's conventions. For a component where criterion B is explicitly about subject fit, that is not a minor difference.

Practical checks before committing. Test the connection in the free session from the room the student will actually use, since building quality varies across the outer districts. Make sure the shared folder holds the drafts and the annotated feedback, so progress is visible without anyone having to ask. Agree in advance that the mentor's comments will name criteria rather than rewrite sentences. And bring the school's written deadline list to the first session, because every plan built without it is a guess.

process.title: Bring the deadline list and whatever exists
process.description: The coordinator's written internal deadlines, the registration subject, the current question in whatever state it is in, and the supervisor's name if one has been allocated. Those four things determine what is realistic, and a first session without them is spent discovering them rather than using them.

process.title: Free first session, spent on the question
process.description: One session at no cost, with no card details taken, used on the thing that decides the mark: whether the question can be answered with evidence the student can obtain, and whether the registration subject suits it. If the question survives that session unchanged, it was a good question.

process.title: A written plan with the criteria attached
process.description: A short note setting out the question, the method, where the evidence will come from, which blocks are being bought and when. It also states what the mentor will not do, so the boundary with the school supervisor is on paper rather than assumed by both sides.

process.title: Blocks, not a standing weekly hour
process.description: Sessions concentrated at the design stage, the draft stage and before the final reflection session, with nothing in between. This is deliberately a smaller purchase than a monthly subscription, because an essay that needs weekly attention for eighteen months has a different problem than mentoring can solve.

process.title: Draft feedback read against the five criteria
process.description: Each criterion addressed separately, the mark band named, and the paragraphs identified as carrying marks or not carrying them. The student does every rewrite. The folder keeps every version, which is also the honest record if anyone ever asks whether the work was the candidate's own.

whyPoints.title: Built on Abu Dhabi's framework, not Dubai's
whyPoints.description: Al Ain schools answer to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation across the emirate. Most UAE tutoring advice names KHDA throughout and describes a framework that does not govern your school. The regulator, the ethics rules and the inspection reports used on this page are the ones that actually apply.

whyPoints.title: The registration decision taken seriously
whyPoints.description: In a small cohort the registration subject is often set by supervisor availability rather than by the question. Criterion B is explicitly about subject fit, so that decision is worth challenging early. Mentoring here starts with whether the question belongs where it has been put.

whyPoints.title: Priced by block, not by month
whyPoints.description: The component needs concentrated input at three or four moments and nothing in between. Blocks cost a fraction of a standing monthly plan across eighteen months, and a family can see exactly what each block was for. That is a smaller sale and a more honest one.

whyPoints.title: A boundary stated in writing
whyPoints.description: The mentor advises, explains criteria and reads drafts the student wrote. No text, data, unread sources or reflections come from the mentor. That is written into the plan rather than left to be inferred, because the consequence of getting it wrong falls on the candidate.

whyPoints.title: Al Ain treated as a research site
whyPoints.description: Hili, the oasis irrigation systems, Jebel Hafeet, local agriculture and a university campus are all reachable in an afternoon and almost never used. Primary evidence feeds the twelve-mark critical thinking criterion directly, which makes this the cheapest available upgrade to an essay.

whyPoints.title: Independent of every school and institution named
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to, endorsement from or formal connection with any school, university or examination board. Institutions appear on this page because a student can approach them for evidence, which is the only reason to list them.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for my child's Extended Essay, the school or the IB?
faqs.answer: Both, in different parts. The IB sets the criteria, the 4,000-word ceiling, the reflection requirement and the marking. The school appoints the supervisor, sets every internal deadline and decides how structured the process is. ADEK licenses and inspects the school itself and sets professional-ethics expectations for its staff. A deadline you think unreasonable is a school decision the coordinator can change; a criterion you think harsh is an IB matter the school cannot alter. Knowing which of the three bodies owns a decision is the difference between getting an answer and spending a term frustrated.

faqs.question: How are the thirty-four Extended Essay marks actually divided?
faqs.answer: Focus and method carries six marks, knowledge and understanding six, critical thinking twelve, presentation four, and engagement six. Critical thinking alone is more than a third of the total, which is why a descriptive question caps a grade before anything is written. Presentation is the cheapest four marks available and students lose two or three of them every year to citation and formatting. Engagement is assessed through the reflections rather than the essay. The order to work in is question and method first, evidence second, drafting third, presentation last as a checklist.

faqs.question: Our Al Ain school has put my daughter's essay in the wrong subject. Can that change?
faqs.answer: Often yes, if you raise it early. Small Diploma cohorts mean registration is sometimes decided by which supervisor is free rather than by where the question belongs, and the cost falls on criterion B, which is explicitly about using the registered subject's terminology and sources. Ask the coordinator one direct question in the spring term of the first Diploma year: which subject will this question be marked in, and does the question suit it. After a draft exists the realistic option is reframing the question to belong where it has been put.

faqs.question: What primary research can a student in Al Ain realistically do?
faqs.answer: More than most candidates attempt. Hili Archaeological Park, the oasis irrigation systems, date agriculture around Zakher and Al Foah, the altitude gradient up Jebel Hafeet, heritage visitor management at Al Jahili, and a university campus in Al Muwaiji are all reachable in an afternoon. Primary evidence feeds the twelve-mark critical thinking criterion directly, which no literature summary can match. The limit is usually nerve rather than access: a short, specific, polite written request naming the student, school, question and time required succeeds often enough to be worth sending several times.

faqs.question: Should we buy weekly sessions for the whole eighteen months?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. The component has three or four moments where a decision is made and long stretches where nothing outside input can usefully touch is happening. A design block of two to four sessions, a draft review block of two to three, one reflection session and perhaps a two-session method block covers it. That is six to twelve sessions across two academic years. A standing monthly plan delivers a great many sessions in the months when the essay needs nothing, and costs several times the block total.

faqs.question: What does Extended Essay mentoring cost at Al Ain market rates?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates put a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and an IB specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives AED 200 to AED 450 and above. A ten-session block programme therefore sits in the low thousands of dirhams across two years. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures with sources named, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Can a paid mentor run the reflection sessions instead of the school supervisor?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering it is describing something that does not exist. The three mandatory reflection sessions, including the concluding viva voce, are conducted by the supervisor the school appointed, who also confirms the work is the candidate's own. A paid mentor is an addition to that arrangement. What a mentor can do is prepare the student to speak honestly in those sessions about their own research decisions, which is what the engagement criterion actually rewards, and that preparation is legitimate and useful.

faqs.question: Why do reflections lose marks when the essay itself is good?
faqs.answer: Because the engagement criterion rewards a record of decisions rather than a summary of content. Six marks sit there, assessed through the reflections form rather than the essay, and the examiner is looking for evidence that the student made choices, hit problems and changed direction. Reflections written as a précis of the finished essay show none of that. Reflections written in one sitting at the end are visible as such. The fix is to record decisions as they happen, including the failures, which is also the only honest way to write them.

faqs.question: When should an Al Ain student actually finish the first draft?
faqs.answer: Before the second Diploma year begins, if the household has any choice in the matter. Nobody sets that deadline, which is exactly why it rarely happens, and it is the single strongest predictor of a calm DP2. A student carrying an unwritten essay into the second year is writing it alongside four or five internal assessments and university applications, and the essay is always what loses. Front-load the question, method and evidence into the first year and keep the second year for revision, reflection and the viva.

faqs.question: Does the UAE academic calendar affect how the essay should be planned?
faqs.answer: Yes, and plans that assume eight months of even effort routinely fail in the third month. The year carries a long winter break, a Ramadan timetable with shortened school days and different energy levels, Eid holidays, and an examination term when every other internal deadline falls at once. Fieldwork and interviews also become much harder once term resumes, so evidence gathering belongs in the first year. Plan around those fixtures explicitly rather than treating the calendar as a flat eighteen months.

faqs.question: Can the essay be registered in Arabic, and is that a good idea?
faqs.answer: It can, and for a confident Arabic speaker it is a strong and under-used option. The drafting load is higher because the writing is in the target language, and the practical constraint in a small Al Ain school is whether a supervisor is available to oversee it, which should be checked before the question is settled rather than after. Questions touching UAE social history, heritage or language policy sit naturally alongside the national subjects a student is already timetabled for, which can make the research load lighter rather than heavier.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education during the Diploma in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: The federal position is that private schools must cover Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum and adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai sets out the detail, including separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Al Ain schools sit under ADEK rather than KHDA, so confirm the exact implementation with your own school. Either way, a DP2 timetable contains more than the Diploma, and essay planning should not assume otherwise.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Extended Essay mentor to a home in Al Ain?
faqs.answer: No. Mentoring for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For this component the format costs nothing, because the essay is a document and a document is better annotated together on a shared screen. In Al Ain it is an advantage: the number of people within driving distance who have supervised an essay in a specific registration subject is small, and removing distance from the decision improves the match.

faqs.question: When are the IB examination and results dates for this cohort?
faqs.answer: Take them from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and not from a tutoring page including this one. Specific session and results dates circulate widely through secondary sources every year and are frequently wrong. For the Extended Essay it matters less than families think, because the deadlines that govern the work are the school's internal ones, set months before any examination. Cambridge and Pearson publish reliable timetables for the IGCSE siblings in a household, but those are different qualifications set by different authorities.

faqs.question: Will the Extended Essay grade matter for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: The essay contributes to the Diploma core and universities read the full diploma result, so it matters indirectly and admissions requirements are set course by course. Check the published entry requirements of the specific programme rather than relying on general advice. On Ministry of Education equivalency, the British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary. No IB points threshold has been confirmed from the Ministry's own pages, so verify any figure on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: What should we ask a mentor in the free session to know whether they are any good?
faqs.answer: Two things. First, ask them to say what is wrong with the current research question, specifically, and what a narrower version would look like. Someone who knows this component will do that in ten minutes; someone who does not will praise the topic. Second, ask them to state in writing what they will and will not do with a draft. A clear answer names the criteria, says feedback will identify bands and paragraphs, and says plainly that no text, data or reflections will come from them.

al-ain/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingHeading: Get the deadline list, then fix the question
al-ain/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingBody: Two documents decide how this component goes, and most families have neither at the point they start looking for help: the coordinator's written list of internal deadlines, and a research question narrow enough that obtainable evidence can answer it. Everything else - the drafting, the citation, the reflections - is work that follows from those two. Bring whatever exists to the free session, including a question you suspect is too broad, and spend that hour on the question rather than on introductions. If it survives the hour unchanged, you have saved yourself eight months of difficulty. If it does not, you have found that out in the cheapest possible way.
